'''Bonnie''', also known as '''Experiment 149''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. She is designed to be an expert in theft and evasion. She also has advanced lingual skills, enabling her to easily communicate with her partner-in-crime, [[Clyde (150)|Clyde]], whom she is programmed to be drawn to. Her one true place was originally in Kokaua Town Prison, but she was paroled in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]". After that, it is unknown where her one true place currently is.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 149 was the 149th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. She was designed to work with Experiment 150 to steal many belongings and evade arrest. 149 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Bonnie & Clyde - Bonnie and Clyde after activation.jpg|thumb|left|Bonnie and Clyde after activation]]
149 and 150's pods eventually made their way into a supply of doughnut holes at [[Kiki's Coffee Hut]]. While off duty, [[Officer Kahiko]] bought a bag containing two dozen doughnut holes at the coffee shack. He then took out 149 and 150's pods and (mistaking them for a new flavor) dipped them into his coffee, activating the two experiments, which proceeded to strip Kahiko and hijack his police car.

The criminal duo next made a vain attempt to break into [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]], but were forced to flee the scene when [[Gantu]], who had been notified of their activation, caught them in the act.

149 and 150 went on to cause countless robberies throughout the [[Kauai|island]] until they were tracked back to their hideout by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], who had gone AWOL after being grounded by [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] earlier. After getting acquainted with each other, 149 devised a plan to encourage Lilo and Stitch's unruly behavior so that they would eventually show the two experiments how to break into Gantu's ship.

At first, Lilo and Stitch's naughty behavior posed as a distraction for 149 and 150 (named Bonnie and Clyde) while they stole from numerous places.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Bonnie & Clyde - Bonnie winks at Clyde.jpg|thumb|Bonnie and Clyde plotting]]
The following night, Bonnie and Clyde managed to convince Lilo and Stitch to help them successfully break into Gantu's ship. However, before the four could steal anything, they were ambushed and captured in [[Prison Capsule|containment orbs]] by Gantu. Lilo and Stitch were able to break out, though, and the four made a narrow escape.

When the outlaw experiments discovered that the police had found and secured their hideout, Bonnie convinced Lilo and Stitch to allow her and Clyde to take cover in the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]].

Bonnie and Clyde attempted to hide in Lilo's laundry, but were discovered by [[Pleakley]] while the latter was taking out the laundry, prompting the two robbers to tie him and [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] up, unclothe them, and strip the house of everything. Jumba and Pleakley were later freed, and then let Lilo and Stitch use [[the Red One]] to chase down Bonnie and Clyde.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Bonnie & Clyde - Bonnie and Clyde in prison.jpg|thumb|left|Bonnie and Clyde in jail]]
While the two thieves fled to their new hideout in Nani's [[X-Buggy|dune buggy]] – along with all of the Pelekais' stolen possessions in tow – they were attacked by Gantu in his [[Manta Shuttle|shuttle]], but saved by Lilo and Stitch, whom Bonnie and Clyde took back to their new hideout: the pre-robbed coffee shack.

However, Lilo and Stitch suddenly revealed their true colors: to re-infiltrate Bonnie and Clyde's hideout in order to capture them. When Stitch pointed a [[Net Cannon|net cannon]] at the two crooks, Bonnie and Clyde attempted to escape out a window that was locked, but were blasted into a net by Stitch, handed over to Officer Kahiko, and sent to prison.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spike - 'Yeah, this is better than taco night at the big house!'.png|thumb|Bonnie and Clyde in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group]]
In "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]", Bonnie was one of the experiments in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group, alongside Clyde. When [[Fibber (032)|Fibber]] used his lie-detecting ability to prove that Bonnie was not as intelligent as she claimed, nor was Clyde at fault for their arrest, the duo got into a fight, which ended when Pleakley convinced Bonnie and Clyde to attempt hugging therapy on each other.

In "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", Bonnie and Clyde were officially paroled, thus allowing them to join Lilo and Stitch on a mission to rescue Gantu's captive experiments. They assisted by opening a passage in Gantu's ship so Stitch and the others could break inside.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Bonnie and Clyde, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Bonnie and Clyde participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Bonnie and Clyde made [[Stitchman Meets Bonnie and Clyde|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where they escaped from Galactic Prison and traveled to the [[Izayoi Island|island]] in order to continue their primary function: theft. Because of this, they could be considered "incompletely rehabilitated". They have also revealed that they've tried to be good, but their programming interferes with it. Thus, it is unknown if they have truly turned good.

==Personality==
Bonnie is a [[wikipedia:Kleptomania|kleptomaniac]]. However, this doesn't stop her from being quite a helpful friend to others, such as Lilo and Stitch (after she was reformed), as seen in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]". Jumba programmed her to be drawn to her partner-in-crime, Clyde. Bonnie can be considered the brains and leader of the duo and is able to [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]]. 

Bonnie has the qualities and characteristics of a true, albeit amateurish criminal mind: manipulative, cunning, street-smart, and a great schemer. She is normally quite laid-back in situations (unless maybe the cops or other enemies are after her). With such a carefree, social, and almost friendly personality, it can be quite easy for the gullible to fall for her rotten tricks, namely Lilo and Stitch. In addition to her deceptive, tomboyish nature, Bonnie appears to have little etiquette and be very rude, as well as a bit short-tempered at times. She has an extremely close bond with Clyde, despite the fact that they have argued a few times before. She is naturally just seeking thrill, fun and adventure, even if it means stealing a few things or joining in on brawls with her other experiment "cousins".

She and Clyde are also seen to be hoarders as well as thieves.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Bonnie is a small, light green koala-like experiment with an hourglass-like figure and a large head. She has a yellow stomach, small antennae, dark blue eyes with eyelashes, two dark green marks on the back of her head, dark green arrow-like patches on her arms and legs, and a yellow V-shaped stripe on her forehead. She also has two fangs sticking out of her mouth.

===Special abilities===
Bonnie is cunning and intelligent with a talent for stealing things. She has some of the basic experiment abilities, such as enhanced durability and damage resistance, as well as having the ability to crawl on walls and ceilings. She is skilled with certain weapons, namely pistols and plasma guns. She can also [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]] with a Brooklyn accent. Her connection to Clyde is programmed into her DNA.

'''Boomer''', also known as '''Experiment 288''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to be a living boomerang. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "[[:Category:Mrs. Hasagawa's experiments|cats]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 288 was the 288th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to act as a living boomerang. 288 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]]. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 288's pod being one of them.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 288's pod for an apricot and washed it, activating the experiment. However, as 288 was not a very evil or destructive experiment, he was able to live a peaceful life with her, due to the latter seeing the former as a mere stray cat who needed a home.

When [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] discovered that Mrs. Hasagawa kept several experiments as pets, they thought they were a danger to her and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], decided to capture them all. Stitch tried to get 288 to willingly go into a [[Prison Capsule|container]], but when he saw [[Mulch (111)|Experiment 111]] rapidly approaching, he grabbed 288, threw him into the air, and used the aforementioned container on 111 instead. When 288 came back (the way real boomerangs do after being thrown), Stitch grabbed another container and caught him in it.

288 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 288 was then named Boomer.

In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Boomer was oddly seen as one of the captive experiments in [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison cell]], although he is barely seen, suggesting [[Gantu]] caught Boomer, but this was an error. Boomer was then sent back to Gantu after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused mischief and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Boomer, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Boomer participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by being thrown at Leroys' heads.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Boomer made [[Meega Going to Disneyland!|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Pix (214)|Pix]], [[Slushy (523)|Slushy]], [[Blowhard (533)|Blowhard]], [[Kixx (601)|Kixx]], and [[Slugger (608)|Slugger]], when [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] visited Tokyo Disneyland.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Boomer is a small white-and-brown experiment with a red nose, a lightweight body and a curved, boomerang-shaped head with two antennae. His face lays in the elbow of the "boomerang" with small three-fingered hands on the tips of the "boomerang".

===Special abilities===
Boomer can use his body as a boomerang.

==Trivia==
*Boomer was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Boomer erroneously appeared with Gantu's other captive experiments, although he is barely seen, but he was already living with Mrs. Hasagawa, and Lilo and Stitch discovered him while Gantu was asleep.

'''Bragg''', also known as '''Experiment 145''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. Originally designed to annoy individuals by telling tall tales, he only appeared in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime where he was [[Transmutation|altered]] by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] to gain power from sympathy. He is an excellent liar, manipulator, and acts generally cute. He is also super-intelligent and talented with both the flute and harmonica, which assists in his gaining sympathy and popularity. He is capable of reaching strength that rivals that of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]'s.

In the English dub, he is given the name '''Flute''' by [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and is correctly referred to as '''Experiment 145''', though the Japanese language episode erroneously refers to Bragg as '''Experiment 021''', which actually belongs to '''Twang''', and mentions that Jumba reused some of Twang's DNA when he created Bragg.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 145 was the 145th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to annoy individuals by telling tall tales. He inherited musical ability from Experiment 021, whose DNA was re-purposed in the creation of Experiment 145. He was later [[Transmutation|altered]] to feed off of sympathy and attention in order to grow stronger. 145 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point, 145 was activated during [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]], although his outcome was never revealed.

Many years later, he was captured by Hämsterviel, brainwashed, and modified to fool the citizens of [[Okinawa New Town|Okinawa]] and capture Stitch.

===''[[Stitch!|Stitch! anime]]''===
This experiment [[Flute (episode)|first appeared]] when [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] found him crying in a picnic basket on the beach. After feeling sorry for him when he explains all the hardship he has been through, Yuna brings him home and eventually names him Flute, because he plays the flute. Flute appears to be sensitive and helpful at first, but when Stitch wakes up in the middle of the night and finds Flute eating all the food, Flute makes it look as if Stitch hurt him after he tried to stop Flute from being bad, thus getting Stitch in trouble.

It turned out that [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] [[Transmutation|altered]] Flute and disguised him, turning him from ugly to "snuggly-wuggly". This made him appear smaller, and his fur color changed from pale green to bright yellow to appeal to more people. He even became unrecognizable by his own creator, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]. He becomes physically stronger and mutates through getting attention, which he is fully capable of as he is a talented player of the harmonica and flute. He is shown to be very smart and athletic, making him very popular on only the first day he came with Yuna to school. Hämsterviel gave Flute the objective to reach his maximum power in order to capture Stitch so that [[Delia]] can get the power cell inside of him. Flute accomplishes this and beats on Stitch, but once he is caught and criticized by the townspeople, Flute loses his popularity, and thus his power, and he fails Hämsterviel miserably. Afterwards, Flute was presumably reverted back to normal, then dehydrated back into an experiment pod and stored in Jumba's vault as shown in "[[Shogun]]".

==Personality==
Bragg acts like a conscientious, sensitive, and generous creature, but in reality is very manipulative and mischievous. He is a great actor, able to keep up an act for weeks. He is sly, able to come up with believable stories to get sympathy from other beings.

Before being modified, Bragg was a mean, nasty, ogre-like brute with a gangster-like voice and a bad attitude, and was not very good at keeping his mouth shut.

After his modification, despite his mischievous and destructive tendency, Bragg is still very friendly, fun-loving, and helpful and has a soft, sweet voice and a good attitude. 

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
In his original form, Bragg is not so cute and rather ogre-like. His fur was a vulgar shade of green, his claws extend, he had an under-bite, a bulbous red nose, a hunched back, and was overall very muscular.

In his current/modified form, Bragg is a yellow long-eared cat/rabbit-like experiment with a white stomach and orange heart-shaped markings on his forehead and all down his back. He has blue tufts of fur sprouting from his ears, violet-colored eyes, and a reddish-orange nose. His tail is short and slightly bushy.

As he grows stronger, he retains in his modified, yellow body, but becomes visibly muscular. At this stage, he possesses two retractable arms, and his voice gets deeper. He can switch between this and his first form at will to absorb more sympathy.

===Special abilities===
Bragg has musical talent and is able to play folksy instruments, such as a flute and harmonica, an ability he inherited from Jumba re-purposing Twang (021)'s DNA when creating Experiment 145. Bragg has superhuman intellect, able to work out complex problems in seconds (similar to Stitch), and is capable of [[:Category:Talking experiments|speaking fluently]].

Aside from this, Bragg is deceptive, able to cause sympathy from any being. He is a highly skilled actor, which is one out of many reasons he is so popular. He uses popularity and sympathy as steroids, growing stronger as he receives more and more attention. This allows him to extend multiple arms, increase in size, and gain much physical muscle mass. He has been shown to have two retractable arms in his powered-up form (although it is unknown if he has retractable arms in his weaker form).

===Weaknesses===
If Bragg is disliked and his popularity decreases, he also decreases in strength and becomes very weak, stuck in his smaller form.

==Trivia==
*Bragg is one of the rare experiments to have sclerae and pupils instead of solid black eyes, the others being [[Mr. Stenchy (254)|Mr. Stenchy]], [[Mrs. Sickly (255)|Mrs. Sickly]], [[Skip (089)|Skip]], [[Clink (086)|Clink]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]], [[Experiments#Other experiments|Tippy]], [[Experiments#3-Series: Psychological|Slobber]], and [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|four unconfirmed experiments]].
*Bragg is one of the few known experiments that can [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]].
*Though this experiment is called 021 in the Japanese episodes, he is actually named Bragg, and the English dub was correcting the error by calling him Experiment 145, but he was [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|erroneously called 021]] by the Japanese team working on the show.
**According to ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', Experiment 021 is known as Twang, and if you translate the kanji (試作品021号ブラッグ) from the Japanese episode, it reads: "Prototype No.021 Bragg".<ref>[https://translate.google.com/#view=home&op=translate&sl=ja&tl=en&text=%E8%A9%A6%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81021%E5%8F%B7%E3%83%96%E3%83%A9%E3%83%83%E3%82%B0 Google Translate]</ref> Confirming that this is indeed Bragg and the English dub was correcting the number error back to Experiment 145, the kanji for "Twang" is [https://translate.google.com/#view=home&op=translate&sl=en&tl=ja&text=twang トゥワング].
**In the English dub of ''[[Stitch!]]'', he is named Flute (regarding the instrument that he plays) by [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]], meaning that this is a new name for him. [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] intentionally changed his appearance so much that Jumba didn't even recognize him.
**This is similar to [[Bonnie (149)|Bonnie]] and [[Clyde (150)|Clyde]] being called 349 and 350 in their [[Bonnie & Clyde|titular episode]], though they are actually 149 and 150; [[Finder (158)|Finder]] being referred to as 458 when he is really 158; and [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]] being referred to as 515 when he is truly 505.
**In an email to [[User:Ronlof|Ronlof]], [[disney:Jess_Winfield|Jess Winfield]] states:
***''"The confusion is understandable. Bear with me for a minute. In the translated script we received from Japan, the experiment in the episode "Stitch's Big Brother" (titled "[[Flute (episode)|Flute]]" in the English version), is identified in all dialogue tags as "Bragg." This would be experiment 145, originally designed to annoy individuals by telling tall tales. In the anime, he has been transmuted to gain power from sympathy as he tells sad stories and acts generally cute. He doesn't remember his past — and thus the name given to him by Lilo. It's Yuna who gives him a new name, "Flute." Later in the episode, Jumba, confusingly, declares him to be 021, Twang, an experiment designed to annoy individuals by playing folk music of Jumba's home planet. Whether the confusion in the Japanese version reflects an error by Jumba (entirely possible, given his jumbled notes — it seems that he did, in fact, re-purpose some of 021's DNA when creating 145, which would explain his facility with the folksy flute) or by the Japanese team, I don't know. For the English dub, we corrected the experiment number to match the script's identification of the character's dialogue tag of "Bragg." Make sense?"''
*Bragg's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green and still mislabeled 021 by the Japanese team.
*Bragg and [[Toons (112)|Toons]] are the only ''Stitch!'' experiments whose functions were changed after their [[transmutation]].

'''Bugby''', also known as '''Experiment 128''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to turn entire civilizations into harmless insects. Those turned into bugs can understand all other insects and arachnids; only Jumba's technology can reverse the process. His one true place is on a [[farm]], protecting farmers' crops by turning rocks into aphid-eating ladybugs.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 128 was the 128th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to turn individuals into harmless insects. 128 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 128's pod landing in the middle of a [[Farm|farm]] crop.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Bugby - Bugby after activation.png|thumb|left|Bugby after being activated]]
When the crop was being irrigated via sprinklers, 128's pod was sprinkled, activating the experiment. 128 then took flight and traversed the island of [[Kauai]] aimlessly.

After a while, 128 was attacked by an eagle but defeated it by turning it into a dragonfly. 128 then fluttered off laughing but accidentally flew into [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]]'s jar. Unaware that 128 was actually an experiment, Lilo named him Bugby and took him [[Lilo's House|home]], where she placed Bugby in her makeshift bug city, [[Bugopolis]].

When [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] grabbed Bugby and attempted to eat him, the latter turned Stitch into an ant in self-defense.

Later, after Lilo got in a fight with [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] for bringing bugs into the house and was sent to her room, she noticed Bugby loose in her bedroom outside of Bugopolis and went to check on the other insects. Bugby then turned Lilo into a ladybug.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Bugby - Bugby firing his laser.png|thumb|Bugby firing his laser]]
Shortly after, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]] went up to Lilo's room to bring her gravel muffins (which Jumba deemed inedible), and the two discovered Bugby, making Pleakley become intrigued. When Jumba then tried to warn Pleakley about Bugby, the latter turned Jumba into a stink bug and Pleakley into a praying mantis.

The four later befriended a [[Chaps, Manny, and Sperk|dung beetle, spider, and caterpillar]], though the bug trio believed Stitch was evil since he ate insects like them. However, Lilo convinced them otherwise, and when the three real bugs were in danger of insect-hating Nani and the exterminator, Stitch rescued them and eventually had a change of heart about eating bugs.

After a few setbacks, including a tussle with an aggressive wild cat, the gang managed to travel to [[Jumba's Ship|Jumba's ship]], where they used a special machine to revert to normal (and enlarge the three real bugs to human size). When the exterminator showed up, thinking the vermin crawled into here, the giant bugs' leader told the exterminator off, scaring him away.

Bugby then attacked, reverting the giant insects to their original size. However, Lilo and Stitch were able to recapture Bugby in Lilo's jar before he could turn her, Stitch, Jumba and Pleakley back into bugs.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Bugby - Bugby captured in Lilo's bug jar.png|thumb|left|Bugby defeated]]
Shortly after, Jumba [[Transmutation|reprogrammed]] Bugby to turn inanimate objects into bugs instead of people and sent the latter onto the same farm where he was first activated, where he found his one true place turning rocks into aphid-eating ladybugs, thus helping farmers protect their crops from unwanted pests.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Bugby, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Bugby participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] probably by turning attacking Leroys into insects.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Bugby is a small light-green, mosquito-like experiment with four purple eyes, four wings and six teal legs.

===Special abilities===
Bugby can fire a purple laser from his stinger that causes individuals hit to turn into bugs and giant insects and arachnids hit to revert to the normal size of bugs. Anyone turned into a bug can communicate with all other insects and arachnids. His ray can also, if [[Transmutation|reprogrammed]], turn inanimate objects into bugs instead of living organisms.

===Weaknesses===
The only way to reverse Bugby's effects is with a machine built by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]. The machine can also enlarge normal-sized insects to the size of average human beings.

==Trivia==
*Bugby, [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]], [[Jam (202)|Jam]], [[Melty (228)|Melty]], [[Wishy-Washy (267)|Wishy-Washy]], [[Snooty (277)|Snooty]], [[Amnesio (303)|Amnesio]], [[Hunkahunka (323)|Hunkahunka]], [[Experiments#5-Series: Elemental and environmental manipulators|Blake]], [[Slugger (608)|Slugger]], [[Witch (610)|Witch]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Miscellaneous|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have wings.
*Bugby, [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]], and [[Clink (086)|Clink]] are the only known experiments that are hexapods. Interestingly, all three are different types of arthropods (insects, arachnids, and crustaceans respectively).
*Bugby is one of the only experiments that Stitch didn't instantly recognize as a fellow cousin.
*Bugby is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to.
**He is also one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to.
*Bugby's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is purple.
*In [[Bugby (episode)|his debut]], Bugby's eyes are purple, but in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', they are black.
*Bugby is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''Leroy & Stitch''.

'''Cannonball''', also known as '''Experiment 520''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to transform bodies of water into giant waves and tsunamis capable of destroying entire planets. Luckily, he has the ability to control the waves he creates. His one true place is making perfect waves for surfing at [[Lahui Beach|the beach]].

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 520 was the 520th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to turn bodies of water into huge, destructive waves and tsunamis. 520 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 520's pod landing in a bird's nest.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Cannonball - Cannonball moments after activation.jpg|thumb|left|Cannonball after activation]]
When a bird discovered 520's pod in its nest, it kicked the pod out, which landed in a nearby lake, activating the experiment. 520 then created a massive tsunami in the lake and began to casually make his way towards the ocean, where he would cause an even deadlier tsunami.

While 520 evaded [[Gantu]]'s clutches, the former passed through the [[Birds of Paradise Hotel]], where he created a tsunami from one of the pools that devastated much of the hotel. In the aftermath, 520 used the diving board to propel himself up until he landed atop a palm tree, where [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] incompetently catapulted him away, much to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]]'s discouragement.

520 later made his way to a reservoir while being pursued by Lilo and Stitch, but before he could cause a tsunami, Stitch fired a suction cup dart attached to a rope at 520 and reeled him in. However, Gantu attacked and captured 520, who was almost stuffed into a [[Net Cannon|net]]. Stitch battled Gantu and slipped a pineapple inside his net, leaving Gantu taking the net with the pineapple back to [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]], while 520 had been recaptured in a [[Prison Capsule|container]].

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Cannonball - Cannonball making waves.jpg|thumb|Cannonball making waves]]
Lilo and Stitch then released 520, and after assuring him that they meant him no harm, the three rushed off to [[Lahui Beach|the beach]] for Lilo's sand-sculpting competition. Stitch and 520 played contentedly until Gantu came by to try and capture 520 one more time, forcing Stitch to build a life-size sand fortress around himself, Lilo and 520.

When Gantu began to tear into the sand castle, 520 jumped from the castle into the ocean, where the latter created a massive tsunami that washed Gantu away to San Francisco, while leaving the [[Kauai|island]] perfectly intact.

520, christened Cannonball, later found his one true place making suitable waves for surfing.

Cannonball reappeared in "[[Elastico (episode)|Elastico]]" as one of the audience members for Lilo's hula dance.

Cannonball made a cameo at the end of "[[Swirly (episode)|Swirly]]", where he slid into a children's wading pool.

In "[[Houdini (episode)|Houdini]]", Cannonball was one of the audience members for Stitch's bungled magic act.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Dupe - Stitch's cousins attending Lilo's slumber party 3.png|thumb|left|Cannonball attending Lilo and Stitch's slumber party]] 
In "[[Finder (episode)|Finder]]", Cannonball was seen playing poker with Stitch, [[Yin (501)|Yin]], [[Yang (502)|Yang]] and [[Richter (513)|Richter]].

In "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]", Cannonball was one of the experiments that came to Lilo and Stitch's slumber party wearing traditional pajamas. However, he was forced by [[Pleakley]] to leave due to his destructive behavior.

In "[[Angel (episode)|Angel]]", Cannonball was one of the experiments that [[Angel (624)|Angel]] reverted to evil using her song. Later, Cannonball and the other depraved experiments attacked Stitch aboard a ship, but Angel turned them to good again before they could finish Stitch off. Working together, the experiments were then able to successfully escape the ship with Stitch.

Cannonball made another cameo in "[[Felix (episode)|Felix]]", where he was destroying the beach with his tidal waves. He was eventually stopped by Stitch, and while Lilo convinced Cannonball to tone down his waves, Stitch cleaned up the beach.

Cannonball was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that joined Stitch in a rebellion against Gantu.

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Cannonball was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
In the film's opening, Cannonball can be seen waving hello to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], along with [[Yin (501)|Yin]] and [[Yang (502)|Yang]]. He was also seen later in the movie making perfect waves for surfing as Lilo was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to make sure all the experiments were happy in the one true place they belonged.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Cannonball, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Cannonball participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by flattening attacking Leroys with his butt.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Personality==
Cannonball, despite his mischievous and chaotic nature, is shown to be shy and harmless, and simply loves producing waves and often tsunamis. He also has a tendency not to look before he leaps, though he is capable of controlling the waves he creates. He is rather timid around people, but gets along quite well with others once he gets to know them. Cannonball can also be very loyal and helpful to his friends, joining Stitch's rebellion to fight off Gantu.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Cannonball is a purplish-pink experiment just slightly bigger than [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] (although he was noticeably smaller than his younger cousin in his [[Cannonball (episode)|eponymous debut]]). He has a big posterior, two spines on his back, black eyes, a round nose, a wide mouth with sharp teeth, short ears, and a short stubby tail.

===Special abilities===
Naturally drawn to water, Cannonball can create a massive wave or tsunami from any body of water he jumps into. It is also shown that he can control the waves he creates. Additionally, bouncing around on his butt seems to be a more effective form of locomotion than walking.

He can roll into a ball as shown in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', but he is only seen briefly in ball form while in midair. Also, Stitch's ball form in "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]" and "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]" resembles Cannonball's ball form.

He can fight enemies by flattening them with his butt.

===Weaknesses===
Cannonball is not particularly fast, and is also shy and harmless.

==Trivia==
*Cannonball was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Cannonball, [[Hertz Donut (022)|Hertz Donut]], [[Sproing (249)|Sproing]], [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Mary (455)|Mary]] are the only known experiments that mostly bounce when traversing land.
*Cannonball and [[Yin (501)|Yin]] are the only known experiments whose functions are related to water. 
*Cannonball's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue.
*Cannonball never rolled into a ball in ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''. However, in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', Cannonball was briefly shown to be able to roll into a ball in midair before he was captured by a [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clone]].
*Cannonball's body appears in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.
*Cannonball appears in ''[[disney:Disney Emoji Blitz|Disney Emoji Blitz]]'' only in a cameo during [[Angel (624)|Angel]]'s Power, but he is unplayable.

'''Carmen''', also known as '''Experiment 123''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. She is designed to make victims dance until they drop with her infectious Latin beats.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 123 was the 123rd genetic experiment created by Jumba with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. She was designed to make victims dance until they drop. 123 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At some point, 123 was activated, captured, tamed, and named Carmen.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Carmen, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], Stitch, Jumba, [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Carmen participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], as in one scene, Carmen was seen strangling a Leroy.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Carmen made [[Stitch's Birthday, Part Two|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime when [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Pleakley]], and [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] travel to the past to the day Stitch was created. She was used to allow them to make their escape by making [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] and his forces dance uncontrollably. It is shown that she does this by firing pink balls of energy out of her maracas.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Carmen is a pink, blue-eyed, four-armed, [[Angel (624)|Angel]]-like experiment with a red nose and dark purple-tipped ears, with a crest resembling a headdress of fruits and holding a maraca in each of her four hands.

Carmen has dark pink fur with splashes of light pink fur on her limbs. Her belly is also light pink. She is somewhat curvier than Angel, but her legs are the shortest of any other experiment with a similar build. She keeps all four of her long arms exposed at all times. Her eyes and tongue are a robin's-egg blue color, and two short antennae extend just beneath her ears. Her most outstanding feature is her fruit headdress, consisting of bananas, grapes, oranges, cherries, and pineapples, that she wears much like her namesake. She also carries four festive maracas at all times that help her carry out her primary function.

===Special abilities===
Carmen can make individuals dance until they drop by firing pink balls of energy from her maracas that pop when they take effect. She can also cancel the effect by clapping the maracas together.

She is also the only experiment that appears to be specifically fluent in Spanish.

==Trivia==
*Carmen was first revealed in a pre-release promo image for ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'' that was identical to the group photo at the end of the film.
*Her name is a reference to [[wikipedia:Carmen Miranda|Carmen Miranda]], a world-famous Brazilian singer and dancer of the early 20th century well known for wearing a headdress of tropical fruits and her use of maracas.
*Carmen is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having light blue eyes instead.
*She and [[Frenchfry (062)|Frenchfry]] are the only two known experiments who natively speak an Earth-based language other than English, with her being the only known Hispanophone (Spanish-speaking) experiment.
*In a brief scene of ''Leroy & Stitch'' during the "[[Aloha ʻOe]]" concert, a towering, rather monstrous version of Carmen can be seen in the background. This version of her has a slightly elongated face; two long arms with larger hands and extended claws; a long, narrow torso; and what seems to be back spines that are extended similarly to Stitch's spines. Perhaps Carmen also has a "metamorphosis" programming like Stitch (provided whether or not his "metamorphosis program" in ''[[Stitch & Ai]]'' is canonical), although in all likelihood, it was either an odd production error or just added in for fun and to see if fans would notice.
*Carmen's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is red in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.
**Jumba also refers to Carmen as "a doozie" in the anime, possibly in the sense of this experiment's unique ability of making others dance.

'''Checkers''', also known as '''Experiment 029''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to give his wearer the power of command over all living creatures, with the exception of experiments created after him, as well as the blind and nearsighted; his hypnotic effects vanish instantly as soon as he leaves his wearer's head.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 029 was the 29th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to make his wearer a king or queen by hypnotizing those around them to worship them as royalty. 029 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo &  Stitch The Series - Checkers - Checkers crawls onto Lilo's head.jpg|thumb|left|Checkers on top of Lilo]]
Experiment 029 was activated off-screen and then chased throughout [[Kokaua Town]] by [[Gantu]], who had been informed about the experiment, but not before making a vain attempt to kill [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]]'s pet cockroach named [[Jimmy the Cockroach|Jimmy]]. 029 was eventually rescued by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and taken [[Lilo's House|home]].

After Lilo discovered 029's powers, the former named him Checkers and donned him, thus becoming a queen. She then started making silly decrees and bossed [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] and other individuals around, even [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]. She also made [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] and [[Elena|the]] [[Teresa|hula]] [[Yuki|girls]] her bodyguards.

Before long, Mertle and the hula girls arrested many "troublemakers" for defying their queen (including [[Pleakley]]), so Lilo decided to step down by removing Checkers. However, before she could figure out his one true place, Gantu arrived and grabbed Checkers. After putting the latter on his head, thus becoming a king, Gantu made his victims his servants.

Fortunately, Stitch and Reuben were immune to Checkers' hypnotic effect, and both cousins rallied an army of other experiments that attacked Gantu and were able to remove Checkers from his head, overthrowing him. As a result, Gantu's ex-servants revolted against him. After the rebellion, Lilo thought about Checkers' one true place, though it was never revealed.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Checkers - Checkers on top of Gantu.jpg|thumb|Checkers on top of Gantu]]
Later, Checkers and the other experiments, along with Jumba and Pleakley, watched Nani as she participated in the Coconut Queen Festival parade (since the original Coconut Queen called in sick) by riding atop a parade float that Lilo, the hula girls, and Stitch's cousins had modified sometime earlier.

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Checkers was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 553 instead of 029.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Checkers, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]], and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Checkers participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did. However, it is presumed that he wouldn't have been able to be very effective, due to the fact that his powers are deemed useless.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Checkers has appeared on multiple occasions in the ''Stitch!'' anime. It is also revealed that he will jump off of his host if he eats intolerably spicy foods. He premiered in "[[Princess Penny]]", where [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] used Checkers to temporarily rule over [[Gantu]] and [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] before taking him on a shopping trip and then asking [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] to watch him while Reuben bought some supplies. Also, when Checkers was being worn on the head of [[Penny (Stitch!)|Penny]], he ate some of her spicy sandwich and a hot pepper, causing him to leap off his host.

Checkers reappeared in "[[King Meega!]]", intended to be used by Hämsterviel to command the inhabitants to capture Stitch, but had escaped on his own to Yuna's school, where everyone intended to use his powers for themselves. Stitch once captured Checkers and wore him on his head, but his hypnotic powers did not work on anyone else. [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] recalls that Checkers' powers do not work on Stitch, as he himself is immune to Checkers' effects. (This actually contradicts what happened in "Princess Penny", as Reuben had used Checkers himself without any problems.)

Checkers also appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Checkers hasn't shown much emotion or individuality, other than once while running from Gantu. He mostly attaches himself to an individual and stays there, almost as if he were an inanimate object.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Checkers is a yellow-and-purple crown-shaped, centipede-like experiment with black eyes, a dark pink nose, and four pairs of legs that sits curled up like a crown on individuals' heads.

===Special abilities===
Checkers can roll into a crown/hat-like shape while on his host's head, and his wearer gains control over all beings who look upon him or her. Checkers' eyes flash purple when causing the hypnosis, and he can scale/crawl walls. The victims of Checkers' effects visualize his bearer as a ruler of authority, and to individuals, they see one as a king or queen with their attire to match, whether or not they are actually wearing the clothing. His effects are undone as soon as he leaves his wearer's head.

===Weaknesses===
Other experiments created after Checkers are completely unaffected by his hypnotic effect, and his effects wear off as soon as he leaves his wearer's head. Also, his hypnotic effects only work on those who see him, so the blind and nearsighted will not be affected. Additionally, he will fall/leap off his host after devouring intolerably spicy foods as seen in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Trivia==
*Checkers was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Checkers is one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to.
*The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Checkers as: "Experiment 029. Primary function: King maker. Gives his wearer power of command over all living creatures."
*Checkers is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.
*In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, Checkers has a tendency to say "Check!" repeatedly when he moves.
*Although Dave Wittenberg voices Checkers in the English dub of both of the experiment's anime episodes, he is only credited in "[[Princess Penny]]" and isn't credited in "[[King Meega!]]" for unknown reasons.
**Also, [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] was able to use Checkers' hypnotic powers in "Princess Penny" without any problems, which contradicts "King Meega!" in terms of Checkers' powers having no effect on experiments that were created after him.

'''Chopsuey''', also known as '''Experiment 621''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]], and the main antagonist of the video game ''[[Disney's Stitch: Experiment 626]]''. He has all of [[Stitch]]'s powers but is less capable. He is jealous of all the attention that Stitch gets.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 621 was the 621st genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was presumably designed either as a prototype of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and [[Reuben]], or for Stitch/Reuben's purpose. His original purpose was to collect strands of DNA around the galaxy to help Jumba create more experiments.

===''[[Disney's Stitch: Experiment 626]]''===
621 had been sent around the galaxy to collect DNA strands to help [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] create more experiments; however, Jumba had been disappointed with his results.

Jumba later gave this mission to [[Stitch (626)|626]] and was more satisfied with 626's achievements. Jealous of Experiment 626 because of all the attention Jumba was giving him, 621 secretly collected his own DNA and used it to mutate himself into a bigger, stronger form. 621 then battled 626, but was defeated when 626 tricked him into electrocuting himself. The unconscious Experiment 621 was apprehended by [[Gantu]] along with Jumba and 626 shortly after.

==Personality==
Experiment 621 is shown to be sadistic, prone to jealous hatred and possesses a superiority complex, shown when he became obsessed with proving he was "superior" to 626 which included trying to kill him. However, this villainous attitude can be somewhat justified, since Jumba harshly criticized and completely neglected 621 when 626 proved to be a more effective experiment.

621 may be mentally unstable due to his unusual tendency to burst into random laughter and because of his merciless rage. Despite this, he appears to be more intelligent than most experiments, including his ability to speak fluent English.

621 does not appear to be a very capable fighter, only fighting his battles with sheer strength rather than skill. He can also be quite reckless and clumsy in such circumstances.

He believes in the saying: "Old age and treachery will always overcome youth and skill."<ref>[https://archive.org/details/stitch-manual/page/n15/mode/2up Disney's Stitch: Experiment 626 Manual (PAL)]</ref>

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
In his regular form (not counting his extra limbs), 621 resembles a slim, dark green koala standing on two, very slim legs. The fur on his belly, bottom jaws, and around his eyes, however, are a dull yellow color. On his rather large-in-proportion head are a pair of bugging black eyes, a large black-green round nose, and a wide underbite with two jutting fangs. His ears are quite long and slim, almost like a bat's own ears, and has creamy yellow insides. He is quite short, standing at three feet, including his dark yellow spiky Mohawk.

He wears a dark brown sleeveless space suit with a circle consisting of a darker brown border and yellow center on his chest and patches consisting of a brown border and yellow center on each of his legs, black belt with a yellow square buckle and collar, which sprouts into very thin arms ending with long black claws and creamy yellow inner hand/paw pads. His slim, short legs all end with round feet dotted with black toes.

When in his mutated form, there is a major difference in his appearance. 621 is now standing at around six feet. His eyes are much bigger and bug out a lot more, while his ears are notably shorter than they were before mutation. His chest is quite thick and large now. Sprouting from his chest are some very slim arms that grow into large, muscular forearms ending with longer black claws. His lower torso is quite small compared to his huge chest, but these sprout into skinny legs with huge monstrous feet. On his back, his three spines have doubled to six, spreading outward towards the sides. They've become much sharper, growing to about one foot long each.

===Special abilities===
621 has similar powers to Stitch, but is not as effective at using them. He is both very physical and well-equipped. He is able to use a jet pack and a grapple gun.

*'''Basic experiment attributes:''' 621 has all of the most basic abilities that many other experiments possess. His green hands and feet can produce a sticky substance that allows him to scale walls and ceilings without falling, much like a bug. He has the ability to see very well in the dark (as seen whenever his eyes turn green), lift individuals/objects that are many times his own weight (he isn't the strongest experiment, but is strong; one can compare his strength to that of an average human weight lifter), and his skeletal structure is so flexible that he can roll around as a ball, curled up while biting onto his legs.
*'''Retractable limbs:''' 621 can retract and extract extra limbs at any time he wishes. He has an extra pair of arms that have already torn holes on the sides of his brown space suit, sharp black claws at the tip of his fingers, three porcupine-like spines tipped with whitish-blue and black that sprout from his back, and two bug-like antennae with no real use.
*'''DNA mutation:''' An ability received after he was genetically altered by Dr. Jumba's mutator machine. His innards, thanks to the special cases of DNA he placed in the machine before mutation, have formed in a way that could boost his strength and adrenaline to alarming rates. Such change occurs upon consumption of fresh genetic material from strong, fast, very well-adaptive creatures (the very well abundant non-magical humans, unfortunately, are out of this category, as they are physically too weak for such use). 
::Such material comes in the form of hair, blood, or even nails. The mutation changed 621's body enough for him to handle such consumption (although, most experiments could already handle such a diet). When enough DNA is absorbed, he takes on this stronger, faster form for five posts. Afterwards, he reverts back to normal and will have to search for more material to consume for another mutation.
*'''Speech:''' Unlike most other experiments, who usually speak [[Tantalog language|Tantalog]] or in no language at all, 621 can also [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluent English]] with a vaguely Russian accent, not unlike his creator Jumba Jookiba, albeit sounding similar to Stitch's nasal voice.

His weapons are two plasma cannons that he normally keeps hidden with his retracted extra arms. He has a secondary gun, used more for self-defense. This gun fires a beam of green energy at targets, and can teleport them short distances no more than fifteen feet. Where the target reappears is random.

621 was able to mutate himself into a much larger and stronger creature by collecting DNA strands. In this form he is physically more powerful than Stitch, but less skilled.

===Weaknesses===
621 is not a skilled fighter and relies more on strength. Also, it is unknown whether or not he shares Stitch's weakness of water, though it is possible, considering he is a prototype of Stitch.

==Trivia==
*''[[Disney's Stitch: Experiment 626]]'', the only media where 621 makes an appearance, had its events retconned from canon in media following the game's release, though 621 could still have the same physical appearance, abilities, and personality.
**Jumba and Stitch were apprehended in ''[[Lilo & Stitch 2: Stitch Has a Glitch]]'' moments after Stitch's creation, contradicting the events chronicled in ''Stitch: Experiment 626''. However, Jumba stated in "[[Kixx (episode)|Kixx]]" that he trained Stitch between his creation and arrest, which also contradicts ''Lilo & Stitch 2''. This would suggest that ''Lilo & Stitch 2'' is actually non-canon or this episode is partially non-canonical.
**Even though 621 never made a physical appearance outside of ''Stitch: Experiment 626'', his name is listed in the [[Experiments/Gallery#Leroy & Stitch|end credits]] of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', suggesting in the game that 621's canon name is Chopsuey.
**If this version of Chopsuey is canon, then he is the only experiment to debut in a video game. Since the game was released on June 19, 2002, two days before ''[[Lilo & Stitch]]'' was released, he is also the one of the earliest experiments to debut.
**Additionally, since all 625 experiments before Stitch were confirmed to have been reformed and found their one true place as stated in the beginning of ''Leroy & Stitch'', the same most likely would have occurred for Chopsuey sometime during [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the TV series]].
*He is one of the few experiments that are actually villains, along with [[Zero (000)|Zero]], [[627]], [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and [[Leroy Clones|his clones]], and [[Dark End]], while all the other experiments were following their primary function.

The '''Cliff Dragons''' are illegal genetic experiments created by [[Jumba Jookiba]]. Two of the three dragons were [[Jumba's Chinese Experiments|the second and the third experiments he created]] in China based on what he learns in ancient Chinese scrolls; the third dragon is the offspring of the two.

==Background==
==="[[Spirals]]"===
After receiving the ancient scrolls, Jumba was inspired to create a genetic experiment based on the Chinese mythical creatures that were in the scroll. He decided to create an experiment based on a Chinese dragon. That is how the male dragon was created. When he saw Stitch, he got angry and ran away. He was later found in a nest on a cliff. Jumba realized that he was waiting for the full moon. Later, [[Wang Ai Ling|Ai]] and Jumba discovered that he was expecting a female on a full moon. At that moment, his Qi energy was at its limit, but if he did not find the female, she would fall and rise again only after a hundred years. Also, he would turn into a dragon demon. Jumba urgently created a female for him and brought her to the male. The two dragon united, but in the morning they were attacked by the [[Woolagong]]s, who were later defeated with the help of the dragons. It also turned out that the dragons had an egg from which a baby hatched at the end of the episode. Later, they were sent to a parallel dimension inhabited by various mythological creatures.

==="[[Monstrosity]]"===
In this episode, the Cliff Dragons and some other Chinese experiments were summoned from a parallel dimension to battle the [[Jaboodie]]s.

==Personality==
By nature, they behave like typical dragons, initially distrusting others. There are also animal instincts such as reproduction, self-defense, protection of baby offspring, and so on. Initially, the male dragon behaved aggressively and saw Stitch as a rival. The female saw Stitch and Ai as prey and wanted to eat them. But later, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and Ai were able to gain both of their trust. After that, Stitch and Ai helped fight the aliens.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
The male and female dragons look like Chinese dragons in tan and teal, respectively. Outwardly, they resemble snakes with whiskers, four legs and a tail. Their baby is red.

===Special abilities===
The Cliff Dragons have a unique Qi power that allows them to fly without wings. This power was later tested on [[Dim Long]] and used in the creation of the [[Xiezhi]]. They have good flexibility and can wriggle. They are also able to breathe fire.

===Weaknesses===
If they have a baby egg, they will have to defend the nest in parallel, which will weaken them. Also, if a male does not find a female on a full moon, he will lose his Qi power.

==Trivia==
*The Cliff Dragons are based on Chinese mythological dragons.
*The male dragons only look for females during a full moon. They are also most aggressive towards other males at this time, as they see them as rivals. If the male doesn't find a female during the full moon, he then loses his Qi power for a hundred years, after which he starts searching for a female again. Also, if he does not find a female, he turns into a dragon demon.
*The tan and teal dragons are the first experiments in [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|the franchise]] to reproduce.
**The baby is the first experiment to be created via reproduction, and thus the first naturally born experiment (unless the "[[Sprout (509)#Stitch! anime|Sproutling]]" in the international edit of ''[[Stitch!]]'' counts).
*Unlike the female dragon, the male has a mustache.

'''Clink''', also known as '''Experiment 086''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to capture and confine enemies inside of him.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 086 was the 86th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to capture and confine enemies in a holding tank in his stomach. 086 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
In "[[Skip (episode)|Skip]]", 086 was used to capture rogue experiments in an alternate future where [[Hämsterviel]] ruled Earth. He captured [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and [[Skip (089)|Skip]] and brought them to [[Gantu]]. He was later tied up by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], freeing Stitch and Skip.

At an unknown point in the original/current timeline, 086 was presumably activated, captured, and named Clink.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
Despite not physically appearing, the first 624 experiments, presumably including Clink, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

It is unknown whether or not Clink participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Clink is a big, green mouthless crab-like experiment with two stalked, lime-green eyes, six legs, two large claws, and a clear container window on his chest.

===Special abilities===
Clink can trap his targets in the holding tank in his stomach by splitting in half and joining together again around the target in his holding cell tank in his stomach. When split, each half of Clink apparently has a separate mind.

===Weaknesses===
When tied up, Clink can easily lose control of his targets while guarding them outside of his tank.

==Trivia==
*"Clink" is slang for "prison", which makes this experiment's name very befitting.
*Clink was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Clink is one of the rare experiments to have sclerae and pupils instead of solid black eyes, the others being [[Skip (089)|Skip]], [[Bragg (145)|Bragg]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], [[Mr. Stenchy (254)|Mr. Stenchy]], [[Mrs. Sickly (255)|Mrs. Sickly]], [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]], [[Experiments#Other experiments|Tippy]], [[Experiments#3-Series: Psychological|Slobber]], and [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|four unconfirmed experiments]].
*Clink, [[Huggo (489)|Huggo]], and Thresher are the only known experiments with stalked eyes, a trait common in the invertebrates that all three are inspired by.
*Clink, [[Bugby (128)|Bugby]], and [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]] are the only known experiments that are hexapods. Interestingly, all three are different types of arthropods (crustaceans, insects, and arachnids respectively).
*Clink, [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]], [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]], [[Gotchu (031)|Gotchu]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have claws/pincers. Interestingly, all four official experiments have characteristics similar to crustaceans.
*Clink is the only experiment to [[Skip (episode)|debut]] and appear in an alternate timeline dimension created by another experiment. Interestingly, Clink and Skip's numbers are very close to each other: 086 and 089.

'''Clip''', also known as '''Experiment 177''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. According to her original creation, she is designed to consume [[Uburnium]], the most powerful and economical fuel source in the universe, and drive prices through the roof. Unfortunately, the word "Uburnium" was the same word used for "hair" in Jumba's native language. Thus, Clip instead eats hair and, if left unchecked, grows larger with all that she consumes. Her one true place is at the [[Beauty Parlor|beauty salon]] as a professional hairdresser.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 177 was the 177th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding, and immediately ate most of Jumba's hair upon her creation. She was originally designed to consume [[Uburnium]], an efficient fuel source, in order to cause an energy crisis. However, as Uburnium was a very similar word for "hair" in Jumba's native language, the result of the genetic experiment was a hair-eater. 177 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 177 was activated.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Clip - Flashback of Clip's creation.jpg|thumb|left|Clip's creation]]
177 went on a hair-eating rampage around [[Kokaua Town|town]], devouring hair from people's scalps. [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] later discovered 177 and were able to capture her in a hatbox outside the [[Birds of Paradise Hotel|hotel]] before [[Gantu]] could. Lilo then took 177, named Clip, back to their [[Lilo's House|house]] and showed her to [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]. However, upon seeing Clip, he was displeased and demanded Lilo to keep that thing away.

Jumba explained that he had originally designed Clip to consume [[Uburnium]], a rare economic space fuel, yet Uburnium was also the same word for "hair" in Jumba's native language. Thus, he had accidentally created an experiment that ate most of Jumba's former hairstyle (leaving him bald with only three hairs), which since caused him to become grouchy. He then decided to disassemble Clip as revenge, but Lilo suggested that Clip should be rehabilitated.

The next day, Lilo and Stitch attempted to deliver Clip to the [[Beauty Parlor|beauty salon]] to benefit its hair problem, but ran into [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] and [[Elena|the]] [[Teresa|hula]] [[Yuki|girls]] before they could do so. Mertle insulted Lilo's hairdo and gave her a bottle of conditioner "for taming wild, unruly hair". This angered Lilo enough that she resolved to punish Mertle by using Clip on her.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Clip - Clip waves to Gantu while riding the Birds of Paradise bus.jpg|thumb|So long]]
Later, Lilo and Stitch stealthily sneaked into [[Mertle's House|Mertle's house]] and planted Clip under her pillow. That night, however, Mertle was away at a sleepover, so Clip feasted on the doll's hair instead, which tasted awful. Gantu then opened a window and tried to grab Clip, but the latter escaped and ate [[Mrs. Edmonds]]' hair just as she entered Mertle's room to investigate the ruckus. After evading Gantu, Clip hitched a ride on a bus, where she devoured all of the passengers' hair.

The next morning, Lilo ran to [[Kaiāulu Hale|hula class]] to witness a bald Mertle, but found nothing different about her hair, much to Lilo's disappointment. Mertle revealed that she had a sleepover with [[Teresa]], then added that her mother had gone completely bald because she got freaked out (attacked) by a yellow furball (Clip). Upon realizing her mistake, Lilo informed Jumba who eventually agreed to help her find Clip.

Lilo, Stitch and Jumba burst into the Edmonds' home to recapture Clip and unintentionally ambushed Mrs. Edmonds, yet calmly sorted things out with her. Mrs. Edmonds didn't seem to mind about her baldness when Lilo tried to apologize, and the former even admitted that she felt like the real her. She also complimented Jumba's haircut, and his Afro unexpectedly grew back, much to his delight.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Clip - Giant Clip.png|thumb|left|Giant Clip]]
Later, a hairless squirrel and a terrified Gantu evaded a humongous Clip (who had grown into a massive hairball from consuming so much hair). Stitch managed to save Lilo and Jumba from Clip but got his rear end shaven in the process. Gantu tried to outrun Clip, but tumbled down a hill and onto a small stage where a hula demo was held. The folks were inspired by Gantu and urged him to dance, so Gantu reluctantly complied but didn't seem to mind after a while.

While the three searched for Clip, Jumba got split ends from maintaining his new hair. Lilo offered him the conditioner she got from Mertle and figured out how to tame Clip, deducing the latter struck the beauty salon next. Clip wreaked havoc at the salon, but she was tamed and returned to her normal size when Stitch doused her with the special conditioner and other hair care products.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Clip - Clip working as a hairdresser.png|thumb|Hairdresser Clip]]
Shortly after, Clip found her one true place in the salon as a hairdresser, where she gave people the perfect haircut that captured "the real them". Jumba then decided to get his Afro cut and told Clip to do her stuff. After she trimmed Jumba's Afro, the latter was given back his normal three hairs, which was how he liked it.

Clip reappeared in "[[Elastico (episode)|Elastico]]" as one of the audience members for Lilo's hula dance.

Clip was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that joined Stitch in a rebellion against Gantu.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
Clip was seen early in the movie giving [[Victoria]] a new hairstyle as [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to make sure all the experiments were happy in the one true place they belonged.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Clip, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Clip participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by eating Leroys' fur, and thus embarrassing them.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Clip made an appearance in [[Experiment-A-Palooza|a later episode]] of the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]], [[Squeak (110)|Squeak]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], and [[Retro (210)|Retro]]. It is revealed that Clip has the ability of flight. Eventually, Clip was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed her pod to help [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Clip wasn't one of the experiments that was activated.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Clip is a small yellow, hairball-like experiment with a pink bow, large dark blue eyes, a thin mouth and long, sharp scissor-like claws.

===Special abilities===
Clip can use her sharp claws to safely cut off all of a victim's hair in seconds, which she will then eat. She is able to roll into a ball, like [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], and glide. She converts the hair she eats into her own, which causes her to grow slightly with each feast. She also has the talent to envision the most fitting haircut for any organism, as well as cut and style it.

In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, Clip is shown to have the ability to fly in a fashion similar to levitating, and she displayed to have the strength to hold up an [[Yuna Kamihara|11-year-old girl]].

===Weaknesses===
As much as Clip likes to eat hair, she seems to dislike certain kinds of hair; it is unknown if she just hates synthetic hair or cellulose-based fibers, such as cotton, but she expressed disgust at eating a doll's hair when she was planted in [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]]'s bedroom as part of a failed prank.

Chemicals in certain shampoos and hair conditioning products, especially in hair lotions used "for taming wild, unruly hair", can restore Clip to her normal size, as well as "tame" her.

==Trivia==
*Clip was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Clip was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Clip is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having dark blue eyes instead.
*Stitch initially suggested that Lilo name 177 "Hairy", which is coincidentally the name of [[Experiments#3-Series: Psychological|Experiment 333]].
*Clip is one of the very few known experiments we have physically seen created by Jumba. Others include Stitch, [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]], and several of [[Jumba's Chinese Experiments]].
*Clip expressed disgust after eating the hair of one of Mertle's dolls, implying that she dislikes synthetic hair or cellulose-based fibers.
*It is unknown why Clip pursued Gantu while she was a giant hairball, considering the fact that Gantu had no hair on him whatsoever.
*Clip's weakness to wild/unruly hair-taming conditioner is similar to [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]]'s weakness to natural air freshener.
*Clip's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is white in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.
*Clip's ability to fly in the anime may have been a misinterpretation of Clip dashing for hair in [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]].
*Though unconfirmed, Clip can possibly be considered a prototype of [[Mashy (225)|Mashy]].
