'''Clyde''', also known as '''Experiment 150''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to be an expert in theft and evasion. He also has advanced lingual skills, enabling him to easily communicate with his partner-in-crime, [[Bonnie (149)|Bonnie]], whom he is programmed to be drawn to. His one true place was originally in Kokaua Town Prison, but he was paroled in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]". After that, it is unknown where his one true place currently is.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 150 was the 150th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to work with Experiment 149 to steal many belongings and evade arrest. 150 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Bonnie & Clyde - Bonnie and Clyde after activation.jpg|thumb|left|Bonnie and Clyde after activation]]
149 and 150's pods eventually made their way into a supply of doughnut holes at [[Kiki's Coffee Hut]]. While off duty, [[Officer Kahiko]] bought a bag containing two dozen doughnut holes at the coffee shack. He then took out 149 and 150's pods and (mistaking them for a new flavor) dipped them into his coffee, activating the two experiments, which proceeded to strip Kahiko and hijack his police car. 150 was then seen wearing Kahiko's shirt for most of the [[Bonnie & Clyde|episode]].

The criminal duo next made a vain attempt to break into [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]], but were forced to flee the scene when [[Gantu]], who had been notified of their activation, caught them in the act.

149 and 150 went on to cause countless robberies throughout the [[Kauai|island]] until they were tracked back to their hideout by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], who had gone AWOL after being grounded by [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] earlier. After getting acquainted with each other, 149 told 150 her plan to encourage Lilo and Stitch's unruly behavior so that they would eventually show the two experiments how to break into Gantu's ship.

At first, Lilo and Stitch's naughty behavior posed as a distraction for 149 and 150 (named Bonnie and Clyde) while they stole from numerous places.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Bonnie & Clyde - Bonnie winks at Clyde.jpg|thumb|Bonnie and Clyde plotting]]
The following night, Bonnie and Clyde managed to convince Lilo and Stitch to help them successfully break into Gantu's ship. However, before the four could steal anything, they were ambushed and captured in [[Prison Capsule|containment orbs]] by Gantu. Lilo and Stitch were able to break out, though, and the four made a narrow escape.

When the outlaw experiments discovered that the police had found and secured their hideout, Bonnie convinced Lilo and Stitch to allow her and Clyde to take cover in the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]].

Bonnie and Clyde attempted to hide in Lilo's laundry, but were discovered by [[Pleakley]] while the latter was taking out the laundry, prompting the two robbers to tie him and [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] up, unclothe them, and strip the house of everything. Jumba and Pleakley were later freed, and then let Lilo and Stitch use [[the Red One]] to chase down Bonnie and Clyde.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Bonnie & Clyde - Bonnie and Clyde in prison.jpg|thumb|left|Bonnie and Clyde in jail]]
While the two thieves fled to their new hideout in Nani's [[X-Buggy|dune buggy]] – along with all of the Pelekais' stolen possessions in tow – they were attacked by Gantu in his [[Manta Shuttle|shuttle]], but saved by Lilo and Stitch, whom Bonnie and Clyde took back to their new hideout: the pre-robbed coffee shack.

However, Lilo and Stitch suddenly revealed their true colors: to re-infiltrate Bonnie and Clyde's hideout in order to capture them. When Stitch pointed a [[Net Cannon|net cannon]] at the two crooks, Bonnie and Clyde attempted to escape out a window that was locked, but were blasted into a net by Stitch, handed over to Officer Kahiko, and sent to prison.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spike - 'Yeah, this is better than taco night at the big house!'.png|thumb|Bonnie and Clyde in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group]]
In "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]", Clyde was one of the experiments in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group, alongside Bonnie. When [[Fibber (032)|Fibber]] used his lie-detecting ability to prove that Bonnie was not as intelligent as she claimed, nor was Clyde at fault for their arrest, the duo got into a fight, which ended when Pleakley convinced Bonnie and Clyde to attempt hugging therapy on each other.

In "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", Bonnie and Clyde were officially paroled, thus allowing them to join Lilo and Stitch on a mission to rescue Gantu's captive experiments. They assisted by opening a passage in Gantu's ship so Stitch and the others could break inside.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Bonnie and Clyde, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Bonnie and Clyde participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], with Clyde taking on at least six Leroys at one time.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Bonnie and Clyde made [[Stitchman Meets Bonnie and Clyde|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where they escaped from Galactic Prison and traveled to the [[Izayoi Island|island]] in order to continue their primary function: theft. Because of this, they could be considered "incompletely rehabilitated". They have also revealed that they've tried to be good, but their programming interferes with it. Thus, it is unknown if they have truly turned good.

==Personality==
Clyde is a [[wikipedia:Kleptomania|kleptomaniac]]. However, this doesn't stop him from being quite a helpful friend to others, such as Lilo and Stitch (after he was reformed), as seen in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]". Jumba programmed him to be drawn to his partner-in-crime, Bonnie. Clyde can be considered the brawn of the duo, as he behaves in the manner of a clueless, dim-witted sidekick, although he is not outright stupid, just less intelligent than his partner.

He doesn't say much, despite being able to [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]], and what he does is usually dictated by Bonnie. He also has a tendency to doubt or question her well thought-out plans or schemes, and is often inclined to argue over her tactics. He sometimes acts indecisively and is usually reluctant to follow most of Bonnie's orders, despite being equally thievish.

He and Bonnie are also seen to be hoarders as well as thieves.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Clyde is a large, yellowish-brown bear-like experiment with a roundly built body and a round face with a wide mouth; in contrast to this, his face has a small black nose, little-pointed ears, little stubby antennae, black eyes, and a lantern chin. In place of a proper left hand, he has a sort of Swiss army knife-like gun on a robotic metal arm from the elbow down that contains a variety of weapons and tools, although he has been shown to have a metal hand on it as well.

===Special abilities===
Clyde's large size and muscular build grant him superhuman strength and durability. In addition, his robotic left arm contains a variety of tools and weapons, such as a saw, drill, or even a robotic hand, to help him break into places he wants to rob. He can also [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]] with a Brooklyn accent. His connection to Bonnie is programmed into his DNA.

'''Coco''', also known as '''Experiment 052''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to turn things into chocolate. [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] gifted Coco to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] as a birthday present in the ''[[disney:Disney Adventures|Disney Adventures]]'' comic ''[[Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|Party Crashers]]''.

==Background==
Experiment 052 was the 52nd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to turn objects into chocolate. 052 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|Party Crashers]]''===
[[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] chased Coco throughout the [[Lilo's House|house]] on [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]]'s birthday, wrecking everything. At first, Lilo was angry with Stitch for ruining her birthday, but Stitch showed her 052's power of turning objects into chocolate. Lilo changes her mind and declares it to be her best birthday ever instead, while she, Stitch, and everyone else enjoys eating the chocolate-converted household objects. 052 was then named Coco.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Coco is a lizard/[[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]-like experiment with light brown hide and a yellow underbelly, two buck teeth, a pink nose, pink spots down his back and tail, and pink hair on his head with chocolate-brown tips.

===Special abilities===
Coco can turn things into chocolate by touching them, though the object will remain the same color.

==Trivia==
*Coco, along with [[Experiments#3-Series: Psychological|Experiment 347 (Slobber)]], [[Experiments#5-Series: Elemental and environmental manipulators|Experiment 531 (Hisee)]], [[Experiments#Other|Tippy]], and [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|several unconfirmed experiments]], have only appeared in the ''[[disney:Disney Adventures|Disney Adventures]]''.
**Coco appeared in the comic called ''[[Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|Party Crashers]]'', where he was activated and given to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]].

*His name, number, and primary function were confirmed by [[disney:Jess Winfield|Jess Winfield]] prior to the end credits of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
**Coco is also the only comic-originating experiment that was fully confirmed and canonized.
*Coco and [[Fudgy (054)|Fudgy]] are the only known experiments with primary functions directly involving chocolate, and both of their names relate to chocolate as well. Interestingly, their numbers are close together.

'''Dark End''' is an alien [[Experiments|experiment]] who appeared in the third season of the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime as a minor antagonist. Dark End was created by [[Delia]] using similar genetic blueprints to that of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and required Stitch's power cell to complete their creation, although a new power cell stolen from Jumba was ultimately used. It is because of this that Dark End does not fall into [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s numbering system. Delia made Dark End as a combatant in order to defeat Stitch.

This character's gender differs between dubs, being a female in the Japanese original and a male in the English dub. As a result, this article will use "they/them" pronouns for consistency purposes.

==Background and appearances==
===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
[[Delia]] began the creation of Dark End at the start of Season 3 of the ''Stitch!'' anime and continued working on them until the [[Boss|penultimate episode]]. After they were created, Delia then invaded Earth and sent out Dark End to defeat [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. Dark End easily had Stitch on the ropes, even with the help of some of the other experiments. However, Stitch eventually defeated Dark End using a hidden power he had. Afterwards, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] caught Dark End in a container, and the [[Grand Councilwoman]] arrested Delia, [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], [[Gantu]] and [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]]. Dark End has not been seen since.

==Personality==
Dark End has a rather unique personality. They have a polite, playful, and carefree attitude with a twisted sense of humor. They introduced themselves to Hämsterviel, Gantu, and Reuben and offered Hämsterviel a handshake, only to lift him off floor and shake him in the air. When they met Stitch, Dark End assumed he was really nice and apologized that they had to defeat him. Dark End is penchant when it comes to manners, as when Hämsterviel ordered them to fight Stitch, Dark End refused and requested him to say it again in a polite manner. Dark End is loyal to Delia and anyone who serves under her, but even Dark End expected Delia to exhibit manners, getting annoyed when she ordered them to do something, as Dark End claimed she could have asked nicely. Despite this, Dark End obeys Delia and follows her orders through.

Despite their politeness, Dark End is vicious, brutal, ruthless, cruel, and enjoys causing chaos and mischief. Their playful attitude comes off as mischievous, but they can also be sadistic; they take joy in taunting and humiliating their foes instead of finishing them off. Dark End wanted to keep tormenting Stitch after pulling him out of the fault that Dark End created, then shaking Stitch in the air. They are also sneaky and dishonest, as they offered Stitch to be friends and a handshake, only to electrocute and toss him in the air. Dark End has no qualms on attacking anyone who gets in their way, especially children, as they were willing to attack [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] when she refused to hand Stitch over. They also fought and attacked some [[experiments]], [[Hiroman]], his soccer team, and Yuna's friends for getting in their way.

Dark End is confident in their abilities and comes off quite condescending to their foes, which they deem their actions futile. As Delia created them as a combatant, Dark End enjoys fighting and expects their foes to put up a challenge, lamenting about defeating Stitch easily to be a letdown. They then got excited when some experiments along with Yuna and Stitch's friends joined in. Dark End also has a low opinion on family and friends, deeming they and Stitch are just experiments to those, and believes when they do not need experiments anymore, they abandon them. Dark End even declares Stitch to be a failed experiment, indicating that Dark End holds themselves superior to Stitch and the other experiments.

Dark End's opinion on friends and their arrogance and failure to recognize the bonds that they forged caused them to underestimate Stitch, thus giving him the power to defeat Dark End.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Dark End is a dark purple, rabbit-like experiment with purple claws, two gold earrings on their right ear, large ears similar to [[Delia]], a small blond Mohawk, white fur on their belly, hands, and around their eyes, and a pink rabbit-like nose. In their second form, they extend a second pair of arms from their waist, two antennae from their head, and three spines or quills from their back, much like [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], and their hair changes color to lavender.

===Special abilities===
As aforementioned, Dark End is able to mutate into a second form with four arms, two long antennae, and three spines on their back. Their eyes can glow bright purple when doing so, and energy radiates off their body which can be fired off as purple energy blasts. They possess Stitch's abilities of enhanced strength, invulnerability, and fighting skills. They also possess other abilities, such as creating faults in the ground, flight, teleportation, and electricity. They are capable of [[:Category:Talking experiments|speaking fluently]].

==Trivia==
*With Dark End being female in the Japanese original and male in the English dub, they are the one of the few known characters in the franchise's non-Western spin-offs whose gender changes between their originating work's native language and the franchise's original English.
*Dark End is the second experiment that was not created by Jumba, as they were created by Delia. The first is [[Skunkuna]] who was created by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]].
*Dark End serves as a foil to Stitch when it comes to family and friends. Unlike Stitch who values both concepts, Dark End believes individuals will abandon experiments once they do not need them anymore.
**The power cell used to create Stitch and Dark End befits how the two are different with their views on family and friendship. Stitch's powers are supercharged when he remembers the bonds he forged, yet Dark End doesn't value either of these concepts, and while they are loyal to Delia, they do not have a special bond, unlike Stitch has with his creator.
*Dark End could be considered an advanced genetic experiment, as they have no known weaknesses. Since they were created after the 629 experiments, Dark End is likely immune to [[Angel (624)|Angel]]'s song but not immune to the other experiments, as Dark End avoided [[Spike (319)|Spike]]'s spikes.
*Dark End has some similarities in character with [[Warracchi]] (a yokai): they both wreak havoc in one way or another, but at the same time, they do not like a rude attitude.
*Dark End is one of the few experiments that are actually villains, along with [[Zero (000)|Zero]], [[Chopsuey (621)|Chopsuey]], [[627]], and [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and [[Leroy Clones|his clones]], while all the other experiments were following their primary function.

[[Gantu]] and [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] then arrived for 515, named Deforestator. In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Deforestator was one of the experiments in [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]]'s dream.

Deforestator was seen on a computer screen in "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]", posing as an evil creation of [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s as part of a hoax to fool [[Mortlegax]], the head of E.G.O. industries.

Deforestator can be seen in the audience cheering.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Deforestator made [[Hämjock Vielvonster|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime when [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] disguised him as a punk and was about to [[Transmutation|use]] him for another plan, but called it off after developing a temporary "soft side" while posing as [[Hämjock Vielvonster (alter ego)|a substitute teacher]]. Because of that, he didn't really do anything during the episode (except punished Hämsterviel for failing [[Delia]] again).

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Deforestator is a large purple, roughly wombat-like creature with dark purple markings on his arms and back, long blade-like claws on his front paws, a maroon nose, and a blade-like neck.

===Special abilities===
Deforestator can spin into a razor-sharp tornado that can cut through most substances. His claws and blade-like neck can rotate and function like a chainsaw, allowing him to spin at high speed, and he can jump real high.

Much like [[Richter (513)|Richter]], Deforestator can only speak [[Tantalog language|Tantalog]].

==Trivia==
*Deforestator was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Deforestator is the first experiment to debut in [[627 (episode)|an episode]] not named after it, and to never have an eponymous episode. He shares this trait with [[Zap (603)|Zap]], who happened to debut in the same episode.

*Even though Deforestator was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]], his [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is white according to "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]".
*Jumba refers to him as: "Experiment 515: The Deforestator"; however, his official name is mentioned in "[[Ploot (episode)|Ploot]]".
*His [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|number was also given to]] [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]] (in "[[Slushy (episode)|Slushy]]") and [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]], most likely due to Jumba's untidy [[Jumba's Computer|database]].
*Deforestator is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.
*Deforestator's body appears in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.

'''Derrick''', also known as '''Experiment 566''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to drill potholes in hard surfaces. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "[[:Category:Mrs. Hasagawa's experiments|cats]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 566 was the 566th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to drill potholes. 566 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]]. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 566's pod being one of them.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 566's pod for an apricot and placed it in a colander for later consumption along with numerous other pods.

After [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] redecorated Mrs. Hasagawa's front yard without her permission, she was less than thrilled with the results, but decided to thank them for their hard work with the "apricots". The pods were then revealed, but before Lilo and Stitch could stop her, she washed them with a watering can, thus activating the experiments.

After his activation, 566 began to carry out his primary function by drilling potholes in Mrs. Hasagawa's floor. Lilo and Stitch believed the experiments to be a danger to Mrs. Hasagawa and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], decided to capture them all. 566 was then [[Prison Capsule|captured]] by unknown means.

566 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 566 was then named Derrick.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Derrick, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Derrick participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Derrick is a grey dinosaur-like experiment with black eyes, brown-orange markings on his tail, a tan stomach from his chin down, and a drill-like tail, wearing a yellow construction helmet.

===Special abilities===
Derrick can use his drill-like tail to drill potholes beneath him.

==Trivia==
*Derrick was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Derrick is very similar to [[Splat (519)|Splat]] in that they both do construction work.
*Derrick, [[Backhoe (040)|Backhoe]], and [[Digger (529)|Digger]], are the only known experiments whose powers are related to excavation.
*Derrick is one of the only four known experiments that wears a hat, the other three being [[Squeak (110)|Squeak]], [[Frenchfry (062)|Frenchfry]], and [[Slick (020)|Slick]]. However, it is unknown if Derrick can remove his hat or not, while it is presumed Squeak can take off his hat since he appears with a fresh hat in [[Leroy & Stitch|the TV film finale]] after an earlier incident with the Evil-liminator, and Frenchfry's "hat" appears to be a part of his head, while Slick is wearing a true hat that he can remove.
*Derrick is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''Leroy & Stitch''.

'''Digger''', also known as '''Experiment 529''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to dig or drill holes through planets, making him capable of digging or drilling through many other surfaces.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 529 was the 529th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to dig or drill holes straight through planets. 529 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

===''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''===
All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 529's pod landing atop a little boy's sand castle on a [[Lahui Beach|beach]].

Later that night, a wave washed over the sand castle, activating the experiment, which proceeded to escape underground.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
529 was captured by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] at an unknown point and named Digger.

In "[[The Asteroid]]", Digger was one of the six experiments that Stitch convinced to come with him and Lilo to save Earth from an approaching asteroid. Along the journey, Digger was shown digging restlessly into his seat. He later drilled a hole through the asteroid's core for which to insert the [[Jumba's Ship|ship]]'s hyperdrive engine into.

Digger was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that presumably joined Stitch in a rebellion against [[Gantu]]. Earlier in the episode, he, along with [[Yin (501)|Yin]] and [[Backhoe (040)|Backhoe]], helped Lilo make mud.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Digger, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Digger participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by sending attacking Leroys into his underground tunnels.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[disney:Aloha `Oe|Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Digger is a yellowish-tan meerkat-like experiment with a long, bony drill-shaped tail, a round body, short arms and legs with sharp claws, a round head with sharp teeth, a dark round nose, black eyes and a row of spikes protruding from his head down to his tail.

===Special abilities===
Digger can use his thick, sharp claws to dig in a fashion similar to a mole, but at a much quicker pace and more efficiently. He also has a tail that is similar in shape and function to a drill, which he can support himself on, and he can start drilling through the ground using this at will.

It has been shown for him to roll into a shape similar to that of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and most other experiments, although due to his tail, it appears as a more wheel-like figure.

==Trivia==
*Digger's design was first revealed in a bonus feature trivia game on the original ''[[Lilo & Stitch]]'' DVD, before he officially debuted in ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''.
*Digger is one of the few known experiments to be turned to good off-screen, as he was seen already rehabilitated in ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]'' after his activation in ''Stitch! The Movie''.
*Digger, [[Backhoe (040)|Backhoe]], and [[Derrick (566)|Derrick]] are the only known experiments whose powers are related to excavation.
*After [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Sparky (221)|Sparky]], Digger is tied with [[Slimy (390)|Slimy]] for the most appearances of experiments that [[:Category:Stitch! The Movie Experiments|debuted]] in ''Stitch! The Movie''. Both appeared in two different episodes of ''Lilo & Stitch: The Series'' as well as ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
*Digger's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] changes color between scenes. In one scene, it was red, and in another, it was purple.
*Digger is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.
*He is also one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''Leroy & Stitch''.

'''Dim Long''' (点长 ''Diǎn zhǎng'') is an illegal genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba]], and [[Jumba's Chinese Experiments|the fourth experiment he created]] in China based on what he learns in ancient Chinese scrolls.

==Background==
Following [[Spirals|Jumba's creation of two cliff dragons who had a child together]], Jumba created Dim Long, a small dragon Jumba created as a beta-test to perfect the ''qi'' power that ancient creatures used for flight so he could utilize it in future experiments, which he did with his next experiment, the Xiezhi. Unlike the other experiments Jumba created in China, Dim Long does not live in the pocket dimension he created to house them. Instead, he lives with Jumba, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], and [[Pleakley]] at [[Wang Ai Ling|Ai]]'s family home, making him a recurring character in ''[[Stitch & Ai]]''.

==Personality==
Dim Long is a playful creature who enjoys flying around and more or less serves as a family pet to the Wangs and the aliens, mainly the latter.

Like many of Jumba's [[experiments]], he has a mischievous streak. When he first appears onscreen, he kicks an unaware Pleakley in the face, knocking him over and causing him to drop his plate of [[wikipedia:Baozi|bao]]. In "[[Dragon Parade]]", as he flies in the titular parade, he decides to fly close to the audience where [[Qian Dahu|Dahu]] was standing, forcing everyone around the spot to duck. He also photobombs Ai and [[Meiying]]'s selfie photo after the parade. Nevertheless, he is good-natured at heart and is a considerably nicer "alien pet" than the self-indulged [[BooGoo]] of the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Dim Long is a small dragon-like experiment with orange fur, a dark orange nose, brown stripes on his back, and yellow antlers, his right one of which is apparently permanently broken, is partially miscolored brown, and has a bandage wrapped around the base. The insides of his ears and the fur flaring at the tip of his tail are yellow. His mouth is big for his head with two teeth sticking out from his long jaw, giving him a prominent underbite. He has four tiny limbs with only two digits on each limb. Unlike [[Experiments|traditional experiments]], he has regular eyes with white sclerae and black pupils.

He was temporarily enlarged by Jumba in "Dragon Parade" to replace an accidentally destroyed dragon puppet. He was returned to his original size off-screen by [[Tell the World|the next episode]].

===Special abilities===
Dim Long's only ability is the ability to fly without wings using ''qi'' energy. He is a particularly zippy flier, although he can be a bit out of control.

===Weaknesses===
As he is a very small creature whose only purpose is to prove that it's possible for Jumba to make creatures who can fly without wings, he's physically weak and not capable of combat, although he was able to kick [[Wendy Pleakley|Pleakley]] in the face to knock him over.

==Trivia==
*Dim Long is the first and only experiment Jumba created in China that was created specifically as a beta test creature for another experiment.
*Dim Long is the only regular recurring experiment other than [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] in ''[[Stitch & Ai]]''.
*His appearance looks similar to [[disney:Mushu|Mushu]] from ''[[disney:Mulan|Mulan]]''.

'''Dorkifier''', also known as '''Experiment 122''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to zap a pink ray that changes anyone's appearance into something ridiculous. Also, the new dorky clothes cannot be taken off the victim unless the horns are rotated upside-down, after which every victim will automatically be restored to normal. He appears in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 122 was the 122nd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to zap a pink ray from his horns that changes anyone's clothing into something ridiculous. 122 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
In his [[Dorkifier (episode)|eponymous debut]], Dorkifier was accidentally sent to [[Gantu]] by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], who originally intended to send [[Hertz Donut (022)|Hertz Donut]] in yet another attempt at capturing [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. However, Hämsterviel was in a rush and selected the pod for 122 instead of 022. After his activation, Dorkifier used his powers to change Gantu's uniform into dorky civilian clothes. Dorkifier then escaped and went on a rampage, changing other people's appearance into something ridiculous, including Stitch, [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]], [[Pleakley]], and [[Hiroman]]. Later, after a long chase, Dorkifier is captured by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], and Stitch reverses Dorkifier's effects by turning down his horns, reverting everyone's dorky clothing to their original clothing. In "[[Shogun]]", it is shown that Dorkifier was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in Jumba's vault.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Dorkifier is a pink and white calf-like experiment with two horns, a red nose, a white belly, and purple hooves.

===Special abilities===
Dorkifier can cause victims to look dorky by zapping them with a pink ray from his horns. The new dorky clothes can only be taken off when his horns are turned down.

==Trivia==
*His name in Japanese is ドーキファイ, which translates directly to Dokifi (pronounced dough-key-fai). This is how the pronunciation of Dorkifier was localized into Japanese.
*Dorkifier is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having dark red eyes instead.
*Dorkifier, along with [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], [[Butter (227)|Butter]], [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]], [[Spike (319)|Spike]], [[Yang (502)|Yang]], [[Richter (513)|Richter]], [[Phoon (540)|Phoon]], [[Tank (586)|Tank]], [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]], and one [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed experiment]], are the only known experiments that are primarily quadrupeds.
*Altering the position of Dorkifier's horns in order to reverse his powers is the same way to reverse the effects of [[Shoe (113)|Shoe]]. Also, the closeness of their numbers (113 and 122) and movable horn feature may suggest that Jumba had been inspired by the same DNA source when creating both. This would be a similar concept to how Jumba reused some for Twang's DNA when creating [[Bragg (145)|Bragg]].
*Dorkifier's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue.

'''Doubledip''', also known as '''Experiment 002''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]]. He is designed to double-dip food. His main instinct is to lick candies or appetizers and put them back in the bowl. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "[[:Category:Mrs. Hasagawa's experiments|cats]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 002 was the second genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to double-dip food. 002 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]]. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 002's pod being one of them.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 002's pod for an apricot and washed it, activating the experiment. However, as 002 was not a very evil or destructive experiment, he was able to live a peaceful life with her, due to the latter seeing the former as a mere stray cat who needed a home, though he frequently licked a bowl of hard candies.

When [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] discovered that Mrs. Hasagawa, kept several experiments as pets, they thought they were a danger to her and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], decided to capture them all. As Mrs. Hasagawa was petting 002, Lilo took the bowl of candy from him and placed it in an open [[Prison Capsule|container]], with the experiment taking the bait. Lilo assured the elderly woman that they would take care of the "problem", though unbeknownst to her, there was no problem to begin with.

002 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 002 was then named Doubledip.

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Doubledip was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 608 instead of 002.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Doubledip, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Doubledip participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Doubledip made a special guest appearance (along with [[Sparky (221)|Sparky]], [[Felix (010)|Felix]], and [[Angel (624)|Angel]]) in the ''Stitch!'' segment "[[Kung Fu Dragon Pleak Lee]]".

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Doubledip is a small purple opossum-like experiment with a light purple stomach from his chin down, two light purple stripes on the back of his ears, light purple stripes on his back, a hairless tail, beady eyes and an orange nose, which was changed to dark purple in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'' and ''[[Stitch!]]''.

===Special abilities===
Doubledip can double-dip foods by licking or double-dipping candies or appetizers and then placing them back.

==Trivia==
*His name and number are a likely reference to the fact that he engages in double-dipping.
*Doubledip, [[Experiments#4-Series: Top secret and mysterious series of militaristic and mostly failed experiments|Char]], [[Experiments#4-Series: Top secret and mysterious series of militaristic and mostly failed experiments|Crusty]], and [[Experiments#4-Series: Top secret and mysterious series of militaristic and mostly failed experiments|Botulator]] are the only known experiments whose functions are related to spoiling food.
*Doubledip was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Doubledip somehow changed in size in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.

'''Drowsy''', also known as '''Experiment 360''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to cause populations to fall into a near-permanent sleep by simply bleating; only spraying water in the victim's face will awaken them, and other experiments are less vulnerable to his bleats. His one true place is putting insomniacs to sleep.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 360 was the 360th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his sleep-inducing bleat to cause his victims to instantly enter a near-permanent sleep. 360 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Drowsy - Drowsy moments after activation.png|thumb|left|Drowsy moments after his activation]]
360's pod was one of the twelve experiment pods recovered by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] in "[[Drowsy (episode)|Drowsy]]". His was one of the final four pods (among [[Stopgo (102)|102]], [[Experiments#2-Series: Technological and scientific|274]] and [[Nosox (204)|204]]) that [[Pleakley]], with some assistance from Stitch, cataloged after being convinced to do so by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]].

Lilo had become restless lately while catching experiments with Stitch, so [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] threatened to ban her from doing any future experiment hunting if she was unable to fulfill her duties or be attentive. Stitch then attempted to get Lilo to fall asleep that night.

Eventually, Stitch activated 360 and used the latter's bleat to put Lilo to sleep. However, Lilo was still asleep the next morning when Nani called for her, and Stitch couldn't wake her up. To try and solve the problem, Stitch tried to make Lilo seem awake by putting sunglasses on her, mimicking her voice, and moving her around like a puppet all over [[Kokaua Town|town]].

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Drowsy - Pleakley using Drowsy on Gantu.png|thumb|Pleakley using Drowsy on Gantu]]
Meanwhile, 360 escaped and was chased throughout [[Kauai]] by Jumba and Pleakley, while 360 put everyone he encountered to sleep by bleating. Pleakley initially caught 360 in his purse, but then opened it to put [[Gantu]] to sleep when the latter was looking for the experiment. At that point, however, 360 jumped out as Gantu fell heavily on Pleakley. Jumba then scolded Pleakley for letting 360 escape.

Gantu was later woken up by a bunch of people on [[Lahui Beach|the beach]], who thought he was a beached whale and dumped water over him (though they fled in fear after hearing him talk). He then received a call from [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] who demanded 360 from Gantu.

Stitch was unable to wake Lilo up all day until Jumba revealed that the cure to 360's powers was to spray water in the victim's face. After Lilo was awakened, Stitch told her that she had to meet someone at the [[Kauai Airport|airport]]. Because she'd been asleep at the time, Lilo started to worry, but Jumba reassured her that Stitch had taken care of all her appointments.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Drowsy - Regis Philbin sleeping with Drowsy.png|thumb|left|Regis Philbin sleeping with Drowsy]]
Later, after a long chase, Gantu and [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] captured 360 in a duffel bag and guarded the [[Birds of Paradise Hotel]]. However, when they tried to use 360 to kidnap [[wikipedia:Regis Philbin|Regis Philbin]] (the man from the airport) while posing as bellboys, Lilo and Stitch were there for Regis since he had disembarked and protected him in every way they could.

Lilo eventually recaptured 360, named him Drowsy, and let Regis spend the night at the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]]. In the end, Drowsy used his sleep-inducing powers to send Regis and everyone in Lilo's ''ʻohana'' to sleep.

In "[[PJ (episode)|PJ]]", Lilo used Drowsy to put Stitch to sleep after claiming he had trouble sleeping lately, allowing her to release [[PJ (133)|PJ]] and use him to avenge her strict substitute teacher. Strangely, however, Stitch woke up on his own.

In "[[Ploot (episode)|Ploot]]", Drowsy was one of the second team of experiments (along with [[Finder (158)|Finder]] and [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]]) formed to try and stop [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]]. However, Ploot was easily able to defeat them, forcing the three experiments to retreat.

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Drowsy was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Drowsy, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

It is unknown whether or not Drowsy participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Drowsy is a greyish light-blue sheep-like experiment with striped ears, short arms and legs, and black fingers and toes who can walk on his hind legs.

===Special abilities===
Drowsy's bleat causes anyone who hears it to enter a near-permanent sleep.

===Weaknesses===
Water sprayed in the victim's face is the one surefire way to awaken them. Also, if the victim blocks their ears, Drowsy's sleep-inducing bleat will have no effect. Additionally, other experiments under Drowsy's effects are less vulnerable and will likely wake up on their own.

==Trivia==
*Drowsy's sleep-inducing bleat and sheep-like appearance are most likely derived from [[wikipedia:Counting sheep|the mental exercise of counting sheep]] in an attempt to fall asleep.
*He is one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to.
*A recurring irony has occurred with Drowsy. Stitch originally used him to get Lilo to fall asleep, and in his [[PJ (episode)|second appearance]], Lilo used him to put Stitch to sleep.
**Stitch wasn't initially affected when Drowsy put Lilo to sleep, though when Stitch was put to sleep by Drowsy, he somehow managed to wake up on his own without having to be splashed by water, possibly indicating that other experiments are not affected as much.
*Drowsy's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is yellow.
*The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Drowsy as: "Experiment 360. Primary function: Sleep inducer."
*Oddly, when Drowsy's image is reflected off of Stitch's eyes in ''[[The Origin of Stitch]]'', he is not yawning for some reason. It is possible that Drowsy's yawning image was taken from ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.

'''Dupe''', also known as '''Experiment 344''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to generate infinite clones of individuals, but his programming is considered a failure because the original's power is distributed evenly among the duplicates, resulting in them being inferior in everything. Luckily, it is possible for him to reverse the cloning. His one true place is making half-calorie [[Luki's Shave Ice|shave ice]] cones with [[Slushy (523)|Slushy]].

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 344 was the 344th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to clone single individuals into entire armies and make infinite weapons, but all of the original's traits were divided between them and the clones. 344 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 344 was activated.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:ScreenCapture-20-01-22-03h22m54s709.png|thumb|left|Dupe duplicating Stitch]]
An estimated twelve hours after his activation, 344 was [[Prison Capsule|captured]] by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and taken back to their [[Lilo's House|house]], but not before being pursued by a relentless [[Gantu]].

After [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] explained about 344's powers, the latter demonstrated by duplicating a lollipop and birthday cake (with less calories in each). Stitch then attempted to use 344 to clone [[Pleakley]] as well, despite the latter's protests. Fortunately, Jumba put 344 away on [[Jumba's Ship|his ship]] to prevent any further chaos.

The following night, after [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] and [[Elena|the]] [[Teresa|hula]] [[Yuki|girls]] did not show up at Lilo's slumber party that she had hosted earlier, Lilo used 344, christened Dupe, to generate clones of herself that she could befriend. However, Stitch hastily intervened, resulting in him being cloned into three instead.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Dupe - Stitch clones on Jumba's ship.png|thumb|Stitch clones]]
Later that night, Gantu, [[Hammerface (033)|033]], [[Heat (609)|609]], [[Thresher (544)|544]] and [[Plasmoid (617)|617]] attacked the Pelekai residence. Stitch and his clones tried to fight back, but due to a side effect from Dupe's replication, they had all become very weak, enabling Gantu and his four henchmen experiments to easily defeat and capture Stitch and his duplicates in containment orbs.

Shortly after Stitch had been kidnapped, Lilo hatched a plan and used Dupe to generate three clones of Pleakley, leaving the original comatose. Lilo and the Pleakley clones then launched a rescue mission on [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]] while taking Dupe with them so he could remerge the Stitch clones.

Gantu complained about the victory feast that [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] made for him and his minions, when he was distracted by Lilo and the Pleakley clones on his ship. After Gantu discovered them and Lilo informed him about Dupe's cloning powers, Gantu grabbed Dupe and cloned Hammerface, Heat, Thresher and Plasmoid each into a hundred replicas. However, as a result of being tricked, the experiments had all become complete weaklings, and thus were easily defeated by Lilo and the Pleakleys.

Lilo then used Dupe to remerge the freed Stitch clones into the original, and Lilo, Stitch, Dupe, and the Pleakley clones escaped the ship. Dupe then remerged the Pleakley clones into the original, and he was later found a one true place making half-calorie [[Luki's Shave Ice|shave ice]].

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Dupe was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Snafu - Dupe duplicating shave ice.png|thumb|left|Dupe with Slushy]]
In "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", Dupe and [[Slushy (523)|Slushy]] were seen using their combined powers to sell multiple low-calorie shave ice cones that [[Charles and Mary|a couple]] bought and enjoyed. Gantu then attempted to revert the rehabilitated experiments to evil by playing a recording of [[Angel (624)|Angel]]'s song with Reuben's help, but due to interference from [[Snafu (120)|Experiment 120]], Gantu's karaoke tape was played instead, much to Slushy and Dupe's humor.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Dupe, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Dupe participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by splitting attacking Leroys into weakling Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Dupe made [[Boss|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where his tweak was [[Transmutation|altered]] by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], so instead of making things weaker once duplicated, the clones are made stronger (and bigger) than the original.

==Personality==
Dupe is shown to be very fun-loving, childish, and immature, due to the fact that he was programmed to be one of the younger experiments (along with [[Mr. Stenchy (254)|Mr. Stenchy]] and [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]]). Because of this, he is often treated as the baby of the heroes' side, as his cloning powers are neither chaotic nor destructive. He is also seen as very playful, friendly, and optimistic.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Dupe is a small, golden-yellow experiment resembling a cross between a monkey, lemur, and raccoon. He has relatively flat ears, a brown round nose, black eyes, a white body, a brown-striped, raccoon-like tail, and brown-striped prehensile appendage protruding from his head.

===Special abilities===
The ray from Dupe's appendage causes any individual or object hit to split into a varying number of duplicates. He can generate multiple clones of anyone or anything.

Dupe also has a reverse setting which causes his ray to remerge the clones into the original.

In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, Dupe was [[Transmutation|altered]] by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], so instead of making things weaker once duplicated, the clones were made stronger than the original, with each newly-created duplicate being slightly bigger and stronger than the one created before it, while the original maintained its normal strength. However, his tweak had a downside in which the enhanced replicas had a significantly reduced shelf life and disappeared after about an hour.

===Weaknesses===
Despite Dupe's ability to generate clones, all of the original's traits (such as strength, power, calories, etc.) will be divided between the duplicates, making the original very weak, and resulting in the original and duplicates being inferior in everything.

==Trivia==
*According to Jumba, Dupe "is [a] duplicator. It can make multiple copies of anyone or anything. Designed to make infinite number of weapons." However, Dupe "was [a] failure. Duplicates were not as powerful as [the] original."
*Dupe is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to.
*Dupe was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*The [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]], [[Heat (609)|Heat]], [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]], and [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]] clones were never remerged into the originals by Dupe, but each of these experiments appeared as one again in later episodes. It is presumed that [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] was somehow able to remerge these clones into the originals, meaning that there are ways to reverse the cloning without Dupe.
*Dupe's antenna and ears appear in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.
*Dupe also appears in the online game ''[[Lilo & Stitch: Alien Interception]]'' along with Plasmoid, [[Tank (586)|Tank]], [[Clyde (150)|Clyde]], [[Yang (502)|Yang]], and Hämsterviel.

'''Elastico''', also known as '''Experiment 345''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to distract hostile forces with his clownish antics and elastic body. His one true place is with the circus.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 345 was the 345th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to distract enemies by performing tricks with his elastic body. 345 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 345 was activated.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Elastico - 'Cousin?!'.png|thumb|left|"Cousin?!"]]
345 eventually found his way to an international circus, where he was taken in and named Elastico by the troupe's [[ringmaster]].

A newspaper article with Elastico's picture in it was almost used as a sandwich wrapper by [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]]. When [[Gantu]] noticed the article on [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]], he snatched it and read the section. Reuben then revealed that Elastico had been activated two weeks ago, so Gantu headed off to the circus to capture the experiment.

Meanwhile, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] was engrossed in a new hula dance, but ignored [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] when he offered to help her. He later noticed Elastico riding atop a circus van, and after Lilo rebuked Stitch for his interference, he followed Elastico to the circus. There, Stitch disguised himself as a clown and attempted to capture Elastico, but the latter teased Stitch and turned the whole chase into a game. Eventually, Elastico calmed down when Stitch grabbed him and called him "cousin".

As the entire audience began cheering for Stitch, he was pulled onto the stage and praised by Elastico's ringmaster, who nicknamed him "The Incredible Indestructorado". However, at that moment, Gantu barged in, strangled Elastico, and stuffed him into a [[Net Cannon|net]] before fleeing.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Elastico - Elastico juggling bowling pins on a tightrope.png|thumb|Elastico juggling bowling pins on a tightrope]]
Stitch revealed that Gantu had kidnapped Elastico, much to the ringmaster's dismay. He then mentioned how Stitch stole the show with his incredible stunts and even invited him to perform in Elastico's stead, to which Stitch happily accepted. He later met the circus troupe, where, after putting on an amazing show, he signed a contract permitting him to travel with the circus.

Meanwhile, Gantu tried to teleport Elastico to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], but the experiment put up quite a fight and proved difficult to control. Reuben wagered a Monte Cristo sandwich on the ordeal, although Gantu soon disabled Elastico by blasting him and put him in shackles. However, he stretched out of the cuffs and under the teleport chamber just before the transfer could be completed. An angry Hämsterviel then contacted Gantu, thinking the latter was pranking him by sending him empty shackles, much to Gantu's shock and confusion.

Elastico somehow packaged himself and then shipped himself back to the circus, reuniting with his ringmaster. When Lilo later discovered that Stitch had run away with the circus, she paid him a visit and attempted to make amends. Just then, Gantu attacked and tried to take Elastico back, but was thwarted by Lilo and Stitch, as well as the entire circus troupe.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Elastico - Elastico with his ringmaster and two other circus members.png|thumb|left|Elastico with his ringmaster and two other circus members]]
As the circus prepared to leave for Las Vegas, Lilo and Stitch made up. When the ringmaster learned that Stitch had a family of his own, the former voided the contract on a technicality (as Stitch had previously signed it with his own name, rather than the nickname he was given by the ringmaster) and let Stitch be with his ''ʻohana''. After Stitch said his goodbyes, he and Lilo decided that Elastico's one true place was staying with the circus.

Elastico was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that joined Stitch in a rebellion against Gantu. Gantu even put Elastico on his head (thinking the latter was [[Checkers (029)|Checkers]]).

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Elastico was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Elastico, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Elastico participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by strangling attacking Leroys with his elastic body.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. Elastico joins them for the song by playing the trombone.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Elastico made [[Elastico 2.0|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] [[Transmutation|modified]] him with the ability to transform things into circus-related items and animals (dogs, monkeys, elephants, seals, etc.) in order to turn [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] into a harmless little puppy, thus making him easier to capture. It is also revealed that Elastico is capable of [[:Category:Talking experiments|speaking fluently]]. However, [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] was turned into a dog by mistake, and Stitch was unaware that it was actually her until he later found her in a circus tent being tortured to do tricks for the circus.

Elastico [[Dark-End|later appeared]] as one of the experiments who helped Stitch fight [[Dark End]]. He also appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Elastico is a very playful, fun-loving and enthusiastic experiment and treats just about anything like a game. He loves entertaining folks, sometimes breaking the rules for his own fun. Being a natural contortionist, he amuses himself by stretching his body into fun shapes or using them to pull little stunts or jokes on others. He can be a bit of a prankster, as he enjoys fooling around and teasing his enemies, often irritating them. Despite this, he can be very jumpy in immediate danger or if someone is trying to catch him. Also, he loves both of his families (his circus family and his ''ʻohana'' with Lilo, Stitch, and the other experiments) very much.

Elastico is generally very friendly and affectionate towards others. The one thing he dislikes more than anything is being grabbed or restrained, with the exception of hugs. He is also very terrified of Gantu, screaming every time he sees him and grabbing onto Stitch's head when Gantu approaches. This is quite reasonable due to the fact that Elastico has been grabbed, choked, netted, kidnapped, pulled, squeezed, blasted and shackled by Gantu. Despite this, he seems to have gotten over his fear by "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]", as he was seen bravely rebelling against Gantu.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Elastico is a green, furless, earless, clownish, roughly monkey-like creature with a small, stumpy tail, a large, red, round clown nose; white face and stomach, wide mouth, black eyes, neck frill, three huge tendrils on his head that resemble a jester's cap, and a purple spot on his stomach. He always wears a pink ruffled collar (like the ones that typical white-face circus clowns wear) around his neck, though it is unknown if it's removable.

===Special abilities===
Elastico can manipulatively stretch and bend any part of his body like taffy; this can range from him flattening himself until he is incredibly thin, to reshaping into anything from a parachute to a rubber raft. He uses this ability to perform amazing stunts and tricks. Like some of his cousins, Elastico can roll into a ball, though it acts more as a bouncy ball than the form [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and other experiments use. He can also inflate himself and float like a balloon. He has shown the ability to transform things into circus-related items and animals, such as dogs, monkeys, elephants, seals, etc. However, he has only displayed this while [[Transmutation|under the effects]] of [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. He is also seen to be able to [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]], though it is unknown if this is because of Hämsterviel transmuting him or if he was always capable of speaking and learned over time.

As part of stretching, Elastico displays some amount of invulnerability. Forced stretching, even under several tons of load, appears to cause him pain and discomfort, but no permanent or even temporary harm. A high degree of protection is also afforded by his skin. Combined with flexibility, this makes him immune to bullets. He can use his elasticity to throw objects with far more force than his slight stature would imply. He has also displayed the ability to shapeshift with his elasticity.

Elastico has shown to be skilled in playing the trombone.

===Weaknesses===
Forced stretching because of someone pulling on Elastico causes him pain and discomfort, but is otherwise indestructible. He is also jumpy around anyone or anything he sees as a threat.

==Trivia==
*Elastico's number was never revealed in [[Elastico (episode)|his debut]], but his number officially appears on the experiments list in the [[Experiments/Gallery#Leroy & Stitch|end credits]] of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
*Elastico was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Elastico is one of the ten known experiments named by someone other than Lilo or Stitch, the other nine being [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Yaarp (613)|Yaarp]], [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]], [[Heat (609)|Heat]], [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]], [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]], [[Morpholomew (316)|Morpholomew]], [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]], and [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]]. 
**Elastico, in particular, was named by the [[ringmaster]] of the circus.
*He is also one of the six known experiments to be rehabilitated by someone other than Lilo and Stitch, the other five being Gigi, Yaarp, [[Spike (319)|Spike]], [[Frenchfry (062)|Frenchfry]], and [[Snooty (277)|Snooty]]. 
**Elastico, in particular, was rehabilitated by the ringmaster of the circus, which became his one true place.
**He is also the only known experiment to be rehabilitated by a one-shot character rather than one of the regulars.
*Elastico's name is Spanish in the masculine form for "elastic" (though the proper spelling is "Elástico" with an acute-accented a), befitting his elasticity and the fact that the ringmaster is all but stated to be Latino and/or Hispanic, as he speaks with a Spanish accent.
**"Elastico" is also Italian for "rubber band".
*While the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime established that Elastico can [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]], his one spoken word in his debut episode in [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]] — the word "cousin" — and the fact that he seemed to understand the word, imply that he always had such speech capabilities.
*Despite being very flexible, Elastico could not seem to escape the [[Net Cannon|net]] he was captured in.
*According to [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]], he describes Elastico as: "Primary function: Distraction of hostile forces."
*Elastico's head appears in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.

The '''Experiment Pod Container''' is a device seen in ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' that [[Jumba Jookiba|Dr. Jumba Jookiba]] had built to store all of his [[Experiments|625 experiments]] in their [[Experiment Pods|dehydrated form]] before he was arrested by the [[United Galactic Federation]] in ''[[Lilo & Stitch]]''.

==Background==
It is a spherical object the size of a globe propped up on a rectangular platform with a view screen. This is the primary database and container for all 625 initial experiments, keeping records of each and every one. It also monitors how many are contained within it and when one is activated; stating their number, primary function, and bringing up a projection of what they look like.

[[Gantu]] has the experiment pod analyzer in ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]'' on [[Gantu's Ship|his crashed ship]]. The analyzer has a mechanical voice, and logs the available experiments it contains. It announces when an experiment is activated, and informs of its number and function. It also shows a 3-D image of the experiment activated for further recognition.

==Trivia==
*The container's automated voice is provided by Rob Paulsen.
*It is unknown what happened to the container after all the experiments were captured and rehabilitated.

'''Experiment pods''' are little spherical pods seen in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]], containing the [[experiments]] in their dehydrated form. Each pod is labeled with the experiment's number. Once a pod gets wet, the experiment will be activated, releasing them. The pods have numbers printed on them and come in six different colors: red, blue, green, yellow, white, and purple.

==Trivia==
*Some of the experiment pods seen in ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' are changed to a completely different color and/or labeled with a completely different number in certain episodes of ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''. The same goes for a few of the pods that [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] showcases on the Internet monitor in the episode "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]".
**Additionally, some of the experiments' numbers in their debut episodes [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|do not match their pod numbers]] when they were in dehydrated form.
**The colors of the pods also change between the original series and ''[[Stitch!]]''. The pod colors in the original series are bright and saturated with colored labels (with fonts that sometimes change), while the pod colors in the anime are pastel with black labels. Also, some experiments have their pod color change between series. For example, in the original series, [[Fudgy (054)|Fudgy]]'s pod is mislabeled and blue, but in the anime, it is labeled correctly and red.
**In the original series, the pods are one of six colors: white, purple, green, yellow, red, and blue. In the anime, the pods are one of four colors: white, blue, red, and green.
*Though not consistent, in the original series, some colors seem to be more common depending on the numbered series.
**0-series: white; 1-series: purple; 2-series: green; 3-series: yellow; 4-series: red; 5-series: blue; 6-series: blue.
**[[disney:Jess Winfield|Jess Winfield]] confirmed that the colors were intended to correlate with the series of the pod, but they lost track of it during the rush of Season 1 production.<ref name="WinfieldTVTome">{{cite web|url=http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|title=L&S Says Mahalo|website=[[wikipedia:TV.com|TV Tome]]|date=December 14, 2004|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305082355/http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|archivedate=March 19, 2016|accessdate=May 27, 2018}}</ref>
*Several of the pods have different sizes. Some are so big that [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] or someone else could hold them in the palm of their hand, while others they could hold with their fingers. [[Poxy (222)|Poxy]]'s pod was one of the smallest, just slightly larger than a grain of sugar.
*The pods appear to be very durable and keep the experiment safe. Poxy's pod survived the entire sugar refining process from sugar cane harvest to consumer purchase; [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]]'s pod was unscathed when a seagull pecked at it; and [[Spats (397)|Spats]]' pod was unharmed after a squirrel tried to bite through it.
**Additionally, [[Gantu]] mentions in "[[Slushy (episode)|Slushy]]" that the pods emanate a heat signature, allowing them to be located even if they are buried under snow and ice. This suggests that the pods also help protect the experiment from the surrounding environment.
*The pods seen in Jumba's vault in the ''Stitch!'' episode "[[Shogun]]" are experiments that appeared in previous episodes of the third season [[Transmutation|transmutated]] by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] and captured by the end of their original appearances of that season.
**The pods shown are those of (in order from left to right and top to bottom) [[Bragg (145)]] (a.k.a. "Flute" in the English dub and misnumbered 021, the number of Twang, as with the original Japanese version of [[Flute|his episode]]), [[Hertz Donut (022)]], [[Dorkifier (122)]], [[Toons (112)]] (who was misplaced in numerical order within the vault and is reactivated in the episode), [[PJ (133)]], [[Sample (258)]], [[Wishy-Washy (267)]], [[Spooky (300)]], [[Spike (319)]], [[Sprout (509)]] (even though it was actually [[Sprout (509)#Stitch! anime|a seedling of the original Sprout]] that appeared in "[[Sprout 2.0]]"), [[Wrapper (521)]] ([[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|mislabeled as 512]], swapping the tens and ones digits), [[Witch (610)]], [[Plasmoid (617)]], and Splodyhead (619).

This is a list of '''experiments''' from the Disney animated [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]], most of them making their first appearance in ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''. These fictional experiments, also referred to as '''Stitch's cousins''', are genetically engineered creatures created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Dr. Jumba Jookiba]] in his lab at "[[Galaxy Defense Industries]]", with the assistance of [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Dr. Jacques von Hämsterviel]] who funded the projects with "shady" business deals. Prior to the events of ''[[Lilo & Stitch]]'', every experiment created was dehydrated into a small orb called an "[[Experiment Pods|experiment pod]]" and stored in a special [[Experiment Pod Container|container]] for transport. In ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'', the container was accidentally opened, and the pods dispersed and rained down on the island of [[Kauai|Kauaʻi]]. The experiments within the pods are reactivated upon contact in water, a point of concern because many of the experiments are dangerous and Kauaʻi hosts one of the wettest spots on Earth.

Upon encountering each experiment, whose information is contained in Jumba's [[Jumba's Computer|database]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]'s human friend and partner [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] gives the experiment a name just as she gave Stitch his name. The two then attempt to rehabilitate the experiments and find a purpose for them on Earth that suits their specific abilities, referred to as the "one true place" they belong.

Stitch, inspired by Hawaii's terminology, refers to the other experiments as his "cousins" and considers them all a part of his ''ʻohana'', or "extended family". [[Gantu]] usually refers to the experiments as "trogs" or "abominations". All of Jumba's original 626 experiments have their names and numbers listed alongside the [[Experiments/Gallery#Leroy & Stitch|credits]] in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.

==Background==
===Biology===
Due to different experiments' original purposes, the majority of experiments each have a unique appearance, powers, and weaknesses. Though all experiments have unique capabilities and functions, most of them have some abilities in common due to Jumba reusing DNA from one experiment as a prototype for a different experiment, like the similarities of body shape, appearance, and even for powers like in the case of Jumba reusing some of Twang (021)'s DNA in the creation of [[Bragg (145)|Bragg]] (145), granting the latter musical ability. Most seem capable of scaling walls like a gecko (as Stitch frequently does); many are able to grow and retract an extra pair of arms. Since they are genetic experiments each created with multiple kinds of DNA that Jumba sampled throughout the galaxy, they all age quite differently than creatures on Earth as seen with Lilo and the rest of humanity when time is lapsed twenty years in "[[Skip (episode)|Skip]]".

It is also shown that some experiments' powers (such as [[Mr. Stenchy (254)|Mr. Stenchy]] (254)'s cuteness, and [[Checkers (029)|Checkers]] (029)'s hypnotic effect) do not affect other experiments, possibly so that these powers do not prevent other experiments from carrying out their primary functions. If affected by other experiments' powers, it might be temporary as Stitch managed to recover from [[Drowsy (360)|Drowsy]] (360)'s sleep-inducing program without being exposed to water. Though [[Angel (624)|Angel]] (624) primarily reverts other experiments (before her time) to evil, [[Amnesio (303)|Amnesio]] (303) and [[Retro (210)|Retro]] (210) can do so as well.

Additionally, it is shown that when an experiment is dehydrated, they will deactivate and turn into a small orb called an experiment pod. If an experiment pod gets wet, the experiment will be reactivated and released. According to Jumba, a home food dehydrator is the only known method of deactivating an experiment a second time.

On numerous occasions, it has been shown that most, if not all, of the experiments have an intentional imperfection added to their design by Jumba: a "fail-safe" of some sort. These imperfections were presumably added in by Jumba in the event his experiments ran out of control, in order to provide him with a way of stopping them in their tracks. Even his most powerful experiments, like [[627]] and [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]], both had their own intentional imperfection, with an overreactive sense of humor and the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]" being their respective imperfections.

===Creation===
Upon each experiment's creation, it is most important that their molecules be charged. If an experiment's molecules are not fully charged, about a year after their creation, they will suffer glitches, during which they will experience seizures and temporarily revert to their original programming. If the molecular charging process is not completed, these glitches will eventually burn out the experiment's circuits like a supernova and kill them.

===Experiment series===
The first digit of the experiment numbers reflects what series of experiments they belong to. The official series of experiments, as stated by [[disney:Jess Winfield|Jess Winfield]], one of the executive producers, are as follows:
*'''0-Series:''' Jumba's test batch, including many household helpers.
*'''1-Series:''' Civic disturbances.
*'''2-Series:''' Technological and scientific.
*'''3-Series:''' Psychological.
*'''4-Series:''' Top secret and mysterious series of militaristic and mostly failed experiments.
*'''5-Series:''' Elemental and environmental manipulators.
*'''6-Series:''' Battlefield and doomsday experiments with galactic implications.

For the most part, the colors of the experiment pods correspond to the series numbers; however, some of the pods are colored incorrectly.
