==Trivia==
*According to [[disney:Jess Winfield|Jess Winfield]], during the development of ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]'', the idea of it focusing on "the other 625 experiments" was birthed from an idea by artist and director Steve Lyons who "suggested that an evil villain clone [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] into a bunch of different creatures that [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and Stitch would chase." Also, the phrase "the other 625 experiments" was coined either by Winfield himself, [[disney:Bobs Gannaway|Bobs Gannaway]], or possibly Barry Blumberg, although Winfield doesn't remember who was first to say it.<ref name="WinfieldTVTome" />
*''[[Disney's Stitch: Experiment 626]]'' featured an experiment series numbered as 700, which were mass-produced by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and served as enemies in the game.
*In ''[[Stitch!]]'', eleven previously unseen experiments created by Jumba were introduced in addition to two experiments created by someone other than Jumba. The first, called [[Skunkuna]], was created by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], and the second was [[Dark End]], created by [[Delia]]. Since neither were created by Jumba, they do not fall under his numbering scheme.
*In ''[[Stitch & Ai]]'', Jumba [[Jumba's Chinese Experiments|creates new experiments]] based on ancient scrolls he is given. Most are based on Chinese mythical creatures, while others appear to be derived from some creatures. It is unknown whether or not Jumba considers these experiments a part of his existing numbering scheme.
*Tippy has also appeared in the comics, but we do not know anything about her except that she is Jumba's experiment. Additionally, her name is not seen in the experiments list in the [[Experiments/Gallery#Leroy & Stitch|end credits]] of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', so she most likely doesn't apply to Jumba's numbering scheme.
*According to the series episode "[[Skip (episode)|Skip]]" (as seen on a monitor) and the [[disney:Magic Kingdom|Magic Kingdom]] attraction [[disney:Stitch's Great Escape!|Stitch's Great Escape!]] (as seen on wanted posters in the exit halls of the attraction), the official shorthand prefix for "Experiment" is "X-" (X with a hyphen). In addition, Jumba referred to [[Spooky (300)|Spooky]] as "X-300" (ex three hundred), [[Kixx (601)|Kixx]] as "X-601" (ex six-oh-one), and [[Morpholomew (316)|Morpholomew]] as "X-316" (ex three-one-six) in their [[Spooky (episode)|respective]] [[Kixx (episode)|eponymous]] [[Morpholomew (episode)|episodes]], further supporting this.
*To date, there are only 127 of Jumba's experiments that have appeared and have their names, numbers, and functions confirmed. This includes [[Coco (052)|Coco]] who has only appeared in the ''[[disney:Disney Adventures|Disney Adventures]]'' comics and was confirmed by Jess Winfield, [[Chopsuey (621)|Experiment 621]] from ''Disney's Stitch: Experiment 626'', and [[Zero (000)|Experiment 000]] who first appeared in the ''Stitch!'' anime. This numbering scheme does not count the new experiments Jumba made in ''Stitch & Ai'' as stated above. 
**Experiments 021, 153, 274, 340, 412, 413, 414, 415, 607, and 611 have their names, numbers, and functions confirmed, but have never physically appeared.
**Experiments 607 and 611 have appeared as stylized graphics on [[Jumba's Computer|Jumba's computer]] and the [[Experiment Pod Container|experiment pod container]]'s screen, respectively.
**[[627|Experiment 627]] has physically appeared, but was never given an official name.
**347,  531 and Tippy have appeared in the comics, but do not have their functions confirmed.
**There are several experiments that have appeared in DVD bonus features, comics, and ''Leroy & Stitch'' that have [[Unconfirmed Experiments|never been assigned to a name and number]].
**Also, [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Miscellaneous|two experiments]] appeared in ''[[Stitch!Now]]'', but they were not confirmed to be Jumba's experiments.
**There are some functions that have never been assigned to a name and number: the experiment designed to turn things into ham was mentioned by [[Wendy Pleakley|Pleakley]] in "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]"; as well as the experiment designed to clog sinks and the experiment with two horns that makes "zzz" sound were mentioned by [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] (respectively) in "Skip" (both were captured by Gantu). Also, some experiments are revealed to have similar abilities of 627.
**Of the 125 experiments that have appeared and been confirmed (including Stitch), ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' [[:Category:Stitch! The Movie Experiments|introduced 7 experiments]], the original series introduced a total of 93 with [[:Category:Season 1 Experiments|45 of them appearing in Season 1]] and [[:Category:Season 2 Experiments|48 appearing in Season 2]], ''Leroy & Stitch'' [[:Category:Leroy & Stitch Experiments|introduced 13]], and ''Stitch!'' [[:Category:Stitch! Experiments|introduced 11]] (excluding Dark End, Skunkuna, and [[Sprout (509)#Stitch! anime|Sproutling]]).
**We have met 20% of Jumba's experiments in [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|the franchise]] that have their names, numbers, and functions confirmed, while we only know around 21% of the experiments' functions.
*In most of the franchise, though more prominently in the anime, Stitch typically prefaces the names of his fellow experiments (other than [[Angel (624)|Angel]]) with "cousin".
*Skunkuna, Dark End and Tippy are the only numberless experiments. The former two are the only known experiments that weren't created by Jumba, as Skunkuna was created by Dr. Hämsterviel and Dark End was created by Delia, which means they are not included in Jumba's numbering. Tippy was created by Jumba as an intelligent toy for Lilo, although it is debatable whether she counts as an experiment, considering she appears as a robot.
*000, 627 and 628 are the only nameless experiments, and thus only referred to by their numbers. The fandom have previously given them nicknames, which have led to erroneous beliefs that those were their canonical names.
**627 was previously called "Evile" by the fandom due to him being evil and saying only that word in ''Lilo & Stitch: The Series''.
**000's popular name in the fandom is "Cyber", due to him being a biomechanical creature, but he is only ever referred to as "Zero" in all dubs of his only anime episode. This also implies that his number is also his name, especially considering the fact that he is referred to as just "Zero" instead of "Zero-Zero-Zero".
**628's name in the fandom varies depending on fan interpretations due to it never being activated in the series. 628 is also the only unseen experiment without known details or other traits that doesn't have an official name, due to Lilo and Stitch never having dealt with it.
*Chronologically, Zero is Jumba's first experiment, while [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] is Jumba's last experiment.
*627 is Jumba's strongest and powerful experiment due to him having the abilities of at least 20 experiments, a highly-muscular body that outclasses Stitch's, the ability to have six arms and two heads, and other things. The most dangerous experiment, however, is Zero, since he can create an armada of robots and a galactic-level nuke.
*Chopsuey, 627, Leroy and [[Leroy Clones|his clones]], Zero, and Dark End are the only experiments that are actually villains, while all the other experiments were following their primary function.
*627, Leroy, Zero and Dark End serve as dark versions of Stitch, with Zero being too difficult to control where he disregarded the notion of family, Dark End having a low opinion on family and friends, 627 being designed to be an evil monster who cannot be rehabilitated, and Leroy being made for Hämsterviel and not ever given the opportunity to reform. 627, Leroy, Zero and Dark End all serve as what Stitch would have become if he had never met Lilo and her ''ʻohana'' and been introduced to the meaning of family.
*628 is the only experiment that was never activated.

===Continuity errors===
*Several experiments [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|have been given multiple numbers]], such as [[Bonnie (149)|Bonnie]] and [[Clyde (150)|Clyde]], who are called 349 and 350 in [[Bonnie & Clyde|their episode]], but called 149 and 150 in the [[Experiments/Gallery#Leroy & Stitch|end credits]] of ''Leroy & Stitch''. The same goes for [[Finder (158)|Finder]] and [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]], who are called 458 and 515 in their [[Finder (episode)|respective]] [[Ploot (episode)|episodes]], but called 158 and 505 in the end credits of ''Leroy & Stitch''.
*Many of the experiments that appear in the background during the [[Aloha Stadium]] battle in ''Leroy & Stitch'' are duplicates or recolors and slight edits of existing experiments. They were put in as screen fillers to make it appear as if all 626 experiments were actually there. For example, [[Houdini (604)|Houdini]] appears five times in the frame, while [[Cannonball (520)|Cannonball]] appears eight times; twice recolored, twice re-edited and four times copied. [[Phoon (540)|Phoon]] is also seen twice in the scene, both in normal and mutated form.
*Experiment 272 was listed as "Mamf" in the end credits of ''Leroy & Stitch''. However, in ''Stitch!'', [[Wormhole (272)|Wormhole]] is called 272 while 275 is given to [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]], who was mistakenly left off the list in the movie. When asked about the numbers of these three, Jess Winfield stated: "The best I can tell you about Tickletummy/Wormhole is that Jumba's genius does not extend to keeping a tidy database. There is some confusion in his records regarding Tickletummy, Wormhole, and a third experiment named Mamf, with different lists giving different numbers for them. Perhaps it will be sorted out someday."

'''Felix''', also known as '''Experiment 010''' (and temporarily '''Oscar'''), is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to clean and sterilize everything in sight, but had a flaw in his programming that caused him to be unable to tell the difference between dirt and living things. Thus, he saw all living beings as giant, filthy germs needing to be sterilized until Jumba temporarily [[Transmutation|reprogrammed]] him into a dirt freak. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]". Although his "one true place" was never depicted in ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]'', he was eventually given one in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, with him becoming a mobile recycling service.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 010 was the tenth genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to keep Jumba's house clean and tidy, but due to a glitch in his program, he viewed all organisms (including individuals) as germs that must be "sterlized" at all costs, and threw away anything even remotely dirty. 010 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Felix - Felix firing his laser at a housefly.png|thumb|left|Felix firing his laser]]
Experiment 010 was activated off-screen and captured by [[Gantu]] at some point. Due to 010's tendency to throw out anything that was even remotely filthy (including prized belongings), Gantu sent 010 to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], but he found 010 annoying as well, and thus sent him back to Gantu, who abandoned 010.

Left with nothing else to do, 010 started cleaning up [[Lahui Beach|the beach]] until he was discovered by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], who captured him in a picnic basket and took him [[Lilo's House|home]]. Later, Lilo brought 010, named Felix, to her [[Kaiāulu Hale|hula school]], where he tidied up the auditorium, but due to a mishap with [[Moses Puloki|Moses]]' oriental rug, Felix was taken back to the Pelekais' house.

Although Lilo and Stitch had become less impressed by the neat freak, Felix's cleanliness proved to be very useful at home, which fascinated [[Pleakley]] to the point that he befriended the cleaning experiment. However, he then started destroying and throwing out Lilo, Stitch, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and Pleakley's personal belongings.

Eventually, Felix decided to "antisepticize" Lilo's ''ʻohana'' as well and, locking them inside the house (save Pleakley, whom Felix locked outside), relentlessly pursued them until they were able to trap him in a [[Prison Capsule|container]]. Jumba then [[Transmutation|reprogrammed]] Felix to be less of a neat freak, but instead of just liking dirt, it caused Felix to begin making things incredibly dirty.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Felix - Felix back with Gantu.png|thumb|Felix back with Gantu]]
Lilo and Stitch later sent Felix (renamed Oscar) back to Gantu as a present, but due to the experiment's new programming, rather than help Gantu clean up [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]] like the latter hoped Felix made it even dirtier. It can be presumed that Gantu sent Felix back to Hämsterviel after this messy incident.

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Felix was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream.

In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Felix was sent back to Gantu along with all of Hämsterviel's other captive experiments after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused chaos and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

Felix reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]" and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by Lilo, Stitch, and several other experiments in a rescue mission.

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Felix was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 602 instead of 010.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Felix, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

It is unknown whether or not Felix participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Felix first appeared in his [[Felix Redux|own episode]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] summoned him so he could get out of cleaning the house. It is shown in this episode that Felix has a defect that kicks in when he is faced with anything aged or antique. However, Felix apparently doesn't understand the concept of antiques, and as far as he knows, they only collect dust. Thus, his programming causes him to terminate anything aged in order to prevent the buildup of dust. In the end, he is [[Transmutation|reprogrammed]] to collect things that can be renewed and recycles them. His one true place after this is as a mobile recycling service.

In the two-part Season 1 finale "[[Stitch vs. Hämsterviel Pt. I|Stitch vs.]] [[Stitch vs. Hämsterviel Pt. II|Hämsterviel]]", [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] puts Felix along with [[Sparky (221)|Sparky]] and [[Angel (624)|Angel]] under his control. He also appeared in "[[Dracula, Jr.]]".

==Personality==
Felix was originally obsessed with cleanliness to the point that he considered even individuals germs that must be "sterilized" at all costs. It is also shown that Felix has a defect that kicks in when he is faced with anything aged or antique because he doesn't understand the concept of antiques, and as far as he knows, they only collect dust.

During Felix's reprogramming, he became obsessed with dirt. The only word that 010 can say is "Dirty!" However, as Felix, he says it disgustedly, while when reprogrammed to Oscar, he exclaims it happily. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, however, where he only appears in his Felix persona, it is generalized to being the only word he says without any tonal consistency; although in [[Stitch vs. Hämsterviel Pt. I|one episode]] of the anime, when he and Sparky inform Stitch about Jumba's [[Evilsaurus Rex|dinosaur robot]] going on a rampage, Felix exclaims, "''E. rex''!" This remains the only instance to date that he says anything other than "dirty". 

Jumba appears to have found the right balance in Felix's programming. Felix is currently obsessed with cleanliness instead of only dirt, respecting antiques and recycling when appropriate. According to Jumba in the anime, Felix only sleeps when his stomach is full.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Felix is a green anteater/elephant-like experiment with a small body, mouth, arms and legs, a thin long tail with a fuzzy brush at the end, a large head with a long tubular elephant/vacuum-like trunk that can suck up debris and fire lasers out, large black eyes, small, short ears, four fingers on each hand and three toes on each foot, all ending in black claws, and three dark-tipped antennae arranged in a crest-like structure.

===Special abilities===
Felix can sanitize with his anteater-like trunk and sweep with his tail. His nose is more than just a rudimentary olfactory device; it is a sophisticated bio-system of tiny brushes and hormonal detergents. He can use his nose as a vacuum or a leaf blower; he can also remove practically every type of stain with his nose. His duty is threefold: one, automatically tidy up all messes; two, digest process all garbage and trash; and three, antisepticize against all unhealthy germs and sources of filth.

For rapid cleaning, Felix can spin himself in a tornado, and when trying to antisepticize, he fires a laser out of his trunk, which is used to disintegrate germs and small creatures. However, there was a flaw in his design; he had a logic problem in his third function. He could not tell the difference between dirt and living things, so he saw living things as giant filthy germs. Jumba [[Transmutation|reprogrammed]] Felix so that he was no longer obsessively neat. However, Jumba reversed his polarity too much, so Felix began to release sucked-up dirt in massive bursts to cause messes.

At some point, Felix's programming was reversed again as Jumba tried to balance out his programming, thus causing him to still "sterilize" anything aged or antique in order to prevent it from collecting dust as seen in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime. He was reprogrammed yet again so that he would understand the concept of renewing and recycling items.

===Weaknesses===
Despite Felix's cleaning habits, he had a problem with doing these tasks: he threw away anything, assuming it was trash, and tried to "sterilize" anyone, assuming they were germs. Felix was upgraded to try to be less of a neat freak. Instead, he turned into a dirt-maker (renamed Oscar), so Lilo gave him back to Gantu, who had previously abandoned him.

The '''Fenghuang''', also called the '''Phoenix''', is an illegal genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba]], and [[Jumba's Chinese Experiments|the seventh experiment he created]] in China based on what he learns in ancient Chinese scrolls.

==Background==
==="[[The Phoenix]]"===
After receiving the ancient scrolls, Jumba was inspired to create a genetic experiment based on the Chinese mythical creatures that were in the scroll. This time, Jumba decided to create a fenghuang to find the shrine [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] was looking for. He created a small phoenix, but it quickly grew and flew away. Later, he was hunted by alien bounty hunters [[Noo-Bing and Zi]]. However, Stitch and [[Wang Ai Ling|Ai]] manage to find and protect the phoenix from the two hunters. In the end, the phoenix leads them to a temple that, although it is not the shrine Stitch is looking for, has a painting on its grounds that prophesizes Stitch transforming into a huge monster. He was later sent to a parallel dimension inhabited by various mythological creatures.

==="[[Monstrosity]]"===
In this episode, the fenghuang and some other Chinese experiments were summoned from a parallel dimension to battle the [[Jaboodie]]s.

==Personality==
The fenghuang is a proud and freedom-loving creature. He was initially distrustful of Stitch, but Stitch later manages to gain his trust. He is also ready to help his friends if necessary.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
The fenghuang is a large bird, though he was initially created small. It has five plumage colors that symbolize the five virtues. It has feathered wings, a beak, and a crest, as well as a cockerel-like tail.

===Special abilities===
The fenghuang has the ability to fly, as well as find an ancient temple from where other phoenixes originated.

===Weaknesses===
It has no power, so it is vulnerable to weapons and can be easily caught, tied up, and frozen.

==Trivia==
*The fenghuang is based on the Chinese mythological creature called the [[wikipedia:Fenghuang|fenghuang]]''.
*The five colors of its plumage symbolize the five virtues.
*It is also unknown if it possesses other phoenix abilities, such as burning itself and being reborn. However, as those abilities are affiliated with [[wikipedia:Phoenix (mythology)|Western phoenixes]], it most likely does not.

'''Fibber''', also known as '''Experiment 032''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to detect lies; the more individuals lie, the more he buzzes, forcing entire populations to tell the truth. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 032 was the 32nd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his lie-detecting ability to force entire civilizations to only ever tell the truth. Based on Jumba's incorrect theory, this would result in a societal collapse. 032 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 032 was activated.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Fibber - Fibber buzzing at Lilo's lie.png|thumb|left|Fibber buzzing at a lie]]
An estimated twelve hours after his activation, 032 was [[Prison Capsule|captured]] by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and taken back to their [[Lilo's House|house]]. The former then tried to look up 032 on [[Jumba's Computer|Jumba's computer]]. When [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] himself revealed which experiment it was, Lilo claimed she knew all along, causing 032 to buzz loudly in reply. He buzzed again when Lilo lied to [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] about cleaning her room, making Stitch openly laugh at Lilo's dishonesty.

That night, while Stitch was forced to share his bed with 032, named Fibber, [[Pleakley]] received a call from [[Mrs. Pleakley|his mother]]. She had been badgering her son about finding a soul mate, and even revealed that she'd found him a perfect bride on [[Plorgonar]] and made plans to bring him home to be married. Pleakley felt heartbroken, not wanting to leave his ''ʻohana'' forever, until Lilo and Jumba convinced him to lie his way out. So Pleakley called his mother back and fabricated his sham engagement, while Fibber kept buzzing.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Fibber - Fibber eating cookies.png|thumb|Fibber eating cookies]]
Shortly after, Pleakley's relatives arrived at the Pelekais' house to witness his proposal to Nani, while the latter reluctantly posed as Pleakley's fiancée after Lilo forced her. Pleakley's charade led to a fake wedding that Nani turned down (Jumba later took her place by dressing up as a bride). Meanwhile, Lilo and Stitch attempted to hide Fibber in all sorts of places to drown out his frequent buzzing caused by Pleakley lying to his family.

When [[Gantu]] returned from a spa weekend, he discovered Fibber's recent activation, which [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] deliberately neglected to notify him about. Gantu later crashed the phony ceremony to try and take Fibber but was foiled by Lilo and Stitch, although Gantu managed to divulge the experiment's lie-detecting nature in the process.

Pleakley eventually told his relatives the truth, and while Fibber buzzed at the false comments they made about Pleakley, they were able to accept the fact that he was happy living on Earth and didn't want to get married. However, as Pleakley's family prepared to depart, Gantu reappeared in his [[Manta Shuttle|shuttle]] and captured Fibber. Regardless, Lilo decided to let Fibber stay with Gantu for now.

Back at [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]], Fibber buzzed when Gantu lied to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] about his whereabouts, while Reuben befriended the lie-detecting experiment.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spike - Fibber buzzing at a lie during Pleakley's seminar.png|thumb|left|Fibber in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group]]
In "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]", Fibber was one of the experiments in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group. He buzzed during the therapy session whenever one of the other experiments lied (mainly [[Bonnie (149)|Bonnie]], when she lied about her being intelligent and falsely accused [[Clyde (150)|Clyde]] of their arrest). Earlier, Fibber buzzed when Pleakley denied that his antenna was prematurely orange and simply dyed green (as stated by [[Nosy (199)|Nosy]]). When the other experiments later began to cause chaos, Fibber watched nonchalantly while smiling.

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Fibber was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream.

In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Fibber was sent back to Gantu along with all of Hämsterviel's other captive experiments after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused chaos and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

Fibber reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by Lilo, Stitch, and several other experiments in a rescue mission.

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Fibber was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 580 instead of 032.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Fibber, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Fibber did not participate in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], instead choosing to retreat with the weaker experiments.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe, during which Fibber can be seen around some of the Leroys as they started to shut down.

==Personality==
Fibber appears to be mute (except when buzzing at a lie) and sometimes blank, but he has displayed emotion on few occasions. For example, in "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]", when Pleakley came out wearing a makeshift suit of armor (to protect himself from [[Spike (319)|Spike]]'s spines), Fibber heavily frowned in bewilderment. However, when Pleakley managed to convince the other experiments in his E.A.R.W.A.X. group to attempt hugging therapy on each other, Fibber ended up shedding tears and "aww"-ing at the sight of Pleakley hugging Spike. His "aww" is the only time he made a verbal sound other than beeping (although this was drowned out by the other experiments around him also "aww"-ing).

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Fibber is a small orange experiment with small body, arms and legs, a very large head with a dark orange marking on the forehead that glows bright yellow whenever he beeps, little antennae, a little mouth with a purple tongue, a round crimson nose, black-blue eyes, and four ears.

===Special abilities===
Whenever Fibber hears a lie, he responds by emitting a loud buzzing sound and lights up the pattern on his forehead. The bigger the lie, the louder he beeps, and the brighter his marking glows. He also appears to possess some level of super strength despite his diminutive size, as he was able to toss a washing machine off of himself after it was placed on him to muffle his beeping.

It should be noted that truths and lies are a matter of perspective, as in what one believes to be true or false. Thus, it can be assumed that if an individual spoke of something that they believed to be true (but is actually false), Fibber will most likely not react, since the "truth" is ''believed'' to be true by the individual who spoke it.

===Weaknesses===
Fibber appears to be defenseless.

'''''Stitch: Alien Experiment Character Guide''''' is an upcoming reference book in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. It will be a complete reference guide to the 127 fully-confirmed genetic [[experiments]] seen throughout the entire franchise, including the animated films, ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]'', the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, and non-animated media such as ''[[Disney's Stitch: Experiment 626]]''.

It is set to be published in Australia and New Zealand on November 1, 2026. No publications in other regions have been announced.

==Official synopsis==
Evil genius [[Jumba Jookiba|Dr. Jumba Jookiba]] has been busy in his laboratory. Hundreds of his illegal genetic experiments have escaped his lab and are now scattered across the island of [[Kauaʻi]]. Enter the Undercover Intergalactic Experiment Retrievers, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]! With the help of their ''ʻohana'', Lilo and Stitch have assembled this handy Alien Experiment Character Guide. Inside you can study the details of all 127 Experiments that have been located so far, and become an Intergalactic Experiment Retriever yourself!

==Summary==
The book is a guide to Jumba's genetic experiments seen throughout the franchise. Although there are about 630 experiments in total, ranging from [[Zero (000)]] to [[Leroy (629)]], only the 127 experiments whose identities are fully-confirmed, with name, number, design, function, and abilities revealed, are documented in the book.

Each page covers one experiment, with each page having a simplistic, scientific-themed format with a grid background and background colors based on the primary body color of the page's featured experiment. The name of the experiment (or names separated by a slash if they are known by more than one name) and their experiment number are on the page header. Each experiment is twice depicted in new artwork made for the book.

Each page has five parameters (after the name and number) detailing the experiment:
*'''Category''': Each experiment is typed into one or two categories relating to their design and/or function, with each category represented by an icon. Based on the available preview images, these include:
**Animal (a pawprint)
**Psychological (a brain)
**Weapon (a [[Plasma Blaster]])
**Practical abilities (crossed wrenches/spanners)
**Household helper (a house)
*'''First appearance''': The experiment's first physical appearance in a work in the franchise. Major work titles (films, television series, etc.) are bolded and italicized (although ''Stitch!'' is rendered as "'''''Stitch!''''' anime"). Television episodes have additional lines, with season and episode numbers written in title case on the second line, and episode titles written in all caps within single quotation marks on the third line.
*'''Engineered by Jumba to''': The experiment's primary function, written as a sentence beginning with the words of this parameter's name.
*'''Project status''': The experiment's "one true place" if known, or other status based on their last appearance. Experiments without a known one true place whose last appearances are left ambiguous will have "Unknown" written in this parameter.
*'''Description''': A description detailing the featured experiment, with a secondary artwork shown within this parameter's field. (The primary artwork is shown above this parameter's field alongside the above four parameters.)

'''Finder''', also known as '''Experiment 158''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to sniff out and uncover any lost or missing individual or item like a hound dog; he can also fly by spinning his ears like helicopter blades to ensure optimal tracking potential. Upon success, he honks like a party blower. His one true place is operating a "Lost and Found" service at [[Lahui Beach|the beach]].

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 158 was the 158th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to track down and detect any missing individual or item. 158 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 158 was activated.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Finder - Finder searching for Nani's car keys.png|thumb|left|Looking for Nani's keys]]
[[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] encountered 158 at an unspecified location in [[Kauai]], where the former had taken him [[Lilo's House|home]] and named him Finder. Meanwhile, [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] was desperately searching for her car keys that she lost.

Finder demonstrated his amazing powers by finding Nani's missing keys in the fridge, which made Stitch rather envious. The latter then attempted to outdo Finder by shredding the sofa cushion and uncovering a few buried items. However, Lilo concluded that Finder was better at finding stuff than Stitch.

Later, Lilo used Finder for show-and-tell at her [[Kaiāulu Hale|school]], where he quickly found all of [[Elena|the]] [[Teresa|hula]] [[Yuki|girls]]' lost belongings, much to [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]]'s jealousy.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Finder - Stitch and Finder debating over which way to go.png|thumb|Stitch and Finder disagreeing on which way to go]]
The [[Grand Councilwoman]] later contacted [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]] to report that [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] had somehow escaped from [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison]] and traveled to Earth. Lilo selected Finder for tracking down the fugitive, but a competitive Stitch set out to beat Finder to the punch. When both cousins debated over which trail led to Hämsterviel after searching through a jungle, Lilo went with Finder, despite Stitch's protests.

Finder deftly tracked Hämsterviel to [[Mertle's House|Mertle's house]], but Lilo began to doubt Finder's accuracy. Earlier, however, Mertle had found Hämsterviel outside a [[Pet Shop|pet shop]], mistook him for a talking gerbil, brought him home, and placed him in a cage for show-and-tell, which led to a conflict between them. When Mertle then tried to cover up for Hämsterviel (after Lilo dropped by to question his presence), Lilo was convinced that Finder had made an error.

After discovering that Finder did uncover Hämsterviel's whereabouts, Stitch burst into Mertle's bedroom that night and attempted to ambush the caged fugitive, but the latter blasted Stitch with a makeshift plasma cannon, knocking him unconscious. The ruckus alerted [[Mrs. Edmonds]], who quickly noticed Stitch and took him to the [[Aloha Animal Rescue|dog shelter]].

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Finder - Finder hovering in midair.png|thumb|left|Finder flying by spinning his ears like helicopter blades]]
The next day, Lilo and Finder arrived at the pound to retrieve Stitch, who revealed to them that Finder had indeed tracked down Hämsterviel. Beforehand, Stitch admitted that he was jealous of Finder and wanted to prove himself to Lilo.

Lilo, Stitch and Finder returned to the Edmonds' home to discover that [[Gantu]] (having joined the hunt for Hämsterviel when the Grand Councilwoman offered to reinstate him as captain if he succeeded) had fled with Hämsterviel in [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]], but also kidnapped Mertle. Thus, Stitch decided to team up with Finder to rescue her. Using his helicopter-like flying ability, Finder tracked down Gantu's ship while carrying Stitch, who then disabled the spacecraft, thereby saving Mertle.

Hämsterviel was arrested, but due to Gantu's blunder, the Grand Councilwoman did not reinstate him to his former position. However, she did congratulate Stitch for helping to nab Hämsterviel, though Stitch revealed that Finder actually did it. When Mertle felt heartbroken over losing her new "pet" that she named Milton, Lilo requested the Grand Councilwoman to let Hämsterviel stay on Earth until after show-and-tell at school, albeit in shackles.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Finder - Finder working at the beach Lost and Found.png|thumb|Finder's one true place]]
Shortly after, Finder found his one true place operating a [[Lahui Beach|beach]] "Lost and Found" service, drolly crossing out "Lost" on the sign with a red marker.

In "[[Drowsy (episode)|Drowsy]]", Finder's picture was seen in [[Lilo's Experiment Book|Lilo's experiment logbook]].

In "[[Skip (episode)|Skip]]", Finder was one of the wanted fugitives who had already been captured in an alternate future where Hämsterviel ruled Earth.

In "[[Ploot (episode)|Ploot]]", Finder was one of the second team of experiments (along with [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]] and [[Drowsy (360)|Drowsy]]) formed to try and stop [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]]. However, Ploot was easily able to defeat them, forcing the three experiments to retreat.

In "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", Finder was one of the experiments that joined Lilo and Stitch on a mission to rescue Gantu's captive experiments. Finder helped break into the ship, and after the rescue team successfully freed the captive experiments, he was seen playing with them in Lilo's obstacle course.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Finder, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Finder participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Personality==
Finder is a very beneficial and resourceful tracker who has a knack for uncovering any missing person or thing. Unlike most experiments, Finder does not cause chaos or mischief with his powers. However, he is a bit competitive as shown when he and Stitch argued over which direction to go while tracking down an escaped Hämsterviel, and gave a huge grin when Lilo favored his advice over Stitch's. Aside from this, Finder appears to be very calm and collected when finding lost individuals or items.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Finder is a red aardvark/shrew-like experiment with little arms and legs, a small, stumpy tail, a long snout, a dark red nose, a little mouth, black eyes, and large rabbit-like ears.

===Special abilities===
Finder can quickly track down any missing individual or thing by using his elongated snout and sense of smell. He is capable of flight by spinning his ears like helicopter blades, a last-minute addition that [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] implemented into Finder's design in order to ensure optimal tracking potential. Upon success, he honks like a party blower.

Based on Finder crossing out "Lost" on the "Lost and Found" sign, he apparently has some sort of knowledge of written languages.

==Trivia==
*Finder is Experiment 158; his correct number was shown on the Experiment Tracker mini-poster included with DVD and VHS copies of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'', as well as in the experiments list seen in the end credits of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''. 
**However, in [[Finder (episode)|his debut]], he is [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|erroneously called 458]], most likely due to Jumba's untidy [[Jumba's Computer|database]], but in "[[Skip (episode)|Skip]]", he is correctly referred to as 158.
**If Finder maintained the number he was originally referred to as canon, he would have been the only 4-series experiment to have been featured in ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''.
*Finder was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Finder's left ear is inconsistent in his appearances. While he is portrayed as having a notch on the outer rim of his upper right ear (similar to Stitch), his left ear is drawn either with or without a notch around the same relative spot between scenes.
*Finder is the only experiment to have appeared in ''[[Stitch Jam]]'', but not in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime itself.
*Finder's ears appear in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.

'''Forehead''', also known as '''Experiment 044''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to sing barbershop tunes annoyingly off-key. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "[[:Category:Mrs. Hasagawa's experiments|cats]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 044 was the 44th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to agonize his victims with annoying off-key barbershop tunes. 044 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]]. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 044's pod being one of them.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 044's pod for an apricot and washed it, activating the experiment. However, as 044 was not a very evil or destructive experiment, he was able to live a peaceful life with her, due to the latter seeing the former as a mere stray cat who needed a home.

When [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] discovered that Mrs. Hasagawa kept several experiments as pets, they thought they were a danger to her and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], decided to capture them all. When Stitch ran by, 044 grabbed him and started singing barbershop style music off-key, while also explaining that this was his primary function, though Stitch eventually managed to break free. 044 was then [[Prison Capsule|captured]] by unknown means.

044 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 044 was then named Forehead.

In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Forehead was oddly seen as one of the captive experiments in [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison cell]], although he is barely seen, suggesting [[Gantu]] caught Forehead, but this was an error. Forehead was then sent back to Gantu after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused mischief and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Forehead was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 564 instead of 044.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Forehead, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Forehead participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did. He probably agonized Leroys with his off-key barbershop singing.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. Forehead can be seen in the audience cheering.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Forehead is a pink, four-headed mustachioed experiment with white markings on each head and his chest and stomach, four arms and four red bow ties on his necks. Even though Forehead is a single entity, it is unconfirmed whether or not each of his heads possesses its own consciousness. However, it is worth mentioning that Forehead refers to himself in third person as "we", not "I" or "me", hinting that each head may indeed have its own consciousness.

===Special abilities===
Forehead can [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]] and sing barbershop songs off-key by singing out of tune.

==Trivia==

*Forehead's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green.

'''Frenchfry''', also known as '''Experiment 062''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to be Jumba's personal chef and prepare delectable, irresistible meals but had a flaw in his programming that caused him to remove all nutrition from his cooking, while those who ate his food would bloat up rapidly, after which he would eat them. If the victim managed to escape, the bloating would wear off after 24 hours. His one true place is running a healthy [[French Fry's|French fry hut]] and making delicious low-fat food, but his actions have promoted him to a restaurant chef.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 062 was the 62nd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to be Jumba's personal chef, but instead made unhealthy food that quickly made individuals fat and overweight, then ate the fattened victims. Presumably, when the food fattened Jumba up to a massive enough size, 062 tried to eat him, but Jumba was able to deactivate him in time. 062 and the other first 624 experiments were later smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 062's pod was found by Jumba and kept hidden away.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Frenchfry - Frenchfry after activation.png|thumb|left|Frenchfry after activation]]
After [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] began restricting [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]'s diet to healthy food, she told [[Pleakley]] to feed them the nutritious meals she left in the freezer before heading to work. However, Lilo, Stitch and Pleakley defied Nani and found 062's pod in a drawer while searching [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s room for a stash of junk food.

When Lilo and Stitch discovered what 062 was created to do, they activated the latter and asked him to make them junk food. 062, named Frenchfry by Lilo, complied but secretly designed the food to fatten Lilo, Stitch and Pleakley up while still being irresistibly delicious, which would culminate in him eating them.

After a while, Lilo grew suspicious of their abnormal bloating, so she and Stitch tried to learn more about Frenchfry on [[Jumba's Computer|Jumba's computer]], although none of its data was helpful to them whatsoever. Frenchfry then distracted the two with a tray of doughnuts, fattening them up even more.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Frenchfry - Frenchfry fattening up Lilo and Stitch with doughnuts.png|thumb|Fattening up Lilo and Stitch]]
[[Gantu]] managed to [[Prison Capsule|capture]] Frenchfry at one point by imitating a "trog call" to lure him out of the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]]. However, after taking a beating from a bloated Lilo and Stitch, Gantu proclaimed that it was his birthday (although he denied this earlier when [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] mentioned it). Frenchfry then made Gantu a cake that he devoured, which fattened him up and caused him to flee in shock.

While Frenchfry continued to make Lilo, Stitch and Pleakley more bloating food, Lilo called Jumba at a public event to find out more about the chef experiment. However, Jumba just barely finished revealing Frenchfry's true intentions when the latter cut the phone line with a pair of pliers.

Lilo and Stitch finally became so bloated from all the unhealthy food that Frenchfry restrained them and attempted to eat them. Before he could do so, Nani, who had heard from Jumba while at work, promptly arrived home and battled and defeated Frenchfry, eventually trapping him under Lilo's wading pool.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch - The Series - Frenchfry - Frenchfry working at French Fry's serving tofu fries.jpg|thumb|left|Frenchfry's one true place]]
The next morning, Lilo and Stitch (back to their trim selves) discovered that Frenchfry had taken a liking to Nani's oatmeal, which Lilo and Stitch initially refused to eat until Nani cleverly enticed them. Thus, they agreed to feed him oatmeal, and in return, he vowed to make healthy meals and not try to eat people.

Frenchfry shortly after found his one true place running a healthy [[French Fry's|French fry hut]], where he made delicious low-fat food.

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Frenchfry was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream.

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Frenchfry was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 558 instead of 062.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
Frenchfry was seen early in the movie giving [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] some low-fat French fries as she was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to make sure all the experiments were happy in the one true place they belonged.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Frenchfry, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Frenchfry participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by transfixing and hitting Leroys with his spatula.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Frenchfry made [[Hämsterviel's Epic Secret|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Squeak (110)|Squeak]], [[Pix (214)|Pix]], [[Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Houdini (604)|Houdini]] after [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] kicked them out for being considered useless. It is shown that Frenchfry's junk food causes individuals to inflate like balloons, rather than gain weight. Unlike his appearance in [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]], he doesn't appear to be motivated to eat others. He is also more easily convinced to make just low-calorie food that won't cause such inflation. He then shortly after gets hired at a restaurant to work as a chef. He also appeared in the specials ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]'' and ''[[Stitch! Perfect Memory]]''.

==Personality==
Frenchfry initially enjoyed causing chaos and mischief through his gourmet cooking. Ironically, however, this was not his intentional programming when he was instead to simply be Jumba's personal chef. He enjoys making food and being complimented for it, appearing friendly and helpful. However, he is actually sneaky and conniving, as he plans on eating the victims he feeds by constantly bombarding them with food, even when they try to restrain themselves, knowing they can't resist his food. After being captured by Nani and enjoying her oatmeal, he decides to eat healthily and no longer has the desire to eat individuals, but still retains his love of cooking. He is also seen to be quite talkative, as he tends to speak French with a heavy accent.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Frenchfry is a small, blue/grey-and-white, mustached experiment with four arms with three fingers on each hand, black eyes, a red round nose, a little mouth, short ears, a chef's hat, and a spatula for a tail.

===Special abilities===
Frenchfry can move at lightning speeds, allowing him to whip up massive meals in seconds by using any kind of food products. He is an expert chef in almost any form of food, and anything he makes is irresistible and delectable. He has a glitch, though; the delicious food he makes has no nutritional value, resulting in empty calories and people never getting full. Thus, his food only fattens his victims up, and when they are big enough, he will eat them. He is also capable of turning into a miniature tornado to move around, prepare food, or throw objects around. He is skilled with any and every cooking utensil, and can turn any tool into a weapon.

Frenchfry is the only experiment that speaks French, most likely a mixture between Parisian and Cajun.

===Weaknesses===
Frenchfry's bloating effects last only 24 hours. Also, if he eats nutritious food, he will make healthy food and no longer try to eat people.

==Trivia==
*Frenchfry's primary function to feed and fatten his victims so he can eat them is similar to that of [[disney:Witch (Babes in the Woods)|the witch]] from the fairy tale ''[[wikipedia:Hansel and Gretel|Hansel and Gretel]]''.
*Frenchfry is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to.
**He is also one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to.
*Frenchfry is one of the only four known experiments that wears a hat, the other three being [[Slick (020)|Slick]], [[Squeak (110)|Squeak]], and [[Derrick (566)|Derrick]]. However, Frenchfry's "hat" appears to be a part of his head, while Slick is wearing a true hat that he can remove, and it is presumed Squeak can take off his hat since he appears with a fresh hat in [[Leroy & Stitch|the TV film finale]] after an earlier incident with the Evil-liminator, while it is unknown if Derrick can remove his hat or not.
*Frenchfry can speak fluent French (roughly a mixture between Parisian and Cajun), despite the fact that Jumba had never been to Earth until after Stitch was created.
**He and [[Carmen (123)|Carmen]] are the only two known experiments who natively speak an Earth-based language other than English, with him being the only known Francophone (French-speaking) experiment. That said, he can also [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluent English]], as he says "More?" and "Yeah!" in [[Frenchfry (episode)|his debut episode]] and speaks a few more English lines in [[Hämsterviel's Epic Secret|his anime debut]] in the English dub of ''[[Stitch!]]'' as well.
*The stereotypical French songs that Frenchfry sings in gibberish when he prepares to cook and eat Lilo and Stitch outside the house are the [[wikipedia:Can-can|can-can]] dance from the comic opera ''[[wikipedia:Orpheus in the Underworld|Orpheus in the Underworld]]'' and the French nursery rhyme "[[wikipedia:Frère Jacques|Frère Jacques]]".
*Frenchfry is the first and only known experiment that Nani caught.
*He is also one of the six known experiments to be rehabilitated by someone other than Lilo and Stitch, the other five being [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Elastico (345)|Elastico]], [[Yaarp (613)|Yaarp]], [[Spike (319)|Spike]], and [[Snooty (277)|Snooty]]. 
**Frenchfry, in particular, was rehabilitated by Nani.
*Frenchfry's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is white.
*Frenchfry is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''Leroy & Stitch''.
*According to [[disney:Jess Winfield|Jess Winfield]], Frenchfry was originally going to be named "Lardo" at one point. His original name, "Lardo", is named after a kind of processed meat made out of pork backfat cured with spices such as peppercorns, oregano, garlic, or star anise — and aged anywhere from a couple of months to several years.<ref name="WinfieldTVTome">{{cite web|url=http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|title=L&S Says Mahalo|website=[[wikipedia:TV.com|TV Tome]]|date=December 14, 2004|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305082355/http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|archivedate=March 19, 2016|accessdate=May 27, 2018}}</ref>

'''Fudgy''', also known as '''Experiment 054''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to drown individuals in his sticky, chocolaty sweetness. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 054 was the 54th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to drown individuals by smothering them in his sweet, sticky chocolate. 054 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
054's pod eventually made its way to a grocery store.

In "[[Houdini (episode)|Houdini]]", [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]], while shopping for groceries, discovered the experiment pod (which he mistook for 611's pod) and brought it back to [[Gantu]] who selfishly took all the credit for it, much to Reuben's anger. Gantu then sent the pod to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], who activated it and got smothered in 054's chocolate. Reuben raved about Gantu's karma, only to get punched by the ex-captain.

054, named Fudgy, reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], and several other experiments in a rescue mission.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Fudgy, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

It is unknown whether or not Fudgy participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Fudgy made [[Chocolate Stitch|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] [[Transmutation|used]] him to invade a chocolate factory. The plan was to turn [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] into chocolate and have Fudgy eat him, thus imprisoning Stitch in his chocolaty stomach-prison. However, the factory starts going haywire and covers [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and company in chocolate. In a feeding frenzy, Fudgy swallows them all. Luckily, Hämsterviel didn't alter Fudgy's fail-safe. Stitch covers himself in chocolate to force Fudgy to eat him so he can infiltrate Fudgy's stomach-prison. Stitch and friends are able to stop Fudgy by expressing their love for each other, causing Fudgy to melt apart and free everyone. After Fudgy is neutralized, he reverts to his smaller size before being captured by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]]. Fudgy was presumably reverted back to normal, then dehydrated back into an experiment pod and stored in Jumba's vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help Stitch in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Fudgy wasn't one of the experiments that was activated.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Fudgy resembles a small blob of chocolate with two antennae, black eyes and a thin mouth. His body is mostly comprised of chocolate. Though his exterior is dripping and melting, his stomach appears to be a solid structure completely made of hardened chocolate.

===Special abilities===
Fudgy can manipulate his body mass to smother a target in his chocolate. He also becomes drawn to chocolate and can increase in size as he consumes more chocolate, but he has only displayed this while [[Transmutation|under the effects]] of [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. Fudgy is capable of imprisoning his victims in his chocolaty stomach-prison, and the chocolate he recently ingested piles up in the center of his stomach. He can also expand and contract the walls of his stomach at will.

===Weaknesses===
In order to prevent Fudgy from becoming too overwhelming, Jumba created a fail-safe to disarm his own creation. Fudgy's fail-safe is triggered by corny sentimentality, which he has a soft spot for. His heart can literally be melted by expressions of love. Once his heart melts, he breaks apart, freeing his victims, and returns to his normal size.

==Trivia==
*Fudgy is Experiment 054. However, in [[Houdini (episode)|his debut]], his [[Experiment Pods|pod]] [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|is labeled 119 and also mistaken for Experiment 611]] ([[Experiments#Battlefield and doomsday experiments with galactic implications|El Fin]]), most likely due to Jumba's untidy [[Jumba's Computer|database]].
**An ironic coincidence in Fudgy being confused for another experiment because his pod was inverted is that Experiment 119's code name is [[Experiments#1-Series: Civic disturbances|Inverto]].
**Even though we saw Fudgy in pod form, he was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
**Additionally, even though Fudgy technically debuted in the [[:Category:Season 1 Experiments|first season]], we do not see him fully until "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]" near the [[:Category:Season 2 Experiments|end of the second season]].
*Fudgy and [[Coco (052)|Coco]] are the only known experiments with primary functions directly involving chocolate, and both of their names relate to chocolate as well. Interestingly, their numbers are close together.
*Fudgy, [[Phantasmo (375)|Phantasmo]], [[Remmy (276)|Remmy]], [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Witch (610)|Witch]] are the only known experiments to have arms but no legs.
*Fudgy's pod color is blue in [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]]. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, it is red.
*Fudgy was possibly mentioned in "[[Skip (episode)|Skip]]" by [[Gantu]] as a brown one, when he was telling [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] which experiments he caught.
*Fudgy is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.
*He is also one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
*In the anime, Fudgy is seen with the ability to grow larger from eating chocolate, similar to [[Tank (586)|Tank]]'s ability to grow larger from eating metal and [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]]'s ability to grow larger from eating garbage.

'''Gigi''', also known as '''Experiment 007''' and '''Yapper''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. She is designed to sit, lie down, fetch, and annoy Jumba's neighbors with her shrill bark. Her one true place is with [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] as her pet.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 007 was the seventh genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. She was designed to behave like a typical "good dog" and annoy Jumba's neighbors with her constant yapping. 007 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Yapper - Gigi yapping loudly at Stitch.png|thumb|left|Gigi barking at Stitch]]
At an unknown point, Experiment 007 was activated and then later adopted by [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]], who named her Gigi.

In "[[Yapper]]", Mertle showed Gigi off to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], and then revealed that she was entering her in a [[Junior Dog Show|dog show]] contest in Honolulu. However, when Gigi's loud, shrill yapping began to annoy Stitch, the latter swallowed her whole. Mertle screamed in horror until Lilo pulled Gigi out of Stitch's stomach and gave her back. Enraged, Mertle called Lilo and Stitch "riffraff" and took Gigi, now covered in slobber, to a pet salon to get her cleaned up.

Believing she could win Mertle's friendship by beating her Gigi, Lilo traveled via limousine to Honolulu with Stitch, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]]. There, she entered Stitch in the same dog show, claiming he was a rare "blue-furred ectoplasmic detection dog" to impress [[Mitzi Suzuki and Kato Stewart|the judges]].

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Yapper - Gigi competing in the dog show.png|thumb|Gigi competing in the dog show]]
After engaging in an unfriendly rivalry, Lilo and Mertle entered Stitch and Gigi into all the competitions, and the contest took place the next day. However, both Stitch's temper (when he fought with a contestant's dog after the latter sniffed him) and overconfidence caused him to lose the first two rounds. In the final competition, Mertle secretly gave Stitch extra strong coffee to make the latter go crazy so that Gigi would win.

Mertle's plan was successful at first until [[Gantu]] suddenly burst into the arena searching for her "dog". Stitch impulsively attacked Gantu, who fired his [[Plasma Blaster|plasma gun]] uncontrollably, but a stray plasma blast caused the ceiling to collapse on top of Stitch. Gantu then took Gigi from a terrified Mertle, after which she complained to Lilo.

Because Gigi was Stitch's cousin, Lilo promised to save her from Gantu. She then gave Stitch more coffee intentionally, thus enabling the latter to defeat Gantu and get Gigi back safe and sound.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Yapper - Gigi with Mertle.png|thumb|left|Gigi with Mertle]]
Grateful but indignant, Mertle gave the "Best in Show" trophy to Lilo. However, when Lilo saw how much Mertle truly cared for Gigi, the former decided to leave Gigi with Mertle.

Gigi reappeared in "[[Amnesio (episode)|Amnesio]]", being accompanied by Mertle and [[Elena|the]] [[Teresa|hula]] [[Yuki|girls]] while Lilo attempted to invite them to her birthday party.

In "[[PJ (episode)|PJ]]", Gigi and a few regular dogs attacked Lilo's substitute teacher who wore squeaky shoes shaped like dog biscuits, which was one of [[PJ (133)|PJ]]'s many pranks.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
Gigi was seen being walked by [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]], the latter stopping to taunt [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] before moving on.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Gigi along with Mertle, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

During the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], Mertle was seen running with Gigi in her arms, trying to avoid attacking Leroys. When Mertle and Gigi were both saved from a Leroy clone by [[Clip (177)|Clip]], Gigi revealed her ability to speak (surprising Mertle) and her status as an experiment, then pushed Mertle out of the way of another Leroy clone's plasma blast.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

Following the battle, Gigi declared that she wanted to be part of Lilo's ''ʻohana'', convincing Mertle to join it with Gigi.

==Personality==
While Gigi fulfills the purpose she was programmed for, which was to annoy individuals with her constant barking, this is not a defining feature or quality of herself. Most of the time, she is well-behaved and appears to look and act like a normal dog: barking, fetching, and listening to orders. She can be distinguished from a real dog by her ability to talk. She is quite affectionate to those she likes, licking Mertle's face and complimenting Clip on cutting a Leroy clone's fur off. She is also loyal and brave, pushing Mertle out of the way of a plasma blast. She holds the ideal of family and ''ʻohana'' very close, having convinced Mertle (albeit somewhat reluctantly) to join Lilo's ''ʻohana'' because she wanted to be in it as well, and seems to get along well with her cousins.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Gigi is a quadrupedal, white Shih Tzu-like experiment with a purple bow, solid black eyes, and a little black nose. Jumba, however, mentions that she is hard to recognize after "so many groomings and much ribbons," implying that her natural appearance is somewhat different, which may also explain why she looks less alien-like than most of the other known experiments.

===Special abilities===
Gigi has an annoying shrill bark and the typical abilities of a common dog, such as sitting, fetching, and licking her owner's face. She also [[:Category:Talking experiments|speaks exceptionally well]] as seen in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.

===Weaknesses===
Gigi is mostly defenseless.

==Trivia==
*Gigi was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Gigi was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Gigi, along with [[Dorkifier (122)|Dorkifier]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], [[Butter (227)|Butter]], [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]], [[Spike (319)|Spike]], [[Yang (502)|Yang]], [[Richter (513)|Richter]], [[Phoon (540)|Phoon]], [[Tank (586)|Tank]], [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]], and one [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed experiment]], are the only known experiments that are primarily quadrupeds.
*Gigi is one of the ten known experiments named by someone other than Lilo or Stitch, the other nine being [[Elastico (345)|Elastico]], [[Yaarp (613)|Yaarp]], [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]], [[Heat (609)|Heat]], [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]], [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]], [[Morpholomew (316)|Morpholomew]], [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]], and [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]]. 
**Gigi, in particular, was named by Mertle.
**Lilo did give a name for 007, namely "Yapper". However, since 007's one true place is being Mertle's "dog", Lilo has accepted her true name as "Gigi", the name Mertle gave her.
**Her episode is named "[[Yapper]]" after the nickname Lilo gave her, but "Gigi", the name Mertle gave her, is her official name on the experiments list in the [[Experiments/Gallery#Leroy & Stitch|end credits]] of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
*She is also one of the six known experiments to be rehabilitated by someone other than Lilo and Stitch, the other five being Elastico, Yaarp, Spike, [[Frenchfry (062)|Frenchfry]], and [[Snooty (277)|Snooty]]. 
**Gigi, in particular, was rehabilitated by Mertle.
*Her number is a reference to the code number of the legendary [[wikipedia:James Bond (literary character)|James Bond]]. This could very well be a coincidence, though Gigi does share one similarity with James Bond: she is an alien undercover as a dog.
*Gigi's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] appeared among a bunch of other blue pods on [[Gantu]]'s [[Gantu's Ship|messy ship]] in the episode "[[627 (episode)|627]]".
*Gigi never spoke in ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''. However, during the climax of ''Leroy & Stitch'', it is revealed that she can [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]] very well and says to [[Clip (177)|Clip]], "Nice one, cousin," after seeing Clip cut a [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clone]]'s fur off. She then says to Mertle, "Look out!" and pushes her out of the way of another Leroy clone's plasma blast.
*Mertle adopting Gigi at the [[Aloha Animal Rescue|animal shelter]] mirrors the relationship between Lilo and Stitch, as Mertle didn't know Gigi was a genetic experiment until she found out in ''Leroy & Stitch''.
*In some recent book releases, like ''Manners Matter, Stitch'' and ''Stitch Goes to School'', Gigi is replaced by a poodle named Cashmere.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kInI3WULCJE YouTube - Read-Aloud: Manners Matter, Stitch]</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phwmbCSoK2o YouTube - Stitch Goes to School - Children's Book Read Aloud]</ref>
