==Background and appearances==
Experiment 223 was the 223rd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to invade technology like a computer virus and cause it to turn on its owners. 223 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Glitch - Glitch after activation.png|thumb|left|Glitch after being activated]]
223's pod eventually made its way to a baseball pitching machine, where it was used as a softball.

When the pitching machine started to go out of control, the experiment pod was batted away by [[Slugger (608)|Slugger]] and flung onto the Lick-o'-Matic (one of [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s inventions) at the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]]. The Lick-o'-Matic, mistaking the pod for a stamp, licked it, activating 223.

223 then took over the Lick-o'-Matic and caused it to throw tomatoes at [[Pleakley]]. Shortly after, 223 passed through the house's power lines and into the main computer, from where he took over all of the house's technology that Jumba had built earlier when he was upgrading their home.

Before long, 223 locked the entire house down, trapping the residents whom he picked off one by one, but not before the five split up to investigate the source of the problem.

When Jumba discovered that 223 had taken over the house's main computer and tried to reason with the latter, 223 locked the former in the bedroom, then later trapped [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] in the attic and Pleakley under the couch.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Glitch - Glitch captured in Lilo's portable game console.png|thumb|Glitch captured]]
223 targeted [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] next by blowing them away with a ceiling fan and nearly putting Lilo in the dryer after her butt got caught in the vacuum cleaner. However, they were able to download 223, named Glitch, out of the computer system and into Lilo's portable video game console, thus trapping him in his one true place.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
At an unknown point, Lilo released Glitch from her handheld video game console.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Glitch, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Glitch participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Personality==
Glitch is a conniving experiment, reveling in wreaking havoc through technology and causing it to turn on its owners. He is fairly intelligent, preferring to get rid of his victims one by one. However, after being removed from the technology he once controlled and trapped in a video game, he has since grown to like being part of it, as he can now battle opponents and make games harder to win.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Glitch is a bright green experiment that appears to be comprised of sentient energy surrounded by yellow light. He has a round torso, pudgy arms and legs, a large round hourglass-shaped head with a wide mouth, round blue nose, dark blue eyes, a small blue arrow-shaped mark above his face, and two thin antennae with green tips. His overall appearance resembles a cross between [[Morpholomew (316)|Morpholomew]] and [[Poxy (222)|Poxy]].

===Special abilities===
Glitch's body seems to be electron-based, and he possesses technopathy abilities. He can therefore convert and morph himself into a machine's wires and circuitry. He can then overload the main control system of the machine and take over, acting like a computer virus. He can turn technology against owners by entering the instrument and controlling it. Glitch has technopathic hacking skills and is able to teleport from place to place in the blink of an eye. He can jump high and curl into a ball. He is able to invade any computer-based devices (PC, smartphone, car entertainment system, cell phone, etc.).

===Weaknesses===
It appears as if when Glitch is intentionally placed or "downloaded" into a machine, he really has no control and becomes a part of it, referring to when Lilo trapped him in her portable game console.

==Trivia==
*Glitch is named after a problem of technologies (e.g. computers or video games), which is also known as "bugs".
*Glitch is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having dark blue eyes instead.
*Glitch is the second known experiment with a primary function involving electronic devices. The first was [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]], who shorts out and breaks technology.
*Glitch, [[Phantasmo (375)|Phantasmo]], and [[Witch (610)|Witch]] are all capable of possession, albeit in different capacities: Glitch possesses technology, Phantasmo can possess any inanimate object, and Witch can possess living beings.
*Glitch is one of two known experiments whose [[Experiment Pods|pod]] got mixed up with some softballs, the other being [[Slugger (608)|Slugger]].
*Glitch's pod color is green.
*Glitch is one of two known experiments that lives with Lilo and Stitch, the other being [[Belle (248)|Belle]].

'''Gotchu''', also known as '''Experiment 031''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to run around and pinch individuals. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "[[:Category:Mrs. Hasagawa's experiments|cats]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 031 was the 31st genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to pinch individuals. 031 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]]. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 031's pod being one of them.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 031's pod for an apricot and placed it in a colander for later consumption along with numerous other pods.

After [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] redecorated Mrs. Hasagawa's yard without her permission, she was less than thrilled with the results, but decided to thank them for their work with the "apricots". The pods were then revealed, but before Lilo and Stitch could stop her, she washed them with a watering can, thus activating the experiments.

After his activation, 031 began to carry out his primary function by pinching Lilo and exclaiming, "Got you!" Lilo and Stitch believed the experiments to be a danger to Mrs. Hasagawa and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], decided to capture them all. Eventually, Stitch wrestled with 031, the former winning, and forcing the latter into a [[Prison Capsule|container]].

031 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 031 was then named Gotchu.

In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Gotchu was oddly seen as one of the captive experiments in [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison cell]], although he is barely seen behind [[Fibber (032)|Fibber]], suggesting [[Gantu]] caught Gotchu, but this was an error. Gotchu was then sent back to Gantu after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused mischief and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Gotchu was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 586 instead of 031.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Gotchu, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Gotchu participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by chasing and pinching Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Gotchu is an orange lobster-like experiment with black eyes, a purple nose, a red belly and four arms with pincers.

===Special abilities===
Gotchu can use his four pincers to pinch individuals hard. He says, "Got you!" when he pinches.

==Trivia==
*Gotchu was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Gotchu, [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]], [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]], [[Clink (086)|Clink]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have claws/pincers. Interestingly, all four official experiments have characteristics similar to crustaceans.
*According to Mrs. Hasagawa, Gotchu has a special neck pillow.
*In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Gotchu erroneously appeared with Gantu's other captive experiments, although he is barely seen, but he was already living with Mrs. Hasagawa, and Lilo and Stitch discovered him while Gantu was asleep.
*Gotchu is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.

'''Hammerface''', also known as '''Experiment 033''' and '''Hammerhead''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to hammer nails around Jumba's house, but he will sometimes pound living things. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 033 was the 33rd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to drive nails around Jumba's house, but he could hammer living organisms as well. 033 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Dupe - Hammerface being duplicated.png|thumb|left|Hammerface being duplicated]]
033's pod eventually made its way to a junk shop, where it (along with [[Heat (609)|609]], [[Thresher (544)|544]] and [[Plasmoid (617)|617]]) was found, stolen, activated, and named Hammerface by [[Gantu]] in "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]".

Back at [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]], Gantu trained and conditioned Hammerface, Heat, Thresher and Plasmoid by simply using [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] for target practice, much to his indignity and chagrin. The four henchmen experiments were then led by Gantu in an attack on the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]], where their boss ordered them to defeat and capture [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and his duplicates after seeing that he had been split into four.

Hammerface engaged one of the clones in a duel. The clone rolled into a ball and slammed into Hammerface, knocking the latter toward the wall, which he clung to. He then jumped onto the floor and ended the fight by slamming his hammer-like head on the opposite end of the floorboard the clone was on, catapulting him into Gantu's awaiting [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]].

After capturing Stitch and his clones, the five returned to Gantu's ship for a victory feast (courtesy of Reuben), but were interrupted by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Pleakley]] and [[Dupe (344)|Dupe]]. When Lilo tricked Gantu into using Dupe's cloning ability, Gantu used Dupe to clone Hammerface into a hundred replicas. However, as the original Hammerface's power was divided among them, they all became complete weaklings, and thus were easily defeated.

Presumably after this, they were all sent to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] who was somehow able to remerge the weakling Hammerface clones into the original.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - The Asteroid - Sparky shocking Hammerface as a prank.png|thumb|Hammerface being shocked by Sparky]]
In "[[The Asteroid]]", Hammerface was one of the six experiments that Stitch convinced to come with him and Lilo to save Earth from an approaching asteroid. Along the journey, [[Sparky (221)|Sparky]] teased Hammerface by shocking him, angering the latter. Later, the hammer-headed experiment started hitting [[Kixx (601)|Kixx]] on the head, only to be ordered otherwise by Pleakley (who referred to him as "Hammerhead" instead of "Hammerface").

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Hammerface was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream.

In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Hammerface was sent back to Gantu along with all of Hämsterviel's other captive experiments after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused chaos and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

Hammerface reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by Lilo, Stitch, and several other experiments in a rescue mission.

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Hammerface was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 525 instead of 033.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Hammerface, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Hammerface participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Hammerface made [[Link-age|an appearance]] in Season 2 of the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Spike (319)|Spike]], [[Woody (507)|Woody]], [[Link (251)|Link]], and [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]]. It is revealed that [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] reverted these experiments to evil using a recording of [[Angel (624)|Angel]]'s song, thus enabling them to wreak havoc on the [[Izayoi Island|island]].

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Hammerface is a blue-grey dinosaur-like experiment with a hammer-shaped head/face, short forearms, small black eyes, and a thick tail and legs. He has claws all over his limbs and very sharp teeth.

===Special abilities===
Hammerface can drive nails into virtually any substance with his hammer-shaped head/face, but his strength allows him to pound living organisms. He also has some of the basic experiment attributes, including the substance on his hands and feet which allow him to scale walls. His tail is occasionally used as an extra support, a third leg.

===Weaknesses===
Like other experiments, when Hammerface is divided by [[Dupe (344)|Dupe]] into a hundred replicas, each one will be virtually harmless.

==Trivia==
*Hammerface is one of the ten known experiments named by someone other than Lilo or Stitch, the other nine being [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Elastico (345)|Elastico]], [[Yaarp (613)|Yaarp]], [[Heat (609)|Heat]], [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]], [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]], [[Morpholomew (316)|Morpholomew]], [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]], and [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]]. 
**Hammerface (alongside Heat, Thresher, and Plasmoid) was named by Gantu.
*Hammerface is Experiment 033. However, in ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'', he is [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|erroneously called 124]], most likely due to Jumba's untidy [[Jumba's Computer|database]].
*In "[[The Asteroid]]", Pleakley referred to Hammerface as "Hammerhead". Presumably because his head is indeed shaped like a hammer.
**Additionally, Hammerface was seen already activated, but because this episode was out of chronological order, he wasn't officially activated until the episode "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]" aired.
*Even though we saw Hammerface in [[Experiment Pods|pod]] form, he was technically [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Hammerface is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.
*In the English dub of the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime episode "[[Link-age]]", [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] states that Hammerface's favorite type of sandwich is ham on flatbread.
**Additionally, his number is mistaken for 032, which belongs to [[Fibber (032)|Fibber]].

'''Heckler''', also known as '''Experiment 322''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to undermine enemy morale with verbal abuse. His one true place is in a dunk tank, provoking people to try and dunk him.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 322 was the 322nd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to crush his victims' pride and self-confidence with verbal insults. 322 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Heckler - Are you pretending to be a cop.png|thumb|left|"What's with that uniform, are you pretending to be a cop?"]]
Experiment 322 was activated off-screen at the [[Birds of Paradise Hotel]], where he managed to impress a crowd of tourists by insulting the tour guide's hair and shirt, earning 322 a round of applause from the crowd.

322 was later chased around [[Kokaua Town|town]] by [[Gantu]], but the former was able to stay ahead by repeatedly insulting Gantu until 322 was soon rescued by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. When 322 antagonized Stitch, the latter attempted to beat him up, only to be stopped by Lilo, who considered 322 to be somewhat useful.

Lilo then brought 322, whom she named Heckler, to [[Mertle's House|Mertle's house]] as revenge, where Heckler insulted [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]]'s hair and glasses, much to Lilo and Stitch's humor.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Heckler - I've seen nicer cardboard boxes on Skid Row.png|thumb|"I've seen nicer cardboard boxes on Skid Row."]]
Lilo and Stitch shortly after took Heckler back to their [[Lilo's House|house]], where he insulted their dwelling and later both [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] and [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]. When Jumba tried to silence Heckler by stuffing Stitch into his mouth, the latter spat Stitch out and insulted how he tasted, which led to them tussling on the floor. Nani rejected Heckler's presence and requested Lilo to keep him out of sight until after the charity event that Nani was hosting.

Later, Lilo and Stitch looked to Heckler for guidance for [[Pleakley]]'s stand-up comedy at Nani's charity event, and Heckler convinced them to give the audience rotten tomatoes to throw at Pleakley's rotten jokes. Although uncertain, Lilo and Stitch took Heckler's advice (unaware that he was leading them astray).

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Heckler - I've seen better digs in my vegetable garden.png|thumb|left|"I've seen better digs in my vegetable garden."]]
At Nani's charity event, Heckler's insults towards the staff caused all of them to quit. When Nani then demanded Lilo to get rid of Heckler, the latter insulted Lilo's voice and nose before attempting to escape. Gantu then barged in for Heckler, but since Nani, Lilo and Stitch were sick of Heckler's verbal abuse, they gladly handed him over.

Gantu took Heckler back to [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]], where he prepared to transport the latter to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. However, Heckler's insults towards Hämsterviel ultimately prompted him to order Gantu to release Heckler.

Thus, Heckler returned to Nani's charity event, where he was soon chased by Stitch. While being pursued, Heckler caused massive chaos at the dining tables by kicking and throwing food at people, including Nani.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Heckler - You throw like a little girl.png|thumb|"You throw like a little girl!"]]
Heckler then threw a rotten tomato at one of Pleakley's bad jokes and went onstage to insult him in front of everyone. At that moment, however, Pleakley and Lilo (as well as the entire audience) accepted that Heckler's insults towards them were true, leaving him defeated and sobbing on the stage.

After Lilo managed to console Heckler, she found his one true place in a dunk tank, where he provoked people to try and dunk him, especially a vengeful Mertle.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Heckler, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Heckler participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Personality==
Although Heckler acts like a jerk most of the time, he really just seems to insult out of impulse. He cannot help but make fun of others, but has been proven to be willing to help individuals, especially when it comes to insult comedy. Most of the time, he does not entirely intend to offend others, but it is in his programming, and he cannot help but throw around a few insults. If not, he breaks down into a fit of self-pity, as he has never had any other purpose. He proved to be so annoying that even Hämsterviel, who usually wanted all of Jumba's experiments, didn't want him.

Heckler has the ability to be kind-hearted, but just has a very strange way of showing it. He loves his job being in the dunk tank and encouraging individuals to try to dunk him for charity, smiling good-naturedly right before Mertle dunked him. When he insults someone, it can be hard to tell if it is out of reflex, just teasing, or actually trying to be hurtful.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Heckler is an orange experiment that resembles a cross between [[Reuben (625)|625]] and [[627]], with short pointed ears, small beady eyes, an oval nose, a wide mouth with large fangs, and a shirt and bow tie imprint on his body. His head also has markings that resemble a balding head, with hair on the sides, much like [[wikipedia:Don Rickles|Don Rickles]]' hair as he got older.

===Special abilities===
As his name suggests, Heckler is a master heckler who can use verbal insults towards others to even defend himself against enemies. He can [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]] and is capable of making jokes about individuals' appearances and/or personalities. Heckler appears to be very agile, as he was able to easily flee from [[Gantu]] while being chased. He also seems to be super strong, as he was able to wrestle [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]].

===Weaknesses===
Heckler's verbal insults can be defused by accepting that they are true, which will leave him defeated and emotionally distraught. He also has no physical strength or powers, meaning he could be easily captured.

==Trivia==
*Heckler was possibly inspired by [[disney:Don Rickles|Don Rickles]], a comedian who was known for insulting individuals for humorous effect.
*According to Jumba, Heckler was programmed "to destroy enemy's confidence by mercilessly taunting and humiliating him," and is one of the best ideas he ever had.
*Heckler was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Heckler is one of the few known experiments that can [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]].
*The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Heckler as: "Experiment 322. Primary function: Undermine enemy morale with verbal abuse."
*Oddly, when Heckler's image is reflected off of Stitch's eyes in ''[[The Origin of Stitch]]'', he is gagged and handcuffed for some reason.
*Heckler is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.

'''Hertz Donut''', also known as '''Experiment 022''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to restrain and immobilize the target's movement with projectile donuts. First he asks, "Ever had a Hertz Donut?" He then fires energy which solidifies into a donut that constricts around the target and says, "Hurts, don't it?" He appears in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 022 was the 22nd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to shoot donuts from his mouth that can restrain the movements of his target. 022 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
[[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] gained possession of Hertz Donut under unknown circumstances and [[Transmutation|modified]] him to wreak havoc on his behalf. In the episode "[[Dorkifier (episode)|Dorkifier]]", Hämsterviel intended to send Hertz Donut to capture [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] but accidentally sent the pod for [[Dorkifier (122)|Dorkifier]] instead. After realizing his mistake, Hämsterviel finally sends Hertz Donut after [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and Stitch, who were already dealing with Dorkifier at the school. Hertz Donut only added to the chaos during a soccer match, but Stitch is able to defeat him. In "[[Shogun]]", it is shown that Hertz Donut was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Hertz Donut is a green seahorse-like experiment with bright purple eyes, a donut-like mouth, six ears, and a long curling antenna winding behind his head.

===Special abilities===
Hertz Donut can confine and restrict movement by firing donuts at a target. He has the ability to [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]] and hops instead of walks.

==Trivia==
*His name and function are a possible reference to the eponymous [[wiktionary:Hertz donut|Hertz donut]] prank.
*Hertz Donut is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having bright purple eyes instead. However, he was entirely under [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Transmutation|control]] in his appearance. Since other experiments under Hämsterviel's possession in the [[Stitch!|anime]] tend to have their eyes diluted to show irises and/or sclerae, it is unknown whether or not Hertz Donut's own purple eyes being visible is a result of Hämsterviel controlling him or if it is a natural part of his appearance.
**Ironically, [[Spooky (300)|Spooky]] (when he appears transmutated) has the same eyes as Hertz Donut.
*Hertz Donut and [[Witch (610)|Witch]] are the only two experiments that first appeared in ''Stitch!'', but were not shown in their original (un-transmutated) form and whose real eye color is unknown.
*Hertz Donut, [[Sproing (249)|Sproing]], [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]], [[Mary (455)|Mary]], and [[Cannonball (520)|Cannonball]] are the only known experiments that mostly bounce when traversing land.
*Hertz Donut is one of the few known experiments that can [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]].
*Hertz Donut's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is red.
*Hertz Donut's English dub voice isn't credited in his only appearance. However, his English voice sounds like Ben Diskin using a lower, more phlegmy-sounding version of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]'s voice.

'''Hocker''', also known as '''Experiment 051''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to spit acidic saliva that can eat through solid matter. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "[[:Category:Mrs. Hasagawa's experiments|cats]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 051 was the 51st genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to spit acid saliva. 051 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]]. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 051's pod being one of them.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 051's pod for an apricot and placed it in a colander for later consumption along with numerous other pods.

After [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] redecorated Mrs. Hasagawa's front yard without her permission, she was less than thrilled with the results, but decided to thank them for their hard work with the "apricots". The pods were then revealed, but before Lilo and Stitch could stop her, she washed them with a watering can, thus activating the experiments.

After his activation, 051 began to carry out his primary function by hocking acidic saliva at Lilo, only to miss and hit the [[Mrs. Hasagawa's House|house]] instead. Lilo and Stitch believed the experiments to be a danger to Mrs. Hasagawa and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley|Pleakley,]] decided to capture them all. 051 was then [[Prison Capsule|captured]] by unknown means.

051 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. Later, Lilo apologized to Mrs. Hasagawa while the latter was petting 051, only for the experiment to spit acid at the wall. 051 was then named Hocker.

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Hocker was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 542 instead of 051.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Hocker, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Hocker participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Hocker made a special guest appearance in the ''Stitch!'' segment "[[Kung Fu Dragon Pleak Lee]]".

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Hocker is a green experiment with a huge teal nose, a pale yellow underbelly, a violet-red spot around both eyes, and a violet-red stripe on each of his ears and tail (in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', the spots and stripes are yellow).

===Special abilities===
Hocker can spit an extremely corrosive acidic saliva that can eat through wood or other solid matter by hocking it up using his abnormally-sized nose.

==Trivia==
*In "[[Mrs. Hasagawa's Cats]]", Hocker's spots and stripes are violet-red. However, in ''[[The Origin of Stitch]]'' and ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', his spots and stripes are yellow.
*Hocker's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green.

'''Holio''', also known as '''Experiment 606''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to transform into a matter-sucking black hole that can destroy entire galaxies. His one true place is sucking up construction debris and litter.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 606 was the 606th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to create a matter-sucking black hole capable of sucking in entire planets. 606 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Holio - Holio moments after activation.png|thumb|left|Holio moments after his activation]]
606's pod eventually made its way to a jewelry maker, who attached the pod to a bracelet as a charm. An elderly vendor fashioned and sold the bracelet to [[Mrs. Edmonds]], which she bought as a birthday present for her daughter, [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]], neither one aware of what one of the trinkets attached to the bracelet actually was.

During Mertle's birthday party, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] pulled a harmless prank on Mertle and [[Elena|the]] [[Teresa|hula]] [[Yuki|girls]]. Lilo then noticed 606's pod on Mertle's bracelet and tried to take it from her, only to get in trouble with Mrs. Edmonds and [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]].

Later, Stitch went undercover as a bunny at a [[Pet Shop|pet shop]], where he inspected the pod number on Mertle's bracelet and messaged Lilo via walkie-talkie. When she looked up 606 and learned about the latter's powers, she fell into despair but got arrested for being in [[Officer Kahiko]]'s police car (though Stitch busted Lilo out).

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Holio - Holio transformed into a black hole.png|thumb|Holio's black hole]]
Despite Lilo and Stitch's best efforts to steal Mertle's bracelet, when she noticed that Lilo was desperate to stop 606's pod from getting wet, Mertle took it back to [[Mertle's House|her house]]. There, out of curiosity, she dropped the bracelet into a glass of water, getting the pod wet and activating 606. The experiment then transformed into a black hole, which began to suck up everything in Mertle's bedroom.

After a while, the hole expanded beyond Mertle's room and started sucking up the entire [[Kokaua Town|town]]. Mertle eventually telephoned Lilo to complain about the massive destruction that 606 was causing. Fortunately, Lilo and Stitch (with some of [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s assistance) were able to enter the black hole in Nani's [[X-Buggy|dune buggy]] and throw an anti-antimatter sphere into the center of the hole, causing it to begin to collapse.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Holio - Mertle demanding her dolls back from Holio.png|thumb|left|"Where's my dolls?"]]
Lilo and Stitch managed to narrowly escape the black hole, which released everything that was sucked in except for Mertle's dolls. She then demanded her dolls back from 606, who complied by releasing the countless dolls through his mouth on top of Mertle.

Shortly after, 606, named Holio, found his one true place sucking up construction debris while repairs were made to the [[Rental Hut]] that had been nearly destroyed by said black hole.

Holio was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that joined Stitch in a rebellion against [[Gantu]]. Holio even tried to suck [[Checkers (029)|Checkers]] off Gantu's head, but he instead sucked off the ex-captain's clothes, leaving him nude.

Holio was seen on a computer screen in "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]", posing as an evil creation of Jumba's as part of a hoax to fool [[Mortlegax]], the head of E.G.O. industries.

Holio was briefly seen in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", creating a black hole to suck litter off the streets.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Holio, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Holio did not participate in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], instead choosing to retreat with the weaker experiments.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe, during which Holio can be seen around some of the Leroys as they started to shut down.

==Personality==
Despite his destructive and chaotic function, Holio has an eerily calm nature when he is not active as a black hole. This is deceptive at first glance, for behind his harmless appearance belies his more chaotic abilities. When not using his powers, Holio is very compliant with demands and eager to help clean up debris as his one true place. He is also shown to be loyal and helpful to his friends, joining Stitch's rebellion to fight off Gantu.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Holio is a small red, chipmunk-like experiment with a large mouth with two teeth sticking out, a pink stomach from his chin down, no visible ears, black eyes, a dark pink nose, two thin antennae and three thin back spines.

===Special abilities===
Holio can flip into a matter-sucking black hole, which can destroy an entire galaxy, at will. Another way he can devour things is through his mouth, which can have a weaker yet similar effect as his black hole form. Also, he can gradually descend from a height.

===Weaknesses===
If an anti-antimatter sphere is thrown into the center of Holio's black hole, the hole will collapse.

==Trivia==
*Holio was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Holio is not referred to by his new name at any point in [[Holio (episode)|his debut]], but his name officially appears on the experiments list in the [[Experiments/Gallery#Leroy & Stitch|end credits]] of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
*In his debut episode, Holio has no tail, but in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]", when he and the other experiments jump ashore, he is seen with a stumpy tail.
*Holio's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue.
*In ''Leroy & Stitch'', Holio did not choose to participate in the battle between the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy army]] and the experiments, which is ironic, considering the fact that he is one of the most powerful experiments.
*Holio's head appears in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.

'''Houdini''', also known as '''Experiment 604''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to make armies and weapons invisible; unfortunately, he was gun-shy on the battlefield and always ran away and made himself invisible instead. His one true place is as a Hollywood star magician, but his actions have promoted him to a shark tank attraction, where he makes sharks disappear to amaze crowds.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 604 was the 604th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to render entire armies and weapons invisible, but due to being cowardly, he instead kept turning himself invisible and fleeing the battlefield. 604 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Houdini - Houdini after activation.png|thumb|left|Houdini after being activated]]
On a small outdoor stage, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and [[Pleakley]] rehearsed a magic act in front of [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and a few experiments for [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]]'s upcoming half birthday, but Stitch kept bungling the act with his failed tricks. When Lilo realized that Stitch was having trouble, she asked Jumba if he had any experiments that could help with Stitch's magic act. Jumba then took out 604's pod, but warned that 604 had cowardly habits.

Using a leash as a restraint, Lilo activated 604 and named him Houdini, but the craven experiment panicked and made himself invisible until Lilo pacified him. She then trained Houdini to turn things invisible upon hearing "Alakablooe" and vice versa upon hearing "Alakazoo" with a blink of his eyes.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Houdini - Houdini photographed.png|thumb|Houdini photographed]]
During Mertle's party, Houdini secretly helped Stitch out with his magic act. However, the former was eventually caught in the act by Mertle, who photographed Houdini. The camera flash spooked him, thus causing Houdini to turn Stitch and numerous other things invisible, including himself.

Before Houdini became invisible, [[Gantu]], who was looking for the experiment, spied on Stitch's magic act and spotted Houdini. However, when Gantu crashed the party in an attempt to nab Houdini, the latter escaped in fear. Mertle later visited [[Lilo's House|Lilo's house]] and condemned her for being a fraud before revealing the photo taken of Houdini.

To make matters worse, [[Mrs. Edmonds]] had booked [[Aunt Stacy|Mertle's aunt]] and her staff to witness Stitch's magic act. Lilo knew that Stitch was unable to do magic without Houdini's help. While Stitch was invisible, Lilo adorned him in different ways so that she could still see him before they searched for Houdini.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Houdini - Invisible Houdini whose footprints are visible.png|thumb|left|Invisible Houdini]]
Later, Gantu, wearing special infrared heat goggles, pursued an invisible Houdini through a jungle. However, the latter was able to slow Gantu down by turning palm trees and other obstacles invisible. Before long, Houdini bumped into an invisible Stitch. The collision caused Lilo to touch what she thought was Stitch (but was actually an invisible Houdini) and drag him into a bush with her. Thus, Gantu ended up [[Prison Capsule|capturing]] what he thought was Houdini (but was actually an invisible Stitch), which he took back to [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]].

Lilo later revealed to Jumba and Pleakley that Stitch couldn't do magic at all, and when she uttered the magic word for making things reappear, Houdini made himself visible again. Lilo then realized that Gantu must have grabbed Stitch by mistake. When Pleakley scolded Houdini, the latter turned invisible out of fright and fled.

Meanwhile, an invisible Stitch began trashing stuff inside Gantu's ship, making Gantu and [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] suspicious. The former then fired his [[Plasma Blaster|plasma gun]] repeatedly in an attempt to subdue the invisible experiment. After a brief struggle, Stitch managed to escape the ship and reunite with Lilo. Eventually, she and Stitch recaptured Houdini after a long chase.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Houdini - Houdini doing telekinesis with playing card.png|thumb|Houdini doing magic]]
While the staff booed Pleakley for stalling them with his promised magic act, Lilo and Stitch arrived with Houdini, who then made the [[Kilauea Lighthouse|old lighthouse]] disappear, much to Pleakley's relief. The crowd cheered, although when Lilo then revealed Houdini to them, the people became intrigued and began taking flash photos of the experiment, causing him to make everything on [[Kauai]] disappear.

Shortly after, Houdini found his one true place in Hollywood as a star magician.

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Houdini was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream, but he is barely seen behind [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]] and in front of [[627]].

Houdini reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", performing a magic act to a crowd by levitating a playing card using telekinesis.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Houdini, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

In the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], Houdini evaded attacking Leroys by turning himself invisible.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Houdini made [[Hämsterviel's Epic Secret|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Frenchfry (062)|Frenchfry]], [[Squeak (110)|Squeak]], [[Pix (214)|Pix]], and [[Tickle-Tummy]] after [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] kicked them out for being considered useless. Houdini also appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Unlike the initial behavior of most experiments, Houdini has no destructive nor chaotic intent; on the contrary, he is a very timid and easily frightened experiment. He is shown to be scared by almost everything, suggesting he has [[wikipedia:Panphobia|panphobia]]. He is also easily intimidated and startled by loud noises. It took a tremendous effort for him to leave show biz to help out his cousin Stitch, and even then he typically stays invisible 95% of the time.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Houdini is a slender, creamy whitish-tan rabbit-like experiment with four brown spots on each elbow and knee, light pink mark around his eyes and on his chest and stomach, dark pink stripes on his arms and legs, purple markings on his back and ear tips, a small mouth with a buck tooth sticking out, dark pink nose, huge beady black eyes and even larger ears.

===Special abilities===
Houdini can instantly render anything, including himself, invisible with a blink of his massive eyes, though he can also make them reappear by doing this. He has also been shown to have some [[wikipedia:Psychokinesis|telekinesis]] in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]" while performing to a crowd.

===Weaknesses===
Houdini is easily scared by almost everything, implying he may have [[wikipedia:Panphobia|panphobia]]. Also, due to the size of Houdini's eyes, they are highly sensitive to camera flashes. One flash temporarily blinds him, forcing him to blink repeatedly to try to get his vision back, and thus ends up making random things invisible, as he cannot see what he is doing.

==Trivia==
*Houdini is named after the famous Hollywood magician [[wikipedia:Harry Houdini|Harry Houdini]].
*Houdini is shown to be easily scared by almost everything, suggesting he has [[wikipedia:Panphobia|panphobia]].
*Houdini is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to.
*Houdini's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is yellow.
*The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Houdini as: "Experiment 604. Primary function: Invisibility generator."
*Houdini's picture in [[Lilo's Experiment Book|Lilo's experiment logbook]] is the same photo that Mertle took of him in [[Houdini (episode)|his debut]].
*Before settling on the name Houdini, the writers of [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]] also considered the names "Blinky", "No-Si-U", and "Shelbo" (which is apparently a long story).<ref name="WinfieldTVTome">{{cite web|url=http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|title=L&S Says Mahalo|website=[[wikipedia:TV.com|TV Tome]]|date=December 14, 2004|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305082355/http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|archivedate=March 19, 2016|accessdate=May 27, 2018}}</ref>
*According to John Wray, who wrote [[Houdini (episode)|Houdini's titular debut episode]], Houdini was originally [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|numbered as 303]] (which is [[Amnesio (303)|Amnesio]]'s number), but this was changed to 604 during production.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reddit.com/r/liloandstitch/comments/1d7vdvd/comment/l738jvs/|title=Comment on Today is 6/04, Houdini Day! 🪄|website=[[wikipedia:Reddit|Reddit]]|date=June 4, 2024|accessdate=May 3, 2025}}</ref><ref>[https://liloandstitch.fandom.com/wiki/File:Lilo_%26_Stitch_The_Series_-_Houdini_-_Script_showing_Houdini%27s_original_number.jpg Lilo & Stitch The Series - Houdini - Script showing Houdini's original number]</ref> This indirectly explains why Jumba's voice sounds different on his two lines mentioning Houdini's number in the episode.

'''Huggo''', also known as '''Experiment 489''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to use his tentacles to squeeze the life out of his victims.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 489 was the 489th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to squeeze the life out of his victims with his tentacles. 489 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

===''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''===
All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 489's pod landing on top of a buoy.

Later, a wave splashed over the buoy, activating the experiment.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point after this, Experiment 489 was presumably captured and named Huggo.

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Huggo was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 144 instead of 489.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
All 624 experiments, including Huggo, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

It is unknown whether or not Huggo participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Huggo is a large purple/blue cephalopod-like experiment, but with six tentacles and two eye stalks.

===Special abilities===
Huggo can squeeze the life out of enemies by using his tentacles.

==Trivia==
*Huggo is one of only two [[:Category:4-Series|4-series]] experiments that have their image, name, number, and function confirmed, the other being [[Mary (455)|Mary]]. Interestingly, both [[:Category:Stitch! The Movie Experiments|debuted]] in ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''.
*With only one brief animated scene and no other appearances in [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|the franchise]] (apart from his image being used in ''[[The Origin of Stitch]]'' and erroneously referred to as Experiment 144), Huggo most likely has the least amount of screen time out of all the fully confirmed experiments. (The aforementioned Mary has a briefer, less animated scene in ''Stitch! The Movie'', but she also appears animated in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.)
*Huggo is one of the only known experiments with six limbs; in this case, they are tentacles. [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]] has six limbs: two arms and four hind tentacles and uses either four or all six for locomotion. [[Swapper (355)|Swapper]] also has six limbs, but only uses two or four for locomotion.
*Huggo, [[Clink (086)|Clink]], and [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]] are the only known experiments with stalked eyes, a trait common in the invertebrates that all three are inspired by.
*Huggo and Thresher have very similar heads/faces. Perhaps they were created using some of the same DNA.
*Huggo and [[Yin (501)|Yin]] are the only known experiments based on cephalopods. Though given Huggo and Thresher's uncanny resemblance, Thresher may also be cephalopod-like.
*Huggo's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] changes color between scenes. In one scene, it was green, and in another, it was red.
**On a similar note, Huggo has appeared in different colors. In ''Stitch! The Movie'', he was purple, but in ''[[The Origin of Stitch]]'', he was blue.
*Huggo is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.
*He is also one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''Leroy & Stitch''.

'''Hunkahunka''', also known as '''Experiment 323''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to cause societies to come to a crashing standstill by causing artificial lovesickness. Once he pecks someone, they fall in love with the first individual they see regardless of their gender, species, and personal preferences; only spraying water in the victim's face will break the spell. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 323 was the 323rd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his fake love-inducing ability to bring entire civilizations to a lovestruck standstill. 323 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Hunkahunka - Hunkahunka pecks David.png|thumb|left|Pecks David]]
At an unknown point, Experiment 323 was activated off-screen (possibly by an ocean wave). 323 then proceeded to cause artificial love across the [[Kauai|island]]. He first targeted [[David Kawena|David]] and pecked the latter to make him fall for some other woman on [[Lahui Beach|the beach]], making [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] jealous after she agreed to go on a date with David.

Later, [[Gantu]] attempted to capture 323 after noticing the experiment, but was thwarted by [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. When Gantu restrained Stitch and prepared to shoot the latter into the ocean (knowing he would drown), 323 pecked Gantu to make him fall in love with [[Pleakley]]. Stitch freed himself and managed to capture 323 in a drink cooler. He then showed 323, named Hunkahunka, to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], who used the experiment's fake love-inducing power to make [[Keoni Jameson|Keoni]] fall for her.

However, Hunkahunka escaped and resumed his love-inflicting rampage while being pursued by Stitch and Gantu. At one point, he pecked Gantu again, causing the latter to temporarily fall for Stitch. While Stitch evaded Gantu, the former was able to recapture Hunkahunka and hide him in a raffle box. When Lilo ran into Stitch, fed up with Keoni's phony love, she attempted to grab the raffle box from him (thinking it contained the antidote), causing the box to open and Hunkahunka to get loose again.

Later on, Hunkahunka entered a dance hall, where he caused countless victims to fall in love, and pecked Nani at one point to make her fall for Gantu. Eventually, after a long chase, Gantu managed to capture Hunkahunka in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] and take off with him. Regardless, Lilo ultimately decided that people should want others to love them for who they are, not merely because some alien bird pecked them.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Hunkahunka - Hunkahunka pecks Hämsterviel.png|thumb|Pecks Hämsterviel]]
Hunkahunka was successfully sent to an impatient [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], where the former then pecked Hämsterviel, causing him to fall for Gantu, much to the latter's surprise. However, he still berated Gantu like he would on a regular basis, implying that either Hunkahunka's love powers had a somewhat different effect on Hämsterviel, or he has a different point of view altogether.

Although Hunkahunka was unseen in "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", he is known to have been sent back to Gantu along with all of Hämsterviel's other captive experiments after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused chaos and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

Hunkahunka reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by Lilo, Stitch, and several other experiments in a rescue mission.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Hunkahunka, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Hunkahunka participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], as he was seen among the other experiments.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Hunkahunka made [[Hunkahunka Burnin' Angel|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] used him on [[Angel (624)|Angel]] after she got mad at him earlier. However, Hunkahunka's spell caused Angel to become overly obsessed with Stitch, therefore teaching him a lesson when Hunkahunka also made others fall in love (including [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], who was about to reveal the antidote before becoming part of Hunkahunka's spell).

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Hunkahunka is a small pink/purple hummingbird-like experiment with a large head, black eyes, dark pink and maroon feathers on his body, a long lavender beak, light pink belly and purple-tipped wings and tail.

===Special abilities===
Hunkahunka can peck a target which injects the victim with a love-inducing drug that affects certain nerves, causing an artificial "love" sensation in which they are attracted to the first individual they see, regardless of the individual's gender, species, and personal preferences.

===Weaknesses===
Victims of Hunkahunka appear to be under a love spell when affected. Water sprayed in the victim's face negates the effects and cures their lovesickness. When the spell is broken, it's as if they are waking out of a trance and do not remember their actions while they were affected. Also, Hunkahunka's pecks only kick in when the victim sees somebody, so if they are unable to see or are in total darkness, the lovesickness does not take immediate effect.

==Trivia==
*Hunkahunka was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Hunkahunka is based on [[wikipedia:Cupid|Cupid]].
*Hunkahunka is named after a lyric in the [[wikipedia:Elvis Presley|Elvis Presley]] song "[[Burning Love]]", played in [[Lilo & Stitch|the original movie]]. Lilo refers to him as a "Hunkahunka bird of love".
*Hunkahunka, [[Bugby (128)|Bugby]], [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]], [[Jam (202)|Jam]], [[Melty (228)|Melty]], [[Wishy-Washy (267)|Wishy-Washy]], [[Snooty (277)|Snooty]], [[Amnesio (303)|Amnesio]], [[Experiments#5-Series: Elemental and environmental manipulators|Blake]], [[Slugger (608)|Slugger]], [[Witch (610)|Witch]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Miscellaneous|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have wings.
*Hunkahunka was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*In [[Hunkahunka (episode)|his debut]], Hunkahunka had dark purple feathers. However, in official media, [[Aloha, E Komo Mai|the show's intro]], the episode "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and his later appearances, he had dark pink and maroon feathers on his body.

'''Jumba's Chinese Experiments''' are characters appearing in ''[[Stitch & Ai]]''. [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] researches and genetically engineers creatures based on Chinese mythological creatures from scrolls given to him by an old monk. They are considered genetic experiments, much like Jumba's [[Experiments|other experiments]]. However, since Jumba creates specific creatures based on legends and myths, it is unknown if he considers them in his existing numbering system.

Jumba creates the following creatures:
*'''[[Qi Lin]]''' - It is super strong and can light itself on fire. It is the first new experiment that Jumba creates in China, debuting in "[[The Scroll]]".
*'''[[Cliff Dragons]]''' - One male and one female, who eventually have a baby. They resemble traditional Eastern dragons and can fly using their chi. They debuted in "[[Spirals]]".
*'''[[Dim Long]]''' - Small, beta-test dragon-like creature that can fly without wings by using qi. Dim Long debuted in "[[The Lock]]".
*'''[[Xiezhi]]''' - One-horned rhino-like creature of justice that eats fire. It points its horn at the guilty and can use its chi to run within clouds. It became out of control, so Jumba had to reverse its function and then recreate it. It debuted in "The Lock".
*'''[[Nian]]''' - Lion-like creature that captures children, loves movies, and wants to be a movie star. It debuted in "[[Tell the World]]".
*'''[[Fenghuang]]''' - It has five colors, each one representing one of the five virtues. Jumba originally attempted to make it at a smaller size, but as soon as it was created it began growing larger. The fenghuang is mentioned to only exist in three star systems and is known by three names, Gleamfax Oongtang, Centaurus vericas, of Fenghuang the phoenix of Earth and it has been a long time since anyone has seen one. This suggests that some species can emerge in different parts of the galaxy. Since Jumba's fenghuang set off an intergalactic scanner, it seems that his experiment's DNA is virtually identical to the ancient species that once inhabited the galaxy. It debuted in "[[The Phoenix]]".
*'''[[Mo]]''' - Dream eater who is based on the [https://www.ancient-origins.net/myths-legends-asia/baku-legend-dream-eater-002383 baku]. It appears in "[[Dream On]]", created by Jumba following [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] around throughout much of the episode, then eating Stitch's nightmares.
*'''[[Naughty Creatures|Eight Naughty Creatures]]''' - A rhino, a shelled creature, one with a clam-like head, a griffin-like one, a green quadruped with an elongated head, a red rabbit-like one, and two dragon/lizard like creatures. Jumba had been planning out the creation of these experiments, but Stitch decided to finish their creation himself. All eight appear in the episode "[[Nuo Opera]]".

Jumba creates a parallel dimension for all of them to inhabit.

==Trivia==

'''Jumba's computer''' is a machine that [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] constructed (or upgraded) to show pictures of the [[Experiments|experiments]] and information on their number and primary function. It can also reveal an antidote for any experiment's power or effect on a person. The experiment's info can also be shown on [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]]'s computer and told on [[Gantu]]'s [[Experiment Pod Container|experiment analyzer]].

Jumba's computer displays crude 2-D representations of the experiments, along with specific information on them and occasionally antidotes for the experiments' effects. Jumba also keeps self-made video diaries which explain his thoughts or the results of his illegal experiments (as displayed in "[[Poxy (episode)|Poxy]]" and "[[Frenchfry (episode)|Frenchfry]]").

Jumba's computer even consists of some of the genetic experiments' powers. In "[[Angel (episode)|Angel]]", after Lilo discovered that Jumba had been reverted to evil by Experiment 624 ([[Angel (624)|Angel]]), she proceeded to use the computer to play Angel's song backwards and successfully turn Jumba back to good.

'''Kernel''', also known as '''Experiment 014''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to pop popcorn for Jumba's movie night. His one true place is popping popcorn for a [[Cinema|movie theater]].

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 014 was the fourteenth genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to pop popcorn for Jumba's movie night. 014 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
014 was mentioned in "[[Angel (episode)|Angel]]" when Jumba, under the effects of [[Angel (624)|624]], claimed that she was designed to "pop popcorn for Jumba's movie night," but he was actually stating the purpose of 014.

At some point, 014 was activated, captured, tamed, and named Kernel.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
Kernel was seen when [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to check on all of the experiments. Right before she met [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]], Lilo was seen in front of the [[Cinema|theater]], where Kernel was doing his job inside an enclosure.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Kernel, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Kernel participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Kernel is a tan gourd-shaped experiment with a large opening at the top of his head, black eyes, a red nose, a thin mouth, short ears and a white stomach.

===Special abilities===
Kernel can produce popcorn, and pop it out of the opening on his head.

==Trivia==
*Though only appearing in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', Kernel was referenced in "[[Angel (episode)|Angel]]". After [[Angel (624)|Angel]] turned Jumba evil again, he lied when he stated that Angel was a "harmless early experiment designed to pop popcorn for Jumba's movie night," which is actually Kernel who is an early experiment with that exact function.
*Kernel is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''Leroy & Stitch''.

'''Kixx''', also known as '''Experiment 601''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to use his kickboxing and wrestling skills to bully and defeat opponents in hand-to-hand combat. His one true place is teaching people kickboxing and hosting his own workout video entitled ''Kickboxing with Kixx''.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 601 was the 601st genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his kickboxing and wrestling skills to beat up and defeat enemies. 601 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 601's pod landing by a cliff face.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Kixx - Kixx raising his left fists.png|thumb|left|Kixx moments after his activation]]
When a dehydrated tourist traveling with his wife tossed a half-full water bottle he drank from over the cliff, it landed by a ravine and trickled out, which touched 601's pod, activating the experiment. 601 then attacked [[Charles and Mary|the aforementioned couple]], beating them up when the husband angered him while mistaking him for a wild purple pig.

Later, when [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] arrived to find and capture 601 (who had proceeded to attack and beat up other tourists), the latter ambushed them. Stitch prepared to fight 601, but due to an earlier snack combo incident in which Stitch's combat training was erased, he faltered. Lilo was then forced to retreat with Stitch, while 601 was distracted with beating up the newly arrived [[Gantu]].

While 601 most likely continued his rampage, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] lent Lilo several books, including one entitled ''Fighting Four-Armed Monsters'', to help her re-train and condition Stitch to fight in combat. After practicing and mastering a few training exercises, Stitch was practically ready to battle 601 hand-to-hand.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Kixx - Kixx versus Stitch in Western style.png|thumb|Kixx vs. Stitch]]
Meanwhile, 601 attacked [[Muscle Bay]], defeating all the boxers with ease. Stitch then came to challenge 601 to a rematch, and a long-drawn-out battle ensued between them. At first, 601 was able to easily overpower Stitch, but with Lilo's tutoring and Stitch's coordination, the latter easily defeated 601, who was restrained with ropes.

601, christened Kixx, shortly after found his one true place teaching other people kickboxing. Back at [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]], [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] and an injured Gantu watched a commercial of Kixx hosting his own instructional workout video on the ex-captain's TV set. It motivated Gantu to learn kickboxing after being pummeled by Kixx.

Kixx reappeared in "[[Elastico (episode)|Elastico]]" as one of the audience members for Lilo's hula dance.

In "[[The Asteroid]]", Kixx was one of the six experiments that Stitch convinced to come with him and Lilo to save Earth from an approaching asteroid. Along the journey, Kixx kicked the back of [[Spooky (300)|Spooky]]'s seat, causing the latter (using his nightmarish morphing ability) to terrify him. Also, when Kixx grabbed at the free refreshments, only to get slapped by [[Pleakley]], the former beat Pleakley up and then took a bag of peanuts for himself. He later endured a clobbering from [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]] and helped Stitch remove the [[Jumba's Ship|ship]]'s hyperdrive engine.

Kixx made a brief cameo in "[[Houdini (episode)|Houdini]]" on Gantu's TV set continuing his broadcast of his recent kickboxing commercial.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Angel - Kixx about to pummel Stitch.png|thumb|left|Kixx about to pummel Stitch]]
In "[[Angel (episode)|Angel]]", Kixx was one of the experiments that [[Angel (624)|Angel]] reverted to evil using her song, causing the former to beat up athletes and forcing Stitch to fight and defeat him again. Later, Kixx and the other depraved experiments attacked Stitch aboard a ship, but Angel turned them to good again before Kixx could land the fatal blow. Working together, the experiments were then able to successfully escape the ship with Stitch.

Kixx reappeared in "[[Slugger (episode)|Slugger]]" as part of Lilo's softball team.

In "[[Shoe (episode)|Shoe]]", Kixx was one of the experiments that helped turn Jumba's ship into a [[Jumba & Pleakley's Bed & Not Breakfast|hotel]].

Kixx was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that joined Stitch in a rebellion against Gantu. Although he did not appear during the battle, he was seen rebuilding the float after Gantu's defeat.

In "[[Ploot (episode)|Ploot]]", Kixx was one of the first team of experiments (along with [[Deforestator (515)|Deforestator]] and [[Richter (513)|Richter]]) formed to try and stop [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]]. However, Ploot was easily able to defeat them, forcing the three experiments to retreat.

Kixx was seen on a computer screen in "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]", posing as an evil creation of Jumba's as part of a hoax to fool [[Mortlegax]], the head of E.G.O. industries.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Kixx, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Kixx participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by beating up attacking Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. Kixx joins them for the song by playing the congas.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Kixx made [[Meega Going to Disneyland!|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Pix (214)|Pix]], [[Boomer (288)|Boomer]], [[Slushy (523)|Slushy]], [[Blowhard (533)|Blowhard]], and [[Slugger (608)|Slugger]], when [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] visited Tokyo Disneyland. He made [[Shogun|a second appearance]] where [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] [[Transmutation|modified]] him with a new samurai style of fighting, along with a samurai outfit to match it. After being defeated, Kixx was presumably reverted back to normal, then dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help Stitch in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Kixx wasn't one of the experiments that was activated. He later appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Kixx is shown to be a talented kickboxer and he loves to pick fights, which would consider him a bully. He also appears to be extremely hotheaded and violent. However, after Lilo and Stitch befriended him, Kixx has shown to control his temper a lot better. Despite his aggression, Kixx is loyal to those who win his trust. He is valiant and an excellent fighter, but also a really big softie deep down. He enjoys kickboxing, wrestling, and baseball and shows a sign of pride.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Kixx is a large purple, muscular, beastly [[w:c:looneytunes:Tasmanian Devil|Tasmanian Devil]]-like creature with a lavender stomach, chest, ear insides and spots around his eyes, bulky legs and torso, four strong gorilla-like arms with three fingers on each paw, a blue oval spot on each elbow, short ears, hardly any neck, a wide mouth, a round nose and black eyes.

===Special abilities===
Kixx has superhuman strength and kickboxing skills, second only to [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. He possesses hand-to-hand combat skills with corresponding agility. He also has professional wrestling skills, as well as the capable strength to hold his own against other opponents. Like Stitch, Kixx can roll into a ball and jump real high, but with more durability and force than when Stitch does it. Similar to [[Deforestator (515)|Deforestator]], Kixx can spin into a tornado to deliver consecutive punches to his opponent and is extremely fast when doing so.

He can speak basic [[Tantalog language|Tantalog]] but has a raspy voice, and when he does speak, it sounds close to a growl. He can also say karate terms, such as "Ya!"

He has a samurai style of fighting, which he has only displayed while [[Transmutation|under the effects]] of [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], along with a samurai outfit to match it.

Kixx has shown to be skilled in playing the congas.

===Weaknesses===
Using the book titled ''Fighting Four-Armed Monsters'', Kixx's attacks can be countered easily, which led to his downfall by Stitch.
