'''Lax''', also known as '''Experiment 285''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to halt the activity of entire work forces, companies, and innocent civilians by turning them lackadaisical with a zap from his antenna, causing civilizations to fail and making it easier to invade their planet, and it even works on technology. His one true place is at the [[Kauai Airport|local airport]], making grouchy tourists enjoy their vacation.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 285 was the 285th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to fire a green laser from his antenna that causes enemies, innocent civilians, and even modern technology to abandon work. 285 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 285's pod landing in some bushes near the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Lax - Lax moments after activation.jpg|thumb|left|Lax moments after his activation]]
The [[disney:Recess|Recess gang]], along with their chaperone [[Muriel Finster|Ms. Finster]], accompany [[Gretchen Grundler|Gretchen]] to Hawaii after she makes a big discovery about a new planet.

Meanwhile, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], a local and her alien friend, have made a mess trying to create a new recipe. Lilo's older sister, [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]], orders them to clean it up and then leaves for work (however, while driving over a puddle, Experiment 285's pod was activated). Instead, they try to make [[Pleakley]], another alien with a love of cleaning, do it. However, after seeing how huge the mess is, Pleakley faints.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Lax - Lax firing his laser.jpg|thumb|Lax firing his laser]]
Sometime after, Stitch wanders outside and does nothing except lie in a hammock. Then, Pleakley is zapped by the same unknown energy that got Stitch, causing him to laze about in a similar fashion. The same goes for another alien named [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], who just arrived.

It turns out the culprit is Experiment 285, or Lax, an alien experiment with an antenna-like appendage that is designed to cause individuals to be very relaxed and lazy. Lilo and a lazy Stitch chase after him but instead find [[Ashley Spinelli|Spinelli]] running towards the pool of the [[Birds of Paradise Hotel|hotel]], followed closely by the rest of the Recess gang. Lilo follows as well, but then [[Mikey Blumberg|Mikey]] and [[Vince LaSalle|Vince]] (though at separate times) are zapped by Lax. Lilo explains everything to [[T.J. Detweiler|T.J.]], and they then try to capture Lax, but they fail and he escapes.

Meanwhile, another alien named [[Gantu]] is made to follow a satellite's directions to find Lax for the evil [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. Lilo and four of the Recess characters, [[Gus Griswald|Gus]], T.J., Gretchen, and Spinelli, catch up to Lax at an [[observatory]]. T.J. and Spinelli try to get Lax themselves, but they too get zapped. Just then, Gretchen finds the new "planet" that she discovers, but Lilo finds out it's only a satellite being used by Hämsterviel (the same one Gantu uses).

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Lax - Lax defeated as Stitch smiles smugly.jpg|thumb|left|Lax defeated]]
Gretchen's Galileo computer is zapped; however, Gretchen gets the idea to use the telescope to zap the satellite. While most of the Recess gang distract Lax by hitting golf balls at him, Gretchen is zapped, but she still works on the plan; apparently, she finds work relaxing. Gus gets chased by Lax, but Lilo distracts Lax just in time for Stitch to pummel him. Lilo, Gretchen and Gus then put their plan into action, and the satellite ends up destroyed. Gantu confronts them, but Lax zaps him, thus ending the threat.

The Recess gang eventually goes back to normal, and Lax finds a hobby in zapping stressed and unpleasant tourists at the [[Kauai Airport|airport]]. Then Spinelli wonders where Finster is. It turns out Finster has never left the spa.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Lax, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Lax participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] probably by making attacking Leroys lackadaisical.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Lax is a purple parrot-like experiment with black eyes, a single green-tipped, [https://www.britannica.com/science/esca esca]-like antenna, a blue-striped beak, and green-striped tail feathers.

===Special abilities===
Lax can emit a green laser from his antenna, which contains a chemical that relieves the sympathetic nervous system, causing the brain to deny stress, and therefore makes the victim feel "on vacation". When the laser hits a machine, the chemical has a similar effect and causes all complex functions or artificial intelligence to shut off, creating the "vacation" effect. Thus, a person hit with Lax's ray will relax, and a machine hit with said ray will shut down.

===Weaknesses===
If the victim of Lax's beam happens to believe work is fun, it will appear as if they were immune to it. Also, the effects of said beam are only temporary; however, they last for quite long periods. Additionally, the ray can be blocked or deflected off reflective surfaces.

'''Leroy''', also known as '''Experiment 629''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] appearing as the titular secondary antagonist of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'' and the last known experiment to be created by [[Jumba Jookiba]]. [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] forced Jumba to create Leroy and design him as an improved version of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] with extra destructive capabilities and less fluffy. Thus, Hämsterviel could use Leroy to take control of the Galactic Federation and finally capture all of the other experiments. Leroy has [[Leroy Clones|an army of clones]] and is a near-unstoppable monster that is impossible to be rehabilitated. His one true place is in [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison]].

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 629 was the 629th and last known genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to have all of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]'s powers, with a little extra boost of strength and speed. He was named Leroy by Dr. Hämsterviel.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
[[File:Leroy & Stitch - Leroy taking over as captain.png|thumb|left|The original Leroy]]
While spending a few years on Earth, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] had an unfinished [[Experiments|experiment]] at his [[Galaxy Defense Industries|laboratory]] in deep space. After [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] had successfully captured and rehabilitated all 625 of Jumba's experiments, he regained access to his lab. During this time, Jumba's evil former partner [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Dr. Hämsterviel]] escaped [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison]] with [[Gantu]]'s help.

Jumba started creating an experiment with explosive saliva from a template similar to Stitch until he was ordered by Hämsterviel, who paid Jumba a visit, to instead make the latter "a new version of 626." Forced to comply after being threatened by Gantu, Jumba created a red, destructive replica of Stitch. 

Hämsterviel decided to mimic Lilo by naming the experiment, just like she did with the other experiments. After [[Spike (319)|trying]] [[Kixx (601)|several]] [[Slugger (608)|failed]] [[Cannonball (520)|experiment]] [[627|names]], due to Gantu pointing out that each one was already taken, Hämsterviel christened the newly created experiment Leroy (much to Jumba and Gantu's amusement).

Shortly after, Stitch attacked the lab to apprehend Hämsterviel, and Leroy was released to battle Stitch. After a long fight ensued between the twin experiments, Stitch eventually had Leroy pinned down, but [[Pleakley]]'s untimely arrival distracted Stitch long enough for Leroy to bat him into a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]].

[[File:Leroy & Stitch - Hämsterviel cloning Leroy.png|thumb|Hämsterviel cloning Leroy]]
After Leroy proved to be more powerful than Stitch (though he had technically won unfairly), the former was [[Leroy Clones|cloned into a huge army]] by Hämsterviel. The original Leroy then took over the [[B.R.B. 9000|B.R.B.]] by posing as Stitch, the captain, and ordered that the [[Galactic Armada Crewmembers|pilots]] take him, Hämsterviel, and the Leroy army to [[Planet Turo|Turo]].

En route, Leroy received a telecommunication from Lilo and, resuming his Stitch disguise, attempted to pose as Stitch. However, he was quickly discovered by Lilo to be an impostor, as he was not wearing the [[Stitch's Necklace|tiki necklace]] that she had given Stitch earlier, prompting Hämsterviel to order Leroy to "hang up" (namely, by blasting the communicator). Upon arriving on planet Turo, the Leroy army was able to overthrow the council and gain galactic domination. 

Meanwhile, a Leroy clone arrived on Earth, where, using [[Lilo's Experiment Book|Lilo's stolen experiment logbook]], he rounded up all of the first 624 experiments there (along with [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] while capturing [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]]) and brought them to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed.

Shortly after, Hämsterviel and the entire Leroy army arrived at the stadium on Earth in the B.R.B. to destroy the captured experiments. Before they could, however, Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, Pleakley, [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]], and a reformed Gantu arrived, and a battle ensued between the experiments and the Leroy clones.

[[File:Leroy & Stitch - The Leroy army at Aloha Stadium.png|thumb|left|The Leroy army]]
Though the experiments were able to overpower the Leroys at first, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand when there were too many of them. However, as the Leroys came close to winning the battle, Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused all the Leroys (including the original one) to shut down due to the original's fail-safe.

Afterwards, all of the Leroys, along with Hämsterviel, were sent to prison on Asteroid K-37, where they were seen happily dancing to the song "[[Jailhouse Rock]]" with an angry Dr. Hämsterviel tapping his foot.

==Personality==
Leroy is an antagonistic, conceited, and ruthless experiment created to serve as Hämsterviel's enforcer, and thus obeys the evil scientist without question. Despite his loyalty to Hämsterviel, Leroy seems to enjoy seeing him suffer, as he is shown laughing sadistically at Hämsterviel when the latter falls to the ground after their cannon is destroyed. Nevertheless, Leroy is completely loyal to Hämsterviel, as he never once tried to betray him.

Like Stitch, Leroy is shown to be very destructive, but in a more vicious than mischievous way. He is also revealed to be a physical, sadistic, cruel, and revolting slob. Despite this, he also possesses some of Stitch's habits, including holding soda cans in his mouth, picking his nose with his tongue, and sharing Stitch's love for [[wikipedia:Elvis Presley|Elvis Presley]]'s music (though "Aloha ʻOe" would be an exception due to his fail-safe), as Leroy and his clones were seen dancing to "Jailhouse Rock" in their prison cells.

Leroy is very cunning and hyperactive like Stitch, though he is not quite as immature despite the "age" difference. Where the similarities end in Leroy is how brutal he is in comparison to Stitch. Leroy isn't above using violence to get things accomplished and enjoys tormenting his foes whenever possible. He will more often than not rely on brute force in battle and tends to not show mercy to his opponents, though he is capable of planning out his attacks and is quite smart. While his English is not perfect, Leroy can still speak it a little bit better than most other experiments.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Leroy resembles an exact duplicate of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] with rougher red fur, a mahogany nose, black claws, toes, and tips of antennae, a light tan/pinkish-orange stomach from his chin down and around his eyes, crimson markings on the back of his head and on his back, frilly, jagged ears with light purple inside, yellow teeth, a fluffy tail, and a slightly deeper voice. He also has two extra, retractable arms, two bent retractable antennae on his head, three bent retractable spines tipped with white and a dark mahogany on his back, and retractable claws on his front and back paws. When his mouth is closed, his canine fangs stick out.

When impersonating Stitch, Leroy dons the same black spacesuit that Stitch wore when he was the captain of the [[B.R.B. 9000]]. Leroy's suit is a black shirt with thick red brims on his shoulders, wrist-length sleeves with red cuffs, along with matching vertical linings on both sides of the shirt and trousers. He also wore a gray belt with a light gray "V" on the front, along with a small gray mark on the upper left chest that resembles a tear drop with a black dot on it. After Leroy and his clones were defeated, the suit was removed.

===Special abilities===
Leroy possesses all of the same powers as Stitch, with an extra boost of strength and speed. He can curl into a ball and roll at very high speeds, dealing heavy damage to anything he hits. He is incredibly durable, being immune to fire, bullets, electricity, and other hazards. He is also smart and can think faster than a supercomputer, and can also absorb electric and fire powers. He is normally very physical, but also good with a [[Plasma Blaster|plasma gun]]. He also has the ability to disguise himself as Stitch by changing his fur color from red to blue and can instantly regrow his fur. Additionally, Leroy is immune to some of the other experiments' powers; since he is created after [[Angel (624)|Angel]], her song presumably has no effect on him and cannot turn him good.

===Weaknesses===
During his creation, Leroy was programmed with a fail-safe that causes him and his clones to shut down when they hear the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]".

Like Stitch, Leroy is not immune to all the other experiments' powers, evident as some of his clones are affected by [[Spike (319)|Spike]] and [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]].

It is unknown whether or not Leroy shares Stitch's weakness of water.

==Trivia==
*Until June 2020, Leroy was not officially called Experiment 629. Prior to this month, in promotional material for the film and on some Japanese and [[disney:Disneyland Paris|Disneyland Paris]] merchandise, Leroy was also referred to as '''Experiment 628''', although this number was not used for his initial appearance in either the Japanese or global versions of ''[[disney:Disney Tsum Tsum (game)|Disney Tsum Tsum]]''. Regardless, Leroy being X-628 is false, as he was only called Leroy in the film and is the evil doppelganger of Experiment 626. Also, the real [[Experiments#6-Series: Battlefield and doomsday experiments with galactic implications|Experiment 628]] (albeit in [[Experiment Pods|pod]] form) was shown in the episode "[[627 (episode)|627]]".
**Leroy was officially referred to in media as Experiment 629 on June 4, 2020, via a limited-time side story of the manga ''[[Stitch & the Samurai]]'' that was released exclusively via the Japanese version of ''LINE: Disney Tsum Tsum''.<ref>[https://twitter.com/LINE_tsumtsum_j/status/1268422230498828288 Tweet from the Japanese ''LINE: Disney Tsum Tsum'' account written on June 4, 2020.]</ref> In the manga, a caption box appears under Leroy, referring to him as "試作品629ルロイ" or "Prototype 629 Leroy". **Leroy's chapter in the side story was not published in English; he did not get numbered as 629 in English until an officially-licensed sticker book, ''The Ultimate Disney Stitch Sticker Book'', was published in 2021.
*Leroy is the only experiment to have not been created by Jumba out of his own free will, as Hämsterviel forced him to create the experiment, though he had originally intended Leroy to be a different experiment.
**In fact, Leroy is the first and only illegal genetic experiment since Stitch to be created by Jumba at [[Galaxy Defense Industries|his own laboratory]] with Hämsterviel's funding.
*Hämsterviel wanted Leroy's fur color to be red instead of blue so as to match his cape, and that he doesn't like the color blue.
**Ironically, Leroy can change his fur color to look like Stitch's.
**It is unknown if he can change his fur color to other colors.
*Leroy's color scheme and attitude seem to be derived from [[627|Experiment 627]]. Much like 627, Leroy could not be rehabilitated.
**627 was suggested as a name by Jumba before Gantu reminded him that 627 was already created.
*Like 627, Leroy's primary color is red to symbolize evil in contrast to Stitch's blue fur.
**Ironically, at the start of [[Lilo & Stitch|the first film]], [[Stitch's Spacesuit|Stitch's spacesuit]] is red to symbolize Stitch's original evil and destructive nature before being adopted by Lilo.
*When Hämsterviel christened the newly created experiment Leroy, everyone, for whatever reason, laughed at the name except Lilo, who considered Leroy to be a fine name, much to Hämsterviel's delight.
**Hämsterviel initially tried to name him [[Spike (319)|Spike]], [[Kixx (601)|Kixx]], [[Slugger (608)|Slugger]], and [[Cannonball (520)|Cannonball]], but Gantu pointed out that they were already taken.
**"Leroy" actually means "king" in French, which is ironic considering that Leroy shuts down when hearing "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", as Jumba used a recording sung by [[wikipedia:Elvis Presley|Elvis Presley]], who was referred as the "'''King''' of Rock and Roll".
*Leroy is one of the ten known experiments named by someone other than Lilo or Stitch, the other nine being [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Elastico (345)|Elastico]], [[Yaarp (613)|Yaarp]], [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]], [[Heat (609)|Heat]], [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]], [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]], [[Morpholomew (316)|Morpholomew]], and [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]]. 
**Leroy, in particular, was named by Hämsterviel, who is also implied to have named Shrink.
**It can also be said that Hämsterviel opened and closed Jumba's career of creating genetic experiments, having named the first and last experiment he funded (Shrink and Leroy, respectively).
*Technically speaking, Leroy is the youngest of all the known experiments, having only come into existence during the events of ''Leroy & Stitch''.
*Leroy is the third experiment shown to share Stitch's habit of picking his nose with his tongue, the first being [[Sparky (221)|Sparky]] and the second being [[Angel (624)|Angel]].
**He is also the first experiment shown to share Stitch's habit of obtaining and enjoying soda.
*Although Leroy is the secondary antagonist, he turned out to be more dangerous than Hämsterviel.
*According to the DVD scene selection, Leroy has about 50,000 [[Leroy Clones|clones]].
*The scene where a Leroy clone crash-lands on Earth in [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]]'s backyard is the same animation when Stitch first crash-landed on Earth in ''Lilo & Stitch''.
*At the [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]], the way Leroy mimics Hämsterviel's postures and gestures mirrors how Stitch once mimicked Lilo's postures and gestures in ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' when they accidentally crashed Mertle's slumber party.
*When Leroy was defeated, his eyes glowed green as Stitch's eyes did in ''[[Lilo & Stitch 2: Stitch Has a Glitch]]''.
*Leroy is a dark reflection of Stitch, similar but not different from 627, [[Zero (000)|Zero]], and [[Dark End]]. 
**While both Leroy and Stitch are clearly designed to be violent and destructive monsters from the start, the difference is that while Stitch was initially an aggressive, bad-tempered, rude and destructive monster in ''Lilo & Stitch'', he learns to change his negative ways thanks to Lilo's influence, while Leroy, on the other hand, remains a complete monster all the way through and is incapable of rehabilitation or reformation. In fact, Leroy can be seen as representing the sort of monster that Stitch would have become if he had never met Lilo and her ''ʻohana'' and been introduced to the meaning of family in the original film.
**Coincidentally, the scene where Leroy took over the [[B.R.B. 9000|B.R.B.]] by posing as Stitch, the captain, and ordered that the [[Galactic Armada Crewmembers|pilots]] take him, Hämsterviel, and the Leroy army to [[Planet Turo|Turo]] is very reminiscent of the deleted original opening scene from the original film, which depicted Stitch as the leader of an intergalactic gang and Jumba as one of his former cronies sent after Stitch by the Intergalactic Council to capture him. Ironically, however, it is the long-reformed Stitch himself that is sent after Leroy by the Intergalactic Council to capture him.
**Similarly, both Stitch and Leroy's respective owners, Lilo and Hämsterviel, are complete antitheses of each other; while Lilo influences Stitch to give up his destructive ways and reform into a good experiment, Hämsterviel, on the other hand, feeds into Leroy's destructive nature and intentionally uses the experiment for his own evil purpose of world domination.
*Leroy can be considered to be one of the only successful prototypes for Jumba's "ultimate monster" experiment, since Jumba deliberately programmed Leroy's weakness to the song "Aloha ʻOe", and no actual failure has been observed. Other notable attempts for such a prototype experiment are 000, [[Ace (262)|262]], [[Woops (600)|600]], [[Reuben (625)|625]], 626, and 627, and each failed for its own reason: 000 is uncontrollable, 262 is good, 600 is clumsy, 625 is lazy, 626 wanted a family, and 627 is weak to laughter.
*He is one of the few experiments that are actually villains, along with Leroy's clones, Zero, [[Chopsuey (621)|Chopsuey]], 627, and Dark End, while all the other experiments were following their primary function.
*While Leroy does not appear in the 2025 live-action remake of ''[[Lilo & Stitch (2025 film)|Lilo & Stitch]]'', 627's appearance in that film closely resembles Leroy.
**Ironically, producer Jonathan Eirich erroneously referred to 627 as Leroy in an interview about the film.<ref>[https://youtu.be/FIfVM2e7FsA Bringing Stitch To LIFE! Lilo & Stitch's Chris Sanders, Tia Carrere, and Courtney B. Vance!]</ref>

The '''Leroy Clones''' are illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiments]] that were cloned from the original [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Dr. Hämsterviel]], and supporting antagonists in Disney's 2006 film ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''. They share the same qualities with the original in terms of physical appearance, abilities, and personality. Their one true place is in [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison]].

==Background and appearances==
===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
After [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Wendy Pleakley|Pleakley]] were defeated by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] (though the original won unfairly, given the untimely arrival of Pleakley during Leroy and Stitch's battle), [[Dr. Hämsterviel]] cloned him into a huge army. The original Leroy then took over the [[B.R.B. 9000|B.R.B.]] by posing as Stitch, the captain, and ordered that the [[Galactic Armada Crewmembers|pilots]] take him, Hämsterviel, and the Leroy army to [[Planet Turo|Turo]].

Meanwhile, after [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] left to help Stitch, Jumba and Pleakley, a Leroy clone arrived on Earth, where he rounded up all of the first 624 experiments there (along with [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] while capturing [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]]) and brought them to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed.

Shortly after, Hämsterviel and the entire Leroy army arrived at the stadium on Earth in the BRB to destroy the captured experiments. Before they could, however, Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, Pleakley, Reuben and a reformed [[Gantu]] arrived, and a battle ensued between the experiments and the Leroy clones.

Though the experiments were able to overpower the Leroys at first, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand when there were too many of them. However, as the Leroys came close to winning the battle, Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused all the Leroys (including the original one) to shut down due to the original's fail-safe.

Afterwards, all of the Leroys, along with Hämsterviel, were sent to prison on [[Prison Asteroid K-37|Asteroid K-37]], where they were seen happily dancing to the song "[[Jailhouse Rock]]" with an angry Dr. Hämsterviel tapping his foot.

==Personality==
Since they are like the original Leroy, the clones all share his personality, appearance, and abilities. They are vicious and love to cause destruction as much as the original Leroy. They're also cunning and intelligent, as the clones use their numbers to take down the experiments in their fight.

They also share their love for [[wikipedia:Elvis Presley|Elvis Presley]]'s music, as they all danced to "Jailhouse Rock" in their prison cells.

The clones are also immune to some of the experiments' powers; since Leroy is created after them, they are immune to [[Angel (624)|Angel]]'s song. However, they are not immune to all of them, as some of them are affected by [[Spike (319)|Spike]] and [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]].

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Their appearance is identical to the original Leroy's, except that the original Leroy wears a black uniform while the clones do not.

===Special abilities===
The clones also share the original Leroy's abilities.

===Weaknesses===
Leroy was programmed with a fail-safe during his creation. Since the clones share his abilities and characteristics, they also share his weakness to shut down when they hear the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]".

==Trivia==
*Dr. Hämsterviel cloning Leroy could possibly mirror his failed attempt to clone Stitch in ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''.
**Hämsterviel cloning Leroy also mirrors Stitch getting cloned into four by [[Dupe (344)|Dupe]] in the ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]'' episode "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]", except that unlike Stitch, who got weakened in strength when cloned in said episode, the Leroy clones, on the other hand, retain their full strength even when cloned.
*The development of the Leroy clones is almost similar to the [[disney: Clone Troopers|Clone Troopers]] from the ''[[disney:Star Wars|Star Wars]]'' franchise.
*According to the DVD scene selection, there are about 50,000 Leroy clones.
*One of the Leroy clones had most of his fur cut off by [[Clip (177)|Clip]]; however, since all of the clones share the same abilities as the original Leroy, it is unknown why the Leroy clone didn't simply regrow his fur (though he probably did so off-screen).
*They are some of the few experiments that are actually villains, along with Leroy, [[Zero (000)|Zero]], [[Chopsuey (621)|Chopsuey]], [[627]], and [[Dark End]], while all the other experiments were following their primary function.

'''Link''', also known as '''Experiment 251''' and '''Linkenstein''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to bind together incompatible individuals so that their arguing causes massive chaos. His glue has indestructible function qualities on fifty different planets (excluding Earth); the only thing that can make it dissolve is mud. His one true place is working at the ''Cliff Diving for Couples'' attraction, teaching arguing couples to do things together by using his binds for bungee jumping.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 251 was the 251st genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to link together squabbling individuals with near-indestructible goo. Thus, the pair's arguing and efforts to break away would result in chaos and destruction. 251 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 251's pod landing embedded in a sandy [[Lahui Beach|beach]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Link - Link after activation.jpg|thumb|left|Link after being activated]]
While [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] were digging for buried treasure on the beach, Mertle accidentally shoveled 251's pod into the path of an incoming tide, activating the experiment.

When Lilo and Mertle began arguing over a treasure map they both found, 251 stuck them together with a viscid blue substance and ran off in search of trouble. Unable to break free from each other (even after [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] attempted to separate them), Lilo told Stitch to go back for help.

251 attacked the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]] next. When [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]] bickered over a messy lab incident, 251 stuck them together as well. He then stuck Stitch and [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] together, thinking they were arguing, when the former tried to drag Nani off, wanting her to help with Lilo's sticky situation.

As a result, Nani was forced to take a reluctant Stitch on a water skiing trip, having to work for a testy young woman and despite Stitch's aquaphobia. While Nani drove the boat, a series of eventful things occurred, such as the motor stalling and Stitch hot-wiring the speedboat to restart the engine. In the aftermath, the boat skidded onto shore and threw all three in some mud, which dissolved 251's glue, much to Nani and Stitch's relief.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Link -  Locking on to Pleakley and Jumba.jpg|thumb|Targeting Jumba and Pleakley]]
Sometime later, Stitch and Nani returned to the house to discover Jumba and Pleakley preparing to use a laser machine to unstick themselves. However, Stitch unstuck them by throwing a bucket of mud over their bonded area. Jumba and Pleakley then made amends, with the former offering to help clean up the mess.

Meanwhile, 251 went on a rampage, sticking squabbling individuals together with his highly effective adhesive. Shortly after, Lilo and Mertle chased 251 through the streets of [[Kokaua Town|town]], then ended the chase when they used the goo binding them to lasso 251 into Lilo's backpack. She decided to name 251 Link (short for Linkenstein), which didn't interest Mertle.

Lilo and Mertle then resumed their conflict until [[Gantu]] showed up and demanded them the experiment (as well as their treasure map). In the commotion, Link escaped Lilo's backpack, while Gantu, Lilo and Mertle chased after him. Eventually, the trio cornered Link, but the latter escaped by sticking Lilo and Mertle to Gantu's head.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Link - Link with a tail while sitting in chair with cold drink.jpg|thumb|left|Link's one true place]]
Link later attacked a [[Golf Course|golf course]], where he targeted two arguing golfers. However, he was blasted into a [[Net Cannon|net]] by Gantu, who took Link back to [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]] with Lilo and Mertle still stuck to his head. Fortunately, Stitch soon arrived with more mud and separated them all. After Stitch freed Link, the latter stuck Gantu and [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] together, allowing Lilo, Stitch and Mertle to escape the ship with Link.

Link later found his one true place teaching arguing couples to do things together by using his binds to help them bungee-jump off a cliff diving attraction.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Link, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Link participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Link made [[Link-age|an appearance]] in Season 2 of the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]], [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]], [[Spike (319)|Spike]], and [[Woody (507)|Woody]]. It is revealed that [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] reverted these experiments to evil using a recording of [[Angel (624)|Angel]]'s song, thus enabling them to wreak havoc on the [[Izayoi Island|island]]. Link used his powers to stick [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] together with [[Penny (Stitch!)|her rival]].

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Link is a small yellow [[w:c:aliens:Grundo|Grundo]]/rabbit-like experiment with large red eyes, a little dark yellow nose, a wide mouth, stubby arms and legs dotted with dark yellow fingers and toes, and two long antennae with orange stripes near the tips.

===Special abilities===
Link can fire a thick, blue, slimy, elastic, super-sticky goo from his antennae that binds arguing pairs together and is nearly indestructible, capable of resisting even Stitch’s and Gantu’s strength.. Also, his eyes have targeting and zooming vision.

===Weaknesses===
Link's immobilizing bind is designed to have indestructible function qualities on fifty different planets. However, Earth is not included on the list, and his binds dissolve when covered in mud.

==Trivia==
*According to Lilo, she named 251 "Link" not because he links individuals together, but because it is short for Linkenstein (the zombie president).
*Link is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having red eyes instead.
*Link is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to.
**He is also one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to.
*Link's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green.
*The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Link as: "Experiment 251. Primary function: Binds together incompatible individuals."
*In the English dub of the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime episode "[[Link-age]]", [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] states that Link's favorite type of sandwich is reverse hot dogs.
*Ironically, his ability ended up having the opposite goal of what Jumba intended, though it is implied he would have reprogrammed Link anyways.

'''Lorider''', also known as '''Experiment 047''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to publicly humiliate victims by pulling down their pants (hence the name Lo-Rider). Jumba would often release him in crowds and meetings. He appears in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 047 was the 47th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to yank down victims' pants, causing humiliation to the victim. 047 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba on his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
In "[[Stitch's Birthday, Part One]]", Lorider was activated, pulled a public speaker's pants down, and when the speaker pulled them up and started to run, Lorider tripped him. Lorider then pulled down the pants of various participants until he was eventually captured by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]].

==Personality==
Lorider delights in humiliating victims, and he won't stop embarrassing them until he gets the full effect. He also acts somewhat like a dog, sniffing the target before embarrassing them.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Lorider is a blue platypus-like experiment with small eyes and a purple accordion-like body.

===Special abilities===
Lorider can extend his accordion-like body to stretch up to someone's waist, and then he pulls down their pants.

Lorider makes quacking noises when he jumps, stretches, or walks.

==Trivia==
*His name in Japanese is ローライダー, which translates directly to Lowrider (a literal translation of its name).

*Lorider is not identified as an experiment in the English dub credits of his only appearance, instead only being credited as "Alien Platypus". It is unknown why the credits removed his proper identity.

'''Manners''', also known as '''Experiment 358''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to give individuals painfully perfect manners. With a wave of dust from his fingers, his victims become too polite to fight back. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "[[:Category:Mrs. Hasagawa's experiments|cats]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 358 was the 358th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to make individuals too polite to fight back against hostile forces. 358 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]]. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 358's pod being one of them.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 358's pod for an apricot and washed it, activating the experiment. However, since 358 was not a very evil or destructive experiment, he was able to live a peaceful life with her, due to the latter seeing the former as a mere stray cat who needed a home.

When [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] discovered that Mrs. Hasagawa kept several experiments as pets, they thought they were a danger to her and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], decided to capture them all. Earlier, 358 politely greeted Lilo and Stitch at [[Mrs. Hasagawa's House|Mrs. Hasagawa's door]] and let them in. Jumba and Pleakley started arguing over who was going to capture 358. Seeing this, the experiment demonstrated his power of making individuals overly polite on them. Despite Jumba and Pleakley being too polite to capture experiments, 358 was [[Prison Capsule|captured]] anyway by unknown means.

358 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 358 was then named Manners.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Manners, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Manners participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did. However, it is presumed that he would have been able to use his powers to make attacking Leroys too polite to fight.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[disney:Aloha `Oe|Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Personality==
Unlike most experiments, Manners does not cause actual mischief nor chaos. Nevertheless, as part of his programming, he is polite to a fault and doesn't like it when others argue or fight. Thus, he will use his powers to force them to be polite and get along. However, he is not mean-spirited and simply wants everyone to be polite and behave.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Manners is a black and white penguin or orca-like experiment with short ears, a brown nose and three black spines with white stripes on his back (yellow in official artwork) that looks like a doorman or butler.

===Special abilities===
Manners can sprinkle a sparkly dust from his fingers that causes his victims to become extremely polite. He can [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]], with a British accent, and is also very polite himself, often acting like a butler.

===Weaknesses===
The effect of Manners' politeness-inducing dust presumably wears off after a while.

==Trivia==
*Manners' appearance and British accent are a likely reference to most classic British butlers.
*Manners was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*The first time Manners' spines appear when he bows, they are yellow; then when the scene changes to where he is beside the door, his spines are black.
*The stripes on his spines are inconsistently colored; they are yellow when he bows and in his official artwork, but are white for the rest of the episode.
*Manners is one of the few known experiments that can [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]].
*Manners is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.

Experiment 455 was the 455th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. ===''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''===

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point after this, Experiment 455 was presumably captured and named Mary.

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Mary was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but she is 536 instead of 455.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Mary, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. Mary is a large, round peach-colored experiment with two long white-tipped antennae, three large white stripes on her back, a white stomach, and a red nose.

===Special abilities===
Being Jumba's bouncer, Mary can hip-check unwanted guests. She also bounces rather than walks.

==Trivia==

'''Melty''', also known as '''Experiment 228''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to liquefy enemy fortresses, weapons, and transportation by firing blue energy blasts that melt any solid object when hit. His one true place is melting metal at the aluminum recycling plant.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 228 was the 228th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his blue energy blasts to melt enemy targets. 228 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 228's pod landing in a palm tree.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Melty - Melty after activation.png|thumb|left|Melty after being activated]]
When a gust of wind blew 228's pod out of the tree, a dog found it on the ground and took it back to its home. There, the dog dropped the pod into its bowl of water, activating the experiment. The dog growled at 228 who proceeded to melt the house, scaring the dog away.

228 later attacked the parking lot near the [[Birds of Paradise Hotel]] while [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] gave chase. He soon captured 228 using a metal chimney cap from the roof of the hotel.

Prior to catching 228, named Melty, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] got knocked into a mud puddle by Melty and made an idiot out of herself in front of [[Keoni Jameson|Keoni]]. She and Stitch later learned about [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s [[Time Machine|time-traveling surfboard]] and decided to use it to go back in time and change the past.

In several alternate timelines created by Lilo and Stitch meddling with time travel, Melty's fate was different:
*In one timeline, Lilo barely avoided embarrassing herself by falling in the pool of mud, but Stitch's change of action caused Melty to melt the hotel, and he was caught in a fashion similar to [[Sparky (221)|Sparky]]. As a result, [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] was promptly fired from her job, causing Lilo and Stitch to start over.
*In the next timeline, Lilo easily avoided her previous mistake, but when Stitch tried to react his original steps, he accidentally threw off the balance of a falling tree, which destroyed [[Officer Kahiko]]'s car, resulting in Lilo and Stitch being thrown in prison.
*In the third timeline, Lilo caused a chain reaction: she placed her hand against a palm tree and startled a butterfly, causing it to fly above the ocean where a fish jumped up and ate it; an eagle then snatched the fish and dropped it onto a ship's windshield, which startled the captain who then fell backward onto a green button, causing his cruise ship to crash into the hotel, but Melty's fate was unknown in this timeline.
*In the fourth timeline, Melty's fate was unknown, as Stitch forgot to turn on the paradox inhibitor, therefore causing him and Lilo to meet themselves.
*In the fifth timeline, Melty was unintentionally hurled into the ocean, where his melting blasts opened up a volcanic fissure in the ocean floor, causing a massive tsunami to form and destroy part of [[Kauai]].
*In the sixth timeline, Melty was captured exactly like in the original, but Stitch caused a chain reaction this time: he blew off a feather that fell onto his arm, causing the feather to land on an unstable coconut, which fell off its pile and bounced down a hill onto a golf tee, where it got whacked into the air by an elderly golfer and hit the roof of [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]] with a loud thud, waking [[Gantu]] up. When [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] revealed Melty's activation to Gantu, the latter then searched for the experiment at the hotel and wrecked it before coming to the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]]. After Melty melted his [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] and their entire house, Gantu recaptured him. The time-traveling surfboard was melted as well, causing future alternate timeline Jumba (whom Lilo and Stitch accidentally met when unintentionally going forward in time) to go back and give them a new time-traveling surfboard.
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Melty - Stitch protecting Melty.png|thumb|Stitch protecting Melty]]
*In the final timeline, and one corresponding to the original, Lilo and Stitch simply imitated their previous actions, but this made Lilo forcibly embarrass herself in front of Keoni again. They captured Melty the same way as before and took him home. Stitch then guarded Melty like a hawk in case Gantu decided to show up and rip off the roof of the house like he did in the previous timeline. Keoni even paid Lilo a visit to cheer her up, and thus everything turned out better than they had expected.

In the original and final timelines (in which Gantu slept peacefully and was never informed about Melty's activation), Melty was given a one true place burning metal at the aluminum recycling plant.

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Melty was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Melty, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Melty participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by shooting attacking Leroys with blue energy blasts.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Melty made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Melty is a rather simple-minded experiment, taking enjoyment in melting anything in sight, even when he is captured. One of his great advantages is that he will not be rendered powerless if his snout gets wet, as he is shown to be able to attack while underwater. He is also shown to be easily irritated and rather blunt, but is loyal to those who win his trust.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Melty is a small, red dragon-like experiment with tan patches on his stomach, chest and around his eyes, small bat-like wings, a long devil-shaped tail, a reptilian head with thin pointed antennae with dark red markings, black eyes and a thin body. His arms and legs are rather stubby in appearance. He prefers walking upright most of the time, though he is capable of quadruped movement.

===Special abilities===
Melty can fire blue balls of energy blasts from his snout that cause anything they hit to melt like chocolate. These energy blasts are extremely heated to the point that they will remain lethal, even when shot underwater. He can also fly.

==Trivia==
*Melty greatly resembles [[disney:Mushu|Mushu]] from ''[[disney:Mulan (1998 film)|Mulan]]'' in appearance, color, and that they are both dragons. However, unlike Melty, Mushu lacks wings and cannot fly.
*Melty, [[Bugby (128)|Bugby]], [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]], [[Jam (202)|Jam]], [[Wishy-Washy (267)|Wishy-Washy]], [[Snooty (277)|Snooty]], [[Amnesio (303)|Amnesio]], [[Hunkahunka (323)|Hunkahunka]], [[Experiments#5-Series: Elemental and environmental manipulators|Blake]], [[Slugger (608)|Slugger]], [[Witch (610)|Witch]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Miscellaneous|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have wings.
*Melty, [[Yang (502)|Yang]], [[Heat (609)|Heat]], [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]], and [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]] are the only known experiments whose powers are related to fire.
*Melty's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green.
*The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Melty as: "Experiment 228. Primary function: liquefaction of enemy fortresses, weaponry, and transportation."
*Melty's body, ears, wings, and tail appear in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.

'''Millie''', also known as '''Experiment 220''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. She is designed to plug up air holes in filters crucial to all hyperdrives.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 220 was the 220th genetic experiment created by Jumba with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. She was designed plug the holes in air filters crucial to all H-drives. 220 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At some point, 220 was activated, captured, tamed, and named Millie.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Millie, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], Stitch, Jumba, [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Millie participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by grabbing and strangling Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Millie is a giant green millipede-like experiment with a koala-like face, a wide mouth, a big blue nose, black eyes, [[Nosy (199)|Nosy]]-like ears and ten short tentacle-like limbs. Her legs are stubby and dotted with black toes.

===Special abilities===
Millie can plug holes in air filters by using her long tentacle-like arms.

==Trivia==
*Millie and [[Yin (501)|Yin]] are the only two experiments with the most limbs out of any known experiments, with ten and eleven respectively. Millie has eight tentacle-like arms and two tentacle-like legs, while Yin has eight tentacles, two tiny arms, and one large slug-like foot.

The '''Mo''' is an illegal genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba]], and [[Jumba's Chinese Experiments|the eighth experiment he created]] in China based on what he learns in ancient Chinese scrolls.

==Background==
==="[[Dream On]]"===
[[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and [[Wang Ai Ling|Ai]] started having nightmares. Then Jumba, based on the new scrolls, decides to create an experiment based on Mo, which devours nightmares. Meanwhile, Ai goes to the valley of dreams and disappears there, and Jumba, Stitch and the Mo rush to her rescue. However, by the time Stitch and the Mo get to Ai, she has already conquered her nightmares. The Mo is a pretty calm experiment that happily performs its function helping to get rid of nightmares.

The Mo is yellow in color with a trunk, antennae and tail. He has two arms and two legs and walks on two legs. He has a white belly and dark yellow patterns on his head, back, and arms.

===Special abilities===
The Mo's main function is to eat nightmares, and he does it with his trunk. He pulls his tongue out of his trunk and sticks it into someone's ear and starts poking around in his head, sticking his tongue out of his ears and nose. After completing the operation, he blows air into the trunk, pulling the creature towards him. Additionally, he is also able to curl up into a ball like Stitch.

*It is also the only Chinese experiment whose congeners were shown that were not created by Jumba.

'''Morpholomew''', also known as '''Experiment 316''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to morph organisms into an exact duplicate of any other, after seeing the target organism or a photo of it for reference; however, the recipient's vocal cords will stay identical. His one true place is at a [[Costumes|costume store]], morphing people into celebrities.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 316 was the 316th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to morph organisms into any other organism. 316 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 316's pod landing on a hay umbrella.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Morpholomew - Morpholomew moments after activation.png|thumb|left|Morpholomew moments after his activation]]
At the very beginning of the [[Morpholomew (episode)|episode]], [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] decided to enter the local skateboarding competition in order to win a brand new skateboard, the Velociraptor 1200, for her crush [[Keoni Jameson|Keoni]]. Before the event, she and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] discovered Experiment 316, whose pod was activated in a fountain after Stitch unstuck Lilo's skateboard from a straw umbrella. According to [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], Experiment 316, or Morpholomew, was a creature capable of giving anyone the appearance of someone else. Lilo used this power in order to enter the competition as Keoni.

In the meantime, [[Jake Long|Jake]], [[Luong Lao Shi|Lao Shi]], [[Fu Dog]], [[Trixie Carter|Trixie]] and [[Arthur Spudinski|Spud]] arrived at the [[Kauai]] skate park. They were investigating reports of undisguised magical creatures lurking on the island of Hawaii (actually Jumba's illegal genetic experiments), although Jake was more interested in winning the contest's grand prize. All of them separated to go on their own business: Lao Shi became enamored with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]; Trixie and Spud headed to the beach; Fu Dog went to place some bets on Jake while the latter signed up for the skateboarding competition.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Morpholomew - Morpholomew eating a chicken leg.png|thumb|Eating a chicken leg]]
Lilo did the same, but soon realized that impersonating Keoni was likely a bad idea when she earned a low score. She asked Morpholomew to change her into absolutely anybody else so she could start over, but registrations closed before she got a chance to sign up again.

Elsewhere, Jake, having spotted Morpholomew with Lilo and mistaking the little red blob for a magical creature, transformed into the American Dragon and got ready to pursue them. However, he was [[Prison Capsule|captured]] by [[Gantu]] who mistook him for Morpholomew. Since Jake didn't show for the competition, Lilo decided to ask Morpholomew to turn her into Jake so she could enter in his stead.

Meanwhile, Jake managed to escape [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]] before he was transferred to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|asteroid]] and went back to the skate park. However, Lilo had already taken his place and failed once again to score any points. Trixie and Spud grew suspicious of Lilo (still disguised as Jake) while she threw a tantrum when Stitch told her that Morpholomew (who earlier got distracted by a rabbit) had been captured by Gantu. They knew something was up when Lilo panicked upon hearing Fu Dog speak. The real Jake (in his dragon form) arrived at that moment and engaged in a duel with Stitch. Before things got too far, Lilo managed to calm everyone down and explain the whole situation.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Morpholomew - Heroes arrive on Gantu's ship.png|thumb|left|Morpholomew with Lilo, Stitch, Jake Long, Trixie and Fu Dog]]
Once everything was clarified, everyone decided to team up to retrieve Morpholomew. They traveled over to Gantu's ship and fought against him for Morpholomew. In the confusion, Jake and company tricked Gantu into thinking he captured Morpholomew, when in reality, Spud assumed the little red blob's form and got kidnapped instead. Thanks to this, the team managed to get Morpholomew back and change Gantu into a little white bunny as punishment for all the trouble he caused.

The gang then headed back to the skateboard competition, where the winner claimed the Velociraptor 1200. Jake and Lilo were a bit bummed out by this, but were happy to have made new friends. They left on good terms and promised to see each other again soon. Meanwhile, Morpholomew was given a one true place at a [[Costumes|costume store]], where he morphed people into celebrities according to the photo he was shown.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
Morpholomew was seen early in the movie morphing the [[Ice Cream Man]] into the famous [[wikipedia:Elvis Presley|Elvis]] as [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to make sure all the experiments were happy in the one true place they belonged.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Morpholomew, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

It is unknown whether or not Morpholomew participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Morpholomew made [[Lilo (episode)|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] [[Transmutation|transmutated]] him to morph his own body instead of others and also [[:Category:Talking experiments|gave him a vocabulary]]. At an unknown time after this, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], now an adult, took a vacation with her daughter, [[Ani Pelekai|Ani]], to an [[Izayoi Island|island]] in Japan where, unbeknownst to them, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] resided at the time. Ani met Stitch, who mistook her for a de-aged Lilo, and they played together contentedly. Hämsterviel took advantage of this and sent [[Gantu]] to use Morpholomew to take the image of her and distract Stitch long enough to capture him.

Morpholomew [[Dark-End|later appeared]] as one of the experiments who helped Stitch fight [[Dark End]]. He also appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Morpholomew is very curious, as seen when he chased a noise which turned out to be a rabbit. He is also one of the few experiments that demands payment, which he considers to be chicken legs. He enjoys chicken legs so much that he can easily go through several buckets of them in only a few minutes. While he is cautious of others at first, he is friendly and trusting, as he immediately befriended Stitch after the latter pursued him and pronounced him his cousin and ally, even shaking hands. He is fairly relaxed and doesn't mind helping individuals. He also seems to have a sense of humor, as he once changed Gantu into a harmless bunny.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Morpholomew is a small, red blob-like experiment with a small body, two small arms, two short legs, a short tail, a thin mouth, and black eyes.

===Special abilities===
Morpholomew can alter the appearance of any organism into any other organism, even if it is not the same species. To do this, he must see the target organism or a photo of the target at least once before he can change them. He then touches the recipient while briefly changing his own head to that of the target organism and morphs their appearance to that of the target's. The recipient's vocal cords stay identical, however.

He can morph his own body instead of others, but he has only displayed this while [[Transmutation|under the effects]] of [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. He is also seen to be able to [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]], though it is unknown if this is because of Hämsterviel transmuting him or if he was always capable of speaking and learned over time.

===Weaknesses===
Morpholomew ''must'' have the image of the requested form in his head for the transformation to work.

==Trivia==
*Morpholomew is one of the ten known experiments named by someone other than Lilo or Stitch, the other nine being [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Elastico (345)|Elastico]], [[Yaarp (613)|Yaarp]], [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]], [[Heat (609)|Heat]], [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]], [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]], [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]], and [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]].
**He also is the only experiment named by a character from outside the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]], as Spud from ''[[disney:American Dragon: Jake Long|American Dragon: Jake Long]]'' named him.
**Lilo initially planned to name 316 "Changer", but Trixie convinced her that he should have a better name, with Spud being the one to name him "Morpholomew".
**His name is a mix between "[[wikipedia:Morphology (biology)|Morphology]]" and "[[wikipedia:Bartholomew the Apostle|Bartholomew]]".
*Morpholomew is one of the rare experiments to turn from bad to good the fastest, as once Stitch introduced himself as his cousin, Morpholomew quickly reformed.
*In [[Morpholomew (episode)|his debut]], it is revealed that Morpholomew loves chicken legs, as he was seen eating them out of a bucket, and said poultry is also used as a fee in his one true place.
*Morpholomew and [[Spooky (300)|Spooky]] are the only known experiments that have shapeshifting/transforming abilities.
*It is unclear if Morpholomew can use his shapeshifting ability on himself or not (aside from changing his face when morphing others), although Gantu assumed the former when Jake Long transformed into his dragon form, as he was mistaken for Morpholomew by Gantu.
*Morpholomew's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is yellow.
*Morpholomew, [[Spats (397)|Spats]], and [[Lax (285)|Lax]] are the only experiments that debuted in [[:Category:Crossovers|crossovers]].
**Morpholomew is also the only experiment from a crossover episode that appeared in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.
**Additionally, Morpholomew's crocodile form in the anime greatly resembles [[disney:Tick-Tock the Crocodile|Tick-Tock]] from ''[[disney:Peter Pan (film)|Peter Pan]]''.
*Morpholomew is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
*The experiments list seen in the [[Experiments/Gallery#Leroy & Stitch|end credits]] of ''Leroy & Stitch'' spells his name as "Morpholemew", with an "e" replacing the third "o"; the [[disney:Disney+|Disney+]] listing of his episode reaffirms the correct spelling of his name to be with three "o"'s and one "e".
**Considering that the partial inspiration for his name is also spelled in English with an "o" before "mew", it can be assumed that the experiments list entry is a misspelling.

'''Mr. Stenchy''', also known as '''Experiment 254''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to use his alluring charm to get the enemy to take him back to their headquarters, where, 48 hours after his activation, he emits a foul odor that makes the location inhospitable. His one true place is on [[Plorgonar]] ([[Pleakley]]'s home planet), where, unlike most places in the galaxy, his stench is considered a rare and valuable perfume.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 254 was the 254th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his cuteness to smitten Jumba's enemies into taking him back to their headquarters, where 254 would emit a noxious stench that would make 40 square miles of the area uninhabitable for decades. 254 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 254 was activated.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Mr. Stenchy - Stitch scowling at Mr. Stenchy while holding him on a vinyl record.png|thumb|left|Mr. Stenchy with Stitch]]
An estimated twelve hours after his activation, 254 was [[Prison Capsule|captured]] by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and taken back to their [[Lilo's House|house]], but not before being pursued by a persistent [[Gantu]]. 

Lilo fell for 254's cuteness and decided to keep the newly-christened Mr. Stenchy, despite [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s warnings of the experiment's inevitable stench that, when released, would make Mr. Stenchy reek. Stitch, however, became jealous of Mr. Stenchy and was immune to the latter's charm. He even relentlessly bullied and tormented Mr. Stenchy.

Later, Lilo began taking Mr. Stenchy to [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]]'s FHGH (Future Hawaiian Girls of Hawaii) tea parties in an attempt for the former to be accepted into their group. Of course, Mertle and [[Elena|the]] [[Teresa|hula]] [[Yuki|girls]] had also fallen for Mr. Stenchy's cuteness after Lilo first introduced him to them.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Mr. Stenchy - Mr. Stenchy offering Stitch a lollipop.png|thumb|Mr. Stenchy offering Stitch a lollipop]]
When Stitch was left home alone with Mr. Stenchy, the latter made a vain attempt to befriend Stitch, not wanting them to be enemies. However, he ignored Mr. Stenchy's efforts and then locked the diminutive experiment in the pantry. Gantu later attacked the house, but Stitch, having two shoulder devils, goaded Gantu into taking Mr. Stenchy so that the former would be rid of them both.

Later, when Lilo and the others returned to discover their home in disarray, Stitch gave his version of what happened. Jumba revealed that Gantu had kidnapped Mr. Stenchy who was likely already transported to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], much to Lilo's sadness. However, back at [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]], Gantu also fell for Mr. Stenchy's charm before he could teleport the latter to Hämsterviel. He then decided to keep the ravishing experiment for a while after developing an affection for him. This made [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] envious like Stitch, though Gantu took little notice.

The next day, Lilo was still depressed and assumed that Mertle and the hula girls wouldn't be her friend if she didn't bring Mr. Stenchy to their tea party. [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] assured Lilo that Stitch was her true friend because although he could often be a nuisance, he always looked out for Lilo and would never try to hurt her. This made Stitch feel very sad and guilty for what he did to Mr. Stenchy. When Lilo later chose to attend Mertle's tea party anyway, Stitch arrived beforehand dressed in a makeshift Mr. Stenchy costume and tried to mingle. However, his overzealous actions caused Mertle to expose "Mr. Stenchy" as an impostor and permanently oust Lilo from the FHGH group.

Later that evening, Lilo had a talk with Stitch. She knew that he dressed up as Mr. Stenchy because he didn't want her to feel left out of Mertle's FHGH tea party. She also blamed herself for letting Gantu take off with Mr. Stenchy and lamented about him never finding his one true place. This caused Stitch to feel even more guilty, knowing that it was actually his fault. He then used [[Jumba's Computer|Jumba's computer]] to pull up a schematic diagram of Gantu's ship and made up his mind to break in and rescue Mr. Stenchy.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Mr. Stenchy - Gantu cuddles Mr. Stenchy.png|thumb|left|Mr. Stenchy with Gantu]]
Meanwhile, Gantu grew attached to Mr. Stenchy and kept pampering him. Reuben voiced his displeasure and became increasingly jealous, though he denied this when Gantu asked him. Just then, Stitch broke into the ship to save his cousin and attacked Reuben, only for Gantu to capture him and put him in a teleport chamber. As Gantu prepared to send Stitch to a desert asteroid, the latter discreetly requested Reuben's help so he could nab Mr. Stenchy, resulting in Gantu discovering Reuben in the teleporter instead. While being distracted, Stitch pounced and forced Gantu into a small room. He then grabbed Mr. Stenchy and tried to leave, but Gantu managed to escape the room and blasted Stitch into a [[Net Cannon|net]].

Shortly after, Lilo, Jumba and [[Pleakley]] broke into the ship as well to help out. After Stitch was freed, he and the others coaxed Mr. Stenchy to come back with them, as did Gantu. Due to Stitch abandoning him earlier, Mr. Stenchy chose Gantu. However, the pint-sized experiment then began to emit his stench, forcing Gantu to hand the former over. Although Lilo, Stitch, Jumba and Gantu were all repulsed by Mr. Stenchy's stink, Pleakley was surprisingly appealed to it, even claiming the odor to be a rare and valuable perfume.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Mr. Stenchy - Mr. Stenchy with his new family.png|thumb|Mr. Stenchy with his family]]
After being rescued, Mr. Stenchy was sent to [[Plorgonar]] in a rocket, where he could be loved in spite of his fetid smell, as it was considered pleasing on Pleakley's home planet. Upon landing, the rocket opened its hatch, and Mr. Stenchy was discovered by an alien couple who got a whiff of his "delicious aroma". They immediately fell in love with Mr. Stenchy, as he smelled just like their "first date", much to his joy.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
Mr. Stenchy inexplicably reappeared back on Earth and not producing his noxious odor, suggesting it wears off after a while.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Mr. Stenchy, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Mr. Stenchy participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe, during which Mr. Stenchy can be seen around some of the Leroys as they started to shut down.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Mr. Stenchy has appeared twice in the ''Stitch!'' anime. In the [[A Stinky Episode|first appearance]], he was seen at the very end being infatuated with [[Skunkuna]], and it is revealed that a mixture of Mr. Stenchy and Skunkuna's odor oddly enough creates an air freshener. In the [[A Very Stinky Christmas|second appearance]], [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] [[Transmutation|mass-produced clones]] of Mr. Stenchy and [[Mrs. Sickly (255)|Mrs. Sickly]] and sold them to many children across Japan and the rest of the world. This is when it is revealed that if the emissions from these two mix, the chemical reaction will cause a cataclysmic explosion capable of destroying the planetary body they inhabit. This leads to [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]], [[Pleakley]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], Hämsterviel and [[Gantu]] on a hunt to round up the clones of Mr. Stenchy and Mrs. Sickly in order to save the world's Christmas. After saving the world's Christmas, Mr. Stenchy (and Mrs. Sickly) was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in Jumba's vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help Stitch in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Mr. Stenchy wasn't one of the experiments that was activated. He also appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Due to his disarming cuteness, Mr. Stenchy gains very much attention from humans and most alien species. He also appears to act as cute as he looks, being very loving and friendly towards anyone who gives him affection. However, he is shown to be somewhat wary, such as when Stitch mistreated him and then later attempted to rescue him.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Mr. Stenchy is a small, irresistibly cute light pink experiment with a big head with big blue eyes, two puffy antennae, a small tuft of hair and a small body.

===Special abilities===
Mr. Stenchy appears disarmingly cute to everyone except other experiments, but then emits an extremely noxious, foul odor 48 hours after he is activated, which makes 40 square miles of an area uninhabitable for decades. If Mr. Stenchy's sour emissions intermix with [[Mrs. Sickly (255)|Mrs. Sickly]]'s nauseatingly sweet emissions, the chemical reaction will cause a cataclysmic explosion capable of destroying the planetary body they inhabit. 

===Weaknesses===
Apart from his disarming cuteness and noxious stink, Mr. Stenchy is mostly defenseless. Also, while humans and most alien species are actually influenced by Mr. Stenchy's charm, other experiments are immune to the effects.

==Trivia==
*Mr. Stenchy was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
**In the Experiment Finder game, Mr. Stenchy's one true place can be inside an alley filled with garbage cans, where individuals won't distinguish his smell from other foul smells.
*Mr. Stenchy was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Mr. Stenchy is one of the rare experiments to have sclerae and pupils instead of solid black eyes, the others being [[Mrs. Sickly (255)|Mrs. Sickly]], [[Skip (089)|Skip]], [[Clink (086)|Clink]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], [[Bragg (145)|Bragg]], [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]], [[Experiments#Other experiments|Tippy]], [[Experiments#3-Series: Psychological|Slobber]], and [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|four unconfirmed experiments]].
*Stitch and Reuben were unmoved by Mr. Stenchy's cuteness, as Jumba pointed out that other experiments are immune to Mr. Stenchy's charm.
*It is revealed that Pleakley's [[Plorgonarian|alien species]] is the only species which finds Mr. Stenchy's stink appealing. This is because their antenna, which also functions similar to a nose, functions somewhat differently when it comes to scents, allowing them to ignore or appreciate odors which humans and most aliens would consider noxious and horrible, as Pleakley and the Plorgonarian couple who found Mr. Stenchy were delighted by his odor; whereas Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, and Gantu were repulsed by it.
*Mr. Stenchy is one of the only known experiments whose one true place is not on Earth.
*In ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', Mr. Stenchy inexplicably returned to Earth from Plorgonar, though it is possible he was simply visiting the planet. Also, he did not produce his stink, suggesting it wears off after a while or he has learned how to control it.
*Mr. Stenchy's head, antennae, and ears appear in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.
*In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, Mr. Stenchy has a wife named Mrs. Sickly.
**Mr. Stenchy's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is white in the anime.
