'''Mulch''', also known as '''Experiment 111''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]]. He is designed to tear up the ground beneath his feet. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "[[:Category:Mrs. Hasagawa's experiments|cats]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 111 was the 111th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to tear up the ground beneath him. 111 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]]. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 111's pod being one of them.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 111's pod for an apricot and placed it in a colander for later consumption along with numerous other pods.

After [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] redecorated Mrs. Hasagawa's yard without her permission, she was less than thrilled with the results, but decided to thank them for their work with the "apricots". The pods were then revealed, but before Lilo and Stitch could stop her, she washed them with a watering can, thus activating the experiments.

After his activation, 111 began to carry out his primary function by tearing up the lawn in Mrs. Hasagawa's yard. Lilo and Stitch believed the experiments to be a danger to Mrs. Hasagawa and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], decided to capture them all. When Stitch was trying to convince [[Boomer (288)|Experiment 288]] to go into a [[Prison Capsule|container]], 111 started approaching. Stitch then threw 288 into the air and used the container to capture 111 instead.

111 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 111 was then named Mulch.

In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Mulch was oddly seen as one of the captive experiments in [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison cell]], although he is barely seen, suggesting [[Gantu]] caught Mulch, but this was an error. Mulch was then sent back to Gantu after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused mischief and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Mulch, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Mulch participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Mulch is a red experiment with a blue nose, three tendrils on his back, gray patches around his eyes, white markings on his chest, stomach and rear that resembles a push-mower.

===Special abilities===
Mulch can tear up the ground beneath him like a push mower by using his mower-like body.

===Weaknesses===
Mulch doesn't always seem to pay attention to where he is going, as he was captured effortlessly in both [[Mrs. Hasagawa's Cats|his debut]] and ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.

==Trivia==
*Mulch doesn't always seem to look where he is going, as Stitch was able capture him by placing a containment orb in his path. Similarly, he was easily captured by a [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clone]] by walking onto a net trap in plain sight.
*Mulch's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue.
*In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Mulch erroneously appeared with Gantu's other captive experiments, although he is barely seen, but he was already living with Mrs. Hasagawa, and Lilo and Stitch discovered him while Gantu was asleep.
*Mulch and [[Splat (519)|Splat]] are the only known experiments to have a set of rollers as limbs. In Mulch's case, they are his hind limbs.
*Mulch is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.

The "'''Naughty Creatures'''" are illegal genetic experiments created by [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. They are considered among the [[Jumba's Chinese Experiments|experiments Jumba created in China]] based on what he learns in ancient Chinese scrolls.

==Background==
==="[[Nuo Opera]]"===
[[Wang Ai Ling|Ai]] does not allow Stitch to attend the opera, saying that he will be naughty there. Then Stitch, offended, decides to create eight prankster creatures in secret from [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] in order to take revenge on Ai. They start wreaking havoc with Stitch. But later, Stitch becomes ashamed, so he re-educates them and directs them to good, helping to carry out the almost cancelled opera. Later, like the rest of the Chinese experiments, they were sent to a parallel dimension.

==Personality==
All eight creatures are restless pranksters who, without listening to anyone, start destroying everything around them. However, as it turned out, they can listen and direct their efforts in a good direction.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
A total of eight creatures were represented:

*Red - A four-legged creature with yellow horns
*Yellow - A baby dragon-like creature with a long tail and brown deer-like antlers
*Blue - A winged blue creature with four legs and light blue appendages
*Russet - A four-legged creature with fangs like 619 ([[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]]), long ears like 158 ([[Finder (158)|Finder]]), and a short tail
*Green - A four-legged creature with light green fur on its chest and a light green tail, as well as a large horn
*Periwinkle - A creature with a huge jaw, multiple arms, and very short legs
*Purple - A turtle-like creature with a brown shell
*Brown - A creature similar to a regular rhinoceros, except light brown in color

===Special abilities===
Every creature has its own ability. The red creature has a huge jaw and can easily gnaw objects, spit objects from his mouth at a rapid rate of fire, grab and swallow objects with his long tongue, and sing. He is also seemingly resistant to poisonous chemicals as he swallowed [[Wang Daiyu|Daiyu]]'s bottle of sanitizer. The blue creature is able to fly. The russet creature can jump very deftly, grab objects with its hind feet, and spin into a vortex. It also used lollipops to deflect gumballs into the others' mouths when they raided a candy store. The green creature can easily throw a person upward using its horn. The periwinkle creature can quickly convert objects put into its mouth into pearls like a [[wikipedia:Pinctada|pearl oyster]] (although this ability does not seem to work on edible objects such as candy), shoot objects from its jaw, and is very strong. The brown creature has durable skin and can ram and batter down objects in its way, much like a real rhinoceros. All creatures can jump well, with the exception of the brown rhinoceros creature, and are difficult to catch.

===Weaknesses===
They are all sensitive to high-pitched sounds, as Jumba blows into a whistle to stop their disruption of the nuo opera's rehearsal, causing them to disperse.

==Trivia==
*They along with the [[Mo]] are the only Chinese creatures that do not appear in "[[Monstrosity]]".
*They were also created by Stitch and not Jumba, so they are the only genetic experiments created by Stitch (and thus the first genetic experiments made by another genetic experiment), and the collective third experiments not created by Jumba.

==Background==
==="[[Tell the World]]"===
After receiving the ancient scrolls, Jumba was inspired to create a genetic experiment based on the Chinese mythical creatures that were in the scroll. This time, he created an experiment of abducting children. He escapes and kidnaps [[Wang Ai Ling|Ai]]'s friends. Then Ai figures out how to defeat Nian, but later it turns out that he loves horror movies and wants to become a star. Then she develops a cunning plan by offering him to act as a monster. He agrees and is working on completing the portfolio. The last task was to play the savior of children, then Nian, unaware of nothing, shows this place to Ai. Then he and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] free the children, and only after almost all the children had escaped did he realize that he had been tricked. He tries to defeat Stitch and Ai, but at that time, Jumba keeps up and sends Nian to a parallel dimension with the help of a new device.

==="[[Monstrosity]]"===
In this episode, Nian and some other Chinese experiments were summoned from a parallel dimension to battle the [[Jaboodie]]s.

==Personality==
Unlike the other Chinese experiments, Nian is extremely aggressive because he had the function of stealing children. He also expressed all emotions as anger. But later, it turned out that he really loves horror stories and filming and dreams of becoming a star. Soon after, the good part of his soul is revealed. It is also easy to fool him. In "[[Monstrosity]]", he is already kind and helps the main characters in the final battle with the aliens. He also laughed in this episode, so he apparently learned to express other emotions.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Nian is a two-legged orange experiment with two arms and claws. His belly looks like the belly of a crocodile or a dragon. It has yellow appendages on its arms and neck.

===Special abilities===
Nian has no special abilities, except for his extreme strength, which even Experiment 626 did not dare to fight him.

===Weaknesses===
His desire to become a star can be considered a weakness, as it can force him to do anything.

==Trivia==
*Nian is based on the Chinese mythological creature, [[wikipedia:Nian|nian]].
*Nian loves horror stories and wants to become a movie star.
*Nian is the only Chinese experiment that was based on a negative Chinese being.
*It is also the only experiment that was forcibly sent to a parallel dimension.
*It has been shown that Nian is unable to express emotions other than anger. However, you could see him laughing in Monstrosity, so maybe he learned it in a parallel dimension.

'''Nosox''', also known as '''Experiment 204''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to steal, hide, or otherwise make socks mysteriously vanish. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 204 was the 204th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to eat socks, and thus make them disappear. 204 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
204's pod was one of the twelve experiment pods recovered by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] in "[[Drowsy (episode)|Drowsy]]". His was one of the final four pods (among [[Stopgo (102)|102]], [[Experiments#2-Series: Technological and scientific|274]] and [[Drowsy (360)|360]]) that [[Pleakley]], with some assistance from Stitch, cataloged after being convinced to do so by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 204, named Nosox, was presumably activated and captured by [[Gantu]], as he was mentioned in "[[Amnesio (episode)|Amnesio]]" when [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] said, "After you sent me a sock hider..."

Nosox appeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by Lilo, Stitch, and several other experiments in a rescue mission.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Nosox, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

It is unknown whether or not Nosox participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Nosox made an appearance in [[Experiment-A-Palooza|a later episode]] of the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]], [[Squeak (110)|Squeak]], [[Clip (177)|Clip]], and [[Retro (210)|Retro]]. Eventually, Nosox was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Nosox wasn't one of the experiments that was activated.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Nosox is a quadrupedal, grey experiment shaped like a four-legged washing machine with a red button for a nose, two small ears, and small white eyes with black pupils, similar to [[Skip (089)|Skip]].

===Special abilities===
Nosox can steal socks and make them disappear by storing them in a washing machine-like container in his stomach.

==Trivia==
*Nosox is one of the rare experiments to have sclerae and pupils instead of solid black eyes, the others being [[Mr. Stenchy (254)|Mr. Stenchy]], [[Mrs. Sickly (255)|Mrs. Sickly]], [[Skip (089)|Skip]], [[Clink (086)|Clink]], [[Bragg (145)|Bragg]], [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]], [[Experiments#Other experiments|Tippy]], [[Experiments#3-Series: Psychological|Slobber]], and [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|four unconfirmed experiments]].
*Nosox, along with [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Dorkifier (122)|Dorkifier]], [[Butter (227)|Butter]], [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]], [[Spike (319)|Spike]], [[Yang (502)|Yang]], [[Richter (513)|Richter]], [[Phoon (540)|Phoon]], [[Tank (586)|Tank]], [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]], and one [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed experiment]], are the only known experiments that are primarily quadrupeds.  
*His name means "No Socks" (No Sox) because he is a sock hider.
*Nosox and [[Experiments#4-Series: Top secret and mysterious series of militaristic and mostly failed experiments|Patter]] are the only known experiments whose functions are related to stealing socks.
*Even though Nosox was mentioned twice in Season 1, he did not officially [[:Category:Season 2 Experiments|appear activated]] until near the end of Season 2.
**Nosox is the only experiment to be mentioned twice by function in two separate episodes without actually appearing activated. Ironically, we saw Nosox in [[Experiment Pods|pod]] form in the [[Drowsy (episode)|last episode]] of Season 1 with one of these mentions, even though he was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]] and captured by Gantu in an [[Amnesio (episode)|earlier episode]] of Season 1.
**This is similar to [[Fudgy (054)|Fudgy]], though he did [[:Category:Season 1 Experiments|appear activated]] in Season 1, but not fully seen. Interestingly, both of them were rescued from Gantu in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]".
*Nosox is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.
*He is also one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
*Nosox's pod color is blue in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

'''Nosy''', also known as '''Experiment 199''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to humiliate enemies by digging up their most embarrassing secrets, but had a flaw in his programming so that he only reveals juicy gossip. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but escaped in "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 199 was the 199th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to reveal his enemies' most humiliating secrets, but due to a glitch in his program, he preferred juicy gossip rather than anything important. 199 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 199 was activated.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Nosy - Nosy saunters off casually.png|thumb|left|Nosy disguised as a kid]]
199, disguised as a kid, had watched the new ''Wasp Mummies'' movie. As he exited the [[Cinema|theater]], he revealed the secret ending aloud to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] before sauntering off. Stitch, at that moment, saw through 199's disguise and captured him while exposing him as a cousin. 199 then rummaged through Lilo's duffel bag and dug up her diary.

Lilo and Stitch later took 199, named Nosy, back to their [[Lilo's House|house]], where he began to snoop around and unearth numerous secrets, including finding Lilo's catalog of local vampires under Stitch's pillow, causing the latter to glare at Nosy after he spilled the beans about it. [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] even regarded Nosy as one of his favorite experiments.

Later, when [[Keoni Jameson|Keoni]] and [[Mr. Jameson|his father]] both arrived at the Pelekai residence, invited to brunch by [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]], Nosy intervened by unveiling the Pelekais' secrets to the Jamesons. He first blurted out that Stitch, Jumba, [[Pleakley]], and Nosy himself were actually aliens, and then mentioned Lilo's obsessive crush on Keoni.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Nosy - Nosy with Gantu.png|thumb|Nosy with Gantu]]
As a result of Nosy becoming a nuisance, Stitch got rid of him, imprisoned him in a [[Prison Capsule|container]], and handed him to [[Gantu]] as a present. Delighted, Gantu expected Nosy to disclose all of Lilo and Stitch's experiment files. Instead, he talked about useless information and revealed secrets about Gantu to [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]], prompting the former to send Nosy to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]].

At the [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison asteroid]], when Nosy revealed Gantu and Reuben's secret disrespect towards Hämsterviel, the latter sent him back to Gantu as revenge (though Nosy was first able to steal Hämsterviel's diary). Nosy read Gantu Hämsterviel's diary, but the former was then kicked out of [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]] for the trouble he caused.

Thus, Nosy returned to the Pelekais' home, where he gossiped endlessly and exposed Stitch (in his "Kenny" disguise) as an alien genetic experiment after their tussle. However, he was shortly after recaptured by Gantu under Hämsterviel's orders, though Lilo and Stitch allowed Gantu to do so. Back at his ship, Nosy and Reuben exchanged rumors about Gantu.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spike - 'I should be taking notes. This is great stuff!'.png|thumb|left|Nosy in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group]]
In "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]", Nosy was one of the experiments in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group. He revealed to everyone that Pleakley's antenna was prematurely orange and simply dyed green before being reprimanded. Shortly after, Pleakley used Nosy in his aromatherapy (in which he rubbed Nosy with a smelly fish). When the other experiments later began to cause chaos, Nosy was chased by [[Spike (319)|Spike]] through the house. Near the end of the episode, Nosy tried out Pleakley's hugging-and-crying therapy.

In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Nosy was sent back to Gantu along with all of Hämsterviel's other captive experiments after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused chaos and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]]. Woops then accidentally smashed open Nosy's containment orb, allowing him to escape.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Woops - 'Yes, I am outta here!'.png|thumb|Nosy freed]]
In "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", Nosy traveled to the Pelekais' house, angry with Lilo for abandoning him and the other experiments to Gantu. He also revealed when Gantu's ship was empty and spied on both Gantu and Reuben, who were foiled by [[Snafu (120)|Experiment 120]] while attempting to revert all of the rehabilitated experiments to evil using a recording of [[Angel (624)|Angel]]'s song.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Nosy, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Nosy did not participate in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], instead choosing to retreat with the weaker experiments.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Nosy has appeared multiple times in the ''Stitch!'' anime, including [[Nosy Meets Tigerlily|one instance]] where he revealed everyone's secrets around the [[Izayoi Island|island]]. He eventually became such a nuisance that [[Angel (624)|Angel]] pummeled him in the end. In [[Stitch's Birthday, Part One|another episode]], Nosy divulged [[Delia]] and [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s plans to [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] on live television. He later appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Nosy behaves exactly the way he was designed and programmed. He will somehow try and discover any juicy info that can be listened to, read, or unveiled in any way, and uncaringly nose his way through other people's business. He will also tell anybody whatever he has managed to dig up, mostly embarrassing things. This is useful when needing to know plans from friends or enemies, but otherwise useless since Nosy likes to gossip about humiliating secrets rather than items of strategy, due to his glitch.

One of Nosy's biggest characteristics is his rather big mouth. Not just literally – he could talk for hours on end about stuff. He is also shown to be very emotional and sensitive, as he was seen crying after Pleakley managed to tame Spike during the E.A.R.W.A.X. seminar. He can hold a grudge, especially when it comes to things that are pinned on himself, such as never being rescued from his capture. Last of all, Nosy is never a fighter – when a battle comes his way, he will run away screaming rather than stand up and fight for himself.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Nosy is a magenta wombat/pig-like experiment with a pink underbelly from the chin down; a huge, round, reddish-brown nose, roughly taking up a good-sized amount of his entire head; a round body with thick, stubby legs ending in round feet and dotted with black toes; small, flabby arms ending in three fingers on each hand without any claws; a large wide mouth with a much bigger lantern jaw; little black eyes; small rabbit-like ears pointed downward; a large, black, blotch-shaped pattern on his back; and two black stripes on the front of his legs.

===Special abilities===
Nosy has expert escaping skills and stealth capabilities. He is talented in finding things that have been hidden or "lost", an example of his snooping. He is quick compared to the average human and is highly durable, though he was designed to embarrass enemies by using their secrets against them and reveal their battle tactics and the such to his master. Due to a programming glitch, however, he prefers juicy gossip rather than anything important. Nosy is among the few experiments that can [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]], although at the same time he can understand [[Tantalog language|Tantalog]].

===Weaknesses===
Nosy is defenseless when it comes to fighting, so he usually runs away from the battlefield instead of trying to fight.

==Trivia==

*He is also one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.
*According to [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]], Nosy is almost as annoying as [[Woops (600)|Woops]].

'''PJ''', also known as '''Experiment 133''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to play practical jokes on unsuspecting victims. His one true place is performing an opening act for [[Moses Puloki|Moses]]' hula gig.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 133 was the 133rd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to play practical jokes on victims, hence his name P(ractical) J(oker). 133 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:ScreenCapture 23.10.13 10-20-44.png|thumb|left|PJ moments after his activation]]
When a man using a metal detector on [[Lahui Beach|the beach]] uncovered an empty soda can with 133's pod, he decided that the pod wasn't worth anything, so he threw it into the water, activating the experiment. 133, named PJ (for Practical Joker), then proceeded to play practical jokes on everyone he could find. 

After a while, PJ ran into [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. When PJ pulled many pranks on Stitch, the latter attempted to beat him up, only to be stopped by Lilo, who pointed out that the annoying prankster was still Stitch's cousin.

PJ was later taken back to the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]], where [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] claimed that PJ's jokes could result in mayhem. Regardless, PJ relentlessly pranked Lilo's strict substitute teacher for her [[Kaiāulu Hale|hula class]], while unknowingly framing Lilo for it.

[[File:ScreenCapture 25.10.13 21-25-09.jpg|thumb|PJ pranking Stitch]]
Later, Lilo wanted to play a spiteful joke on her harsh substitute teacher, despite Stitch's protests. PJ then pulled some more pranks on Stitch when the latter tried to capture him. However, Stitch eventually scooped PJ in a [[Prison Capsule|container]] so that he wouldn't cause further chaos.

When Stitch refused to allow PJ to help with Lilo's scheme, she used [[Drowsy (360)|Drowsy]] to put Stitch to sleep and released PJ from containment for his assistance. PJ then cleverly formulated a plan to humiliate Lilo's substitute teacher with the ultimate practical joke.

Stitch somehow later woke up on his own and triggered a booby trap set up by PJ, resulting in Stitch getting stuck inside PJ's containment orb. The next morning, Stitch was freed from containment by [[Pleakley]]. The former then rushed to Lilo's hula school, hoping to prevent her and PJ from pulling their prank.

[[File:ScreenCapture 16.11.13 1-04-28.jpg|thumb|left|PJ caught in his own contraption]]
Meanwhile, PJ waited to unleash his practical joke on Lilo's substitute teacher, which ended up backfiring (due to Stitch intervening), and thus caused PJ to literally get his butt kicked (several times actually). Luckily, PJ was freed from his own contraption by a sympathetic Stitch.

Shortly after, PJ found his one true place as an opening act performer for [[Moses Puloki|Moses]]' hula gig.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including PJ, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

PJ participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. PJ joins them for the song by playing the trumpet.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
PJ made [[P.J. 2.0|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where he was [[Transmutation|released]] by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] to play practical jokes around [[Okinawa New Town|town]] while disguised as [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] in order to frame him for the pranks. In "[[Shogun]]", it is shown that PJ was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault. PJ [[Dark-End|later appeared]] as one of the experiments who helped Stitch fight [[Dark End]]. He also appeared in the special, ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
PJ is incredibly silly and mischievous, even towards other experiments. Being an expert prankster, PJ uses his intelligence to create ingenious pranks. As Lilo describes, PJ can be annoying with his pranks, and while his pranks can be mean, he doesn't seem to be purposely malicious, but merely carries out his programming. Like most experiments, he dislikes it when his goals do not carry through or are interrupted. He is also seen to be quite an impressive comedian, as he likes making individuals laugh with his practical jokes.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
PJ is an orange and tan koala-like experiment with a white face and white belly, a wide mouth, a small red nose, black eyes, large black eyebrows, two thin yellow-tipped antennae on his head resembling rabbit-like ears, and a functioning blow-horn for a tail (reminiscent of [[wikipedia:Harpo Marx|Harpo Marx]]'s trademark horn), which he honks instead of speaking. He wears joke eyeglasses with a large fake exaggerated human nose and a small brown mustache resembling those of [[wikipedia:Groucho Marx|Groucho Marx]].

===Special abilities===
PJ is a skilled practical joker. He can play practical jokes by using his surroundings, various joke gags (e.g. hand buzzer, whoopee cushion, squirt flower, etc.), and other things he finds.

PJ has shown to be skilled in playing the trumpet.

==Trivia==
*Jumba refers to PJ as a "Practical joke gone mad! Unholy offspring of science and evil!" His "harmless little pranks soon become clever, medium-sized booby-traps, then extra-large dangerous sabotage, and then *makes explosion and siren noises* EVIL!" Though Jumba later admits that most of it was his own practical joke.
*PJ's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is white.
*In the group photo taken at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'' and the Disney.com Lilo and Stitch experiment gallery, PJ is not wearing his glasses. It is possible that he either took them off or they got broken during the battle.

'''Phantasmo''', also known as '''Experiment 375''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to take possession of inanimate objects and, through them, create utter chaos. Being ghost-like, he is intangible and can phase through obstacles, thus making him virtually uncatchable. His one true place is keeping the Macki Macaw animatronic functional at the [[Macki Macaw's|titular pizza restaurant]].

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 375 was the 375th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to possess inanimate objects and cause massive mischief and chaos through them. 375 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Phantasmo - Phantasmo moments after activation.png|thumb|left|Phantasmo moments after his activation]]
375's pod eventually made its way into a pearl oyster inside the crane game at [[Macki Macaw's|Macki Macaw's pizzeria]]. [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] played the claw game and won the oyster, but a glitch in the machine caused him to shake it in frustration, prompting [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] to intervene and scold Stitch. After the oyster freed itself, despite Stitch's misconduct, the employee let [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] keep the prize, and she and Stitch took it [[Lilo's House|home]] with them.

When Lilo tried to give Stitch a bath (after Nani mentioned the word "bath"), the latter fled and hid in the laundry hamper, but she tricked Stitch into coming out and then dragged him to the bathroom. There, an incident with the bathtub, which overflowed after Lilo immersed Stitch in the water, resulted in the oyster opening and the pod inside getting wet, activating 375.

That night, 375 wreaked havoc in the kitchen. When Stitch was alerted, he attempted to save [[Pleakley]]'s dishes, but 375 made Stitch lose his balance and shatter them. 375 then possessed [[Scrump]] and used the doll to paint Nani's face green, sabotage [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s [[Jumba's Computer|experiment analyzer]], steal Pleakley's begonia, break Lilo's record player, brush Nani's toothbrush on Stitch's toes, and frame Stitch for it all.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Phantasmo - Phantasmo inside Scrump and grinning evilly.png|thumb|Inside Scrump]]
The next morning, Nani, thinking Stitch was the culprit, threw the latter outside and made Lilo chain him up as punishment until Nani returned from work. However, Stitch noticed 375 using Scrump again to unravel Lilo's [[wikipedia:Elvis Presley|Elvis]] videotapes. Stitch broke free and attacked Lilo's doll, only to arouse her suspicion. When Stitch was later being prosecuted, he saw 375 (still inside Scrump) wink at him, causing Stitch to lash out at Lilo's doll.

Later that day, while 375 was attempting to break Pleakley's flower pot to get Stitch into deeper trouble, Lilo caught him right in the act. 375 revealed himself and possessed a rope, with which it tied Lilo, Jumba and Pleakley up. He then repossessed Scrump and prepared to execute the three with Jumba's [[Plasma Blaster|blaster]], but a wary and vigilant Stitch ambushed 375 and freed his ''ʻohana''.

While the four searched for 375, he possessed a vacuum cleaner and almost sucked Pleakley up with it. Lilo and Stitch then made a vain attempt to [[Prison Capsule|capture]] the intangible experiment, forcing 375 to retreat into [[Kokaua Town]].

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Phantasmo - Phantasmo inside Macki Macaw animatronic.png|thumb|left|Inside the Macki Macaw]]
After a long pursuit through town, when 375 turned the tables, Nani gave Lilo and Stitch a lift in her jeep and led 375 to Macki Macaw's, where he used the claw machine to trap Stitch. The former then chased Lilo backstage and possessed the Macki Macaw animatronic that had malfunctioned earlier. After Lilo raised the curtain, 375 put on a show for an audience.

375, christened Phantasmo, was then convinced by Lilo that using the animatronic parrot to entertain children and receive adoration was a better way of gaining attention than causing chaos, thus rehabilitating him now that he had found his one true place.

Phantasmo made a cameo at the end of "[[Snooty (episode)|Snooty]]" on [[Gantu]]'s TV set continuing his duty inside the Macki Macaw animatronic as the ex-captain watched the show with great interest.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Phantasmo, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Phantasmo participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did. Although he was seen among some of the Leroys, it is presumed that he wouldn't have been able to be very effective, due to the fact that his powers are deemed useless.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Phantasmo made a special guest appearance in the ''Stitch!'' segment "[[Kung Fu Dragon Pleak Lee]]".

==Personality==
Phantasmo is a mischievous, ghostly experiment whose intangibility allows him to possess inanimate objects and wreak havoc through them. He also has a tendency to gloat by laughing in a squeaky voice and is rather quite smart too. When possessing an object, he tries to do so when nobody is around and will act as the object he is possessing to avoid being exposed. Due to advanced programming, he would dispose of those who discover his true identity. Being always on the move, jumping from object to object, he craves attention. This is ultimately exploited in order to get him to perform for attention instead of causing chaos.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Phantasmo is a green, semi-transparent ghost-like experiment with short arms, a large conehead with two light green stripes, a koala-like face, long rabbit-like ears, and dark pupil-less eyes. Instead of legs, Phantasmo has a continuous wisp-like tail.

===Special abilities===
Phantasmo has intangibility and can possess and bring to life any inanimate object, making him highly elusive and deadly, but he can choose to leave the host item at any time. When wreaking havoc, he usually laughs in a squeaky voice. He can also phase through anything, making him impossible to keep in one place, including weapons and materials typically used to capture experiments (such as [[Net Cannon|nets]] and [[Prison Capsule|capsules]]), which can normally keep experiments under containment.

==Trivia==
*Phantasmo was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*An early version of Phantasmo appears on an old downloadable activity printout for ''Stitch! The Movie''. This beta design depicts him with a rounder Stitch-like head, a round nose, tufts of fur on his head and chest, and two short antennae.
**This design is confirmed to be him through [https://wendygriebstoryboards.blogspot.com/2022/01/lilo-and-stitch-phantasmo.html storyboards of his episode] by storyboard artist Wendy Grieb.
**It is likely that his design was changed because he resembled Stitch too much.
*Phantasmo is clearly a spectral being, as he possesses intangibility and the ability to phase through obstacles, thus making him the only experiment that cannot be restrained or captured.
**Due to this, it is unknown how Jumba managed to create him, let alone dehydrate him into an [[Experiment Pods|experiment pod]].
**This would come into question in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'' on how he was captured by a Leroy clone. Also, he was seen being chased by another Leroy clone with a [[Plasma Blaster|plasma gun]], despite his inability to sustain physical injuries.
*Phantasmo, [[Fudgy (054)|Fudgy]], [[Remmy (276)|Remmy]], [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Witch (610)|Witch]] are the only known experiments to have arms but no legs.
**Interestingly, excluding Fudgy, all of these experiments are capable of levitation. Remmy is always seen levitating. Phantasmo and Witch primarily levitate but often possess objects or living beings to move by other means. Tickle-Tummy is also able to levitate, but has been seen bouncing as well.
*Phantasmo, [[Glitch (223)|Glitch]], and Witch are all capable of possession, albeit in different capacities: Phantasmo can possess any inanimate object, Glitch possesses technology, and Witch can possess living beings.
*Phantasmo has the ability to [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]], but he only does so after possessing the Macki Macaw animatronic. Also, he replaces the animatronic's pre-recorded voice with that of his own and inexplicably knows who Macki Macaw and the Hammerheads are.
*Due to being voiced by Nancy Cartwright, his voice is similar to [[w:c:simpsons:Bart Simpson|Bart Simpson]].
*As Phantasmo's possession of objects brings them to life, the possessed objects are able to perform actions that they normally cannot do.
**Despite being lightweight and having a flexible body, [[Scrump]] was able to not only move "herself", but "she" also gains the strength to lift or pull objects, such as a cloth that had Pleakley's plant on it. The same goes to a bunch of bananas in the Pelekais' kitchen that Phantasmo possesses shortly after his activation, as he uses them to open a microwave oven's door.
**A traffic light sprouted arms and legs, grabbing some coconuts and running off until Stitch runs it over with the [[X-Buggy]], destroying it.
**A tiki statue from a store facade was able to move its own limbs and run off. Its eyes were also able to narrow and widen.
**The Macki Macaw animatronic was actually repaired by his possession and vastly upgraded, being able to fly without flapping its wings, play its ukulele, and speak independently (though with Phantasmo's own voice). The animatronic also became more lifelike and less robotic, as its exposed joints and bolts seemingly vanished after his possession.
*Phantasmo's pod color is yellow.
**Interestingly, electrical discharge can be seen when Phantasmo's pod gets wet and activates.
*Phantasmo's ears appear in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.

'''Phoon''', also known as '''Experiment 540''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. She is designed to create devastating, typhoon-like winds; in her mutated form, she has enhanced strength and can fire projectiles at enemies, while her blasts are more powerful. Her one true place is creating winds for windsurfers at [[Lahui Beach|the beach]]. 

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 540 was the 540th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. She was designed to produce destructive, typhoon-like winds. 540 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 540's pod landing on a rooftop weather vane.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Phoon - Phoon after activation.jpg|thumb|left|Phoon after being activated]]
A breeze caused 540's pod to fall off the weather vane into the roof's rain gutter and roll down into a rain barrel, activating the experiment. 540 then created a powerful typhoon-like wind and proceeded to destroy the house.

Later, 540 blew down some palm trees near [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]]. When [[Gantu]] went out to try and capture 540, the latter blew a tree onto Gantu's head. The resulting concussion left him confused and disoriented, which [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] took great notice, but Gantu still resumed searching for 540.

Meanwhile, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] decided to temporarily quit experiment hunting after an unfortunate mishap. She then attended [[Hip Hop Fusion Studio|Hip Hop Fusion]], where she impressed some rich hippie girls by telling falsehoods about her life.

When Gantu later came to the school, thinking Lilo was hiding the experiment from him, Lilo tried to cover up the situation by telling the hippie girls that Gantu was her eccentric uncle Chester who wasn't quite right in the head. Due to his concussion caused by the blow he took earlier, Gantu believed the lies that Lilo told the hippie girls and ended up thinking that aliens were only figments of his imagination. He then decided to go surfing at [[Lahui Beach|the beach]].

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Phoon - Phoon in mutated form confronting Jumba and Pleakley.jpg|thumb|Phoon in her mutated form]]
Shortly after, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] (dubbed Wenceslaus by Lilo) arrived and attempted to tell Lilo about 540's hurricane. The hippie girls initially questioned Stitch's body language, but then assumed he was an exotic pet. Unfazed by their opinion, Stitch tagged along with Lilo and the hippie girls.

Later on, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]] tracked 540 down, where Jumba tested his latest invention, the [[Plasmatic Englobulatron]], in hopes of catching 540, despite Pleakley's objection to this. Instead, the ray mutated her into a gigantic monster (as stated by Jumba: "76.3% chance will instantly capture experiment, 23.5% chance will destroy entire planet with big boom. This was other 0.2% chance."). After blowing down Jumba and Pleakley, 540 resumed her rampage.

Meanwhile, a delusional Gantu was chilling at the beach, while Reuben tried to tell the former that if he didn't catch 540, [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] would be furious. However, Gantu ignored Reuben, even after the latter managed to get Hämsterviel on the phone, thinking both were figments of his imagination. Hämsterviel then subtly advised Reuben to kick Gantu in the rear. In doing so, Gantu immediately came to his senses and set off in search of 540.

Sometime later, 540 arrived at Hip Hop Fusion and wreaked havoc with her devastating blasts of wind. She was soon followed by Jumba and Pleakley, and later Gantu. When the hippie girls grew suspicious, Lilo was forced to lie to them even more.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Phoon - Phoon providing wind for windsurfers.jpg|thumb|left|Phoon in her one true place]]
The mutated 540 destroyed a large portion of [[Kokaua Town]] until Stitch arrived and, after a long battle, succeeded in putting 540 to sleep by rocking her in his arms while singing a lullaby. This caused the Plasmatic Englobulatron effect to wear off, and 540 shrunk down to her normal size and form. When Gantu then attempted to capture 540 in a [[Prison Capsule|container]], Stitch drooled menacingly, forcing Gantu to surrender.

540, christened Phoon, later found her one true place at the beach providing gusts of wind for windsurfers.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Phoon, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Phoon participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by creating cyclones that sucked up attacking Leroys and hurled them through the air.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Phoon made [[Stitch's Birthday, Part Two|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where the gang went back in time and tampered with [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]'s creation, which started up his glitch and therefore almost erased him from existence. Phoon, along with [[Ace (262)|Ace]] and [[Sparky (221)|Sparky]], helped gather enough energy to re-energize Stitch. She later appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Phoon is playful and energetic, hopping around cheerfully after being activated while taking in her surroundings. However, she also enjoys causing destruction, as she proves to be conniving and giggles mischievously as she destroys things with her powerful wind gusts.

When Jumba accidentally mutates her with his Plasmatic Englobulatron, she becomes quite aggressive and furious while she continues to destroy things. She dislikes when individuals try to stop her and will attack anyone who does. However, she enjoys being rocked and hearing lullabies, which soothe her and put her to sleep, as well as reverts her to her normal size. After being reformed, she decides to use her powers on a lighter level for individuals to enjoy her wind for windsurfing. However, she will use her powers to defend herself when need be, such as during the battle against the [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] [[Leroy Clones|clones]].

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Phoon is a quadrupedal, bright red, round-bodied elephant-like experiment with green eyes with single long eyelashes, two ears that look like tails, a short trunk and four legs (two of which can serve as arms) that also resembles an [[w:c:zelda:Octorok|Octorok]] or a [[w:c:pikmin:Fiery Blowhog|Fiery Blowhog]]. She has a dark red stripe pattern with bumps running down her back and a light-colored underbelly.

In her mutated form, she is massively larger and walks upright instead of quadrupedal. She now has three spines sticking out of her head. In addition, her eyes are slanted downward to make her appear menacing. Her teeth and claws are more pronounced in this form, as they are shown sticking out and are never retracted.

===Special abilities===
Phoon can create massive wind blasts by sucking up vast amounts of air and blowing it out with enormous force. These blasts can range from a windy day to tornado-powerful blasts capable of devastating buildings and trees.

When applied to Jumba's [[Plasmatic Englobulatron|Plasmatic Englobulatron ray]], Phoon mutates to a larger, more powerful form in which she has enhanced strength and can fire projectiles at enemies. In this form, her blasts are greatly enhanced as well, as she was able to blow [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] away without effort.

===Weaknesses===
When applied to rocking and soft music, Phoon falls asleep, despite however awake she may be. Sleep also defies the effects of the Plasmatic Englobulatron, therefore reverting her from her mutated form to her original.

==Trivia==
*In [[Phoon (episode)|her debut episode]], Lilo refers to Phoon as a male, despite Phoon clearly being a female based on her voice and the presence of eyelashes.
*Phoon's wind blasts are actually recycled sounds of [[disney:Hathi, Jr.|Hathi, Jr.]]'s trumpeting from ''[[disney:The Jungle Book|The Jungle Book]]''.
*Phoon is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having green eyes instead.
*Phoon, [[Felix (010)|Felix]], [[Blowhard (533)|Blowhard]], and one [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed experiment]] are the only known experiments that have trunks similar to elephants and tapirs.
**Phoon and Blowhard are also the only known experiments with primary functions directly involving wind, and both of their names relate to wind as well.
*Phoon, along with [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Dorkifier (122)|Dorkifier]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], [[Butter (227)|Butter]], [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]], [[Spike (319)|Spike]], [[Yang (502)|Yang]], [[Richter (513)|Richter]], [[Tank (586)|Tank]], [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]], and one [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed experiment]], are the only known experiments that are primarily quadrupeds.
*Phoon's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue.
*The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Phoon as: "Experiment 540. Primary function: Generates devastating wind blasts."
*In ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', both Phoon's mutated and normal forms appeared, possibly indicating that she has learned to morph in between the forms.

He is designed to take bad pictures of individuals. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "[[:Category:Mrs. Hasagawa's experiments|cats]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 214 was the 214th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to take pictures of individuals in which they look awful. 214 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]]. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 214's pod being one of them.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 214's pod for an apricot and washed it, activating the experiment. However, as 214 was not a very evil or destructive experiment, he was able to live a peaceful life with her, due to the latter seeing the former as a mere stray cat who needed a home.

When [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] discovered that Mrs. Hasagawa kept several experiments as pets, they thought they were a danger to her and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], decided to capture them all. While Pleakley was backing away from [[Manners (358)|Experiment 358]], he bumped into 214, who then proceeded to take his picture. 214 then stuck out his tongue, revealing the developed photo. Pleakley was at first surprised that he looked bad in the picture, with cracked skin and a bloodshot eye, but Jumba then explained that 214 was designed to take bad pictures of individuals. Stitch then slammed a [[Prison Capsule|container]] over 214, capturing him.

214 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 214 was then named Pix.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Pix, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Pix participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did. However, it is presumed that he wouldn't have been able to be very effective, due to the fact that his powers are deemed useless.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Pix made [[Hämsterviel's Epic Secret|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Frenchfry (062)|Frenchfry]], [[Squeak (110)|Squeak]], [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Houdini (604)|Houdini]] after [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] kicked them out for being considered useless. It is shown that Pix can use his abilities to distort his photos like a funhouse mirror. He made [[Meega Going to Disneyland!|a second appearance]], along with [[Boomer (288)|Boomer]], [[Slushy (523)|Slushy]], [[Blowhard (533)|Blowhard]], [[Kixx (601)|Kixx]], and [[Slugger (608)|Slugger]], when [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] visited Tokyo Disneyland.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Pix is a blue mouse/camera-like experiment with light green patches around his black eyes, a light blue patch running down from his chin to his stomach, light blue insides of his ears, a camera lens-like nose, two arms with three legs similar to a tripod.

===Special abilities===
Pix can take pictures of individuals through a camera lens in his nose, as well as develop them like a Polaroid, with the pictures coming out of his mouth. The individuals in the photos actually look more horrifying than in real life. He distorts the photo much like a funhouse mirror as seen in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Trivia==
*In his initial appearance, Pix has light reflections in his eyes as typical of most genetic experiments, although they only appeared when he was up close. By default, Pix's eyes are devoid of any detail.
*Pix was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Pix, [[Zero (000)|Zero]] (in cyborg form), and [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]] are the only known experiments whose legs resemble a tripod.
*In [[Hämsterviel's Epic Secret|one episode]] of the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, Pix was shown kicked out by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] for being considered useless. Ironically, in [[Meega Going to Disneyland!|another episode]], Pix was actually seen battling [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and company.

'''Plasmoid''', also known as '''Experiment 617''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to attack by firing balls of plasma from his scorpion-like tail. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 617 was the 617th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to shoot plasma balls from his scorpion-like tail. 617 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Dupe - Plasmoid firing a plasma ball.png|thumb|left|Plasmoid firing a plasma ball]]
617's pod eventually made its way to a junk shop, where it (along with [[Hammerface (033)|033]], [[Heat (609)|609]] and [[Thresher (544)|544]]) was found, stolen, activated, and named Plasmoid by [[Gantu]] in "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]".

Back at [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]], Gantu trained and conditioned Hammerface, Heat, Thresher and Plasmoid by simply using [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] for target practice, much to his indignity and chagrin. The four henchmen experiments were then led by Gantu in an attack on the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]], where their boss ordered them to defeat and capture [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and his duplicates after seeing that he had been divided into four.

While his teammates each battled one of the clones, Plasmoid engaged the original Stitch in a duel. Plasmoid attacked by firing plasma balls at Stitch, only for the latter to dodge them all. The scorpion-like experiment then fired a plasma blast at an overhead lamp. Stitch taunted Plasmoid, saying he missed, but this was proven wrong as the lamp then fell on Stitch's head, knocking him out. Gantu finished the battle by placing Stitch in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] along with his clones.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Dupe - Plasmoid about to be duplicated.png|thumb|Plasmoid about to be duplicated]]
After capturing Stitch and his clones, the five returned to Gantu's ship for a victory feast (courtesy of Reuben), but were interrupted by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Pleakley]] and [[Dupe (344)|Dupe]]. When Lilo tricked Gantu into using Dupe's cloning ability, Gantu used Dupe to clone Plasmoid into a hundred replicas. However, as the original Plasmoid's power was divided among them, they all became complete weaklings, and thus were easily defeated.

Presumably after this, they were all sent to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] who was somehow able to remerge the weakling Plasmoid clones into the original.

Although Plasmoid was unseen in "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", he is known to have been sent back to Gantu along with all of Hämsterviel's other captive experiments after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused chaos and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

Plasmoid reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by Lilo, Stitch, and several other experiments in a rescue mission. Plasmoid even helped with the escape by breaking Gantu's [[Plasma Blaster|gun]] in two with a plasma blast, allowing [[Tank (586)|Tank]] to eat it.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Plasmoid, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Plasmoid participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by firing plasma blasts at attacking Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Plasmoid has appeared twice in the ''Stitch!'' anime, both times with [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]]. In the [[Stitch Power|first appearance]], Plasmoid and Splodyhead combated [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] when he was hypnotized by [[Swirly (383)|Swirly]] into fighting for [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. In the [[New Town (episode)|second appearance]], Plasmoid and Splodyhead were [[Transmutation|modified]] by Hämsterviel to attack Stitch. Plasmoid was given a new ability of vacuuming up objects and using them as projectiles. In "[[Shogun]]", it is shown that Plasmoid was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help Stitch in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Plasmoid wasn't one of the experiments that was activated.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Plasmoid is a large green, six-legged scorpion-like creature with black eyes, an oval nose, two antennae, no pincers and a pincer-less tail. He has small fangs sticking out from the top of his mouth, although they are significantly enlarged and more prominent in ''[[Stitch!]]''.

===Special abilities===
Plasmoid can shoot explosive balls of plasma from his tail. He has also displayed the ability to vacuum up objects and use them as projectiles while [[Transmutation|under the effects]] of [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. He also has microscopic and telescopic vision.

===Weaknesses===
Like other experiments, when Plasmoid is divided by [[Dupe (344)|Dupe]] into a hundred replicas, each one will be virtually harmless.

==Trivia==
*Plasmoid is one of the ten known experiments named by someone other than Lilo or Stitch, the other nine being [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Elastico (345)|Elastico]], [[Yaarp (613)|Yaarp]], [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]], [[Heat (609)|Heat]], [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]], [[Morpholomew (316)|Morpholomew]], [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]], and [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]]. 
**Plasmoid (alongside Hammerface, Heat, and Thresher) was named by Gantu.
*Plasmoid, [[Bugby (128)|Bugby]], and [[Clink (086)|Clink]] are the only known experiments that are hexapods. Interestingly, all three are different types of arthropods (arachnids, insects, and crustaceans respectively).
*Plasmoid, [[Yang (502)|Yang]], and [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]] are the only known experiments that shoot plasma/lava balls. Also, Plasmoid, Yang, [[Melty (228)|Melty]], Heat, and Splodyhead are the only known experiments whose powers are related to fire.
*Even though we saw Plasmoid in [[Experiment Pods|pod]] form, he was technically [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Plasmoid's pod color is yellow according to "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]". In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, it is blue.
*Plasmoid is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.
*Plasmoid appears in the online game ''[[Lilo & Stitch: Alien Interception]]'', along with [[Clyde (150)|Clyde]], [[Dupe (344)|Dupe]], Yang, [[Tank (586)|Tank]], and [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]].

'''Ploot''', also known as '''Experiment 505''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to ingest trash and pollution, growing exponentially larger as he collects more, then metabolizes the waste material into toxic sludge he releases in order to cause environmental disasters. His one true place is cleaning up litter and pollution at [[Lahui Beach|the beach]].

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 505 was the 505th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to flood entire cities with toxic sludge created from accumulated trash and pollution, growing exponentially bigger as he collected more. 505 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Vlcsnap-2013-06-30-09h39m59s155.png|thumb|left|Ploot after being activated]]
505's pod eventually made its way into a bag of trash, where it was thrown over a nearby cliff by a couple of polluters into [[Pudge]]'s underwater grotto, activating the experiment. 505, named Ploot, first began collecting all the pollution in the grotto, then started collecting trash throughout [[Kokaua Town|town]], but not before he was discovered by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] while they were busy cleaning up [[Lahui Beach|the beach]].

Unaware of what Ploot was really doing, Lilo and Stitch decided to let him carry out his primary function rather than attempt to stop him. However, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] later revealed Ploot's true intentions after Lilo informed him about the experiment.

Eventually, Ploot collected enough trash and pollution to grow into a monstrous form, and then began his rampage by spreading toxic sludge around the island of [[Kauai]]. Before long, most of Kokaua Town was covered in Ploot's toxic goo, which contaminated everything, including Pudge's grotto.

While an ailing Stitch was recuperating from an earlier garbage-eating incident (which Jumba theorized as a rare space disease), Lilo rallied several other experiments to try and stop Ploot from wrecking the environment. Despite their best efforts, Ploot was simply too strong for them.

[[File:Vlcsnap-2013-05-26-15h13m25s250.png|thumb|Ploot's monster form]]
Ploot eventually kidnapped Lilo in one of his giant claws, ignoring her complaints about his destruction, but she was saved by Stitch, who had fully recovered from his illness. Lilo then defeated Ploot by using natural air freshener (a product that Jumba and [[Pleakley]] discovered) to reduce the latter to his original size.

Ploot was then captured in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] by Stitch, rehabilitated, and found a one true place cleaning up litter and pollution.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
Ploot was seen early in the movie cleaning up litter on the [[Kauai|island]] as [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to make sure all the experiments were happy in the one true place they belonged.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Ploot, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Ploot participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], as he was seen in his alternate pollution form fighting attacking Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Ploot made [[The Return of Ploot|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where he grew to his monstrous size and polluted everything again. This also caused a chain reaction since the [[Izayoi Island|island]] was somehow the center of Earth's power, and it nearly destroyed the planet itself.

==Personality==
Ploot has a two-sided nature, one that is benevolent and one that is chaotic. His initial appearance and helpful manner belie his true purpose and form: a giant ozone-polluting beast. In this form, he is very aggressive and dangerous, squirting pollution everywhere and harming those who get in his way, not even caring about the environment. However, after being sprayed with air freshener, Ploot's personality changed for the better, as he now cleans up the pollution and doesn't spit it out, helping to clean the environment as a result.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Ploot is a small, blue-green gastropod-like experiment with a small green pouch on his stomach, small black eyes, a thin mouth, green crab-like claws, and two spinning sweeper brushes for feet. In his pollution form, he is heftier, darker, and has green sludge dripping from his mouth. When in this form, his two antennae become like giant smokestacks, letting pollution into the air.

===Special abilities===
Ploot has a metamorphosis programming that activates as he collects trash and pollution. As he consumes such waste material, he grows exponentially larger until he literally becomes a walking pollution factory. The accumulated trash is converted into a thick, toxic sludge which he then begins spreading to create devastating environmental disasters. Also, his two antennae become like giant smokestacks, letting pollution into the air. He makes dolphin-like chirping sounds at normal size and monstrous roars when grown to bigger size. He can also roll into a ball at normal size and spin into a tornado.

After being rehabilitated, Ploot appears to have gained control over his pollution form, since he turned into it to fight off [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] [[Leroy Clones|clones]] with his cousins without an ill effect on his personality.

===Weaknesses===
Natural air freshener is shown to shrink/evaporate Ploot's toxic sludge and revert him to his normal size, as well as tame him and make him clean instead of pollute.

In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, Ploot is instead defeated after ingesting [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and his "monsterbot", only for Stitch to attack the walls of Ploot's stomach, giving the polluting experiment indigestion and causing him to revert to his normal size and form.

==Trivia==
*In [[Ploot (episode)|his debut]], Ploot is [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|erroneously called 515]], a number taken by [[Deforestator (515)|Deforestator]], who ironically appears in that episode as well.
*The episode Ploot debuted in was aired on Earth Day.
*Ploot, [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]], [[Clink (086)|Clink]], [[Gotchu (031)|Gotchu]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have claws/pincers. Interestingly, all four official experiments have characteristics similar to crustaceans.
*Though Ploot was initially "collecting" pollution, he appeared to be over-obsessive in doing so (similar to [[Felix (010)|Felix]]), such as when he disrupted an unkempt man who was enjoying his burger and soda.
*Ploot's weakness to natural air freshener is similar to [[Clip (177)|Clip]]'s weakness to wild/unruly hair-taming conditioner.
**His weakness to the compounds in air fresheners is ironic; historically, aerosol-based air fresheners often use ozone-depleting chemicals, especially chlorofluorocarbons, as their main propellants, which are not the safest chemicals to the environment.
*In ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', Ploot was seen in his alternate pollution form during the battle between the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy army]] and the experiments.
**He is also one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''Leroy & Stitch''.
*Ploot's ability to grow larger from eating garbage is similar to [[Tank (586)|Tank]]'s ability to grow larger from eating metal and [[Fudgy (054)|Fudgy]]'s ability to grow larger from eating chocolate in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

'''Pop''', also known as '''Experiment 009''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to use his tail to blow up a balloon to the size of the room he is in, then popping the balloon, discombobulating those involved near the explosion of the balloon and causing frizzy hair. He appears in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 009 was the ninth genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to discombobulate and disorient enemies by using his tail to blow up and pop balloons. 009 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
In "[[Stitch's Birthday, Part Two]]", Pop was displayed by a young [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] to [[Delia]] approximately around the time of [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]]'s creation, accidentally letting Pop out of his [[Prison Capsule|containment capsule]]. Naturally, he carried out his primary function, inflating his tail in front of an interested Delia. Hämsterviel jumps on the enlarging balloon, but is propelled with the balloon. Delia soon realizes what is happening, and as she tries to escape, the balloon gets too big and immobilizes her, pressing her against Hämsterviel. The balloon eventually pops, yet Pop's fate afterwards is unknown, although he somehow ended back with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]].

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Pop is a small, orange and caramel-colored monkey-like experiment with two pink orbs on the top of his head with three stubby, multi-colored antennae. He has a white face and stomach and a small red nose, as well as green markings on his rear and back. His tail is a pump which he uses to blow up pink balloons, which re-form on his tail after they pop.

===Special abilities===
Pop can use his tail to blow up a balloon to the size of the room he is in, then popping the balloon, discombobulating those involved near the explosion of the balloon and causing frizzy hair.

==Trivia==
*With only one brief animated scene, Pop most likely has the least amount of screen time out of all the fully confirmed experiments that appeared in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.
