'''Poxy''', also known as '''Experiment 222''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to act as a virus and infect popular planetary leaders, giving them purple pimples, smelly feet, a swollen right eye, and uncontrollable burping; the symptoms vanish instantly when Poxy leaves his host. He was captured by [[Gantu]] (whom he temporarily infected), but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]". According to a DVD bonus feature game in ''[[Lilo & Stitch 2: Stitch Has a Glitch]]'', his one true place is fixing health issues.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 222 was the 222nd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his disease-transmitting ability to infect popular planetary leaders, resulting in the public revolting against the infected leader. 222 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 222's pod landing in a sugar crop.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Poxy - Poxy noticing Lilo and Stitch.png|thumb|left|Poxy noticing Lilo and Stitch]]
222's pod was caught up in a harvester used to extract sugar cane from the crop. The pod eventually made its way into a box of sugar, which [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] likely bought at a grocery store. [[Pleakley]] poured a heap of sugar with 222's pod into his bowl of cereal, the milk added to it activating 222 before it was eaten with the cereal by Pleakley.

When Pleakley later got infected by 222's disease and displayed the above symptoms, he headed off to the nearest health clinic, believing that human doctors could help him. While he sat in the waiting room to be admitted, [[Gantu]] showed up looking for 222. He then noticed an ailing Pleakley and chased the latter, since he was afflicted with the experiment.

Fortunately, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] followed Pleakley to the clinic and managed to rescue him by subduing Gantu with laughing gas. While Gantu was temporarily incapacitated, Lilo and Stitch rushed Pleakley out of the hospital back to their [[Lilo's House|house]], where [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] revealed his ingenious method of removing 222, which would cure Pleakley.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Poxy - Poxy stuck in Pleakley's earwax.png|thumb|Stuck in Pleakley's earwax]]
Using Jumba's [[Reducer Ray|shrink ray]] and Nani's [[X-Buggy|dune buggy]] to aid them, Lilo and Stitch got shrunk to microscopic size and entered Pleakley's body to find and capture 222. After a long chase through Pleakley's body, Lilo and Stitch were able to capture and extract 222 when the latter became stuck in Pleakley's earwax.

Before Lilo and Stitch finished their task and safely exited Pleakley's body, he was kidnapped and imprisoned by Gantu, who later took a beating from a healthy but dysfunctional Pleakley. When Gantu attempted to crush Pleakley afterwards, the former was shrunk to microscopic size and captured by Jumba.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Poxy - Gantu under Poxy's influence.png|thumb|left|Gantu under Poxy's influence]]
In the end, Lilo planted 222, christened Poxy, inside Gantu, who fell deathly ill. [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] mocked Gantu about him finally catching an experiment, although the latter protested that he didn't want to actually catch Poxy's virus.

As Gantu was in good health in later episodes, it can be presumed that Poxy was somehow extracted from Gantu's body and sent to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], then back to Gantu in "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]" along with all of Hämsterviel's other captive experiments after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused chaos and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

Poxy reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by Lilo, Stitch, and several other experiments in a rescue mission.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
Despite not physically appearing, the first 624 experiments, presumably including Poxy, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

It is unknown whether or not Poxy participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Personality==
Poxy is a microscopic experiment that is very devious, yet carefree. He never really worries about anything and is seen multiple times messing with Lilo and Stitch. His worry-free attitude might also be a result of his great confidence. To him, everything seems more of a nuisance than an actual threat because he is unharmed while infecting somebody, not even by antibodies. So, he just makes himself right at home inside his host.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Poxy is an incredibly tiny, pale green-grey, single-celled experiment with a white inner body, black eyes, a round nose, a wide mouth, pink-purple spots and four grey-tipped antennae.

===Special abilities===
Poxy acts like a virus and can enter a victim's body, causing the host to suffer from purple pimples, smelly feet, a swollen right eye, and uncontrollable burping. He can also split his body and bend it around with no effort, implying that he may be a single-celled organism. He displays no need to breathe without air once inside his host, presumably because he filters the oxygen from the host's blood.

Poxy is also unharmed by antibodies, as they pay no attention to him whatsoever. This may be because they do not see him as a threat, he appears as part of them, he has taken control of them, or [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] simply made him immune to them.

===Weaknesses===
Poxy can become easily stuck in earwax.

==Trivia==
*Poxy's design was first revealed in a bonus feature trivia game on the original ''[[Lilo & Stitch]]'' DVD before he officially debuted in ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''. He was the only one of the three experiments seen in that game who appeared in the show; the other two remain [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Miscellaneous|unconfirmed]].
**Poxy is also the only experiment whose one true place was confirmed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Lilo & Stitch 2: Stitch Has a Glitch]]'' instead of [[Poxy (episode)|his debut]] in the series.
*Poxy also appeared in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Poxy is the smallest known experiment ever created by Jumba.
*Poxy's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green.
*In his debut, Poxy was microscopic size. However, in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", he was the standard size of an experiment. This might imply that he can change size while functioning as a germ, but it is also possible that his [[Prison Capsule|container]] somehow acted like a lens and magnified him to a noticeable size, as he disappeared when he was released.
*Poxy's holographic silhouette appeared in both "[[Amnesio (episode)|Amnesio]]" and "[[Fibber (episode)|Fibber]]".
*Poxy was possibly mentioned in "[[Skip (episode)|Skip]]" by [[Gantu]] as a small green one, when he was telling [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] which experiments he caught.
*Poxy did not appear in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', most likely due to his microscopic size.

'''Remmy''', also known as '''Experiment 276''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to infiltrate victims' dreams and transform them into nightmares. If the victim wakes up while Remmy is still inside, he will remain within his host's mind forever to turn all future dreams into nightmares. His one true place is at [[Kimo's Arcade]], sending gamers into virtual realities of their fantasies after Jumba [[Transmutation|reprogrammed]] him.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 276 was the 276th genetic experiment created by Jumba with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to enter enemies' dreams and transform them into nightmares. 276 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 276's pod landing in a turtle's nest on [[Lahui Beach|the beach]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Vlcsnap-2012-07-02-19h38m09s180.png|thumb|left|Remmy after activation]]
When a sea turtle discovered 276's pod in its nest, it threw the pod out, which then landed in the path of an incoming tide, activating 276.

Later, 276 traveled to the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]], where, after [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] settled down for a nap to cope with her grief (as it was the anniversary of [[Mr. and Mrs. Pelekai|her parents]]' death), he proceeded to invade Lilo's dreams.

[[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]] entered Lilo's dreams to capture 276, who dissolved Lilo's initial dream and caused a chain reaction of dream sequences. When the four eventually had a chance, they tried to suck 276 up with a vacuum, but the latter was able to use a fire hydrant to block the nozzle. Angered at the four's attempt to capture him, 276 replaced Lilo's dream with a happier one, which later turned into a nightmare.

[[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] soon came into Lilo's room to wake her up, only to be stopped by Pleakley, who had just exited the nightmares. He then explained that if Lilo awakens, 276 will remain inside her head forever and cause future nightmares. Nani sang Lilo a lullaby when the latter began stirring in her sleep. She then convinced Pleakley to re-enter Lilo's nightmare and show her a photo of their parents, believing it would help make her feel better.

[[File:7734238239393939.jpg|thumb|Invading Lilo's dream]]
When the monsters in the nightmare eventually had Lilo, Stitch and Jumba cornered, Pleakley re-entered Lilo's nightmare and then gave her the Pelekai family photo. Looking at it allowed Lilo to remember the happy times she and Nani had with their parents. Lilo's laughter destroyed the nightmare and defeated 276, rendering him powerless. He was shortly after captured and extracted by Jumba.

276, named Remmy, was then [[Transmutation|reprogrammed]] by Jumba to be completely harmless and given a one true place sending gamers at the [[Kimo's Arcade|local arcade]] into virtual realities of their fantasies, but without giving them nightmares.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Remmy, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Remmy participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Remmy has made two appearances in the ''Stitch!'' anime where he infiltrated both [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]'s dreams. His first appearance was in Season 2 in "[[A Recurring Nightmare]]". As it is explained later in the episode, Remmy was happy in his one true place in [[Kimo's Arcade]] in Kauai, but was eventually abandoned due to the decreasing popularity of video arcades in favor of video games at home. Because of this, he reverted back to his evil, nightmare-granting ways.

He came to the island for revenge and despite Stitch trying to stop him, infiltrated Yuna's dreams. [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] decides to send Stitch, [[Pleakley]], and [[BooGoo]] into Yuna's dream to get Remmy out before Yuna wakes up and they're all trapped inside her dreams forever. Eventually, the group reaches the location where Remmy has his base set up. After getting inside, he challenges everyone to a quiz show, using Yuna's memories as the questions. After a few easy questions, he asks for the lullaby that Yuna's deceased mother used to sing to her when she was a baby. Unfortunately, Yuna doesn't remember, so they lose the game.

Remmy sends the group to three different locations in his base to play "virtual reality" games to make up for losing the quiz show. He sends Stitch to a racing game, Pleakley to a shooting game, and Yuna and BooGoo to a zombie-fighting game. Stitch and Pleakley both lose their games and wake up. Remmy and BooGoo are still in the dream, however, so Stitch, Jumba, and later Pleakley all go back to Yuna's dream to help. Seeing her treasured ''ʻohana'' fighting alongside her, Yuna gains control of her dream, giving Stitch the power to defeat all the enemies and weakening Remmy enough for Jumba to capture him.

Remmy regrets his actions and makes up for it by showing Yuna her deepest memory: her mother's face and lullaby. As Yuna starts to wake up, Remmy's base collapses, so Stitch, Pleakley, Jumba, BooGoo, and Remmy all leave Yuna's dream. In the morning, however, Remmy still needs someone to give nightmares to, so Jumba sends him to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] to turn his dreams into nightmares.

In his [[Stitch's Dreams|second appearance]], Remmy is [[Transmutation|released]] by Hämsterviel to give Stitch nightmares so that [[Gantu]] and [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] can have the chance to capture him and send him back to Hämsterviel. Therefore, Yuna and Jumba have to go inside Stitch's dreams while Pleakley keeps Stitch from waking up or becoming too agitated from the nightmares. They manage to capture Remmy at the last second before Gantu and Reuben can transport him.

==Biography==
===Physical appearance===
Remmy is a light blue, floating ghostlike experiment with a huge head, a dark blue marking on top, little antennae, black eyes, and a thin mouth in a perpetual grin. He resembles the ''[[wikipedia:Pac-Man|Pac-Man]]'' ghost [[w:c:pacman:Inky|Inky]] and can fly.

===Special abilities===
Remmy can cause nightmares by entering through a victim's ear and infiltrating their dreams. Also, he was designed to attack at the peak of the person's subconscious enjoyment. If the victim wakes up while Remmy is still inside, he will remain there permanently to turn all future dreams into nightmares.

Jumba later [[Transmutation|reprograms]] Remmy to be harmless and transport people on fantastic journeys in virtual reality games without causing nightmares.

In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, Remmy is able to [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]] and also has complete control over the mind once inside a host. This is proven when he displays the ability to show [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] a forgotten memory.

===Weaknesses===
If Remmy's host is reminded of something happy, the host will be able to turn the nightmare back into a dream, leaving Remmy weak and powerless. 

==Trivia==
*His name is a reference to the [[wikipedia:Rapid eye movement sleep|REM stage of sleep]] in which dreams occur (REM means Rapid Eye Movement).
*Remmy resembles the [[w:c:pacman:Ghosts|ghosts]] from the ''[[w:c:pacman:Pac-Man (series)|Pac-Man]]'' video game series (particularly [[w:c:pacman:Inky|Inky]] in terms of color). 
*Remmy, [[Phantasmo (375)|Phantasmo]], [[Fudgy (054)|Fudgy]], [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Witch (610)|Witch]] are the only known experiments to have arms but no legs.
**Interestingly, excluding Fudgy, all of these experiments are capable of levitation. Remmy is always seen levitating. Phantasmo and Witch primarily levitate but often possess objects or living beings to move by other means. Tickle-Tummy is also able to levitate, but has been seen bouncing as well.
*Remmy's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green.

'''Retro''', also known as '''Experiment 210''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to reduce individuals, animals, enemy weapons, and technology to their primitive or prehistoric state; wrapping his tongue around the de-evolved object or victim and spanking his bottom three times will reverse the transformation. His one true place is at a [[Kokaua Wildlife Preserve|wildlife park]], resurrecting extinct animals for a Mesozoic zoo.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 210 was the 210th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to reduce enemy weapons and technology to their primitive state, thus rendering them useless, but could also reduce individuals and animals to a primitive or prehistoric state. 210 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 210's pod landing in a palm tree by a [[Lahui Beach|beach]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Retro - Retro after being activated.jpg|thumb|left|Retro after being activated]]
When [[Charles and Mary|a vacationing couple]] used the beach's palm tree to catapult themselves into a nearby lake, 210's pod fell out of the tree and was accidentally splashed, activating the experiment. 210 then used his tongue to transform the couple's clothes into medieval clothes, their cell phone into a 1930 candlestick telephone, and their car into a 1920 station wagon.

210 later attacked a [[Kokaua Wildlife Preserve|wildlife preserve]], reducing some of the animals to their prehistoric state, including an elephant (turned into a woolly mammoth), a tiger (turned into a ''[[wikipedia:Smilodon|Smilodon]]'', also called a saber-toothed tiger), and a squirrel (turned into a saber-toothed squirrel).

Eventually, after a long chase, 210 was captured by [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], but the former escaped aboard a yacht and turned [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], and [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]]'s [[Ellen and Lona|middle school friends]] into cave people.

Stitch then recaptured 210 using a tablecloth and took him back to the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]] to discover how to reverse the latter's powers via [[Jumba's Computer|Jumba's computer]].

When Stitch found the answer, he muzzled 210 and took the latter back onto the yacht. There, Stitch released 210, who then turned the yacht into an Ice Age canoe. Stitch then wrapped 210's tongue around Lilo, Jumba, Pleakley, and Nani's junior high friends and spanked his bottom three times, returning the victims to their modern state.

Later, 210, christened Retro, found his one true place at the wildlife preserve, turning modern animals into dinosaurs and prehistoric animals for a Mesozoic zoo. He eventually somehow resurrected an extinct ''[[wikipedia:Tyrannosaurus|Tyrannosaurus rex]]'', which wreaked havoc.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Retro - Retro wearing a park ranger's shirt.jpg|thumb|Retro's one true place]]
In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Retro was oddly seen as one of the experiments in [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison cell]], suggesting that [[Gantu]] caught Retro, but this was an error. Retro was then sent back to Gantu along with all of Hämsterviel's other captive experiments after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused chaos and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Retro, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Retro participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did. Although he was seen chasing after some of the Leroys, it is uncertain if his powers had any effect on them.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Retro made an appearance in [[Experiment-A-Palooza|a later episode]] of the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]], [[Squeak (110)|Squeak]], [[Clip (177)|Clip]], and [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]]. It is shown that when Retro's powers are used on [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], he reverts to his original programming. This is because that was Stitch's earliest state after his creation. In "[[Shogun]]", it is shown that Retro was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help Stitch in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Retro wasn't one of the experiments that was activated. He also appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Retro is a small orange, mammalian/reptilian dinosaur-like experiment with black eyes, a purple nose, tiny gold-tipped ears, gold markings on his back and gold spots around his eyes, and a thick, short tail and legs. His tongue is notably extendable.

===Special abilities===
Retro can wrap his extendable tongue around an individual or object, and as he lets go, the individual or object de-evolves into its primitive/prehistoric state. He can also "de-evolve" something that is already deceased as long as its remains are still intact, as he was able to bring a ''[[wikipedia:Tyrannosaurus|Tyrannosaurus rex]]'' back to life, although it is unknown what animal he de-evolved to do so.

Retro can de-evolve multiple individuals/objects at once when he wraps his tongue around them altogether, and the same applies to reversing the de-evolving effects.

===Weaknesses===
Any de-evolved object or victim can be returned to its modern state by wrapping Retro's tongue around the object or victim and spanking his bottom three times.

==Trivia==
*In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Retro erroneously appeared with Gantu's other captive experiments, but he was captured by Lilo and Stitch.
*Retro's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue.
*Retro is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
*In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, Stitch reverted to his original programming while under Retro's powers, as this was Stitch's earliest state after his creation. Strangely, however, [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] was able to turn Stitch back to normal by simply reaching out to him and reminding him of his promise, as opposed to reversing the effects the usual way.

'''Reuben''', also known as '''Experiment 625''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]], a frequent henchman of [[Gantu]], and a major character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]], first appearing in ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''. He is the last failed prototype of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. He possesses all of Stitch's powers and is equipped with advanced lingual skills. The main flaws in his programming are cowardice and laziness; the most strenuous thing he ever does is make sandwiches, albeit delicious ones. His one true place is with Gantu as his galley officer and chef. 

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 625 was the 625th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed for [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]'s purpose but was considered a failed experiment due to his lazy nature. 625 and the previous 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture Experiment 626. 

===[[disney:Disney Adventures|''Disney Adventures'' prequel comics]]===
Before Stitch's creation and when Jumba was struggling with creating his ultimate monster, 625 served as Jumba's primary assistant in the labs, though this mostly involved him making sandwiches for his master. When Stitch first gets loose on [[Planet Turo|Turo]], 625 comes with Jumba to help him track the creature down, but the arrest would eventually come and 625 would be podded.

These events have since been retconned by the events described in ''[[Lilo & Stitch 2: Stitch Has a Glitch]]'', where Stitch is apprehended directly after his creation and Reuben is nowhere to be seen.

===''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''===
[[File:Stitch! The Movie - Reuben after activation.png|thumb|left|Reuben after activation]]
While [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]] were fighting over the [[Experiment Pod Container|experiment pod container]], unseen to them, 625's experiment pod slipped out.

[[Gantu]] later discovered the pod while abducting Jumba and took it with him back to [[Dr. Hämsterviel's Ship|Hämsterviel's ship]] for interrogation.

When Jumba refused to reveal the location of the other [[Experiment Pods|experiment pods]], Gantu and [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] decided to activate Experiment 625 (who Jumba stated has all the powers of 626) and use him to torture Jumba. However, Gantu and Hämsterviel were awestruck to discover 625's lazy nature when he was seen making sandwiches instead of tormenting Jumba.

625 later frequently attempted to gain new bologna for his sandwiches, until he was trapped on Earth after [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]] crashed with Gantu and 625 on board.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Swirly - Reuben making sandwiches.png|thumb|Reuben making sandwiches]]
625 is still stranded on Earth along with [[Gantu]] and spends most of his time relaxing, making sandwiches, and ridiculing Gantu for his frequent failures and bumbling. He turns out to be quite intelligent and gives plenty of information about the experiments to Gantu. He is portrayed as Gantu's wisecracking sidekick and often tags along during experiment hunting. 

625 was once commanded by Gantu to battle [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], but due to his lazy nature, he did not fight and was easily beaten. Ironically, he used his powers twice in the series: when he climbed up the [[Gantu's Ship|ship]]'s window and also kicked Gantu across [[Lahui Beach|the beach]] in "[[Phoon (episode)|Phoon]]". In addition, he proved to be more tolerant of water than Stitch, such as when he plunged into the ocean to get out of harm's way in "[[Splodyhead (episode)|Splodyhead]]", and when he and Gantu got sunk while aboard different watercraft in "[[Sinker (episode)|Sinker]]". In "[[Mr. Stenchy (episode)|Mr. Stenchy]]", 625 was actually jealous of Gantu's affections towards the newfound experiment [[Mr. Stenchy (254)|Mr. Stenchy]].

Throughout the series, 625 serves as Gantu's reluctant sidekick, although he usually refuses to help, messes up Gantu's plans, or even helps [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and Stitch instead of Gantu on occasion.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
[[File:Leroy & Stitch - Reuben after falling off the ceiling.png|thumb|left|Reuben after falling off the ceiling]]
With [[Gantu]] having lost all the experiments he had captured other than 625 himself, the former abandoned 625 on Earth and left to free [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] from [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison]]. Hurt and/or infuriated at this, 625 decided to convert [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's deserted ship]] into his own sandwich shop.

Sometime later, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] visited 625 to use the ship's videophone, and even made him a PBJ sandwich as a peace offering. 625 initially rejected Lilo's plea until she discovered that she had never given him a name (he was still 625 to this point). After a few failed attempts, 625 finally agreed to the name Reuben. Lilo then convinced Reuben to repair the ship's communication system so that she could contact [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]].

After the call was placed, the two discovered that the Stitch in control of the [[B.R.B. 9000|B.R.B.]] was an [[Leroy (629)|impostor]]. Realizing that Stitch was in danger, Lilo asked for Reuben's help, but the latter claimed it wasn't their problem. Lilo then enlightened Reuben on how he could do whatever Stitch can and convinced him to make something of himself. Although hesitant, Reuben complied after Lilo persuaded him. He then repaired the ship, while revealing his incredible powers, and the two flew it to [[Planet Turo|Turo]] to warn the [[Grand Councilwoman]].

However, when Lilo and Reuben arrived, they discovered that they were too late, as Hämsterviel and his [[Leroy Clones|Leroy army]] had already overthrown the Galactic Alliance. Hämsterviel ordered Gantu to arrest Lilo and Reuben, but Gantu was fired in the process due to Leroy being Hämsterviel's new henchman. However, Lilo and Reuben were soon broken out by a reformed Gantu after Reuben convinced him to switch sides. Before the three were able to escape, they were caught by a group of Leroy guards. Despite Reuben using his powers to help his friends evade the clones, he and the others were eventually cornered. However, they were saved by Stitch, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], and [[Pleakley]]'s timely arrival and escaped back to Earth in time to save the captured experiments that were taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed.

[[File:Leroy & Stitch - Reuben playing a saxophone.png|thumb|Playing a saxophone]]
Reuben participated in the following battle between the experiments and the Leroy clones by slipping up attacking Leroys with sandwiches. When the Leroys gained the upper hand in the battle, Lilo, Stitch, Reuben (playing a saxophone), and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the entire Leroy army to shut down due to the original's fail-safe.

Following the battle, when the Galactic Alliance was reinstated and Gantu returned to his job as captain, the latter hired Reuben as his galley officer.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
In the ''Stitch!'' anime, it is revealed in the English dub that he and [[Gantu]] were fired from the [[Galactic Armada Crewmembers|Galactic Armada]] because of some incident involving bad karaoke singing. Since they needed money, they once again sought out [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] for employment. Since then, Reuben has been in almost every other episode of the anime with Gantu and Hämsterviel.

In [[Reuben 2.0|one episode]] of Season 3 of the anime, Hämsterviel [[Transmutation|modifies]] Reuben to be able to use his powers as often as possible, giving him the ability to easily defeat [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. This transformation also gave him a "bad boy" personality, and it is because of this that [[Angel (624)|Angel]] dumped Stitch for Reuben until Stitch saved her from plummeting to Earth. Reuben was later snapped out of this trance when he saw someone making a sandwich incorrectly. Reuben was last seen in the anime's [[Dark-End|final episode]] when he, Gantu, Hämsterviel, and [[Delia]] are put in prison by the [[Grand Councilwoman]].

Reuben also appeared in the specials ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]'' and ''[[Stitch! Perfect Memory]]''.

===[[Lilo & Stitch (2025 film)|''Lilo & Stitch'' (2025 film)]]===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch (2025) - Reuben cameo.png|thumb|Reuben's cameo in the live action film.]]
Reuben makes a cameo in the live-action remake. When Jumba threatens to alter Stitch into a more powerful and even worse experiment, Reuben can be seen on his visual aid, appropriately labeled as "625".

==Personality==
Despite having all the powers of Stitch, Reuben is an incredibly lazy coward. However, during the events of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', Reuben finally made something of himself and used his powers to help save the entire galaxy. He is actually very humble, friendly, and sympathetic, though he often makes wisecracks. He is usually quite crabby toward others when they disturb him (especially Gantu). He has tagged along with Gantu and Dr. Hämsterviel during many villainous plots, but has stated that he doesn't really care who wins.

Reuben constantly insults Gantu's bumbling and incompetent nature, but is sometimes very compassionate and thoughtful towards him, secretly seeing him as his best friend and companion. He can also be considered somewhat of a coward, especially when Gantu forces Reuben to battle Stitch on a few occasions. Unlike Gantu, however, Reuben has no fear of Hämsterviel, who scorns him for his laziness. (This may explain why Gantu has never attempted to send Reuben to Hämsterviel, unlike other experiments he captures.)

Another of Reuben's defining traits is a passion for sandwiches; he displays thorough knowledge of sandwich crafting and history, and he is usually seen either holding (or eating) a finished sandwich, or making one. His sandwiches are apparently very tasty, as even Gantu will request them from Reuben on occasion.

During the course of the series, it has been shown that Reuben secretly sees Stitch as his cousin and vice versa. Also, just like Stitch, he has a crush on [[Angel (624)|Angel]], therefore making him Stitch's rival for Angel's love. Despite his wisecracks and laziness, Reuben is also shown to have a sensitive side as seen in ''Leroy & Stitch'', when Gantu abandons him and leaves him alone on Earth, causing him to become bitter and lonely.

Aside from this, Reuben is incredibly intelligent and clever, especially when it comes to the experiments. Although he was the second-to-last experiment to be created, Reuben has excessive knowledge of every experiment, even the ones that were created far before his time, such as [[Ace (262)|Ace]], most likely due to being Jumba's former assistant. There are also a few instances where Reuben acts like kind of an "inside man" for Lilo and Stitch, like telling Lilo how to beat [[627|Experiment 627]] (but this was only so 627 would leave him alone, not for the sake of the galaxy).

Reuben is also shown to be inquisitive. In "[[Babyfier (episode)|Babyfier]]", his curiosity led to him releasing [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]] from his container on Gantu to find out what Gantu's alien species started out as.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Reuben is a golden yellow (teal blue in the ''[[disney:Disney Adventures|Disney Adventures]]'' magazines), chubby koala/marmot-like experiment that looks like [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], with a big head with short ears that flop down at the sides of his head, large black eyes, three small brown-tipped antennae that look like a tuft of fluffy fur, bright yellow stomach, chest and around his eyes, three dark yellow toes on each foot, big red nose, four pointed fingers on each hand, short stumpy legs, two brown markings on his back (one hourglass-shaped and an oblong marking above it), and two flat buck teeth sticking out of his mouth and overlapping his bottom lip. He also has brown retractable claws on his fingers. Additionally, he has only three toes on each foot, unlike his immediate successor and immediate predecessor who both have four toes on each of their feet, although he has been depicted with four toes in error before.

He stands slightly shorter than Stitch (his three antennae and droopy ears ignored), but the height difference is very subtle, to the point that the animation doesn't seem to depict this very well. The anime-based video game ''[[Stitch Jam]]'' has arguably the best depiction of their height difference (along with that of [[Angel (624)|Angel]] and [[Felix (010)|Felix]]), as on the character select screen for the game's Free Mode and Challenge Mode, Reuben is slightly shorter than Stitch and Felix (both of whom stand at the same height), while Angel is shorter than all three of them.

===Special abilities===
Reuben possesses all of Stitch's powers, including the ability to grow an extra pair of arms (it is unknown if he has the three back spikes and two additional antennae on top of his head). He can lift objects up to 3,000 times his own weight, think faster than a supercomputer, roll into a ball, see in the dark, and scale walls and ceilings. He can also [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]] (with a hint of a Brooklyn accent), though he is capable of understanding [[Tantalog language|Tantalog]], his native tongue, and is a very talented sandwich maker (and sandwich eater). Obviously, he is too lazy for much physical combat or use of his powers, and therefore prefers to stand on the sidelines. He also has knowledge of advanced technology, as he was able to repair a telecommunications array using pickle juice as a conductor.

===Weaknesses===
Reuben was originally very lazy and cowardly. He is proven to be ticklish when [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]] tickle tortures him in the episode "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]". Also, he doesn't seem to be anywhere near as durable, suffering painful-looking injuries after taking a beating from [[Hammerface (033)|Gantu's]] [[Heat (609)|four]] [[Thresher (544)|henchmen]] [[Plasmoid (617)|experiments]] in "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]". However, as it has been repeatedly stated that he has all of Stitch's powers, he may very well be as durable, and the pain he received may be either psychological in nature or from a lack of mental attitude to tolerate pain as well as Stitch. It is uncertain whether or not Reuben shares Stitch's weakness of water, although he doesn't seem to mind being in water as much as Stitch does.

'''Richter''', also known as '''Experiment 513''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to cause geological disruption; his programming allows him to locate the weakest geological point from which he can create massive earthquakes capable of causing planets to bifurcate. His one true place is shaking milkshakes at the [[Rental Hut|Rental Shack]].

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 513 was the 513th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his earthquake-making ability to split entire planets in two. 513 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 513's pod landing in a palm tree by a [[Lahui Beach|beach]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Richter - Richter after activation.jpg|thumb|left|Richter after being activated]]
513's pod fell out of the tree and into a drink cooler below, the melting ice activating the experiment. 513 then created a deadly earthquake with one thump of his tail, causing massive damage throughout the beach, before the experiment escaped in search of an underground fault.

513 was later intercepted by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], but the former managed to escape them and [[Gantu]] into a dormant volcano. Lilo and Stitch followed 513 into the volcano and attempted to encase him in green sticky goo, but the latter was able to force them out and cave in the entrance. 513 then set off a chain reaction in the volcano's fault, which would eventually cause a chain reaction of quakes and split the entire planet in two.

Later, Lilo and Stitch returned to the dormant volcano using a [[X-Buggy|drill machine]], and, despite 513's best efforts to evade them, they were eventually able to corner him. However, Gantu arrived at that moment, capturing 513 in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] and taking him back to [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]] to send to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]].

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Richter - Richter shaking milkshakes.jpg|thumb|Richter shaking milkshakes]]
Gantu prepared to teleport 513 to Hämsterviel. However, due to Lilo and Stitch's timely arrival, as well as interference caused by the vibrations, they managed to rescue 513 before Gantu could transport him, resulting in Gantu being teleported instead.

Lilo and Stitch took the recaptured 513, christened Richter, to a fissure, where he could create another chain reaction of quakes that would counter the first in a backfire effect. Richter agreed to do so if he could have Stitch's orange ball, which the latter had been treating very preciously after Lilo taught him how to care for things.

Lilo then released Richter from containment, and the latter quickly went underground and successfully stopped the quake. After being dug out of the ground, Richter earned Stitch's orange ball and found his one true place at the [[Rental Hut|Rental Shack]] shaking milkshakes.

In "[[Holio (episode)|Holio]]", Richter helped repair the Rental Hut after it was nearly destroyed by [[Holio (606)|Experiment 606]].

Richter reappeared in "[[Elastico (episode)|Elastico]]" as one of the audience members for Lilo's hula dance.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Dupe - Stitch's cousins attending Lilo's slumber party 3.png|thumb|left|Richter attending Lilo and Stitch's slumber party]] 
In "[[Finder (episode)|Finder]]", Richter was seen playing poker with Stitch, [[Yin (501)|Yin]], [[Yang (502)|Yang]] and [[Cannonball (520)|Cannonball]].

In "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]", Richter was one of the experiments that came to Lilo and Stitch's slumber party wearing children's sleepers. However, he was forced by [[Pleakley]] to leave due to his destructive behavior.

In "[[Angel (episode)|Angel]]", Richter was one of the experiments that [[Angel (624)|Angel]] reverted to evil using her song, causing the former to create massive earthquakes. Later, Richter and the other depraved experiments attacked Stitch aboard a ship, but Angel turned them to good again before they could finish Stitch off. Working together, the experiments were then able to successfully escape the ship with Stitch.

Richter reappeared in "[[Slugger (episode)|Slugger]]" as part of Lilo's softball team.

Richter was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that joined Stitch in a rebellion against Gantu.

In "[[Ploot (episode)|Ploot]]", Richter was one of the first team of experiments (along with [[Kixx (601)|Kixx]] and [[Deforestator (515)|Deforestator]]) formed to try and stop [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]]. However, Ploot was easily able to defeat them, forcing the three experiments to retreat.

Richter was seen on a computer screen in "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]", posing as an evil creation of [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s as part of a hoax to fool [[Mortlegax]], the head of E.G.O. industries.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Richter, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Richter participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by creating quakes that opened up fissures in the earth, which trapped the Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. Richter joins them for the song by playing the congas.

==Personality==
Despite his destructive function, Richter is shown to care for things and share Stitch's fondness for the orange ball that both of them cherish. He is simple-minded and comes off as very stubborn when confronted. He has a one-track mind and tends to let his actions speak louder than words a lot of the time. He is also very sneaky and cunning, capable of causing trouble and mischief whenever he gets a chance to do so. Richter can be quite a good friend to those who win his trust. He is also shown to be loyal and helpful to his friends, joining Stitch's rebellion to fight off Gantu.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Richter is a quadrupedal, bulky, purple experiment resembling an [[wikipedia:Ankylosaurus|Ankylosaurus]]. He has a huge flat tail with a triangular shaped portion at the end, a round face with a wide mouth with two of his bottom teeth sticking out, and a single horn on his head. He also has a lavender stomach, chest, and patches around his eyes, a large reddish-brown round nose, large black eyes, small, short pointed ears, tiny dark purple round spikes down his back, and a darker purple marking in the middle of his back that reaches all the way to his tail.

===Special abilities===
Richter can cause devastating earthquakes with a single thump of his tail. He can also, if he uses this ability in fault lines within a planet's crust, set off a chain reaction of quakes which will split the planet in two if not countered with the backfire effect. He can roll into a ball and climb walls, similar to [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], but is too heavy to jump. He sticks close to the ground due to being a quadruped, but he is capable of standing on two legs if he so desires.

Richter has milkshake-making skills and a knack for treating things preciously like Stitch's orange ball (or "citrus orb", as [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] describes it).

Much like [[Deforestator (515)|Deforestator]], Richter can only speak [[Tantalog language|Tantalog]].

Richter has shown to be skilled in playing the congas.

===Weaknesses===
Richter can be easily encased in a green sticky substance.

'''Sample''', also known as '''Experiment 258''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to record random sounds he hears and replay them in endless loops in an annoying, musical rhythm in order to drive the entire population into madness. His one true place is providing backbeats for the band Fox Roswell and the Tall Grays.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 258 was the 258th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to annoy enemies by recording, replaying, and looping random sounds that he hears. 258 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 258's pod landing on a [[Golf Course|golf course]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Sample - Sample after activation.jpg|thumb|left|Sample after activation]]
258's pod was mistaken for a golf ball, where a golfer whacked it into a pond, activating the experiment. 258 then deftly recorded and sampled the noises of a parrot and frog, causing the golfers to become annoyed by the racket.

Later, 258 sampled the sound of a jackhammer and casually made his way to [[Kokaua Town|town]], where he was almost captured by [[Gantu]], who was out looking for the experiment. However, 258 was instead caught by the dogcatcher, who mistook the former for a dog and took him to the [[Aloha Animal Rescue|dog shelter]].

The [[Susan Hegarty|dog pound lady]] contacted [[Merwin and Dean]], two alien hunters who eagerly accepted 258 and almost took him to an alien convention. However, when [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and a reluctant [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] later arrived at the pound to get Stitch his shots, Merwin and Dean (seeing that Stitch was an alien too) attempted to grab him to take him to the convention as well. When Lilo and Stitch saw 258, they decided to rescue him from the two alien hunters.

Lilo, Stitch and 258 managed to escape Merwin and Dean, but when the trio attempted to hide from them, 258 kept playing his rhythm, despite being told to be quiet by Lilo. The two alien hunters were alerted by 258's music and soon caught up. However, Gantu intervened, causing Merwin and Dean to try to catch him instead, since he was also an alien. They chased after Gantu, forgetting about Stitch and 258.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Sample - Sample playing a mixture of recorded sounds.jpg|thumb|Sample playing a mixture of recorded sounds]]
Safe for now, Lilo, Stitch and 258 arrived [[Lilo's House|home]], where [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] explained 258's powers. Due to the latter's skills, Lilo decided to name 258 Sample (whom Stitch locked in the closet after getting clearly irritated by the cacophony of recorded sounds). Shortly after, [[Pleakley]] left to attend the alien convention, with a wary Jumba tagging along.

Later, Gantu came to the Pelekais' house in order to hide from Merwin and Dean. Although hesitant, Lilo and Stitch complied after Gantu promised to behave and not take Sample away. As the two alien hunters tried to break in, Sample began sampling random noises, despite Lilo and Stitch's best efforts to silence him. Everyone then quickly escaped out a window, but Gantu got stuck halfway and was captured by Merwin and Dean.

Lilo, Stitch and Sample went back to rescue Gantu, but he blasted the trio into a [[Net Cannon|net]] and then put Stitch and Sample into [[Prison Capsule|containment orbs]]. Lilo reprimanded Gantu's betrayal, though he informed her that he had called a truce with Merwin and Dean by allowing them to showcase Stitch and Sample, the latter of whom they would give back to Gantu in return.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Sample - Sample posing smugly.jpg|thumb|left|Rapper Sample]]
Stitch and Sample were taken to the alien convention, where Merwin and Dean planned to have them be shown in front of an audience to prove aliens were real. However, Stitch escaped and released Sample. Gantu unsuccessfully tried to stop them from running away. Merwin and Dean then forced Gantu to pose as an alien in front of the entire audience.

Sample later found his one true place providing backbeats for the band Fox Roswell and the Tall Grays, whose rhythm was initially out of sync.

In "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", Sample was one of the experiments that joined Lilo and Stitch on a mission to rescue Gantu's captive experiments. Sample stood watch outside [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]] and was told to count to 242 and crow like a rooster if the coast was clear, while the others all broke into the ship. While he was standing guard, [[Snafu (120)|Experiment 120]] somehow convinced him to imitate the ship's alarm system, thus alerting Gantu to their location.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Sample, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Sample participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by annoying Leroys with his cacophony of recorded sounds.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Despite appearing prominently in certain intros of Seasons 1 and 2 of the ''Stitch!'' anime, Sample only appeared in one episode of Season 3: "[[Yuna vs. Jessica]]". In this episode, he was "[[Transmutation|transmutated]]" by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] so that instead of just repeating sounds he hears, he can fire waves of light yellow dust from his ears, causing anyone it touches to dance uncontrollably when he plays his music (similar to [[Carmen (123)|Carmen]]'s ability).

He was given the assignment to use his ability to get [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] to the top of a hill, where a pre-built transportation device would be waiting to send him to [[Delia]]. He managed to form a parade out of several people he affected, including [[Jessica]], [[Toriko]], [[Makiko]], [[Hiroman]] and his entire soccer team, and even Stitch. However, when he tried to use his power on [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]], the dust reflected off her umbrella, hitting him and breaking his spell on everyone. Stitch was then able to use the spandex-covered inside of the umbrella to absorb Sample's dust and dump it on him, knocking him unconscious.

He was then placed in a machine built by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] that would reverse the transmutation, but he still used his dancing power on Yuna when a little bit of the remaining dust from the umbrella fell on her. Stitch then discovered that the machine wasn't plugged in, but decided to enjoy Yuna dancing for a while, despite her protests.

Eventually, Sample was reverted back to normal, then dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in Jumba's vault as shown in "[[Shogun]]". Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help Stitch in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Sample wasn't one of the experiments that was activated. He later appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Sample is a lively, upbeat and energetic experiment. He is usually happy and easily amused by his own music and any other sound, commonly dancing by bouncing from one foot to the other. His perky, carefree attitude may be a result of him being blissfully unaware of the situation at hand. He also shows great curiosity towards any sound that is new or unfamiliar to him. He doesn't like to be silent unless he can play his music (or any sound) to amuse himself. He normally just tends to do his own thing, completely disregarding the simple command to be quiet, yet following complex instructions during a rescue mission. He doesn't have a real voice (he can only dub someone else's voice) but finds a way to communicate through his backbeats, head nods, and basic hand signals.

When he appears [[Transmutation|transmutated]] in ''[[Stitch!]]'', however, he becomes more aggressive, as he forces others to dance to his beat. He also gets angry when others try to stop his rhythm and not dance along.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Sample is a bright orange koala/cat-like experiment with a wide mouth, a big round oval-shaped nose with purple and magenta stripes, which functions as an amplified microphone, stubby soft paws, pointed fingers, short, stumpy legs, fluffy stomach, hourglass-shaped markings on his legs, black slanted eyes, and big round ears resembling speakers.

When he is [[Transmutation|transmutated]] in ''[[Stitch!]]'', he is a darker orange color, gains green irises, and has [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s insignia ("H") on his nose.

===Special abilities===
Sample can record any sound that he hears through his nose (microphone) and play it through his mouth and ears (loudspeakers) with other recorded sounds in loops and backbeats that can be annoying or catchy. He can also climb walls and ceilings, similar to [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. He has shown the ability to use his speakers to launch out yellow rings of dust that make individuals dance uncontrollably. However, he has only displayed this while [[Transmutation|under the effects]] of [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. He is also able to [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]] using his own voice, although it is filtered due to him being biologically designed with loudspeakers.

===Weaknesses===
He does not stop making noise that can come from no other source, therefore completely giving away his location to everyone, which makes it almost impossible for him, along with those near him, to stay hidden. Also, if his sound blasts are deflected back at him, it reverses his uncontrollable dancing effects.

==Trivia==
*Sample seems to always be smiling and can apparently tolerate anything, including being captured.
*Sample appears, along with several other ''[[Lilo & Stitch]]'' characters, in a [[Stitch Meets High School Musical|parody]] of the [[disney:Disney Channel|Disney Channel]] [[disney:Disney Channel Original Movie|Original Movie]] ''[[disney:High School Musical|High School Musical]]'', which was broadcast as part of the ''High School Musical: Around the World'' one-year anniversary special.
*Sample's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is white in [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]]. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, it is blue.
*The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Sample as: "Experiment 258. Primary function: Sonic annoyance. Drives people mad by sampling sounds and repeating them in an endless, grating rhythm."
*Sample's ears appear in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.
*In the French dub, Sample is named "Echo", which is the same name as [[Experiments#0-Series: Jumba's test batch, including many household helpers|Experiment 048]].

'''Shoe''', also known as '''Experiment 113''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to generate negative events; however, adjusting his cranial horseshoe controls the type of event (luck) generated. In a downward position, he causes bad luck; in an upright position, he causes good luck. His one true place is at the [[Golf Course|mini-golf course]], making miniature golfers score holes-in-one.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 113 was the 113th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to generate bad luck, but could also cause good luck. 113 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 113's pod landing on a [[Golf Course|miniature golf course]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Shoe - Shoe after activation.png|thumb|left|Shoe after being activated]]
113's pod was used as a golf ball, where a miniature golfer whacked it. The pod landed in the moat obstacle, activating 113, who then went around the [[Kauai|island]] causing bad luck.

[[Gantu]] had been informed about 113, but [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] refused to have a bad luck experiment. Gantu then had a squabble with [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]], who tried to tell the former about 113's good luck ability. When Reuben later managed to reveal this to Gantu (and deftly tape-recorded his earlier protests), the latter then decided to track down and capture 113.

Meanwhile, 113, traveled to the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]], where his bad luck caused [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]]'s jeep to break down, thus forcing her to walk to work. He was later caught raiding the kitchen by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]]. 113 kept generating bad luck for Lilo's ''ʻohana'', despite their best efforts to change his bad luck effects and hide him someplace where the bad luck he created could not affect them.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Shoe - Shoe captured by Gantu.png|thumb|Shoe captured by Gantu]]
When Lilo reluctantly admitted that 113, named Shoe, was a jinx and unable to bring good luck, the latter, unfortunately, overheard her and promptly left, feeling hurt and abandoned. After Jumba revealed that Shoe could generate good luck, Lilo and Stitch set out to find him. The two discovered Shoe sitting alone on a cliff, but before they could act, Gantu overtook Stitch and scooped Shoe in a [[Prison Capsule|container]]. Despite being captured, Shoe's bad luck allowed him to evade both Gantu and Stitch.

After a series of mishaps, Gantu managed to reclaim Shoe and turned the latter's horns upward, causing him to generate good luck for Gantu. Shoe was then left alone on [[Lahui Beach|the beach]] after his good luck caused Gantu to become rich, making the experiment feel just as useless as when he generated bad luck.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Shoe - Shoe generating good luck at miniature golf course.png|thumb|left|Shoe generating good luck]]
Shoe was eventually found by Lilo, who apologized to the former for giving up on him. After generating good luck for Lilo's ''ʻohana'' and bad luck for Gantu, Shoe found his one true place at a mini-golf course (the same one where he was activated) using his "good luck setting" to allow golfers to score holes-in-one.

In "[[Skip (episode)|Skip]]", Shoe was one of the wanted fugitives who had already been captured in an alternate future where Hämsterviel ruled Earth.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Shoe, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Shoe participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Personality==
Shoe appears to be mute, but also friendly and sociable as shown when he tried to make friends with Stitch. Unlike most experiments, Shoe doesn't mean to cause chaos intentionally; it is merely the way he was programmed. He is also shown to be very sensitive about his bad luck powers, as seen when he overheard Lilo say that he cannot seem to change his bad luck and is apparently useless. He felt abandoned and hurt after hearing this and even ran away. However, when Lilo learned that Shoe could generate good luck, she apologized to him after finding him, and he seemed to forgive Lilo when he hugged her.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Shoe is a teal/green-and-white sloth-like experiment with a wiry body and a horseshoe-shaped head with a round face with black eyes, a small dark purple round nose, a little mouth and two long, curved horns.

===Special abilities===
Shoe is a luck-manipulating experiment. When his cranial horseshoe, or the "horns" on his head, are facing down, bad luck occurs. When the horseshoe is turned up, the opposite luck is generated. The events can be predicted to happen whenever the tips of his horns glow, and also a faint bleep is heard. Shoe cannot control the luck his powers provide to others, however, and is dependent on the horns' position.

==Trivia==
*Lilo stated that she didn't name 113 "Shoe" because of his horseshoe-like horn, but because she thinks he needs shoes, despite the fact that none of the experiments wear shoes.
**According to [[disney:Jess Winfield|Jess Winfield]] on his TV Tome thread, in real life, Shoe was actually partly named after a production associate, Jennifer "Shoe" Hsyu.<ref name="WinfieldTVTome">{{cite web|url=http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|title=L&S Says Mahalo|website=[[wikipedia:TV.com|TV Tome]]|date=December 14, 2004|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305082355/http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|archivedate=March 19, 2016|accessdate=May 27, 2018}}</ref>
*According to Jumba, the moment he created Shoe, his [[Galaxy Defense Industries|laboratory]] exploded, which occurred after the insurance policy on the laboratory had canceled.
*Altering the position of Shoe's U-shaped horn in order to reverse his powers is the same way to reverse the effects of [[Dorkifier (122)|Dorkifier]]. Also, the closeness of their numbers (113 and 122) and movable horn feature may suggest that Jumba had been inspired by the same DNA source when creating both experiments. This would be a similar concept to how Jumba reused some of Twang's DNA when creating [[Bragg (145)|Bragg]].
*Shoe's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is purple.
*The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Shoe as: "Experiment 113. Primary function: Negative event generator."
*His number is a likely reference to the number 13, which is considered unlucky by most Western cultures.
*Shoe's holographic silhouette appeared in "[[Snooty (episode)|Snooty]]".
**Shoe is shown to have two different graphic designs on [[Jumba's Computer|Jumba's computer]].

'''Shortstuff''', also known as '''Experiment 297''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to sabotage mechanical devices; specifically, he is naturally drawn to electrical machinery, which he then shorts out to create utter chaos. Due to him being accidentally enlarged, his one true place is as a carnival ride.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 297 was the 297th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to sabotage mechanical devices. 297 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 297's pod landing in a sewage pipe.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Shortstuff - Shortstuff moments after activation.png|thumb|left|Shortstuff moments after his activation]]
[[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] (in his "Kenny" disguise) was too short to participate in any of the carnival rides, so [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] tried to treat him to some lemonade instead. However, when the vendor offended Stitch about his size, the latter broke the vendor's lemonade cart. When lemonade from the broken cart trickled into the pipe, it touched 297's pod, activating the experiment.

[[Gantu]], who was at the amusement park with [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]], criticized the carnival games, while Reuben was having fun winning prizes and later attempted to eat a colossal submarine sandwich, but Gantu thwarted him. Gantu suddenly saw 297 and grabbed him, but the latter was able to escape by simply pinching Gantu.

While 297 likely began his rampage, Stitch, who wanted to be bigger than his normal size, rummaged through [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s devices. Since Jumba was away doing community service, Lilo allowed [[Pleakley]] to enlarge Stitch with Jumba's [[Protoplasmic Growth Ray|growth ray]].

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Shortstuff - Giant Shortstuff due to Jumba's growth ray.png|thumb|Giant Shortstuff]]
Unfortunately, during Stitch's growth process, Gantu came to the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]] looking for 297, whom Lilo lied about capturing. Gantu then saw a humongous Stitch towering over him after he overconfidently compared his vast size to Lilo's. When she explained what had happened and threatened to make Stitch even bigger, Gantu was forced to retreat.

Later, 297 had proceeded to sabotage every ride at the amusement park before being chased by Lilo and Stitch, the latter having great difficulty due to his enormous size that made him unbalanced. 297 was then captured in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] and taken back to the house, where Lilo named him Shortstuff (because he liked to short out stuff).

While Stitch was asleep on the couch, Lilo convinced Pleakley to shrink him back to his normal size. Unfortunately, while Pleakley fired up Jumba's growth ray, Shortstuff was able to use his claws to escape containment and attempted to sabotage the device. However, in the process, the ray enlarged Shortstuff into a behemoth just as he fled outside. Stitch then requested to be enlarged into an equal behemoth so he could take on Shortstuff.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Shortstuff - A giant Shortstuff versus a giant Stitch.png|thumb|left|Shortstuff vs. Stitch]]
Meanwhile, a humongous Shortstuff resumed his rampage at the carnival, where he engaged an equally gigantic Stitch in battle. At first, Shortstuff was able to easily overpower Stitch, but after Jumba arrived and shrunk Stitch back to his normal, functional size with the shrink ray, the latter easily defeated Shortstuff, who was restrained with ropes.

Shortstuff's size was never reverted, and as a result, he found his one true place as an amusement park ride, which Lilo and Stitch got to try out.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Shortstuff, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Shortstuff participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by swatting attacking Leroys with his huge claws until a bunch of Leroys ensnared Shortstuff, causing him to fall over.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Shortstuff made [[We Wishy You a Washy Christmas|a cameo appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime as an image on a computer screen (where he was shown to be at his normal size). [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] was going to unleash him on the [[Izayoi Island|island]], but [[Gantu]] somehow confused Shortstuff's number (297) with [[Wishy-Washy (267)|Wishy-Washy]]'s number (267) and accidentally sent the latter instead.

==Personality==
Shortstuff is shown to be short-tempered, reckless and clever. Armed with four pincers, he is not exactly afraid to take on bigger opponents. He also seems to be quite tolerant of his enormous size after he was accidentally enlarged. As a giant, he was still able to wreak havoc and overpower an equally giant Stitch in battle. When Shortstuff was tamed and became a carnival ride after his defeat, he didn't seem to mind at all.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Shortstuff is a small, red-orange crab-like experiment with four pincer-like claws, four spindle legs, dark blue eyes, a thin mouth with a turquoise tongue, and two small antennae on his head. Originally the size of a crab, he was accidentally enlarged to twice the size of a house. He was also returned to his normal size as seen in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

===Special abilities===
Shortstuff can sabotage machinery by entering and then cutting the mechanism's electrical wiring using his claws, thus short-circuiting the appliance. He is also able to swivel at the waist more than 360 degrees. At his giant size, Shortstuff could overpower an equally giant [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] in battle.

===Weaknesses===
Shortstuff can only carry out his original function at his smaller size. When he was exposed to [[Protoplasmic Growth Ray|Jumba's growth ray]], he could no longer wreak havoc on machinery.

==Trivia==
*Shortstuff is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having dark blue eyes instead.
*Shortstuff, [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]], [[Clink (086)|Clink]], [[Gotchu (031)|Gotchu]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have claws/pincers. Interestingly, all four official experiments have characteristics similar to crustaceans.
*Shortstuff, along with [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Dorkifier (122)|Dorkifier]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], [[Butter (227)|Butter]], [[Spike (319)|Spike]], [[Yang (502)|Yang]], [[Richter (513)|Richter]], [[Phoon (540)|Phoon]], [[Tank (586)|Tank]], [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]], and one [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed experiment]], are the only known experiments that are primarily quadrupeds.
*Shortstuff's manner of defeat is very similar to Part I of ''[[wikipedia:Gulliver's Travels|Gulliver's Travels]]''.
*Shortstuff's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green.
*Oddly, when Shortstuff's image is reflected off of Stitch's eyes in ''[[The Origin of Stitch]]'', he is facing directly at the screen instead of to his right.

He is designed to shred important documents. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "[[:Category:Mrs. Hasagawa's experiments|cats]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 134 was the 134th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to shred important documents. 134 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]]. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 134's pod being one of them.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 134's pod for an apricot and placed it in a colander for later consumption along with numerous other pods.

After [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] redecorated Mrs. Hasagawa's yard without her permission, she was less than thrilled with the results, but decided to thank them for their work with the "apricots". The pods were then revealed, but before Lilo and Stitch could stop her, she washed them with a watering can, thus activating the experiments.

After his activation, 134 began to carry out his primary function by shredding Mrs. Hasagawa's important mail. Lilo and Stitch believed the experiments to be a danger to Mrs. Hasagawa and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley|Pleakley,]] decided to capture them all. 134 was then [[Prison Capsule|captured]] by unknown means.

134 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 134 was then named Shredder.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Shredder, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Shredder participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Shredder is a sea-green experiment with a shredder-shaped head, sharp steel teeth, large ears, slightly closed black eyes and a blue nose.

===Special abilities===
Shredder's head acts as a shredder; sheets of paper can be inserted through a slot in the back of Shredder's head and then be shredded through his mouth.

==Trivia==
*In ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]'', Shredder is seen with a purple nose, but in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', he is seen with a green nose.
*Shredder was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*An error on the ''Leroy & Stitch'' DVD cover shows Shredder's ears on his back instead of his head.
