'''Sparky''', also known as '''Experiment 221''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is the first experiment to be activated and rehabilitated, and first appeared in ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''. He is designed to create crippling electric surges. His one true place is powering [[Kilauea Lighthouse]], which had been previously abandoned for years due to it requiring too much electricity. 

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 221 was the 221st genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his electrical abilities to create crippling electric power surges. 221 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

===''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''===
[[File:Stitch! The Movie - Sparky moments after activation.png|thumb|left|Sparky moments after his activation]]
[[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] activated 221's pod in the bathtub (whose faucet served as a handy water source) so he could recharge [[Jumba's Ship|Jumba's ship]] in order for them to go back in space and rescue [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], who had been kidnapped by [[Gantu]]. However, 221 had other ideas, and after destroying the [[Lilo's House|house]]'s power supply, he then escaped onto the [[Kauai|island]].

221 managed to evade capture while short-circuiting some portions of [[Kokaua Town]] until he attacked the [[Birds of Paradise Hotel]], where Lilo and Stitch were able to catch him by trapping him in a glass vase.

Lilo and Stitch took 221 back to their house, where the latter and Stitch discovered from their interaction that they had much in common and were truly ''ʻohana''. Thus, Stitch refused to allow 221 (later named Sparky) to be handed over to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] as part of a ransom.

When Lilo, Stitch and Sparky arrived at the location of the ransom exchange, Stitch saved Jumba while Lilo released Sparky to prevent him from being recaptured by Hämsterviel. However, when Sparky saw the [[Grand Councilwoman]] prepare to destroy the other remaining experiments along with Hämsterviel, he chose to overload her [[Federation Ship|ship]]'s power grid, saving the experiments and, unintentionally, allowing Hämsterviel to escape with them. When Sparky noticed this, he, along with Lilo and Stitch, stowed away on [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's leaving ship]].

Later aboard [[Dr. Hämsterviel's Ship|Hämsterviel's mothership]], when Sparky discovered Stitch about to enter a cloning process in which he would be vivisected by a laser, the former freed his cousin by overloading the machine, and the two took revenge on Hämsterviel.

When Lilo and Stitch later trapped Gantu and [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] aboard Gantu's ship, Sparky disabled the ship's navigation and ejected it from Hämsterviel's mothership. The three then used the mothership to return to Earth with Hämsterviel in tow.

[[File:Stitch! The Movie - Sparky powering Kilauea Lighthouse.png|thumb|Sparky powering the lighthouse]]
Afterwards, Lilo and Stitch found Sparky's one true place powering the abandoned [[Kilauea Lighthouse]], where he could make the giant beacon light work again, and as it was big enough, he would not short it out when he touched it.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
After the film, Sparky became a supporting character in the series. [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] often visited him along with other experiments for various problems.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - The Asteroid - Sparky watching idly at lighthouse.png|thumb|left|Sparky keeping watch at the lighthouse]]
Sparky reappeared in "[[Elastico (episode)|Elastico]]" as one of the audience members for Lilo's hula dance.

In "[[The Asteroid]]", Sparky was one of the six experiments that Stitch convinced to come with him and Lilo to save Earth from an approaching asteroid. Sparky used his electric powers to jump-start the ship and, along the journey, tease [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]] and shock [[Pleakley]] when the latter touched him.

In "[[Angel (episode)|Angel]]", Sparky was one of the experiments that [[Angel (624)|Angel]] reverted to evil using her song. Later, Sparky and the other depraved experiments attacked Stitch aboard a ship, but Angel turned them to good again before they could finish Stitch off. Working together, the experiments were then able to successfully escape the ship with Stitch.

In "[[Skip (episode)|Skip]]", Sparky was one of the wanted fugitives who had already been captured in an alternate future where Hämsterviel ruled Earth.

Sparky was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that joined Stitch in a rebellion against Gantu. Sparky even used his electrical powers on Reuben when the latter lazed about instead of rowing the boat they were on.

In "[[Ploot (episode)|Ploot]]", Lilo tried to convince Sparky to help her defeat [[Ploot (505)|Ploot]], but he was unable to because an off-screen spectator complained about them tampering with the lighthouse.

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Sparky was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Snafu - Sparky surrounded by Gantu's weapon system.png|thumb|Sparky surrounded by Gantu's weapon system]]
In "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", Sparky was one of the experiments that joined Lilo and Stitch on a mission to rescue Gantu's captive experiments (in actuality, Lilo lured Sparky away from the lighthouse with a trail of batteries, which he ate). Sparky helped break into the ship, and after the rescue team successfully freed the captive experiments, he was seen playing with them in Lilo's obstacle course.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
In the film's opening, Sparky can be seen from the [[Kilauea Lighthouse|lighthouse]] waving hello to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]].

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Sparky, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Sparky participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by shocking attacking Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Sparky has appeared multiple times in the ''Stitch!'' anime. He premiered in "[[An Electrifying Experience]]" where Sparky is kidnapped by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] and put under mind control in an attempt to steal [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]'s [[Good Deed Counter]]. Sparky is sent to [[Izayoi Island]] where he causes chaos, thus having Stitch and [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] search the town to investigate. They hear stories of a yellow ghost roaming about and finally catch up to him. Stitch was very excited to see his cousin, but this changed after Sparky shocked Stitch and ran off.

Later on, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] notices the head cap on Sparky's head, recognizing it as a mind-controlling device. Suddenly, [[Gantu]] and Sparky arrive at Yuna's house, but after a confrontation with Yuna's [[Gramma|grandmother]], Sparky runs away. In the woods, Sparky takes Stitch's Good Deed Counter, but lightning (courtesy of the [[Chitama Spiritual Stone|Spiritual Stone]]) causes Sparky's head cap to come apart, freeing him from mind control. Sparky and Stitch let bygones be bygones and reunite. Sparky would later make other cameo appearances and have a recurring role as one of Stitch's closest friends.

In the two-part Season 1 finale "[[Stitch vs. Hämsterviel Pt. I|Stitch vs. Hämsterviel]]", Hämsterviel puts Sparky along with [[Felix (010)|Felix]] and [[Angel (624)|Angel]] under his control. He later appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Like his cousin Stitch, Sparky is shown to be highly mischievous and destructive, as well as very hyperactive and fun-loving. He also shares Stitch's habit of picking his nose with his tongue. Sparky was once a bad experiment, as he was programmed into his very being by the alien mad scientist, Jumba Jookiba. His original purpose was to cause massive electrical surges that would disorientate those caught in it, but he changed when he was captured and rehabilitated shortly after his activation.

After his reformation, Sparky became a different kind of genetic experiment. Overall, he is very friendly, though he's quite cautious in new places. He also still holds a mischievous side to him, and although he has turned good, he sometimes cannot help but mess with electronics and machines.

Sparky holds his ''ʻohana'' — a word that another experiment (Stitch) and a little girl (Lilo) taught him — very close (''ʻohana'' meaning "family" in Hawaiian). He will help his family and friends whenever they need a hand, and though he might occasionally get into an argument with them, he is not one to turn down a cry for help.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Sparky looks like a bipedal mutated cross between a koala, ground sloth, Chinese dragon, and gecko. He has light yellow fur and a pale yellow chin, belly and mouth. He has a small body, small, short, hollow, round but triangular ears at the sides of a large, narrow, oval-shaped head, and big dark blue eyes. He has a round, brown nose, a large wide mouth and two long forked antennae that protrude from the sides of his muzzle. His arms are skinny with a brown pad-mark in the center of each paw. His legs are stubby and he has a long, bent, slightly twisted tail in a Z-shape with a pointed brown tip. He has a set of large flat jagged teeth, and the inside of his mouth is a blue color with a turquoise tongue.

When he turns himself into an electrical current, the lower half of his body turns into a streak of electricity, making himself somewhat resemble an Asiatic dragon.

In this form, he has a stronger electrical dragon-like appearance, and will closely resemble a dragon when flying as well, with a scratchy alien voice.

===Special abilities===
Sparky can turn his body into an electrical current, allowing him to fly or travel through electric-powered generators, appliances, devices, outlets, power lines, machines, and other similar things. Another electrical current is generated between the two long antennae on his head, which can be used to create crippling electrical surges and send jolts towards foes (or when he gets irritated, annoyed, or is pulling pranks). He can also shoot lightning blasts from his antennae and generate and release massive discharges of electrical energy. It is shown that he likes eating batteries. Originally designed to short-circuit electric-powered devices, Sparky can also use these electrical currents to power machines, lights, and such. 

Like his "cousin" [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], he has a second pair of retractable arms at his side, though he rarely uses them. His short body can extend into a large streak of a tail as he moves through the air at high speeds, his body shining with electricity. Also, like Stitch, he can climb onto walls, hang from ceilings, and see in the dark.

Sparky can speak a broken English. He can also speak [[Tantalog language|Tantalog]], which is his original language. What he says seems to have a distinctive "buzz" to it (Example: "Cuz-z-zin…", which is how he says "cousin").

===Weaknesses===
While he does not appear to be weak to water (having resided in a lighthouse close to the ocean), Sparky cannot pass through non-conductive objects and obstacles, which allowed Lilo to trap him in a glass vase and a [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clone]] to capture him with a net.

==Trivia==
*Sparky's design was first revealed in a bonus feature trivia game on the original ''[[Lilo & Stitch]]'' DVD, before he officially debuted in ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''.
**Sparky also appeared in a DVD bonus feature of ''Stitch! The Movie'' in the experiment gallery.
*Sparky and [[Zap (603)|Zap]] are the only two known experiments with primary functions directly involving electricity, and both of their names relate to electricity as well.
*Sparky is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having dark blue eyes instead.
*Sparky is the first experiment to be turned from bad to good in ''Stitch! The Movie'', which is actually the pilot to ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]'' that premiered shortly after.
*Along with Stitch and [[Kixx (601)|Kixx]], Sparky is one of the few known experiments to say the infamous quote: "Meega, nala kweesta!" during his moment of appalling Stitch.
**He is also the first experiment shown to demonstrate sharing Stitch's trait of having two extra arms, the others being [[Deforestator (515)|Deforestator]], [[Ace (262)|Ace]], and [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]].
**Additionally, he is the first experiment shown to share Stitch's habit of picking his nose with his tongue, the second being [[Angel (624)|Angel]] and the third being [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]].
*Sparky appears, along with several other ''Lilo & Stitch'' characters, in a [[Stitch Meets High School Musical|parody]] of the [[disney:Disney Channel|Disney Channel]] [[disney:Disney Channel Original Movie|Original Movie]] ''[[disney:High School Musical|High School Musical]]'', which was broadcast as part of the ''High School Musical: Around the World'' one-year anniversary special.
*Sparky's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green.
*To date, Sparky is the first (and so far only) Disney character by [[disney:Disney Television Animation|Disney Television Animation]] to appear in the [[disney:Kingdom Hearts (series)|''Kingdom Hearts'' series]].
*Sparky is also the few experiments aside from Stitch and Angel to be majorly popular, such as being a costumed character at the [[disney:Disney Experiences|Disney Parks]].
*Sparky's antennae and tail appear in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.
*Sparky appears in ''[[disney:Disney Emoji Blitz|Disney Emoji Blitz]]'' in a cameo during Angel's Power, but he is unplayable.

'''Spats''', also known as '''Experiment 397''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to cause local populations to argue with each other so they do not notice someone taking over their planet. If the afflicted individuals count to ten, their belligerence will dissolve. His one true place is with [[Wizard Kelly]], making his professional wrestlers fight more convincingly.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 397 was the 397th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to instigate arguments between individuals. 397 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 397's pod landing in the window of [[Jumba's Ship|Jumba's ship]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:ScreenCapture 09.07.13 14-21-24.png|thumb|left|Spats after being activated]]
When [[disney:The Proud Family|the Proud Family]] visits [[Kauai]] for a vacation, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]] invite their guests to stay at "[[Jumba & Pleakley's Bed & Not Breakfast]]" hotel. [[Penny Proud]] gets more acquainted with Lilo and Stitch, while [[Oscar Proud]] complains about the hotel's accommodations. Later, [[Suga Mama Proud|Suga Mama]] soaks herself in a hot tub, while her dog [[Puff]] sleeps on a throw rug.

Meanwhile, a squirrel appears inside one of the windows of [[Jumba's Ship|Jumba's ship]] and notices 397's experiment pod. The squirrel mistakes the pod for a nut and attempts to eat it. When it finds out it could not eat the pod, the squirrel throws it into a bowl of bath bombs. Shortly after, Suga Mama reaches for a bath bomb, but takes out 397's pod instead. Mistaking the pod for a bath bomb, Suga Mama drops it into the bathtub, activating 397, named Spats. He then zaps the squirrel and Puff, causing the two animals to fight.

[[File:ScreenCapture 09.07.13 14-24-21.png|thumb|Spats firing his laser]]
Spats causes more mischief in [[Kokaua Town|town]] by zapping numerous pairs who end up fighting as well. His victims include [[BeBe & CeCe Proud|BeBe and CeCe]], followed by Oscar and [[Trudy Proud]], then Jumba and [[Mr. Cooper]], and later Lilo and Penny. A [[Charles and Mary|newlywed couple]] also becomes affected by Spats' argument-inducing ray.

Elsewhere, Stitch notices Spats being pursued by [[Gantu]]. However, he manages to evade both Gantu and Stitch, and eventually hitches a ride in the back of a jeep that Pleakley is driving. Spats then teases Stitch when the latter is unable to catch up with him. After making a vain attempt to break up Penny and Lilo's conflict, Stitch chases after Spats in [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]]'s [[X-Buggy|dune buggy]], taking the feuding girls with him.

Later, Stitch manages to track Spats down to an outdoor wrestling match, where the two cousins face off against each other on the roof of the arena. After a long battle between both experiments, Spats falls off the roof and into Penny's arms. She is angered by his presence at first, but after noticing Spats' cuteness, she starts to soften up. When Penny tries to talk to Lilo, the latter still wants to fight with her. Fortunately, Penny manages to resist her urge to fight by counting to ten and then convinces Lilo to do the same, which she does.

[[File:ScreenCapture-19-11-25-19h07m54s210.png|thumb|left|Spats with Penny Proud]]
After Lilo and Penny make up, the former is able to relieve the other brawling pairs by telling everyone through an overhead microphone to count to ten after Gantu, who was wrestling with Suga Mama all this time (due to Spats zapping them when Suga Mama attacked Gantu after he threatened to take Spats away from Penny earlier), went down for the count.

The next day, Lilo and Stitch find Spats a one true place with [[Wizard Kelly]]. He uses Spats to make his international wrestlers fight more convincingly. Penny reveals to Lilo about having a perfect newspaper article for her school, and she along with the rest of the Proud Family leave on good terms.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Spats, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Spats participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] probably by making attacking Leroys fight each other.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Personality==
Spats is sneaky, clever, and cunning and will do whatever it takes to start an argument. He loves to cause a ruckus and provoke a fight or quarrel. He is also a good actor and does a great job of faking being innocent and cute to get what he wants or to trick individuals.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Spats is a small, yellow squirrel/cat-like experiment with two short antennae above his eyes, black-violet eyes, a small red-orange round nose, a wide mouth with sharp cat-like fangs and a green tongue, and two prongs on the tip of his long bushy tail (seen when fully outstretched). He has orange spots on his forehead, a white belly, and orange markings on his back. He spends most of his time on all fours like a quadruped, but does have the ability to walk on two feet, like a biped.

===Special abilities===
Spats can fire a yellow ray from the prongs on the tip of his tail that causes any two individuals zapped to constantly argue with each other. The sound of a bell is heard when this happens.

===Weaknesses===
The arguing effect of Spats' ray can be reversed by counting to ten.

==Trivia==
*Stitch and Pleakley are the only two main characters to not get zapped by Spats.
*He is one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to.
*Spats' [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is yellow.
*Spats, [[Morpholomew (316)|Morpholomew]], and [[Lax (285)|Lax]] are the only experiments that debuted in [[:Category:Crossovers|crossovers]].
*The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Spats as: "Experiment 397. Primary function: Argument instigator."

'''Spike''', also known as '''Experiment 319''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to alter the intelligence of entire populations by shooting quills that increase their silliness by 99% when struck, leaving them only 1% clever for the next 48 hours. His one true place is in [[Pleakley]]'s E.A.R.W.A.X. group, hugging and thus taming other truant experiments, after he is given protective armor to cover his goofiness-inducing spines.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 319 was the 319th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to fire spines like darts that make his victims unintelligent by causing any hit victim's goofiness level to increase by 99%, leaving them only 1% clever. 319 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 319's pod landing by an outdoor stage.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spike - Spike climbs onto stage after activation.png|thumb|left|Spike after being activated]]
When a clumsy servant carrying drinking water bumped into [[Dr. Gladys Okra|the public speaker]], the water bottle on the tray fell onto the stage and trickled out, which touched 319's pod, activating the experiment. 319 then climbed onto the stage and spiked Dr. Okra and her servant, causing them to act goofy. He next rolled in front of the entire audience and attacked them as well, scaring them all away.

Later, 319 attacked a [[Museum of Natural History Kauai|museum]] until he was captured in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] by [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], but not before spiking him and [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]. Luckily, 319's goofiness-inducing spines didn't seem to affect Jumba as much as Stitch (since the former was already a genius).

319 was then taken back to the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]] and named Spike, who ultimately served as one of the experiments in [[Pleakley]]'s E.A.R.W.A.X. group. While the captive Spike was being rehabilitated, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] made a vain attempt to get a goofy Stitch to become smart again in time for the upcoming Ohana-Rama.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spike - Captive Spike at Pleakley's seminar.png|thumb|Spike in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group]]
During Pleakley's seminar, he bored most of the experiments while discussing therapy topics from Dr. Okra. When a fight broke out between [[Slushy (523)|Slushy]] and [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]], a stray fireball from Splodyhead destroyed Spike's container, freeing him. Spike then went on a rampage, chasing [[Nosy (199)|Nosy]] around the house and eventually targeting Pleakley.

Forced to resolve the issue, Pleakley left for a moment, rummaged through the closet, and donned makeshift armor against Spike's spines. He then attempted hugging therapy on Spike, which surprisingly pacified the latter who sobbed pitifully. The other experiments, awed by Spike's outcome, tried out Pleakley's hugging-and-crying method as well.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spike - Spike offering Lilo a hug.png|thumb|left|A rehabilitated Spike offering Lilo a hug]]
The following night, Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, Pleakley and Spike attended the Ohana-Rama, where [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] sunk Lilo's team by answering each question correctly. Spike then offered Lilo a hug to cheer her up when she felt discouraged. She declined, however, because although Spike was rehabilitated, a stray spine would likely affect her intelligence.

Later during the quiz contest, Lilo and Spike followed Stitch backstage (when he ran after an [[wikipedia:Elvis Presley|Elvis]] CD he unstuck from his nose) to discover that [[Teresa]] was secretly helping Mertle cheat. Thus, Lilo convinced Spike to hug Teresa, who got pricked and kept giving Mertle completely silly answers as a result. After Lilo won the Ohana-Rama, Mertle stormed out in a rage. Spike felt sorry for Mertle and decided to hug her as well, spiking the latter.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spike - Nosy hugs Spike as other experiments applaud.png|thumb|Spike hugging Nosy]]
Spike later found his one true place in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group, where he used hugging therapy to tame other truant experiments while wearing similar protective armor to cover his goofiness-inducing spines, with Nosy even becoming one of Spike's patients.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Spike, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Spike participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by firing goofiness-inducing spines at attacking Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Spike has appeared multiple times in the ''Stitch!'' anime, including [[Link-age|one instance]] in Season 2, along with [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]], [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]], [[Link (251)|Link]], and [[Woody (507)|Woody]]. It is revealed that [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] reverted these experiments to evil using a recording of [[Angel (624)|Angel]]'s song, thus enabling them to wreak havoc on the [[Izayoi Island|island]]. In [[Spike 2.0|another episode]], Spike was also used by Hämsterviel to try to sabotage a quiz competition. His abilities were [[Transmutation|modified]] in this episode so that he only reduces the victim's intelligence, and it can be magnified by squeezing his nose. It is also shown that he has the ability to roll into a ball and launch his spikes while spinning at incredibly high speeds. In "[[Shogun]]", it is shown that Spike was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault.

Spike [[Dark-End|later appeared]] as one of the experiments who helped [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] fight [[Dark End]]. He also appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Spike is shown to be troublesome, as his spines pose a dangerous threat to anyone pricked by them. He also has a feisty side to him and will attack any target, even if he is outnumbered. However, he is not afraid to express emotion as shown when he tearfully cried his heart out while Pleakley hugged him during the E.A.R.W.A.X. session. This not only rehabilitated Spike, but also motivated him to be a hugging therapist and follow Pleakley's hugging-and-crying method.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Spike is a large, quadrupedal, dark blue pangolin/porcupine-like experiment covered in incredibly sharp white-tipped spines from his head down to his long tail. He has black eyes, a red nose, and sharp black claws. His face, underbelly, and paws are white, and the only areas not covered in spines.

===Special abilities===
Spike can fire his spines like darts that are capable of hitting multiple targets at once. His quills also contain a venom that increases the victim's goofiness by 99% when struck, leaving them only 1% clever. His quills can poke and affect anyone, even if Spike had no intention when he is being friendly. He is able to roll into a ball and launch his spikes while spinning at incredibly high speeds as seen in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

===Weaknesses===
The effect of Spike's goofiness-inducing spines only lasts for 48 hours. He is also emotionally susceptible to hugging therapy.

==Trivia==
*Spike is clearly based on porcupines, but unlike him, real-life porcupines cannot throw/shoot their quills, nor are their spines poisonous.
*When Jumba got pricked by Spike, he did not appear to be affected. However, he states that he is not immune to the effects of his creation, and that he does not act silly because even 1% of his intelligence is far superior to that of an average human being's intelligence.
*Spike is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to.
*Spike, along with [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Dorkifier (122)|Dorkifier]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], [[Butter (227)|Butter]], [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]], [[Yang (502)|Yang]], [[Richter (513)|Richter]], [[Phoon (540)|Phoon]], [[Tank (586)|Tank]], [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]], and one [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed experiment]], are the only known experiments that are primarily quadrupeds.
*Spike is one of the six known experiments to be rehabilitated by someone other than Lilo and Stitch, the other five being Gigi, [[Elastico (345)|Elastico]], [[Yaarp (613)|Yaarp]], [[Frenchfry (062)|Frenchfry]], and [[Snooty (277)|Snooty]]. 
**Spike, alongside Yaarp, was rehabilitated by Pleakley.
*Spike's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is yellow in [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]]. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, it is white.
*In the English dub of the anime episode "[[Link-age]]", [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] states that Spike's favorite type of sandwich is a [[wikipedia:Shish kebab|shish kebab]] [[wikipedia:Gyros|gyro]].

Splat can use the small roller between his front legs to level roads and other surfaces.

'''Splodyhead''', also known as '''Experiment 619 '''and '''Splody''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to attack using fiery plasma blasts from his nozzle-like nose; he can also pitch softballs similarly. His one true place is lighting tiki torches at the luau.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 619 was the 619th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his fiery plasma blasts to cause massive chaos and damage. 619 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Splodyhead - Splodyhead struggles in the ocean.png|thumb|left|Splodyhead after activation as he struggles in the water]]
619's pod was eventually discovered by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and [[Gantu]], who were chasing after it while unintentionally disrupting an outdoor wedding at one point. During their struggle, a seagull snatched the pod and took it back to its nest on a cliff face by the Forbidden Island of [[wikipedia:Niihau|Niʻihau]]. When the gull was unable to peck 619's pod open, it angrily kicked it out, causing the pod to plummet into the ocean, activating the experiment. 619 then quickly jumped ashore and proceeded to take over the seagull's nest.

Later, 619 spotted Lilo, Stitch, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] and Gantu arriving on the island for him. Becoming extremely hostile, he attacked and destroyed both factions' campsites, which put the six in jeopardy. Stitch and Gantu, believing the other one was at fault, had a short-lived battle with each other before Lilo intervened to break it up.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Splodyhead - Splodyhead preparing to fire plasma blast.png|thumb|FIRE IN THE HOLE!!!]]
When the two factions saw 619, whom Lilo named Splodyhead, invading the nest, he attacked with raining plasma blasts, forcing Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, Pleakley, Reuben and Gantu to take cover. Using his plasma attacks, Splodyhead managed to keep the six trapped, yet refused to come down to finish them off, due to him being outnumbered.

While Splodyhead waited to pick them off one by one, Stitch and Gantu resumed their conflict, since they both thought the other one was evil. Learning what Splodyhead was up to, Lilo told the two rivals that if they wanted to be rescued, they would have to put their differences aside and try to work together. Stitch and Gantu initially refused, but after both factions took a vote, Lilo was nominated to lead them to safety.

As the evening progressed, the six built and sent out a decoy raft as bait, which Splodyhead targeted and blew up. Convinced the danger was over, Splodyhead left the nest, thus allowing Lilo and Jumba to ambush him and temporarily incapacitate his plasma weapons with water. Defenseless, Splodyhead attempted to escape back to the nest but was stopped when Stitch tackled him, enabling Gantu to capture Splodyhead in a makeshift net and put him into a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]].

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Splodyhead - Splodyhead charring a piece of cake.png|thumb|left|Splodyhead scorching cake]]
Realizing they had worked together, Stitch attempted to make amends with Gantu by shaking hands with the latter, but Gantu ungratefully pushed the former aside. The two factions and Splodyhead were soon rescued from the island by [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] and [[David Kawena|David]] driving motorboats, but not before Lilo briefly lectured Gantu's brash nature.

Splodyhead was shortly after taken back to [[Kauai]], where Lilo and Stitch found him a one true place lighting tiki torches at the luau. He also charred a piece of cake with his fiery plasma before devouring it.

In "[[Houdini (episode)|Houdini]]", Splodyhead was one of the audience members for Stitch's bungled magic act.

In "[[Slushy (episode)|Slushy]]", Jumba adjusted Splodyhead's thermostat so he wouldn't overheat in hot temperatures, to which he politely thanked Jumba in return. Splodyhead was later sent to [[Slushy (523)|Slushy]]'s ice fortress to defeat the latter. After a long-drawn-out battle between the two experiments, Splodyhead was defeated when Slushy froze him into a block of ice. He was later freed and blasted a fireball into the sky at the top of [[Waialeale Peak]] to clear Slushy's snowstorms.

Splodyhead reappeared in "[[Slugger (episode)|Slugger]]" as part of Lilo's softball team.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spike - Splodyhead and Slushy performing hugging-and-crying therapy.png|thumb|Splodyhead and Slushy hugging]]
In "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]", Splodyhead was one of the experiments in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group. When a stray snowball from Slushy accidentally hit Splodyhead (who had suffered from boredom), a battle ensued between the two experiments, which ended when Pleakley convinced Slushy and Splodyhead to attempt hugging therapy on each other.

Slushy and Splodyhead were seen on a computer screen in "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]", posing as evil creations of Jumba's as part of a hoax to fool [[Mortlegax]], the head of E.G.O. industries.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
Splodyhead was seen early in the movie lighting an overhead tiki torch as [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to make sure all the experiments were happy in the one true place they belonged.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Splodyhead, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Splodyhead participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by blasting attacking Leroys away with plasma.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Splodyhead made [[The Return of Amnesio|a cameo appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime as one of the experiments in [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison cell]]. He has also appeared numerous other times, twice with [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]]. In the [[Stitch Power|first appearance]], Splodyhead and Plasmoid combated [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] when he was hypnotized by [[Swirly (383)|Swirly]] into fighting for Hämsterviel. In the [[New Town (episode)|second appearance]], Splodyhead and Plasmoid were [[Transmutation|modified]] by Hämsterviel to attack Stitch. Splodyhead was given a new ability to fire purple balls of a repulsive odor. Also, after the effects were reversed, Splodyhead could expel pink gas of an aromatic smell, the opposite of his modified ability. In "[[Shogun]]", it is shown that Splodyhead was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault. He made [[Dark-End|a final appearance]] in aiding Stitch in battle against [[Dark End]].

==Personality==
Splodyhead is an experiment controlled by his fiery disposition: he is fierce, greatly dislikes the water, and is shown to be hotheaded when provoked. He is loyal to his friends, but he does have an attitude. He knows when he is outnumbered, so he will often pick off his victims one by one. He likes his food "well done", as Lilo puts it, which usually means he burns or melts it. While he cannot talk (though he does understand what individuals are saying), he can still be intelligent and polite, as shown in "[[Slushy (episode)|Slushy]]" when he thanked Jumba for fixing his thermostat so he wouldn't overheat. He is known to be hostile and apparently shares a grudge with Slushy due to his opposing elemental power, but they resolved it in "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]".

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Splodyhead is a small-bodied, red six-legged (two arms and four hind tentacles) dragon-like experiment with a hole-like nose. He has a red and purple striped horn on his head with brick-red markings on his forehead and back. He has dark blue eyes with purple-red spots around them, two short red ears, and sort of pink fur from the bottom end of his belly all the way to the bottom of his mouth. He also has a turquoise tongue and a short red tail.

===Special abilities===
Splodyhead can fire plasma blasts from his nozzle-like nose, and this is achieved by a small nuclear reactor inside his body. He has also shown to channel these plasma blasts in streams of fire and/or shoot flames, and has displayed the ability to manipulate these flames into types of shields; he once created a large, monster-like shield out of liquid flames/lava, making it stop towards [[Slushy (523)|his victim]]. He can substitute almost any solid sphere for his plasma balls (such as softballs) if inserted into his nozzle/nose, and blast it with just as much force.

Splodyhead can also see in the dark, has heat vision, a targeting scanner, and zoom in/out abilities. His feet and hands create a sticky substance which lets him scale walls and ceilings, similar to [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. Splodyhead is able to stand on either all six of his legs or on just four.

He has the ability to fire purple balls of a repulsive odor while [[Transmutation|under the effects]] of [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], and has also shown to release pink gas of an aromatic smell.

===Weaknesses===
Water is shown to temporarily incapacitate Splodyhead's plasma-shooting ability. Also, he cannot swim and is unable to use his cannon when hurt badly.

==Trivia==
*In [[Splodyhead (episode)|his debut]], Splodyhead's number was pronounced as "six-nineteen" by Jumba, rather than the typical by-digit pronunciation of most other experiments (which would be "six-one-nine" in Splodyhead's case).
*Splodyhead is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having dark blue eyes instead.
*Splodyhead, [[Yang (502)|Yang]], and [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]] are the only known experiments that shoot plasma/lava balls. Also, Splodyhead, Yang, Plasmoid, [[Melty (228)|Melty]], and [[Heat (609)|Heat]] are the only known experiments whose powers are related to fire.
*Splodyhead, along with [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Dorkifier (122)|Dorkifier]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], [[Butter (227)|Butter]], [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]], [[Spike (319)|Spike]], Yang, [[Richter (513)|Richter]], [[Phoon (540)|Phoon]], [[Tank (586)|Tank]], and one [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed experiment]], are the only known experiments that are primarily quadrupeds.
*Splodyhead's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue in [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]]. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, it is red.
*In "[[Slushy (episode)|Slushy]]", Jumba somehow [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|erroneously referred to Splodyhead as 515]], a number taken by [[Deforestator (515)|Deforestator]].
*Splodyhead appears to share a grudge with [[Slushy (523)|Slushy]], but they resolved it in "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]".
*Splodyhead's head appears in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.
*Splodyhead made a cameo in ''[[disney:Big Hero 6|Big Hero 6]]'' as one of the pillows on [[disney:Fred (Big Hero 6)|Fred]]'s bed (alongside a Stitch pillow). This makes him the only experiment other than Stitch to appear in a [[disney:Disney Animated Canon|Disney Animated Canon]] film. He is also the only [[disney:Disney Television Animation|Disney Television Animation]] character to appear in a [[disney:Walt Disney Animation Studios|Walt Disney Animation Studios]] production.

'''Spooky''', also known as '''Experiment 300''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to terrify entire populations into submission by morphing into their worst fears; his forms are distinguishable by his glowing green eyes and hissing voice. His one true place is scaring trick-or-treaters on Halloween and (for the rest of the year) haunting the [[Haunted House|old, abandoned mansion]].

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 300 was the 300th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to terrorize his victims by morphing into their worst fears. 300 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 300's pod landing on a house roof.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spooky - Spooky after activation.png|thumb|left|Spooky after being activated]]
On Halloween night, a gust of wind caused 300's pod to roll down the roof's rain gutter and into a rain barrel, activating the experiment. 300 then noticed a mouse and scared it off by turning into a wild cat. When a dog attacked 300 because of the cat form, the latter frightened the dog away by turning into a dogcatcher, then fled the scene in his elastic form.

Shortly after, 300 attacked a children's Halloween party held at [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]]'s [[Kaiāulu Hale|school]], scaring [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] and [[Elena|the]] [[Teresa|hula]] [[Yuki|girls]] off by turning into a headless Lilo, then terrifying [[Moses Puloki|Moses]] by turning into a giant spider. Presumably after this, 300 lurked somewhere inside and waited for his next victim.

Lilo and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] later arrived to discover the party in disarray. When Stitch entered the kitchen to raid the fridge, 300 locked himself in the kitchen with Stitch and almost drowned the latter by turning into floodwaters. However, 300 was forced to retreat up through an air vent when Lilo noticed his presence, relieving Stitch.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spooky - Spooky transforms into Cobra Bubbles.png|thumb|Cobra Bubbles]]
Sometime later, 300 arrived at the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]], where he terrified [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] by turning into [[Cobra Bubbles]] and claiming he had come to take Lilo away. However, when Lilo and Stitch returned to the home and noticed Cobra to be 300 from his hissing voice, they exposed 300, named Spooky, as an impostor, thus forcing him to slip away again.

Lilo, Stitch, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]] followed Spooky into the [[Haunted House|abandoned mansion]], where he surprised and terrorized Lilo by turning into a clown. Lilo's shriek startled Stitch so much, he unintentionally fell into an indoor swimming pool. Spooky then chased after Lilo in his clown form, scaring her to the point where she clung to a high pillar screaming for help.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spooky - Spooky transforms into a clown.png|thumb|left|A clown]]
While Spooky left Lilo and Stitch to their fate, the latter attempted to save Lilo, but he lost his grip on the pool's diving board and sank to the bottom. However, he overcame his aquaphobia by singing "[[Aloha ʻOe]]" (a song that Lilo taught him as a coping tactic), and after emerging from the pool, he managed to rescue Lilo in the nick of time.

Meanwhile, Spooky defeated Jumba and Pleakley by turning into their worst fears: [[Mrs. Pleakley|Pleakley's mom]] and Jumba's ex-wife, but Stitch eventually saw and attacked Spooky's latter form. When Spooky noticed that Stitch had successfully faced his fears, and was thus undaunted by any other scary transformations, the former turned into a bat and attempted to escape up the chimney, but was ambushed and captured in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] by Stitch.

Spooky then found his one true place scaring trick-or-treaters on Halloween and (on other occasions) haunting the old, abandoned house.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - The Asteroid - Spooky transforms into an asteroid.png|thumb|An asteroid]]
In "[[The Asteroid]]", Spooky was one of the six experiments that Stitch convinced to come with him and Lilo to save Earth from an approaching asteroid (Spooky briefly morphed into one to clarify). Along the journey, [[Kixx (601)|Kixx]] kicked the back of Spooky's seat, causing the latter (using his nightmarish morphing ability) to retaliate. Spooky later attempted to use a monstrous form to scare Pleakley into giving him free soda, but Pleakley only replied with an order for Spooky to return to his seat.

Spooky was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that joined Stitch in a rebellion against [[Gantu]]. Spooky even morphed into Gantu for clarification, then later morphed into a spiky, sea urchin-like fruit when the ex-captain was about to bite into him.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Spooky, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Spooky participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by using nightmarish forms to scare Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Spooky made [[Spooky Toons|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where he was [[Transmutation|released]] by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] along with [[Toons (112)|Toons]] to scare the children of a summer camp. It is revealed that he uses a form of telepathy to read his victim's mind and discover their worst fears. In "[[Shogun]]", it is shown that Spooky was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Spooky wasn't one of the experiments that was activated.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
In the form of an individual or other creature, Spooky is completely indistinguishable from the real thing, except for glowing, olive-green eyes and a hissing voice.

In his true form, Spooky is a green blob-like experiment with glowing, olive-green eyes, a wide mouth with a turquoise tongue, two stubby arms and legs, and three round, stubby spikes on his back, greatly resembling the other Disney (and Halloween-based) character [[disney:Oogie Boogie|Oogie Boogie]]. In the anime, when he appears transmutated, Spooky has bright purple eyes.

===Personality===
Spooky causes chaos by fulfilling the purpose he was programmed for: terrifying his enemies by turning into their worst fears. However, he went further by directly harming his victims, aside from just scaring them, and seems to be more dangerous than most experiments. Originally malicious and slightly sadistic, he often chooses to not only provoke fear in his victims, but also cause other mental trauma such as sadness and terror. He tends to slither and hiss like a snake, despite his most common form of being a blob. When victims are brave enough to stand up against his scares, Spooky becomes annoyed and apparently powerless against them. However, after being reformed, Spooky only scares individuals for fun on Halloween. He is also loyal and helpful to his friends, joining Stitch's rebellion to fight off Gantu.

===Special abilities===
Spooky can shapeshift/morph into his victims' deepest, darkest fears by taking the form of any person, animal or object. Spooky also turns elastic when moving. As shown in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, he can use a form of telepathy to read his victim's mind and discover their worst fears, but he has only displayed this while [[Transmutation|under the effects]] of [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]].

====Forms====
Spooky has morphed into many forms. These include:
*A wild cat (a mouse's worse fear)
*A dogcatcher (a dog's worst fear)
*A fat, elastic, slug-shaped version of his true form
*Headless Lilo ([[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] and [[Elena|the]] [[Teresa|hula]] [[Yuki|girls]]' worst fear)
*A giant spider ([[Moses Puloki|Moses]]' worst fear)
*Floodwaters ([[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]'s worst fear of drowning)
*[[Cobra Bubbles]] (representing [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]]'s worst fear of losing her sister)
*A clown ([[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]]'s worst fear)
*[[Mrs. Pleakley]] (twice; representing [[Pleakley]]'s worst fear of disappointing his mother)
*Jumba's ex-wife (twice; [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s worst fear)
*A water monster
*A twister
*A People Eating Puss Monkey (from ''[[The Origin of Stitch]]'')
*A bat
*A giant python (a random boy's worst fear)
*An asteroid
*[[Gantu]]
*A spiky, sea urchin-like fruit
*A version of his true form with massive fangs
*A large, muscular version of his true form with an alligator-like snout (a.k.a. "Spookymorp" according to [[disney:Stitch's Great Escape!|Stitch's Great Escape!]])
*A Goo Gobbling Booger Beast (from ''The Origin of Stitch'')
*A zombie
*[[Angel (624)|Angel]] (when she is angry at Stitch)
*A [[Tigerlily Sakai|Tigerlily]] dinosaur-like creature

===Weaknesses===
As Spooky's ability to turn into his victims' worst fears is his only weapon and defense, if one overcomes their fears, Spooky will be rendered defenseless.

==Trivia==
*Spooky was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Spooky is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having glowing, olive-green eyes instead.
*Spooky is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to.
**He is also one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to.
*Spooky and [[Morpholomew (316)|Morpholomew]] are the only known experiments that have shapeshifting/transforming abilities.
*Spooky is shown to have the ability to speak, although he appears to be only capable of [[:Category:Talking experiments|speaking fluently]] when shapeshifting into something that can talk.
*Jumba referred to Spooky as "X-300" (ex three hundred) and mentions that his impression of Jumba's ex-wife is frightening.
**Disney has used "X-" (X with a hyphen) in promotional material as a shorthand prefix for "Experiment".
*Unlike most experiments, Spooky's number is pronounced as a whole number ("three hundred") instead of three individual digits (which in his case would have been "three-oh-oh") as per the norm for the experiments.
**The only other experiment seen in [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]] whose number is also referred to as a whole number is [[Woops (600)|Woops]] (Experiment 600). This implies that experiments whose number is divisible by one hundred (100) are the primary exceptions to the normal by-digit pronunciation of experiment numbers.
*Spooky's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green in the original series. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, it is red.
*Spooky makes a cameo in the pre-show of [[disney:Stitch's Great Escape!|Stitch's Great Escape!]] when Gantu shows guests a quick look at the "criminals" of the galaxy (which are all experiments). However, he does not appear in his true form, but rather the form he used on Pleakley shown in "[[The Asteroid]]". Underneath the image, his name is rendered as "300M/Spookymorp" (presumably meant to be "Spookymorp''h''") in [[Tantalog language|Tantalog]].

She is designed to use her spring-like body to launch boulders. Her one true place is helping people reach high heights.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 249 was the 249th genetic experiment created by Jumba with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. She was designed to launch boulders. 249 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At some point, 249 was activated, captured, tamed, and named Sproing.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
Sproing was seen when [[Lilo_Pelekai|Lilo]] was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to check on all of the experiments, and she finished up near the movies, where Sproing was elevating a man who was changing the letters on the display outside the [[Cinema|theater]].

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Sproing, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Sproing participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by trapping Leroys in her coils.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Sproing is a dark navy blue and white roughly koala-like experiment. She vaguely resembles Stitch with a coiled spring-like body, a large white patch on her face, a wide mouth, red round nose, large dark beady eyes, and two small ears and antennae.

===Special abilities===
Sproing can launch boulders by using her spring-like body, bounce and jump really high. She is able to hold heavy weights with her strong coils.

==Trivia==
*Her unique design is a reference to [[wikipedia:Slinky|Slinky]] toys.
*Sproing and [[Lorider (047)|Lorider]] are the only known experiments that can extend their bodies.

'''Sprout''', also known as '''Experiment 509''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to sprout into an uncontrollable forest of destruction by burrowing into the ground and producing tendrils that grow replicas of his head. His one true place is atop the [[Pineapple Water Tower|pineapple water tower]].

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 509 was the 509th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to spawn into an uncontrollable killer forest. 509 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Sprout - Sprout after activation.png|thumb|left|Sprout after being activated]]
509's pod eventually made its way into a post office, where [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] found it on the floor while mailing a letter to her pen pal Henry. She then took the pod [[Lilo's House|home]] to [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] who described 509's powers, but Jumba, unwilling to risk activating 509 due to the destruction the latter would cause, locked the pod away.

Since Lilo wanted to enter something in one of the competitions, she and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] stealthily stole 509's pod from Jumba's desk drawer the following night. Lilo then activated the experiment, named him Sprout, transplanted him, and fed him super-fertilizer.

The next day, Lilo took a rapidly-growing Sprout to an orchid competition at the [[Kokaua Town]] fair. When [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] approached Sprout and noticed he was not an orchid, Sprout lashed out at her, causing Mertle to accidentally break his pot open.

Sprout then rooted into the ground and grew into a massive forest of killer plants which took over the fair, causing widespread panic and Stitch to lose the rodeo to [[Zach Makeli|a five-time champion cowboy]]. [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] and Jumba soon learned of the disaster that was broadcast on TV and became angry with Lilo for activating Sprout against Jumba's wishes.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Sprout - Giant sprout contained as people stare at him.png|thumb|Giant Sprout contained]]
Eventually, Stitch managed to lasso the original Sprout, uproot him, and drag him into a [[Pineapple Water Tower|pineapple-shaped water tower]] slated for demolition, thus trapping the latter and causing the forest to die off without the original Sprout. Lilo was unsure if this was truly Sprout's one true place, but it was apparently the best she and Stitch could do on such short notice.

Sprout was seen on a computer screen in "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]", posing as an evil creation of Jumba's as part of a hoax to fool [[Mortlegax]], the head of E.G.O. industries.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Sprout, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Sprout participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. Sprout joins them for the song by playing the drums.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
[[File:ScreenCapture 08.04.13 2-56-42.png|thumb|Sprout in the anime episode "[[Son of Sprout]]"; in the English dub, he is actually a Sproutling instead.]]
Sprout was mentioned twice in the ''Stitch!'' anime. Although Sprout reappeared twice in the Japanese version of the anime, he makes no appearances in the English dub, where he was mentioned by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] to still live on [[Kauai]]. Instead, in both appearances, they are a seedling spawned from Sprout called a '''Sproutling''', codenamed '''Experiment 509-A'''. It is revealed that Sprout can produce seed pods and launch them into space, where they cling to asteroids.

A seedling first appeared in "[[Son of Sprout]]". It had attached to a meteor that later crashed onto [[Izayoi Island]]. Once it got its roots into the ground, it quickly began to grow, carrying out his father's original programming, before eventually being neutralized.

In "[[Sprout 2.0]]", [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] reveals that he has [[Transmutation|enhanced]] another one of Sprout's seedlings with the DNA of [[627|Experiment 627]], disguised it as a plant, and hid it on a deserted island in an attempt to capture [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. [[Gantu]] and [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] disguise themselves and convince Stitch and the gang to go find a flower that grants wishes, but is truly the seedling. Shortly after arriving on the island, the gang finds and almost instantly captures the seedling. However, when the seedling escapes, 627's DNA causes him to grow and become unstoppable. Luckily, this also gave the seedling 627's only weakness: laughter. Eventually, Stitch and the others defeat the seedling by tickling him to submission, causing him to shrink back to his original size.

In "[[Shogun]]", it is shown that Sprout was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in Jumba's vault.

==Personality==
Sprout is wild and tends to be aggressive, often trying to bite individuals when he was still confined in a flower pot. After he rooted into the ground and grew to enormous proportions, he became very dangerous and quite intimidating, spreading his vines like weeds to attack victims. However, he apparently calmed down after being uprooted and contained. He also seems to like Lilo.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Sprout is a plant-like experiment with a thick green stem, leaf-like body, eight tentacle-like vines, a purple head shaped like a [[wikipedia:Venus flytrap|Venus flytrap]], a large mouth with a lizard-like face, little sharp teeth, dark blue pupil-less eyes, three leaves surrounding his head like a frill (one leaf under his chin and the other two behind his head), and a single antenna on his head.

===Special abilities===
Sprout can grow from a small experiment to an immense monstrosity at a rapid rate. Using his burrowing capabilities, Sprout can initiate his growth once he roots into the ground, allowing him to sprout a destructive forest of vicious duplicates, and sends out tendrils that can grow new heads and act like weeds, all with replicas of Sprout's head. Looks like harmless plant one moment, but suddenly rises up like savage beast and attacks (as stated by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]). 

In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, he is able to produce seed pods and launch them into space, where they cling to asteroids. One of these pods landed on the [[Izayoi Island|island]] and grew into a "Sproutling" (509-A) that carried out Sprout's original programming before being neutralized. The Sproutling [[Transmutation|enhanced]] with [[627]]'s DNA in "[[Sprout 2.0]]" is also much tougher and can move around on his own, although he doesn't show his original ability to spawn more heads.

Sprout has shown to be skilled in playing the drums.

===Weaknesses===
If the original Sprout's roots are separated from the forest and contained, all of his duplicates will die off. Sprout is also vulnerable to plant-trimming or weed-cutting machines, such as a tractor or lawn mower.

==Trivia==
*Sprout was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Sprout is an obvious parody of [[w:c:villains:Audrey II|Audrey II]] from ''[[wikipedia:Little Shop of Horrors (film)|Little Shop of Horrors]]''.
*Sprout bears a great resemblance to most real-life [[wikipedia:Venus flytrap|Venus flytraps]].
*Sprout's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue.
*Sprout's holographic silhouette appeared in both "[[Amnesio (episode)|Amnesio]]" and "[[Fibber (episode)|Fibber]]".
**Sprout is shown to have two different graphic designs on [[Jumba's Computer|Jumba's computer]].
*During the battle between the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy army]] and the experiments in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', Sprout did not grow into an uncontrollable forest of destruction like he did in [[Sprout (episode)|his debut]].
*In the English dub of ''[[Stitch!]]'', Sprout is said to produce seeds called Sproutlings (a.k.a. Experiment 509-A) that carry out the same primary function as their father.
**In the Japanese version of ''Stitch!'', this experiment is still just Sprout. However, the international version attempted to fit the anime into the canon of ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]'', and so Sprout stays in Hawaii, whereas instead, both of his appearances are considered to be seedlings that he has spawned.
*As a reference to many [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|experiments being mislabeled]] with the excuse that Jumba's database is untidy, [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] and [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] ask if the experiment used to enhance the Sproutling was 672 or 726, and not [[627]]. However, it is rather obvious that it's 627, since Experiment 672 or 726 was never made; the last made experiment was 629 ([[Leroy (629)|Leroy]]), which means 627 is the only choice left. The fact the Sproutling is weak to laughter is further proof that the Sproutling was, indeed, infused with 627's DNA.
*According to [[disney:Jess Winfield|Jess Winfield]], Sprout was originally going to be named "Weedy" at one point.<ref name="WinfieldTVTome">{{cite web|url=http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|title=L&S Says Mahalo|website=[[wikipedia:TV.com|TV Tome]]|date=December 14, 2004|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305082355/http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|archivedate=March 19, 2016|accessdate=May 27, 2018}}</ref>

'''Squeak''', also known as '''Experiment 110''' and '''Squeaky''' (in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime), is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to annoy entire planets with his nonstop talking.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 110 was the 110th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to irritate individuals and entire populations by talking incessantly. 110 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 110 was activated and captured by Jumba.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
In "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]", [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] revealed 110 inside a container and proceeded to test a new device called the Evil-liminator, designed to turn bad experiments to good (in 110's case, make him less talkative). However, the machine failed, simply exploding, and 110, named Squeak, continued to blabber on incessantly, causing [[Pleakley]] to shout at Squeak to stop talking.

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Squeak was one of the experiments in [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]]'s dream.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Squeak, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Squeak participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but was briefly threatened by the original [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]]'s plasma gun when Squeak wouldn't stop talking. He also made a referee whistle sound when [[Kixx (601)|Kixx]] punched a Leroy clone over one of the stadium's goalposts.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Squeak made [[Hämsterviel's Epic Secret|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Frenchfry (062)|Frenchfry]], [[Pix (214)|Pix]], [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Houdini (604)|Houdini]] after [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] kicked them out for being considered useless. He made [[Experiment-A-Palooza|a later appearance]], along with [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]], [[Clip (177)|Clip]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], and [[Retro (210)|Retro]]. He made [[Dark-End|a third appearance]] in aiding [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] in battle against [[Dark End]]. He also appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Squeak fulfills what he was programmed to do, which is to annoy enemies by talking nonstop. Although not malignant like most experiments, he is very energetic and can talk for hours on end without stopping, tiring out, or even showing signs of needing to breathe. Despite being programmed for nonstop talking, Squeak seems to have some level of self-control as shown when he annoyed the original Leroy by talking incessantly, to which Leroy threateningly shot a blast at him, causing Squeak to immediately become quiet.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Squeak is a small red mouse-like experiment, wearing a blue hat, vaguely resembling animator Friz Freleng's character [[wikipedia:Sniffles|Sniffles]] from the Warner Brothers ''[[wikipedia:Merrie Melodies|Merrie Melodies]]'' series.

===Special abilities===
Squeak can [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]] and go on talking nonstop for a considerably long amount of time. He can talk extremely fast in a high-pitched, squeaky voice, hence his name. He is also capable of using his mouth as a microphone.

'''Stamen''', also known as '''Experiment 103''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to intercept and prevent pollination by attracting bees and other pollinators to himself instead of flowers. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 103 was the 103rd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to prevent the pollination of flowers by attracting bees to himself. 103 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 103 was activated and captured by [[Gantu]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
In "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", Stamen was freed along with [[Gantu]]'s other captive experiments by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], and several other experiments in a rescue mission.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Stamen, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

It is unknown whether or not Stamen participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[disney:Aloha `Oe|Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Stamen is a tan-grey, upside-down ice cream cone-shaped, koala-like experiment with an oval body, little arms and legs, big ears with a black silhouette of a stamen inside, a big mouth, no tail, black eyes, a round blue nose, and rabbit-like ears.

===Special abilities===
Stamen uses his floral attributes to attract colonies of bees and other pollinators to him instead of natural fields of agriculture, thus causing pollination to be prevented.

==Trivia==
*Stamen was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Stamen and [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]] are the only experiments rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]" that had never been seen or referenced before. [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]] had never been seen before, but was mentioned in "[[Amnesio (episode)|Amnesio]]" and seen in [[Experiment Pods|pod]] form in "[[Drowsy (episode)|Drowsy]]".
*Stamen is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.
*He is also one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
