'''Swirly''', also known as '''Experiment 383''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to hypnotize individuals into obeying the next order or suggestion they hear; snapping one's fingers will break the victim's trance. His one true place is hypnotizing guests at children's parties.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 383 was the 383rd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to hypnotize his victims into obeying the next order or suggestion they heard. 383 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 383's pod landing on a [[Lahui Beach|beach]] shore.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Swirly - Swirly after activation.png|thumb|left|Swirly after being activated]]
When a small wave washed over the shore, 383's pod got wet, activating the experiment. 383 then hypnotized a surfer, who had witnessed his activation, and left the scene.

After hypnotizing [[Ice Cream Man|a tourist]] (who, based on a comment from [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]], began clucking like a chicken), 383 was discovered by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], but just before they could take action, [[Gantu]] ambushed them and captured 383 in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]]. 383 was soon caught in a fight between Lilo, Stitch and Gantu, which ended with Lilo and Stitch retrieving 383. Gantu was then forced to flee from a swarm of bees after Stitch upset their hive.

Lilo and Stitch took 383, named Swirly, back to their [[Lilo's House|house]] and learned about his powers from [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]. They then tried to hide Swirly from a very strict [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]], who prohibited any of Jumba's experiments besides Stitch, when she returned from work. However, in the ensuing chaos, Swirly managed to hypnotize both Lilo (who, based on a suggestion from [[Pleakley]], started behaving like her rival Mertle) and Stitch (who, based on a comment from the hypnotized Lilo, became an obsessive fan of the reality show ''Look at This!'') and escaped outside.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Swirly - Swirly hypnotizing Stitch.png|thumb|Hypnotizing Stitch]]
Gantu later recaptured Swirly and was briefly hypnotized by the latter back at [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]]. This fascinated [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]], who then amused himself by making Gantu do silly stuff. Even [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] became intrigued after seeing this and toyed with Gantu a bit before snapping him out of his trance.

Later, Gantu traveled to the TV studio, where he used Swirly to hypnotize the manager into putting him on the ''Look at This!'' show, which was part of Hämsterviel's clever scheme. Gantu then planned to have Swirly turn the show's viewers into slaves. Lilo and Stitch, who just so happened to be on the show, were still under Swirly's hypnosis from before.

Back home, Jumba, who was watching the show on TV out of curiosity, soon found out what was going on. He then came to the show in person and managed to snap Lilo and Stitch out of their trances so they could rescue Swirly.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Swirly - Gantu using Swirly's hypnosis.png|thumb|left|Gantu using Swirly's hypnosis]]
Gantu prepared to hypnotize the show's viewers into slaves using Swirly, but Lilo and Stitch pulled the plug on Gantu's charade by recapturing Swirly. He later found his one true place hypnotizing guests at a children's party that Stitch had won from being on the show, with Mertle becoming one of Swirly's victims.

In "[[The Asteroid]]", Swirly was one of the six experiments that Stitch convinced to come with him and Lilo to save Earth from an approaching asteroid. Along the journey, Swirly hypnotized the extraterrestrial asteroid squatter to prevent him from distracting Lilo and the others as they safely diverted the asteroid using the [[Jumba's Ship|ship]]'s hyperdrive engine.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Swirly, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Swirly participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by hypnotizing attacking Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Swirly made [[The Return of Amnesio|a cameo appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime as one of the experiments in [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison cell]]. He made [[Stitch Power|another appearance]] where Hämsterviel used him to hypnotize [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] into fighting for the alien scientist. [[Gantu]] is also hypnotized by Swirly; this time, making him believe he is a scared chicken. Hämsterviel notes that he should have hypnotized Gantu sooner and decides to keep him in a trance. For the rest of the episode, Gantu is seen in the background acting like a chicken and even tries to lay an egg. This episode also featured [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]] and [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]] who helped combat Stitch while he was under Swirly's hypnosis. 

Swirly later appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]'', where he was captured by Hämsterviel. After breaking free, Swirly finds Gantu and hypnotizes him once again. This time, he makes Gantu destroy several of Hämsterviel's robots. Later, Swirly is seen at a party with the rest of the experiments, playing cards with Gantu who is still hypnotized.

==Personality==
Swirly is a troublesome experiment, although very mute at that. He is quite active with his hypnosis, as it is performed at the most inadequate of times to humiliate others, but he is otherwise harmless. He often stares into space when not using his powers, being somewhat blank-minded.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Swirly is a small turquoise koala-like experiment with a huge head, an expressionless face with a little mouth, little nose, huge black pupil-less eyes (with white swirling lines when using his powers), rabbit-like ears, a single small antenna on the middle of his head, and a large lizard-like tail.

===Special abilities===
Swirly can hypnotize anyone who looks into his eyes to obey the next order or suggestion they hear by making his eyes swirl.

===Weaknesses===
Swirly's hypnotized victims will snap out of their trance once they hear someone snap their fingers. Also, if no order or suggestion is heard within a few minutes, the effect wears off.

==Trivia==
*In [[Swirly (episode)|his debut]], Swirly's fur color is green, but in promotional artwork and all of his other animated appearances, including ''[[Stitch!]]'', his fur color is grayish blue.
*When Swirly hypnotizes the [[Ice Cream Man]], his eyes can be seen.
*Swirly is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to.
**He is also one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to.
*Swirly's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is yellow.
*Swirly's head, antenna, and ears appear in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.

'''Tank''', also known as '''Experiment 586''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to consume metal in vast amounts and grow exponentially larger with all that he eats. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 586 was the 586th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to consume metal and grow exponentially bigger with each feast. 586 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 586's pod landing in a car's grille.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Tank - Tank after activation.png|thumb|left|Tank after being activated]]
When the owner washed down his car with a hose, 586's pod got wet, activating the experiment. 586 then ate the driver's automobile, leaving only the rubber tires, and ran off.

Later, 586 devoured a huge factory that was being shown to some tourists riding in a van, then proceeded to eat metal throughout [[Kokaua Town|town]] until he grew to a large enough size to go on a rampage.

[[Gantu]] had been informed about 586 and realized he couldn't possibly catch the experiment in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]], due to how large it had grown. He then prepared the cargo bay of [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]] for abducting 586.

Meanwhile, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] won tickets to the Elizabethan Fair and invited [[Elena|the]] [[Teresa|hula]] [[Yuki|girls]] (who ditched [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] when she refused to participate with Lilo), but neglected [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] after he told her an experiment was running amok. Later, Stitch (who couldn't attend the fair because no dogs were admitted) teamed up with a lonely Mertle in hopes of stopping 586.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Tank - Giant Tank at medieval fair.png|thumb|Giant Tank]]Stitch and Mertle evaded the gigantic 586 in [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]]'s [[X-Buggy|dune buggy]] after he got distracted from his metal-eating feast. After a while, a tractor beam abducted Stitch and Mertle into Gantu's ship. Though Gantu was briefly discouraged that he failed to capture 586, he locked Stitch and Mertle in teleport chambers and prepared to try again.

[[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] was inexplicably fascinated by Mertle. She used this to her advantage by soft-soaping Reuben, who released her from containment as a result. Mertle then locked Reuben in the teleport chamber, and after she freed Stitch from the adjacent one, they escaped the ship as well as 586's clutches.

Gantu later chased down 586 in his ship, but the former was thwarted by Lilo, who brought down Gantu's ship and had two jugglers halt his progress. Meanwhile, Stitch attempted to battle 586, but the latter's enormous size rendered him impossible to defeat, despite Stitch's best efforts. Seeing that Stitch was outmatched by 586, Lilo turned to Gantu for help.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Tank - Tank abducted by Gantu.png|thumb|left|Captured by Gantu]]
586's rampage continued to spread, where, after an attack on Stitch, he was abducted by a tractor beam from Gantu's ship, since Lilo had convinced Gantu earlier to get the humongous experiment away from Stitch. Mertle later reunited with the hula girls, who agreed to take her back if they could play dolls less often, and Lilo made amends with Stitch.

Presumably after this, 586, named Tank, was sent to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] who somehow found a way to shrink him back to his normal size and confine him in a container.

Although Tank was unseen in "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", he is known to have been sent back to Gantu along with all of Hämsterviel's other captive experiments after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused chaos and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

Tank reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by Lilo, Stitch, and several other experiments in a rescue mission. Tank even helped with the escape by eating Gantu's [[Plasma Blaster|gun]] after [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]] broke it in two with a plasma blast.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Tank, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Tank participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by eating attacking Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Personality==
Tank is a giant experiment whose intimidating nature only grows with his size. He is shown to be extremely insatiable and voracious, having an enormous appetite for metal. He will hurt anyone who gets in his way and can hold a grudge against them, like he did with Stitch, but otherwise ignores individuals who run from him.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Tank is a round, quadrupedal, orange armadillo/bulldog-like experiment with thick legs, black eyes, a brown oval nose, a large, wide mouth, sharp metal-like teeth, a short tail, two small ears, and plates going from the front of his head to the end of his tail.

===Special abilities===
Tank has exponential jaw strength that enables him to chew any type of metal with ease, such as iron, tin, steel, copper, silver, aluminum, etc. His teeth/jaws are highly durable and capable of processing metal, while his overbite jaw is able to stretch amazingly, allowing him to eat things many times his size (such as a factory) and/or many times his length (such as an automobile bumper) without struggle. His body size increases exponentially with any metal he consumes, thus his digestive system must work hundreds of times faster than a regular human being's.

===Weaknesses===
If Tank goes without eating any metal after a while, he will gradually revert to his normal size.

==Trivia==
*Tank was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Tank is not referred to by his new name at any point in [[Tank (episode)|his debut]], but his name officially appears on the experiments list in the [[Experiments/Gallery#Leroy & Stitch|end credits]] of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
*Tank, along with [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Dorkifier (122)|Dorkifier]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], [[Butter (227)|Butter]], [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]], [[Spike (319)|Spike]], [[Yang (502)|Yang]], [[Richter (513)|Richter]], [[Phoon (540)|Phoon]], [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]], and one [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed experiment]], are the only known experiments that are primarily quadrupeds.
*Tank's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue.
*The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Tank as: "Experiment 586. Primary function: Metal consumption. Experiment grows exponentially larger with everything it eats."
*Tank has shrunk from a massive size back to his normal size between his debut and "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", suggesting he returns to his normal size after a while without eating any metal.
*Tank is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.

'''Thresher''', also known as '''Experiment 544''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to thrash crops and beat his victims up with his mace-like tentacles. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 544 was the 544th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to smash up crops with his mace-like tentacles, although he could also use them to attack and battle enemies. 544 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Dupe - Thresher using his mace-like tentacles.png|thumb|left|Thresher using his mace-like tentacles]]
544's pod eventually made its way to a junk shop, where it (along with [[Hammerface (033)|033]], [[Heat (609)|609]] and [[Plasmoid (617)|617]]) was found, stolen, activated, and named Thresher by [[Gantu]] in "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]".

Back at [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]], Gantu trained and conditioned Hammerface, Heat, Thresher and Plasmoid by simply using [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] for target practice, much to his indignity and chagrin. The four henchmen experiments were then led by Gantu in an attack on the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]], where their boss ordered them to defeat and capture [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and his duplicates after seeing that he had been split into four.

Thresher engaged one of the clones in a duel. The clone picked up a broom and started spinning it similar to a bo staff. While he did this in front of Thresher, the latter appeared to be mesmerized, but stretched out one of his mace-tipped tentacles and poked the clone in the shoulder. When the clone turned his head, Thresher aimed another tentacle at his victim's face. [[Pleakley]], seeing Thresher's plan, tried to warn the clone but was too late, as Thresher managed to knock him unconscious. The slug-like experiment then used his long tentacles to pick up his defeated opponent and place him in one of Gantu's [[Prison Capsule|containment orbs]].

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Dupe - Thresher being duplicated.png|thumb|Thresher being duplicated]]
After capturing Stitch and his clones, the five returned to Gantu's ship for a victory feast (courtesy of Reuben), but were interrupted by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], Pleakley and [[Dupe (344)|Dupe]]. When Lilo tricked Gantu into using Dupe's cloning ability, Gantu used Dupe to clone Thresher into a hundred replicas. However, as the original Thresher's power was divided among them, they all became complete weaklings, and thus were easily defeated.

Presumably after this, they were all sent to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] who was somehow able to remerge the weakling Thresher clones into the original.

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Thresher was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream.

Although Thresher was unseen in "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", he is known to have been sent back to Gantu along with all of Hämsterviel's other captive experiments after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused chaos and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

Thresher reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by Lilo, Stitch, and several other experiments in a rescue mission.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Thresher, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Thresher participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], as during the climax, when Stitch points to the stage in the stadium, Thresher can be seen bonking a Leroy clone on the head.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. Thresher joins them for the song by playing the marimba.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Thresher made [[The Petite Queen|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime where [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] [[Transmutation|used]] him to attack [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] during a magic show. In this episode, he looks more muscular and has bright orange eyes. He later appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Thresher is a small blue-purple, roughly slug-like experiment with a slim body, a wide mouth, two light green eyes on two stocks, six spiky, extendable, mace-like tentacles, two short legs, and a stubby tail. In his [[Transmutation|transmutated]] form, he looks more muscular and has bright orange eyes.

===Special abilities===
Thresher can thrash crops or beat his victims up using his six extendable, mace-like tentacles.

Thresher has shown to be skilled in playing the marimba.

===Weaknesses===
Like other experiments, when Thresher is divided by [[Dupe (344)|Dupe]] into a hundred replicas, each one will be virtually harmless.

==Trivia==
*Thresher is one of the ten known experiments named by someone other than Lilo or Stitch, the other nine being [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Elastico (345)|Elastico]], [[Yaarp (613)|Yaarp]], [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]], [[Heat (609)|Heat]], [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]], [[Morpholomew (316)|Morpholomew]], [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]], and [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]].
**Thresher (alongside Hammerface, Heat, and Plasmoid) was named by Gantu.
*Some sources have spelled this experiment's name as "Thrasher", but "Thresher" is the correct spelling.
*Thresher is one of the rare experiments to have sclerae and pupils instead of solid black eyes, the others being [[Clink (086)|Clink]], [[Skip (089)|Skip]], [[Bragg (145)|Bragg]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], [[Mr. Stenchy (254)|Mr. Stenchy]], [[Mrs. Sickly (255)|Mrs. Sickly]], [[Experiments#Other experiments|Tippy]], [[Experiments#3-Series: Psychological|Slobber]], and [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|four unconfirmed experiments]].
*Thresher, [[Huggo (489)|Huggo]], and Clink are the only known experiments with stalked eyes, a trait common in the invertebrates that all three are inspired by.
*Thresher and Huggo have very similar heads/faces. Perhaps they were created using some of the same DNA.
*Even though we saw Thresher in [[Experiment Pods|pod]] form, he was technically [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Thresher is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.

'''Tickle-Tummy''', also known as '''Experiment 275''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. She is designed to tickle anyone into submission, rendering opponents helpless with laughter; they sometimes even cause an accident in the process. She was captured by [[Gantu]] but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 275 was the 275th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. She was designed to tickle individuals into utter hysterics. 275 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All the experiments were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 275 was activated and captured by [[Gantu]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
In "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", Tickle-Tummy was freed along with [[Gantu]]'s other captive experiments by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], and several other experiments in a rescue mission. She then tickled [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] into hysterics, after he denied being ticklish.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
Despite not physically appearing, the first 624 experiments, presumably including Tickle-Tummy, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

It is unknown whether or not Tickle-Tummy participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Tickle-Tummy made [[Hämsterviel's Epic Secret|an appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Frenchfry (062)|Frenchfry]], [[Squeak (110)|Squeak]], [[Pix (214)|Pix]], and [[Houdini (604)|Houdini]] after [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] kicked them out for being considered useless.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Tickle-Tummy is a round, pink experiment with rabbit-like ears, no legs, a clownish face, big blue eyes, long arms with two hands with long skinny fingers and a large patterned torso, which she uses to jump really high.

===Special abilities===
Tickle-Tummy has the ability to tickle anyone into submission by using her long fingers. She is also capable of floating in the air.

==Trivia==
*Tickle-Tummy was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*Tickle-Tummy is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having dark blue eyes instead. Interestingly, she shares this trait with [[Bonnie (149)|Bonnie]], [[Welko (074)|Welko]], and [[Witch (610)|Witch]], three other female experiments.
*Tickle-Tummy and [[Stamen (103)|Stamen]] are the only experiments rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]" that had never been seen or referenced before. [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]] had never been seen before, but was mentioned in "[[Amnesio (episode)|Amnesio]]" and seen in [[Experiment Pods|pod]] form in "[[Drowsy (episode)|Drowsy]]".
*Tickle-Tummy, [[Phantasmo (375)|Phantasmo]], [[Fudgy (054)|Fudgy]], [[Remmy (276)|Remmy]], and Witch are the only known experiments to have arms but no legs.
**Interestingly, excluding Fudgy, all of these experiments are capable of levitation. Remmy is always seen levitating. Phantasmo and Witch primarily levitate but often possess objects or living beings to move by other means. Tickle-Tummy is also able to levitate, but has been seen bouncing as well.
***Tickle-Tummy, [[Hertz Donut (022)|Hertz Donut]], [[Sproing (249)|Sproing]], [[Mary (455)|Mary]], and [[Cannonball (520)|Cannonball]] are the only known experiments that mostly bounce when traversing land.
***Tickle-Tummy, along with [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Welko (074)|Welko]], [[Carmen (123)|Carmen]], [[Bonnie (149)|Bonnie]], [[Belle (248)|Belle]], [[Sproing (249)|Sproing]], [[Mary (455)|Mary]], [[Phoon (540)|Phoon]], [[Witch (610)|Witch]] and [[Angel (624)|Angel]] are the only known female experiments in a [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|franchise]].
*Tickle-Tummy's appearance changed between her debut in ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]'' and her second franchise appearance in ''[[Stitch!]]''. In the former, her torso has a light pink stomach surrounded by a pattern of purple and blue markings, whereas the anime removes the stomach and blue markings, leaving only the purple markings. It is likely that this was done to simplify her design for economic purposes.
*Tickle-Tummy is one of the few experiments to not have her one true place revealed.
*She is also one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
*Tickle-Tummy is the only experiment that was [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|not on the list of the original 626 experiments]] in the [[Experiments/Gallery#Leroy & Stitch|end credits]] of ''Leroy & Stitch'', but she is called 275 in the ''Stitch!'' anime. 275 is the number [[Wormhole (272)|Wormhole]] is listed as in the end credits; however, in the anime, Wormhole is called Experiment 272, which was originally the number of an unconfirmed experiment called Mamf. When asked about the numbering, [[disney:Jess Winfield|Jess Winfield]] stated: "The best I can tell you about Tickletummy/Wormhole is that Jumba's genius does not extend to keeping a tidy [[Jumba's Computer|database]]. There is some confusion in his records regarding Tickletummy, Wormhole, and a third experiment named Mamf, with different lists giving different numbers for them. Perhaps it will be sorted out someday."

'''Toons''', also known as '''Experiment 112''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to turn anyone into a cartoon. When [[Transmutation|transmuted]] by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], he can transform into the subject of any drawing inserted into his mouth. When reprogrammed, he can bring 2D images to life in 3D. He appears in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 112 was the 112th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to either turn everyone into cartoons, turn into the subject of any pictures, or bring 2D pictures to life. 112 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Stitch!|Stitch! anime]]''===
Toons appeared in two episodes of the third season of the ''Stitch!'' anime. His debut was in "[[Spooky Toons]]" as one of two [[Transmutation|transmutated]] experiments under [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s control to capture [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] (the other being [[Spooky (300)|Spooky]]).

When [[Gantu]] and [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] arrived at the island [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]]'s class was staying on, her drawing of a false island legend (which had blown away in the breeze) smacked into Gantu's face. He thought it was scary and decided to give it to Toons to help in Stitch's capture. Toons then turned into the drawing.

Later, after Yuna, Stitch, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Dolores]], and [[BooGoo]] managed to convince [[Jessica]] that the legend was real, she let out a sneeze, which (according to Dolores) caused the monster to appear. Coincidentally, after she sneezed, Toons (transformed into the monster) showed up. Per Gantu's orders, he tried to capture Stitch.

While they fought, Jumba saw the H-mark on his forehead and figured out who he really was. He then drew a small picture of a butterfly and told Stitch to feed it into the monster's mouth. Stitch complied and due to Toons' programming, he turned from a giant monster into a small butterfly and was easily captured.

After his capture, a machine built by Jumba reversed Hämsterviel's reprogramming and turned Toons back to normal. He was then dehydrated and stored in Jumba's secret vault until he was needed again.

In his second episode "[[Shogun]]", Yuna had to do a report on ancient Japanese warriors, including what they ate. But when she looked in the history book Pleakley showed her, she couldn't make out what the shogun in the picture was eating. Pleakley mentioned that Toons could help as he was designed to bring pictures to life, but he was locked in Jumba's vault. Fortunately, Yuna knew the codes to open it. She then took Toons' pod and dropped it in a glass of water, reactivating him. She fed the whole book into his mouth, and he animated not only was the shogun was eating, but Shogun himself! Unfortunately, Jumba was away and since no one else knew how to reverse Toons' work, they were stuck with him.

Later, Jumba returned and would help Shogun go back to where he came from. Before he left, [[Tigerlily Sakai|Tigerlily]] gave him a big plate of spaghetti (which he had developed a fondness for) as a parting gift. Jumba then grabbed Toons' mane and spun it like a disk counterclockwise. Shogun was sucked back into Toons and turned back into the history book, much to Tigerlily's shock and dismay. The next morning, Stitch shows Yuna and Tigerlily the picture again and in it, Shogun is eating Tigerlily's spaghetti!

Toons was dehydrated again and was put back in Jumba's vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help Stitch in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Toons wasn't one of the experiments that was activated.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Toons is a yellow platypus/[[wikipedia:Axolotl|axolotl]]-like experiment with an orange mane and a rectangular vacuum-like mouth.

===Special abilities===
Toons' function and abilities changed over the course of two reprograms, so he has three functions at different stages:
#'''Original:''' He can turn anyone into a cartoon.
#'''Transmuted:''' He can transform into the subject of any drawing inserted into his mouth.
#'''Reprogrammed:''' He can bring 2D images to life by consuming the 2D subject and spitting it back out, making it appear 3D.

Spinning Toons' collar counterclockwise reverts his creations back to their original state.

==Trivia==
*Toons is the only experiment [[:Category:Stitch! Experiments|introduced in ''Stitch!'']] that appeared activated in more than one episode, having appeared activated in two [[Spooky Toons|different]] [[Shogun|episodes]].
*Although Toons' original function was to turn everyone into cartoons, after being reprogrammed, his new function was to bring images to life.
**His original function and function after reprogramming are opposite in action.
**Also, reversing his reprogrammed function (by spinning his collar) is similar to his original one.
*Toons' [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green.
*Toons and [[Bragg (145)|Bragg]] are the only ''Stitch!'' experiments whose functions were changed after their [[transmutation]].
*Although Toons makes sounds in the English dub, his English voice actor was never credited.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 025 was the 25th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his bright light to pose as a beacon for an invasion to the [[Galactic Armada Crewmembers|Galactic Armada]]. 025 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Topper - Topper moments after activation.png|thumb|left|Topper moments after his activation]]
025's pod was found by [[Gantu]] on Christmas Eve, which he planned on having it gift-wrapped and sent out to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] as a Christmas present after [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] suggested this to Gantu beforehand.

Meanwhile, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] was attempting to teach a naive [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] about Christmas and all the traditions associated with the holiday, when the latter soon noticed a woman putting 025's pod in a gift box. Stitch hastily grabbed what he thought was the gift-wrapped pod, but when he tried to tell Lilo, she ignored him.

When Gantu later dropped by to pick up 025's pod, the same woman who had gift-wrapped it earlier hinted that there was a mishap involving Stitch, much to Gantu's anger. He then swore to avenge Stitch for stealing Hämsterviel's Christmas gift.

In an attempt to find the pod, Stitch stole countless presents from every house and the [[Orchard Falls Mall|local mall]] on [[Kauai]]. Lilo assumed Stitch was selfishly hoarding Christmas gifts for himself, but after the latter was [[Prison Capsule|captured]] and interrogated by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], Stitch revealed what he was really trying to do. Shortly after, Gantu attacked the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]] and managed to make off with all the stolen presents.

Lilo and Stitch clashed with Reuben on [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]] and forced him to reveal the location of the experiment pod. After they pinpointed the pod in [[Kokaua Town|town]], Lilo and Stitch tussled with Gantu dressed in a Santa outfit, as did Jumba and [[Pleakley]]. Stitch snatched the gift-wrapped pod from Gantu, although he retrieved it after a long chase. When he then attempted to crush Lilo for meddling, she reprimanded Gantu until he admitted that he intended to give 025's pod to Hämsterviel as a Christmas present.

Just then, a little girl asked Gantu for a mere Christmas gift, believing he was actually Santa. Forced to comply, Gantu ended up giving 025's pod to her and later distributed presents to other children, thereby honoring the true spirit of Christmas.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Topper - Topper atop the Pleakley Christmas tree.png|thumb|Topper's one true place]]
After Jumba discovered 025 to be harmless, Lilo activated 025 in a fountain. She then named him Topper, shared him with the little girl seen previously, and gave him a one true place atop the local Christmas tree (actually a decorated Pleakley) as a Christmas star, while Topper's bright light unintentionally signaled the [[Galactic Armada Crewmembers|Galactic Armada]].

Topper reappeared in "[[Elastico (episode)|Elastico]]" as one of the audience members for Lilo's hula dance.

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Topper was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 591 instead of 025.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Topper, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Topper participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did. However, it is presumed that he wouldn't have been able to be very effective, due to the fact that his powers are deemed useless.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Topper made [[The Return of Amnesio|a cameo appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime as one of the experiments in [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison cell]].

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Topper is a small yellow-orange star-shaped creature with a little white-tipped antenna on his head, small dark blue eyes, a thin mouth, white-tipped limbs and a white marking on his belly.

===Special abilities===
Topper can produce a brilliant light visible even from space that helps alien fleets locate him.

==Trivia==
*Topper was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Topper is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having blue eyes instead.
*Topper's primary function is to use his bright light to signal the alien attack fleet. However, on the Disney site, it is incorrectly stated that Topper's light is designed to keep people awake.
*Even though Topper found his one true place atop a Christmas tree, it is unknown what he does during the other seasons.
**It is possible that he stays with the little girl whom he was given to for the rest of the year.
*Topper's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is white.
*His number is a likely reference to Christmas Day (December 25).

Transmutation:
[[File:Stitch! - Spooky Toons - Toons' Japanese name caption.png|Experiment 112 (Toons) with the "H" signifying that he has been transmutated by Hämsterviel.|thumb|250px]]
'''Transmutation''' is the process in which [[experiments]] are reprogrammed, turned to/from bad or good, and/or altered using the DNA of other experiments.

==Background and appearances==
===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
In the original series, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] reprograms some of his experiments, notably [[Felix (010)|Felix]], [[Bugby (128)|Bugby]], and [[Remmy (276)|Remmy]]. [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] is also transmutated and controlled by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] in "[[Bad Stitch]]". In "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]", Jumba attempts to create a machine called the Eviliminator in order to transmutate experiments from bad to good. He tested his creation on [[Squeak (110)|Squeak]], but it failed as the device only exploded. [[Angel (624)|Angel]], another one of Jumba's creations, has the same capabilities of the Eviliminator, being able to convert rehabilitated experiments built before her to evil.

===''[[Stitch!]]''===
In the anime, primarily the third season ''Stitch! ~Best Friends Forever~'', transmutation is mostly performed by Hämsterviel to force experiments to be his evil minions. This mostly consists of Hämsterviel "re-eviling" experiments. However, in some instances, he alters their primary function, enhances them with the DNA of other experiments, and occasionally alters their appearance. An experiment under Hämsterviel's control during season three can be noted by an "H" branded somewhere on their body. According to [[Ace (262)|Ace]] in the episode "[[Ace's Back!]]", he defeated dozens of transmutated experiments that Hämsterviel dispersed throughout the galaxy to wreak havoc.

===''[[Stitch & Ai]]''===
Stitch's metamorphosis program in the Chinese series can be seen as an internally programmed transmutation function, as when his destructive programming is fully triggered — which happens at the end of "[[Brothers]]" — he grows into a giant monster who can cause much greater destruction than what he is normally capable of. He also gets brainwashed into becoming obsessed with causing as much destruction as possible, with glowing red eyes and small growth spurts every time he causes some significant enough destruction. When he gets shocked by high-voltage power lines in "[[Monstrosity]]", he gains another massive growth spurt and grows four laser-firing tentacles from his back, making him even more powerful. [[Wang Ai Ling|Ai]] manages to successfully get Stitch to gain self-control over his program when she screams to get his attention, negating his brainwashing and the red glow from his eyes, which also convinces him to turn his destructive capabilities from the developing city to the [[Jaboodie]] armada. After rescuing Ai from the Jaboodies and putting her down on the ground for safety, he then disables his metamorphosis program by shrinking back down to his regular size and retracting the tentacles.

A straighter example of transmutation happens in the episode "[[Dragon Parade]]", in which Jumba enlarges and teleports [[Dim Long]] to have him take the place of the destroyed dragon puppet in the town's parade. Dim Long returns to his original size off-screen after the parade. Also, in "[[The Phoenix]]", Jumba's fenghuang quickly grows shortly after its creation, despite Jumba not intending for that to happen.

'''Weasel''', also known as '''Experiment 148''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to crawl up planetary leaders' pants during public speeches.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 148 was the 148th genetic experiment created by Jumba with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to crawl up planetary leader's trousers during public appearances. 148 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At some point, 148 was activated, captured, tamed, and named Weasel.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Weasel, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], Stitch, Jumba, [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Weasel participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[disney:Aloha `Oe|Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Weasel is a brown weasel-like experiment with black eyes, red-orange stripes and tan eye patches and a tan stomach from the chin down.

===Special abilities===
Weasel can climb up planetary leaders' pant legs during public appearances using sneak tactics, along with his size and obvious agility due to his weasel attributes.

'''Welko''', also known as '''Experiment 074''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. She is designed to blow temporary indestructible bubbles. She appears in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 074 was the 74th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. She was designed to produce temporary indestructible bubbles. 074 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Welko [[Tigerlily (episode)|first appeared]] when [[Gantu]] gained possession of her through unknown means and used her in [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s sinister plot to get rid of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]].

Stitch gets kidnapped and tied to one of Welko's balloons during the foretasted typhoon, where he would drown when the balloon popped and have no chance of survival, as he would be restrained from movement. The bubble cloud suddenly pops beneath Hämsterviel, and he plummets to the ground. Later, Gantu sets a trap for Stitch with Welko accompanying him, but [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] falls into it instead.

The plan changes and it is decided that Yuna would be bait for Stitch, so they suspend her in a hot air balloon made of dozens of Welko's balloons. Nobody notices Yuna until five minutes before the balloons pop. When the clock reaches zero, her makeshift gondola hits the water, and Stitch dives in to save her, almost making it before sinking. [[Tigerlily]] then saves them both.

The fate of Welko after this is unknown.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Welko is a pink, balloon-shaped doglike experiment with dark blue eyes, orbs on either side of her head, big red lips, and a red heart-like tail. Her hind legs appear to be vestigial nubs, and she seems to be constantly levitating. It is unknown if she is capable of terrestrial locomotion.

===Special abilities===
Welko can blow indestructible bubbles from her mouth that last only temporarily. Her bubbles are able to somewhat stick together, and thus can be formed into a cloud. Her body contains a form of helium or another light air, and this causes her to float.

Through some means, she can inflate indestructible balloons that last around 30 minutes. Such means are probably accomplished through her tail or the pink orbs on her head, which is in the same shape as some of her balloons.

==Trivia==
*Her unique design is a reference to animal-shaped [[wikipedia:Balloon modelling|balloon art]].
*Welko is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having dark blue eyes instead. Interestingly, she shares this trait with [[Bonnie (149)|Bonnie]], [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Witch (610)|Witch]], three other female experiments.
*Welko, [[Zap (603)|Zap]], [[Remmy (276)|Remmy]], [[Cloudy (320)|Cloudy]], and [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]] are the only known experiments that are always seen levitating.
**[[Phantasmo (375)|Phantasmo]] and Witch primarily levitate but often possess objects or living beings to move by other means. Tickle-Tummy is also able to levitate, but has been seen bouncing as well.

'''Wishy-Washy''', also known as '''Experiment 267''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to grant any wish he hears, but the wishes are usually granted literally. He also has a wish limit meter on his stomach; when the gauge is depleted, he loses his wish-granting power and is deemed useless.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 267 was the 267th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to grant any wish that he hears, but he takes the wishes literally, and thus they rarely turn out quite as expected. Jumba once tried to use 267 to become the supreme ruler of the universe by wishing it, but due to 267's literal nature, when the wish was granted, Jumba turned into a school ruler. How he turned back remains unknown. 267 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:ScreenCapture-19-12-24-22h03m06s637.jpg|thumb|left|Wishy-Washy moments after his activation]]
267's pod eventually made its way into a bag of birdseed, where an elderly woman threw it along with some of the seed into a flock of pigeons. One pigeon flew off with the pod, but an attack from another pigeon caused it to accidentally drop it into the [[Birds of Paradise Hotel|hotel]]'s swimming pool, activating 267, which caused the children in the pool to flee in terror.

When 267 heard a nearby woman wishing to her friend that she had a husband, the former granted the wish by replacing the woman's friend with a disgusting husband, then fled the scene.

267 later spied on [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and [[David Kawena|David]] on [[Lahui Beach|the beach]]. When David wished that there were some big waves to surf, 267 granted the wish by causing tsunami-sized waves to appear.

Stitch then spotted 267 and pursued him until both cousins shinnied up a palm tree. When Stitch tried to coax 267 down, the latter used his wand to throw Stitch off the tree. Lilo then wished to herself that they could just skip to the part where they capture the experiment, causing 267 to grant the wish by teleporting into Lilo's arms. 267 hugged Lilo affectionately while Stitch threw a brief tantrum.

[[File:ScreenCapture-19-12-24-22h04m19s624.jpg|thumb|Granting a wish]]
Lilo and Stitch then took 267, named Wishy-Washy, back to their [[Lilo's House|home]], where [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] stated Wishy-Washy's past. The former once tried to become the supreme ruler of the universe by wishing it, but since Wishy-Washy was very literal when granting wishes, Jumba turned into a school ruler (although he never revealed how he turned back).

Lilo and Stitch later brought Wishy-Washy to the beach, where he granted Lilo's wish that David was the smartest man in the world. However, David suddenly began talking like a professor, and though Lilo (as well as [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]]) couldn't understand a word he said, Jumba seemed impressed.

Lilo and Stitch eventually made Wishy-Washy [[Pleakley]]'s responsibility. However, Pleakley selfishly used up many wishes on ''Magnificent Man'' toys and gifts before [[Gantu]] arrived at the Pelekai residence and wished to have Wishy-Washy, which the latter granted.

[[File:ScreenCapture-19-12-24-22h39m43s145.jpg|thumb|left|Wishy-Washy with Gantu]]
Gantu took the [[Prison Capsule|captured]] Wishy-Washy back to [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]], where he wished for [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] to turn into a caged pet rat, for the ship to become invisible, and for all the goods in the galaxy. However, in spite of all these wishes, Gantu remained depressed until after getting a sudden jolt of inspiration, he wished for Cinta, his college crush. Regardless, it turned out that Cinta had become rather hideous and spiteful over the years, prompting Gantu to order Wishy-Washy to undo the wish.

Lilo and Stitch shortly after launched a rescue mission on Gantu's invisible ship, during which Gantu wished his [[Plasma Blaster|blaster]] was ten times more powerful. Lilo then wished for Gantu's enormous blaster to turn into a giant salami, and [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]] wished for that humongous salami to turn into a colossal Italian salami sandwich, which he ate.

[[File:ScreenCapture-19-12-24-23h20m22s706.jpg|thumb|Wishy-Washy powerless]]
Lilo and Stitch then escaped the ship with Wishy-Washy back to their house, where Jumba discovered that there was only one wish left from all the wishes granted on Gantu's ship. Lilo used this last wish to simply undo all of the wishes that were previously granted, returning everything to normal and rendering Wishy-Washy useless.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Wishy-Washy, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Wishy-Washy participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did. Although the wand on his head was seen flashing throughout the battle, it is presumed that he wouldn't have been able to be very effective, due to the fact that his powers are deemed useless.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Wishy-Washy has appeared multiple times in the ''Stitch!'' anime, including [[We Wishy You a Washy Christmas|one instance]] where he caused a Christmas wish to go awry. Of course, this would mean that there is a way to replenish Wishy-Washy's powers once all of his wishes are depleted, possibly by dehydrating him then reactivating him, as his gauge was full when he was first activated. In [[Stitch Goes to Wishlanda|another episode]], Wishy-Washy was [[Transmutation|used]] by [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] to wreak havoc at an amusement park that the alien scientist created. In "[[Shogun]]", it is shown that Wishy-Washy was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Wishy-Washy wasn't one of the experiments that was activated.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Wishy-Washy is a light-bluish teddy bear-like experiment with small white fairy-like wings that enable him to fly. He also has a "wand" on his head that lights up every time a wish is granted and is useful for throwing an unsuspecting opponent, like [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. His tongue also functions similar to a chameleon's tongue. Additionally, he has a wish limit meter on his belly, which starts out completely pink. As wishes are granted, the gauge slowly diminishes. Once all the wishes are depleted, the gauge appears white and Wishy-Washy is deemed useless.

===Special abilities===
Wishy-Washy can grant any wish he hears, with the exception of the wish for more wishes, of course. Unfortunately, he is very literal, and the wish will likely not quite turn out as expected. Also, Wishy-Washy has a wish limit meter and loses his wish-granting power when it runs out. He will respond to requests to undo any wish, though it is unknown if the wish is put back on his gauge or if the reversal counts as a wish.

===Weaknesses===
Wishy-Washy becomes powerless once the wish limit meter is depleted. He will also reject the wish for more wishes.

==Trivia==
*Wishy-Washy's name is based on his ability to grant wishes and also the word's meaning which is "lacking strength", referring to his uselessness once his meter has been depleted.
*Wishy-Washy's diet apparently includes books and papers.
*Wishy-Washy, [[Bugby (128)|Bugby]], [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]], [[Jam (202)|Jam]], [[Melty (228)|Melty]], [[Snooty (277)|Snooty]], [[Amnesio (303)|Amnesio]], [[Hunkahunka (323)|Hunkahunka]], [[Experiments#5-Series: Elemental and environmental manipulators|Blake]], [[Slugger (608)|Slugger]], [[Witch (610)|Witch]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Miscellaneous|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have wings.
*It is unknown exactly how Wishy-Washy grants wishes; it could be he warps reality, manipulates probability, or just breaks the laws of physics.
**Jumba refers to Wishy-Washy as a "fulfiller of wishes" and as a failure because his "experiment was too literal" since "programming for wish fulfillment is very difficult", and "they never turned out quite as expected."
**Ironically, given that Jumba stated in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime that [[Witch (610)|Witch]] is the only magic-using experiment, it is very unlikely that Wishy-Washy uses magic to fulfill wishes.
*Theoretically, Wishy-Washy could act as a watered-down version of [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]] if someone wished to regain some years of youth; given how literal the wishes are, if not worded properly, it could also reset the wisher's memory to match what it was at the age they wished to be.
*The experiments list seen in the end credits of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'' spells his name as "Wishy Washy" (no hyphen). Interestingly, the [[disney:Disney+|Disney+]] listing of [[Wishy-Washy (episode)|his episode]] also spells it the same way.
*Although it is said Wishy-Washy would lose his wish-granting power once his meter was depleted, every time he has appeared, his wishing gauge was replenished, implying that he loses his wish-granting power only temporarily and must wait for the energy to replenish.
*Wishy-Washy's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green.
*The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Wishy-Washy as: "Experiment 267. Primary function: Granting wishes."
*Wishy-Washy is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.
*He is also one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
*Wishy-Washy is one of the few characters to have had more than once voice actor in the English dub of the anime; Derek Stephen Prince voiced Wishy-Washy in the second season episode "[[We Wishy You a Washy Christmas]]", while Roger Craig Smith voiced the character in the third season episode "[[Stitch Goes to Wishlanda]]".

'''Witch''', also known as '''Experiment 610''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. She is designed to utilize supernatural forces in order to subdue and abduct planetary leaders. Her powers include intangibility, animation, and many other reality-bending abilities. She is capable of possessing individuals and channeling her powers through their vessel, but she can be forced out of her victim if she sees her reflection. She appears in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 610 was the 610th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. She was designed to use magic and reality-bending abilities to defeat and kidnap planetary leaders. 610 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
In her [[Witch (episode)|eponymous debut]], [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] gained possession of Witch and [[Transmutation|reprogrammed]] her to be able to possess humans so as to enhance her abilities. Witch was sealed in a box and released when [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and [[Jessica]] opened it. She possessed Jessica afterwards and turned her into an evil witch. After a tough battle, Witch was surrounded with six mirrors, forcing her out of Jessica and into [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s capture container.

When Witch turns Jessica into an evil witch, Jessica's hair turns grey and her eyes turn light purple. She also wears an orange dress with a small black jacket, as well as black gloves with black boots.

When Witch transforms Jessica into her demonic form, her hair has a little more twist. Her arms and legs grow purple fur with claws. She now wears the black dress with an extra red skirt. This time, she grows a tail and bat-like wings. There is also a red color around her eyes.

In "[[Shogun]]", it is shown that Witch was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in Jumba's vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed her pod to help [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Witch wasn't one of the experiments that was activated.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Witch is a purple bat/pikaia/ghost-like experiment. The back of her head is shaped like a cone and curved at the bottom to resemble a witch's hat, while her ears are small bat wings. She also has two wide arms resembling flippers and dark blue eyes with eyelashes. Her stomach is light purple and her chest has a yellow heart. She has a continuous wisp-like tail instead of legs, similar to [[Phantasmo (375)|Phantasmo]]. Her witch-like hat has a pattern of purple and then light purple stripes. She also has a yellow "H" on her forehead, which is a product of [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[transmutation]] process.

===Special abilities===
Witch was designed to have many supernatural abilities. These include the abilities of a ghost and being able to possess others in order to turn them into evil witches too. Once possessed, the victim is under Witch's complete control and also has her variety of abilities such as animation, spontaneous generation, levitation, demonic transformation, and other forms of reality-bending abilities.

===Weaknesses===
Hämsterviel's transmutation of Witch makes it possible to force her out of her victim if she sees her reflection, much like how the evil creature [[wikipedia:Medusa|Medusa]] was defeated in mythology, as well as making her weak to red peppers.

==Trivia==
*Witch is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having dark blue eyes instead. Interestingly, she shares this trait with [[Bonnie (149)|Bonnie]], [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Welko (074)|Welko]], three other female experiments.
**Witch is also one of the few experiments with visible irises. However, she was entirely under [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Transmutation|control]] in her appearance. Since other experiments under Hämsterviel's possession in the [[Stitch!|anime]] tend to have their eyes diluted to show irises and/or sclerae, it is unknown whether or not Witch's own irises being visible is a result of Hämsterviel controlling her or if it's a natural part of her appearance.
*Witch and [[Hertz Donut (022)|Hertz Donut]] are the only two experiments that first appeared in ''Stitch!'', but were not shown in their original (un-transmutated) form and whose real eye color is unknown.
*Witch, [[Bugby (128)|Bugby]], [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]], [[Jam (202)|Jam]], [[Melty (228)|Melty]], [[Wishy-Washy (267)|Wishy-Washy]], [[Snooty (277)|Snooty]], [[Amnesio (303)|Amnesio]], [[Hunkahunka (323)|Hunkahunka]], [[Experiments#5-Series: Elemental and environmental manipulators|Blake]], [[Slugger (608)|Slugger]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Miscellaneous|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have wings.
*Witch, [[Phantasmo (375)|Phantasmo]], [[Fudgy (054)|Fudgy]], [[Remmy (276)|Remmy]], and Tickle-Tummy are the only known experiments to have arms but no legs.
**Interestingly, excluding Fudgy, all of these experiments are capable of levitation. Remmy is always seen levitating. Phantasmo and Witch primarily levitate but often possess objects or living beings to move by other means. Tickle-Tummy is also able to levitate, but has been seen bouncing as well.
*Witch, Phantasmo, and [[Glitch (223)|Glitch]] are all capable of possession, albeit in different capacities: Witch can possess living beings, Phantasmo can possess any inanimate object, and Glitch possesses technology.
*Witch's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green.
*According to Jumba, Witch is the only experiment that can perform magic (witchcraft).

'''Woody''', also known as '''Experiment 507''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to eat wood at a rapid pace. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "[[:Category:Mrs. Hasagawa's experiments|cats]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 507 was the 507th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to eat wood at a rapid rate. 507 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]]. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 507's pod being one of them.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 507's pod for an apricot and placed it in a colander for later consumption along with numerous other pods.

When [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] redecorated Mrs. Hasagawa's front yard without her permission, she was less than thrilled with the results, but decided to thank them for their hard work with the "apricots". The pods were then revealed, but before Lilo and Stitch could stop her, she washed them with a watering can and thus activated the experiments.

After his activation, 507 began to carry out his primary function by gnawing on one of the wooden beams that supported [[Mrs. Hasagawa's House|Mrs. Hasagawa's awning]]. Seeing him as a mere stray cat, she petted him and called him "kitty". When Lilo questioned this, Mrs. Hasagawa explained that several "unusual" stray cats come to live with her, the "kitties" turning out to be more experiments. The wooden beam 507 was gnawing on then crashed down, taking half of the awning with it. Lilo and Stitch believed the experiments to be a danger to Mrs. Hasagawa and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], decided to capture them all. Lilo was eventually able to capture 507 by placing a long plank of wood on the ground leading into a [[Prison Capsule|container]], and the experiment nibbled right into his capture.

507 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 507 was then named Woody.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Woody, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Woody participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]].

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Woody made [[Link-age|an appearance]] in Season 2 of the ''Stitch!'' anime, along with [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]], [[Babyfier (151)|Babyfier]], [[Link (251)|Link]], and [[Spike (319)|Spike]]. It is revealed that [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] reverted these experiments to evil using a recording of [[Angel (624)|Angel]]'s song, thus enabling them to wreak havoc on the [[Izayoi Island|island]].

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Woody is a light brown beaver-like experiment with black eyes, grey-tipped antennae, grey patches around his eyes and markings on his tail, a pink stomach from the chin down, light yellow buckteeth and beetle-like mandibles. Woody's mandibles receive a minor redesign in ''[[Stitch!]]'', as there is now a prong on the outside of them.

===Special abilities===
Woody can eat through wood very quickly by using his pincers.

==Trivia==
*Woody's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue.
*In the English dub of the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime episode "[[Link-age]]", [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] states that Woody's favorite type of sandwich is anything fibrous.

'''Woops''', also known as '''Experiment 600''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is one of the failed prototypes of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], possessing all the same powers, but turned out to be a real klutz; he accidentally knocks over and/or breaks anything he touches and only says, "Woops!" after doing so, hence his name. His one true place is at [[Kokaua Town Lanes]] as a champion bowler on [[Pleakley]]'s bowling team, the Kokaua Bowling Brawlers.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 600 was the 600th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed for [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]'s purpose, being indestructible and capable of anything, but was instead a destructive klutz who did nothing except break everything in his path. 600 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture Experiment 626.

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo  & Stitch The Series - Woops - Woops moments after activation.png|thumb|left|Woops moments after his activation]]
600's pod was found by [[Gantu]] and sent to [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. When the latter discovered that 600 was a prototype of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], Hämsterviel activated the experiment. However, he and the captive experiments were awestruck by 600's klutzy behavior around the [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison]], which alerted the [[UGF Troopers|guards]] and almost blew Hämsterviel's cover in the process.

As a result, Hämsterviel was forced to teleport 600 and the other captive experiments back to Earth on [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]], with orders to get rid of 600, as he gave Hämsterviel a headache, and to hold on to the other experiments until Hämsterviel was clear to hold them captive in his prison cell again. Meanwhile, 600's clumsiness around the ship ruined Gantu's azaleas, broke his [[Plasma Blaster|blaster]], and freed [[Nosy (199)|Nosy]] from [[Prison Capsule|containment]], allowing him to escape.

Eventually, the mayhem caused by 600's clumsiness drove Gantu crazy enough to offer him to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and Stitch. 600 was then taken in and named Woops by Lilo. Though initially dismayed by the clumsy experiment, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] discreetly suggested bringing Woops to [[Pleakley]]'s domino tournament (in a quite evil voice). However, upon seeing Woops, Pleakley panicked and then demanded Lilo to lock the klutz away until the tournament was over.

Inside a containment orb at the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]], Woops just so happened to sneeze, causing a chain reaction that transported him onto the streets of [[Kokaua Town]]. He soon started to bounce toward the dominoes.

Just before impact, Stitch caught Woops and then let the latter out of his container. Woops suddenly sneezed again, which caused Stitch to stagger backward into the [[Ice Cream Man]], causing the ice cream from his cone to hit the dominoes, much to Pleakley's horror.

Towards the end of the domino toppling, a startled cat hit a trash can, causing another chain reaction of objects hitting each other until the [[Kilauea Lighthouse|old lighthouse]] was destroyed, plummeting into the ocean.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Woops - Woops wins Pleakley's bowling tournament.png|thumb|Woops wins Pleakley's bowling tournament]]
The events caused Lilo to discover that Woops was good at knocking things over (thanks to his clumsiness), and the latter found his one true place at the [[Kokaua Town Lanes|local bowling alley]] as a talented bowler (one of the few things where knocking stuff over is ''good'') on Pleakley's bowling team, the Kokaua Bowling Brawlers.

In "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", Nosy revealed to Lilo and Stitch that Woops blew the secret about Hämsterviel's captive experiments, so he sent them all back to Gantu. Nosy then added that he got lucky because his container broke thanks to Woops.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Woops, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Woops participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Personality==
Woops is a very clumsy, accident-prone, and unbalanced experiment. He is easily guilty but never mourns over past accidents or incidents. He apologizes as often as he falls, and his personality is rather clownish and dim-witted. He is usually seen swaying side to side, laughing awkwardly, and picking his nose with his finger. He is left-footed and can get upset if abandoned or contained for periods of time.

An amiable sort, Woops merely wants to do the right thing but just can't seem to do it. He can hardly seem to stand on his own two feet, let alone keep his balance, and is always running into objects and knocking them over. Most individuals find him unbearably annoying, but he is a bowling champion.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Woops is a pale grayish-purple, skinny [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]-like experiment with a small bean-shaped body, thick limbs, huge yellow buckteeth, a large Adam's-apple, a football-shaped head with small eyes, a huge, bulbous nose, three short pale mint green-tipped antennae sticking out of his head, a short, pale mint green-tipped tail and long, gangling legs dotted with black toes. His ears are smaller than Stitch's and stick out on either side of his head.

===Special abilities===
He was originally designed to be an indestructible experiment that could do anything, but he instead turned out as a destructive experiment that could do nothing. However, he has the uncanny ability to destroy everything around him unintentionally, and accidentally bumps into everything.

Woops has all of Stitch's powers, but he fails miserably and is instead too much of a klutz to use them at all. Woops can barely walk through an open door, much less keep his balance. The only word he can say for himself is "Woops!" when he does something by accident.

===Weaknesses===
Similar to [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]], Woops is too clumsy and unbalanced to use his powers, whereas Reuben was simply too lazy to do anything but make sandwiches.

==Trivia==
*Woops is the first known prototype of Stitch and is a massive failure.
**Despite being a failure, Woops did help Stitch more than most other [[experiments]]: by freeing [[Nosy (199)|Nosy]], he started the chain of events seen in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", which ended up with Lilo and Stitch saving all the other 17 experiments imprisoned by Hämsterviel, including [[Angel (624)|Angel]], whom Stitch was feeling the most guilt for letting her be captured by Gantu and shipped to Hämsterviel. Ironically, Woops never met Angel (due to Angel somehow not appearing in Woops' [[Woops (episode)|debut episode]]).
*Unlike most experiments, Woops' number is pronounced as a whole number ("six hundred") instead of three individual digits (which in his case would have been "six-oh-oh") as per the norm for the experiments.
**The only other experiment seen in [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]] whose number is also referred to as a whole number is [[Spooky (300)|Spooky]] (Experiment 300). This implies that experiments whose number is divisible by one hundred (100) are the primary exceptions to the normal by-digit pronunciation of experiment numbers.
*Woops' [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue.
*Woops is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.
*Woops' design bears a great resemblance to [[w:c:iceage:Sid|Sid]] from the ''[[wikipedia:Ice Age (franchise)|Ice Age]]'' films. Coincidentally, Disney currently owns the ''Ice Age'' franchise following the studio's acquisition of [[disney:20th Century Studios|20th Century Fox]] in 2019.
