'''Wormhole''', also known as '''Experiment 272''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to generate portals to parallel universes. He also has advanced language programming to assist him as he traverses alternate realities. Jumba implanted a tracking device so that he would be able to locate Wormhole in whatever universe the experiment travels to. Once a transdimensional portal is created, it only lasts for a short period of time. Luckily, Wormhole has the ability to locate any portal he creates so he can leave before it closes. He appears in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 272 was the 272nd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to create portals to parallel universes. Jumba got angry at 272 for being too nice and threw his favorite slipper at the experiment, but it unfortunately went into one of 272's wormholes and became trapped in another dimension. 272 was deactivated at some point and, along with the other 624 experiments, smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All the experiments were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point, 272 was activated during [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]] and named Wormhole, who then continued on his quest to find Jumba's slipper that he had lost long ago.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Approximately 25 years later, prior to Wormhole's [[Wormhole (episode)|eponymous debut]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] had left [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and found a new owner, [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]], who came across Wormhole when she was upset at her cousin, [[Tigerlily Sakai|Tigerlily]].

Wormhole explains his backstory to Yuna while informing her that he was about to set out to another dimension, and she quickly asks if she could tag along. Wormhole warns Yuna that it would be drastically different than her current dimension, though she chimes that "it couldn't be worse than this one." As Yuna is entering, Stitch spots her going into Wormhole's portal and tries to stop her, but ends up getting dragged along himself.

From there, Wormhole sets off to find [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s slipper, exclaiming he could sense it was near and being oblivious to Yuna and Stitch's predicament. Wormhole also ignores Yuna and Stitch's pleading to go back because he is so sure the slipper ended up in some dimension.

By the end of the episode, Wormhole finds the alternate dimension and Jumba's slipper in his closet, and the alternate Jumba watches confusedly as Wormhole drags it out. He then agrees to find his previous wormhole – but there wasn't much time until it closed. They barely make it through the portal, and Wormhole delightedly returns the slipper to his creator, who is surprised to see it again.

==Personality==
Wormhole is generally nice, rather than the standard evil programming, and his feelings can get easily hurt. He has a deep respect for [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], his creator, and if he holds a grudge against him, Wormhole will spend every moment possible searching for a way for his creator to like him again. Also, if he lost something of Jumba's, he will search every corner of every universe to find it. He can be quite oblivious, but is actually helpful if he can finish whatever he was doing (or looking for) before.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Wormhole is a purple and cyan caterpillar-like experiment with black eyes, two dark purple-tipped antennae, eight dark purple-tipped legs, and a blue inner mouth. His antennae also flicker and light up.

===Special abilities===
Wormhole creates portals to other dimensions by jumping up in the air and folding himself into a ball then spinning. This opens up a wormhole directly behind him. These portals only last for a few days, and Wormhole can locate any one of them which is open. While he can create one at any time, he has absolutely no power over which universe the portal may lead to.

Wormhole has advanced language programming, and his ability to [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]] helps him as he traverses alternate realities.

==Trivia==
*Wormhole's number was [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|listed as 275]] in the [[Experiments/Gallery#Leroy & Stitch|end credits]] of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', which is [[Tickle-Tummy (275)|Tickle-Tummy]]'s number in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime. Tickle-Tummy does not appear in the end credits of ''Leroy & Stitch'', while 272 is listed as Mamf.
*Wormhole is one of the few known experiments that can [[:Category:Talking experiments|speak fluently]].
*Wormhole is the only known experiment with eight legs. [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]] has eight limbs, but only uses four for locomotion.

After freeing the one-eyed alien, she used the wrapping as a makeshift lasso to save Mrs. Hasagawa when she was blown into the air by [[Blowhard (533)|Experiment 533]].

Wrapper can use the roll of tape on his back to mummify anyone or anything he crawls over in tape.

'''Xiezhi''' is an illegal genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba]], and [[Jumba's Chinese Experiments|the fifth experiment he created]] in China based on what he learns in ancient Chinese scrolls.

==Background==
==="[[The Lock]]"===
After receiving the ancient scrolls, Jumba was inspired to create a genetic experiment based on the Chinese mythical creatures that were in the scroll. This time, Jumba wanted to create an experiment capable of possessing the power of Qi, flying without wings. He tested this on a beta experiment by creating [[Dim Long]]. After a successful experience, he tried to materialize Xiezhi, but he was aggressive and wanted to attack Pleakley and was dematerialized. Later, he was re-materialized in the rocks, where [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] and [[Wang Ai Ling|Ai]] were attacked by aliens again. Xiezhi began to administer justice and, with the help of Stitch, eliminated all the aliens. He was later sent to a parallel dimension inhabited by various mythological creatures.

==="[[Monstrosity]]"===
In this episode, Xiezhi and some other Chinese experiments were summoned from a parallel dimension to battle the [[Jaboodie]]s.

==Personality==
Xiezhi was initially aggressive on the first attempt. On the second attempt, he began to fulfill his function of administering justice. Back then, he was formidable and serious as a judge. He is also one of the few Chinese experiments that is guided by moral principles.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Xiezhi looks like a lion, with a long mane, four legs with claws and a tail. But besides that, he also has a yellow horn on his forehead.

===Special abilities===
Xiezhi has a large set of abilities. Its main function is to administer justice and protect the innocent. First, he figures out the culprit by turning his head. Then, if he finds the culprit, he turns his horn on him and begins an attack. He has Qi energy with which he can fly without wings, move through clouds without falling down. He is also very strong and can easily rip apart a spaceship. He also has the ability to eat fire, so he is immune to fire projectiles.

===Weaknesses===
If he is in the clouds, he may not see the culprit if they disappeared under the clouds.

==Trivia==
*Xiezhi is based on the Chinese mythological creature, [[wikipedia:Xiezhi|xiezhi]].
*Xiezhi is one of the few Jumba experiments that is guided by moral principles.
*It is also similar to 262 ([[Ace (262)|Ace]]), as both experiments save innocent people, but unlike Xiezhi, 262 is not designed to attack but merely save people.

'''Yaarp''', also known as '''Experiment 613''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to create devastating sonic blasts that can shatter windows, flatten buildings, and cause acute loss of hearing. Luckily, he can also reduce these noises to soft, gentle honks. His one true place is at [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]]'s [[Kaiāulu Hale|hula school]] as an alien invasion alarm and buzzer.

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 613 was the 613th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his sonic-blasting ability to cause massive damage and deafen nearby victims. 613 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 613's pod landing in [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s [[Hasagawa Fruits|fruit stand]].

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Yaarp - Yaarp in Mrs. Hasagawa's fruit stand.png|thumb|left|Yaarp after being activated]]
When [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] watered her fruit, 613's pod got wet, activating the experiment. After being admired by [[Charles and Mary|a couple]] on their honeymoon, 613 then proceeded to cause massive chaos using his destructive shock waves.

Later, when [[Gantu]], wearing special earmuffs, chased 613 into an electronics store, the latter was captured in a [[Prison Capsule|container]], but rescued and freed by [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. Instead of showing gratitude, 613 emitted a sonic blast that made Stitch go temporarily deaf, then fled the store with Gantu in hot pursuit.

Since Stitch's ears were highly sensitive to 613's shock waves, [[Pleakley]] was chosen for the task, as he did not have ears and was therefore unaffected by the sound blasts. After [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], Stitch and [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] attempted to train and condition Pleakley, he was equipped with special experiment catching gear. The four tracked 613 down to a cave, where Stitch, using a conch, posed as the experiment and acted like a decoy. He then imitated 613's sonic blast to alert Gantu, who donned his earmuffs and pursued Stitch.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Yaarp - Yaarp saved by Pleakley.png|thumb|Yaarp saved by Pleakley]]
Meanwhile, a reluctant Pleakley entered the cave, where he discovered 613. When Pleakley unintentionally blasted 613 with a vacuum, the latter retaliated using a massive shock wave. However, when a sudden cave-in endangered 613's life, he was then saved by Pleakley. 613 gratefully kissed him three times, while Pleakley christened him Yaarp.

Pleakley and Yaarp soon fled the crumbling cave and made it out safely. When Yaarp first noticed Lilo, he growled until Pleakley assured him that she was a friend, causing Yaarp to emit a gentle honk. Unfortunately, Stitch got captured by Gantu (who thought Stitch was actually Yaarp) during the process, and the latter demanded a ransom exchange.

As part of a setup, Lilo arrived at the [[Museum of Natural History Kauai|local museum]] with Yaarp in a pet carrier, where the former made Gantu believe that Yaarp was rehabilitated. However (as planned), when Gantu removed his earmuffs and bartered the captive Stitch for Yaarp, the latter unleashed a sonic blast upon Lilo's signal, alerting the authorities and forcing Gantu to flee.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Spike - Yaarp keeping score at the Ohana-Rama.png|thumb|left|Yaarp at the Ohana-Rama]]
After Lilo revealed Yaarp to the [[Mayor Anolo|mayor]] and [[Nicolé|chairwoman]], he was given a one true place as an alien invasion alarm at Lilo's [[Kaiāulu Hale|hula school]].

Yaarp reappeared in "[[Elastico (episode)|Elastico]]" as one of the audience members for Lilo's hula dance.

In "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]", Yaarp served as the scorekeeper for the Ohana-Rama, and was also briefly seen hiding under the couch during Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. session.

In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Yaarp was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
In the film's opening Yaarp can be seen greeting [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] with sonic blasts from his megaphone-like antenna.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Yaarp, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Yaarp participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by presumably using his sonic blasts to deafen and push Leroys back.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. Yaarp joins them for the song by playing the built-in foghorn-like device on his head.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Yaarp made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
Despite his destructive nature, Yaarp is quite friendly, but he reacts quickly and dramatically to the way others treat him. For example, if he feels intimidated or provoked, he will emit loud sonic blasts. If he feels safe or unthreatened, he will emit small, gentle honks as a sign of affection and friendship.

Yaarp, for the most part, is pretty easygoing and laid-back. However, he is very ready-minded and cautious, but is loyal to those who win his trust. He is also a bit jumpy and nervous, often sounding his horn at improper times because something trivial had startled him.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Yaarp is a small, turquoise/blue lemur-like experiment with four arms, small floppy [[Drowsy (360)|Drowsy]]-like ears, and a foghorn-like antenna on his head. The antenna, the tips of his ears, and the single ring on his tail, as well as the tail's tip, are all blue. The area around his eyes, his muzzle and chest/belly, and his paw pads are all a lighter variant of his body color.

===Special abilities===
Yaarp can produce devastating sonic blasts through his megaphone-like antenna. These noises can range from small, gentle honks to massive shock waves that can shatter buildings and cause acute loss of hearing. His tail can act like a spring, as he often bounces on it instead of using his limbs.

Yaarp has shown to be skilled in playing the foghorn-like device on his head like a trumpet.

==Trivia==
*Yaarp was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Yaarp is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to.
*Yaarp is one of the ten known experiments named by someone other than Lilo or Stitch, the other nine being [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Elastico (345)|Elastico]], [[Hammerface (033)|Hammerface]], [[Heat (609)|Heat]], [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]], [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]], [[Morpholomew (316)|Morpholomew]], [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]], and [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]]. 
**Yaarp, in particular, was named by Pleakley.
*He is also one of the six known experiments to be rehabilitated by someone other than Lilo and Stitch, the other five being Gigi, Elastico, [[Spike (319)|Spike]], [[Frenchfry (062)|Frenchfry]], and [[Snooty (277)|Snooty]].
**Yaarp, alongside Spike, was rehabilitated by Pleakley.
*Yaarp was named after a word from Pleakley's [[Plorgonar|home planet]].
*According to Jumba, Yaarp "was [his] first attempt to wreak havoc with high-decibel sonic disturbance, resonant compression, and oscillating vibrational distortion." Simply put, Yaarp "makes loud noises", while his "sonic blasts can shatter windows, flatten buildings, and cause acute loss of hearing."
*Yaarp's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is yellow.
*In "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]", only Spike, [[Fibber (032)|Fibber]], [[Nosy (199)|Nosy]], [[Bonnie (149)|Bonnie]], [[Clyde (150)|Clyde]], [[Slushy (523)|Slushy]], and [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]] were part of Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group, but in one scene, Yaarp can clearly be seen hiding under the couch.
*Yaarp's torso and tail appear in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.

'''Yang''', also known as '''Experiment 502''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to attack by firing balls of lava from his back spouts. His one true place is creating a new island with [[Yin (501)|Yin]].

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 502 was the 502nd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to spout balls of lava. 502 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]], with 502's pod landing in a fissure in the ground on a mountain road.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Yin Yang - Yang after activation.png|thumb|left|Yang after being activated]]
When a stranded man poured water into his jeep's burnt-out engine, the water leaked out into the fissure and onto 502's pod, activating the experiment. 502 then erupted to the surface and set out to cause chaos.

While 502 was attempting to cross a road in front of an approaching car, the owner scolded him to get out of the way, causing the angered experiment to destroy the driver's automobile.

502 later entered [[Kokaua Town]] and went on a rampage, destroying everything in sight. [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] jumped onto one of 502's back lava spouts to try and stop the latter, but 502 simply blasted Stitch off and most likely continued his rampage.

Stitch's incompetence caused a rift between him and [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], and the two insisted that they each could catch an experiment without the other. After wagering an official contest, Stitch joined up with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] while Lilo joined up with [[Pleakley]], with each pair hunting down an individual experiment.

Later, while 502 was scratching himself, he was blasted into a [[Net Cannon|net]] by [[Gantu]]. However, 502 was able to escape by simply using his lava to melt through the net.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Yin Yang - Yin and Yang meet for the first time.png|thumb|Yin and Yang meet]]
502 was later chased by Stitch and Jumba through a jungle, but the two failed to catch the former. While continuing to flee his pursuers, Experiments 502 and [[Yin (501)|501]] met for the first time. Jumba erroneously stated that if they both touched in any way, Earth would be destroyed. However, they were ambushed and captured in [[Prison Capsule|containment orbs]] by [[Gantu]] before they could make physical contact.

While returning to [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]] with the two captured experiments, Gantu fell for a sandwich trap laid by [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]], allowing 501 and 502 to escape.

When Lilo later tracked 502 down, the latter attacked her with fireballs. However, Lilo was able to block off 502's lava attacks long enough for Stitch to immobilize 502 via anti-heat foam, rendering him defenseless.

501 and 502 were then rehabilitated, named Yin and Yang, and given a one true place using their combined powers to create a whole new island.

Yang reappeared in "[[Elastico (episode)|Elastico]]" as one of the audience members for Lilo's hula dance.

In "[[Houdini (episode)|Houdini]]", Yang was one of the audience members for Stitch's bungled magic act.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Dupe - Stitch's cousins attending Lilo's slumber party 3.png|thumb|left|Yang attending Lilo and Stitch's slumber party]] 
In "[[Finder (episode)|Finder]]", Yang was seen playing poker with Stitch, Yin, [[Richter (513)|Richter]] and [[Cannonball (520)|Cannonball]]. He won the poker hand and the entire bet (which was cookies). 

In "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]", Yang was one of the experiments that came to Lilo and Stitch's slumber party wearing boxer shorts and bunny slippers. However, he was forced by Pleakley to leave due to his destructive behavior.

In "[[Angel (episode)|Angel]]", Yang was one of the experiments that [[Angel (624)|Angel]] reverted to evil using her song. Later, Yang and the other depraved experiments attacked Stitch aboard a ship, but Angel turned them to good again before they could finish Stitch off. Working together, the experiments were then able to successfully escape the ship with Stitch.

Yang reappeared in "[[Slugger (episode)|Slugger]]" as part of Lilo's softball team.

In "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]", when [[Mortlegax]] arrived on Earth to decide whether or not Jumba was still evil, Yin and Yang posed as mutant creations as part of a hoax to fool the head of E.G.O. industries.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
In the film's opening, Yang can be seen waving hello to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], along with [[Yin (501)|Yin]] and [[Cannonball (520)|Cannonball]]. He was also seen later in the movie creating a new island with Yin as Lilo was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to make sure all the experiments were happy in the one true place they belonged.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Yang, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Yin and Yang participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by using their combined powers to encase Leroys in rock. Yang also shot balls of lava at attacking Leroys.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Yang made [[The Return of Amnesio|a cameo appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime as an image on a computer screen. He later appeared in the special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
An experiment of few words, Yang was shown to be fiery, short-tempered and hotheaded before his rehabilitation. He is single-minded and will focus only on what is right in front of him, paying little heed to anything else going on around him. This clearly demonstrates overconfidence in his own powers, as Yang considers them more than adequate to handle any threat. He is shown to not really care what other individuals want him to do, and has a tendency to be boastful. However, he would defend his friends and ''ʻohana'' loyally, alongside Yin.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Yang is a quadrupedal, orange-and-red weasel/lizard/dragon-like experiment with four volcano-like spouts along his back, two volcano-like antennae on his head, black eyes, a round nose and a wide mouth with two fangs sticking out.

===Special abilities===
Yang can fire balls of lava from the spouts on his back at targets and enemies, and heat solid ground or other land with his feet. It is also shown that when Yin and Yang combine their powers, they are able to create rock/land.

===Weaknesses===
Anti-heat foam can incapacitate Yang and render him defenseless.

==Trivia==
*Yang was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
**An earlier, unused design for Yang was also shown in a promotional image for ''Stitch! The Movie''.
*His name is derived from the concept of [[wikipedia:Yin and yang|yin and yang]]; in this case his name stems from the force of yang, which is associated with masculinity, fire, and heat, fitting his nature.
*Yang, along with [[Gigi (007)|Gigi]], [[Dorkifier (122)|Dorkifier]], [[Nosox (204)|Nosox]], [[Butter (227)|Butter]], [[Shortstuff (297)|Shortstuff]], [[Spike (319)|Spike]], [[Richter (513)|Richter]], [[Phoon (540)|Phoon]], [[Tank (586)|Tank]], [[Splodyhead (619)|Splodyhead]], and one [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed experiment]], are the only known experiments that are primarily quadrupeds.
**Although Yang has been seen on his two hind legs, he is mostly seen on all fours.
*Yang, [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]], and Splodyhead are the only known experiments that shoot plasma/lava balls. Also, Yang, Plasmoid, [[Melty (228)|Melty]], [[Heat (609)|Heat]], and Splodyhead are the only known experiments whose powers are related to fire.
*Yang is the only experiment besides Stitch to escape a [[Net Cannon|net]] by himself.
*Yang's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue.
*Yang appears in the online game ''[[Lilo & Stitch: Alien Interception]]'', along with [[Clyde (150)|Clyde]], [[Dupe (344)|Dupe]], Tank, [[Plasmoid (617)|Plasmoid]], and [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]].

However, they were ambushed and captured in [[Prison Capsule|containment orbs]] by [[Gantu]] before they could make physical contact.

While returning to [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]] with the two captured experiments, Gantu fell for a sandwich trap laid by [[Reuben (625)|Experiment 625]], allowing 501 and 502 to escape.

When Stitch later tracked 501 down to a backyard, the latter used a running tap to gain an infinite supply of water to use as ammo. However, her ammo ran out when Lilo turned the tap off, allowing Stitch to easily capture 501 in a container.

501 and 502 were then rehabilitated, named Yin and Yang, and given a one true place using their combined powers to create a whole new island.

Yin reappeared in "[[Elastico (episode)|Elastico]]" as one of the audience members for Lilo's hula dance.

In "[[Houdini (episode)|Houdini]]", Yin was one of the audience members for Stitch's bungled magic act.

[[File:Lilo & Stitch The Series - Dupe - Stitch's cousins attending Lilo's slumber party 3.png|thumb|left|Yin attending Lilo and Stitch's slumber party]] 
In "[[Finder (episode)|Finder]]", Yin was seen playing poker with Stitch, Yang, [[Richter (513)|Richter]] and [[Cannonball (520)|Cannonball]].

In "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]", Yin was one of the experiments that came to Lilo and Stitch's slumber party wearing a pink bathrobe and matching nightcap. However, she was forced by Pleakley to leave due to her destructive behavior.

In "[[Angel (episode)|Angel]]", Yin was one of the experiments that [[Angel (624)|Angel]] reverted to evil using her song. Later, Yin and the other depraved experiments attacked Stitch aboard a ship, but Angel turned them to good again before they could finish Stitch off. Working together, the experiments were then able to successfully escape the ship with Stitch.

Yin reappeared in "[[Slugger (episode)|Slugger]]" as part of Lilo's softball team.

In "[[Shoe (episode)|Shoe]]", Yin was one of the experiments that helped turn [[Jumba's Ship|Jumba's ship]] into a [[Jumba & Pleakley's Bed & Not Breakfast|hotel]].

Yin was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that joined Stitch in a rebellion against Gantu. Earlier in the episode, she, along with [[Digger (529)|Digger]] and [[Backhoe (040)|Backhoe]], helped Lilo make mud.

In "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]", when [[Mortlegax]] arrived on Earth to decide whether or not Jumba was still evil, Yin and Yang posed as mutant creations as part of a hoax to fool the head of E.G.O. industries.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
In the film's opening, Yin can be seen waving hello to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], along with [[Yang (502)|Yang]] and [[Cannonball (520)|Cannonball]]. She was also seen later in the movie creating a new island with Yang as Lilo was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to make sure all the experiments were happy in the one true place they belonged.

Later, the first 624 experiments, including Yin and Yang, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Yin and Yang participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by using their combined powers to encase Leroys in rock. Yin also sprayed water at attacking Leroys until a Leroy clone completely tied her tentacles up, leaving her powerless and Yang to fight on his own.

However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Yin made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime special ''[[Stitch and the Planet of Sand]]''.

==Personality==
An experiment of few words, Yin was shown to be cocky, short-tempered and reckless before her rehabilitation. She is single-minded and will focus only on what is right in front of her, paying little heed to anything else going on around her. This clearly demonstrates overconfidence in her own powers, as Yin considers them more than adequate to handle any threat. She is shown to not really care about other individuals' surroundings when using her squirting powers. However, she would defend her friends and ''ʻohana'' loyally, alongside Yang.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Yin is a teal blue, amphibious cephalopod-like experiment with eight water hose-like tentacles, a long, thin body, a slug-like foot, two small arms, black eyes and three tendrils on her head.

===Special abilities===
Yin can absorb water into her head through her tentacles, and then release the stored water in powerful sprays when she wishes. Her tentacles can also be used for filling swimming pools. It is also shown that when Yin and Yang combine their powers, they are able to create rock/land.

===Weaknesses===
If Yin does not have any stored water or access to a water source, she will be rendered harmless. Also, if her tentacles are tangled up, she will be unable to carry out her primary function.

==Trivia==
*Yin was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery.
*Yin and [[Millie (220)|Millie]] are the only two experiments with the most limbs out of any known experiment, with eleven and ten respectively. Yin has eight tentacles, two tiny arms, and one large slug-like foot, while Millie has eight tentacle-like arms and two tentacle-like legs.
*Yin and [[Huggo (489)|Huggo]] are the only known experiments based on cephalopods. Though given Huggo and [[Thresher (544)|Thresher]]'s uncanny resemblance, Thresher may also be cephalopod-like.
*Yin and [[Cannonball (520)|Cannonball]] are the only known experiments whose functions are related to water.
*Lilo referred to Yin using masculine pronouns in the experiment's debut episode. In the episode "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]", Yin wore a pink bathrobe and nightcap to Lilo and Stitch's slumber party, but this still did not officially confirm the experiment's gender. Yin's true gender would not be re-confirmed as female until September 2018 and January 2019 in the respective Japanese and global versions of the mobile game ''[[disney:Disney Tsum Tsum (game)|Disney Tsum Tsum]]'', during a ''Lilo & Stitch: The Series''-themed event in [[:File:Yin Disney Tsum Tsum.png|the game that featured Yin]] and other experiments.
*Her name is derived from the concept of [[wikipedia:Yin and yang|yin and yang]]; in this case her name stems from the force of yin, which is associated with femininity, water, and cold, fitting her nature.
*Though Yin apparently has no visible mouth, a mouth appears on her in "[[Angel (episode)|Angel]]" when she and other experiments carry Stitch out of a ship. A mouth is also seen on Yin in a few scenes of "[[Slugger (episode)|Slugger]]", especially during Lilo and [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]]'s argument over the game rematch. A mouth appears on Yin again during the pillow fight scene in "Dupe".
*Yin's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is blue.
*Her [[:Category:Mislabeled Experiments|number was also given to]] [[Richter (513)|Richter]] (in "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]"), most likely due to Jumba's untidy [[Jumba's Computer|database]].
*Yin's head and body appear in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''.

He is designed to be a living laser bolt. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 603 was the 603rd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to act as a living laser bolt. 603 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]].

At an unknown point after this, Experiment 603 was activated.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
In "[[627 (episode)|627]]", 603 attacked a farmhouse, but was defeated when [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] trapped him in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]]. However, [[Gantu]] and [[627]] arrived shortly after, and both easily managed to take 603 from an inattentive Stitch. 603, named Zap, was later seen multiple times flying around [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]].

Zap reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], Stitch, and several other experiments in a rescue mission.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Zap, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
Zap made [[The Return of Amnesio|a cameo appearance]] in the ''Stitch!'' anime as one of the experiments in [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison cell]].

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Zap is a bright yellow living laser beam with lightning-shaped antennae, dark blue eyes with lightning-shaped pupils, a round brown nose, a wide mouth with sharp teeth, a green tongue, two brown stripes on his back, and a small, earless, limbless dog-like body.

===Special abilities===
Zap can hover in place and move side-to-side without moving forward, similar to a helicopter. He is capable of destroying targets at incredibly high speeds and can fly and bounce off surfaces like an ordinary laser bolt.

==Trivia==

*Zap is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed.

'''Zawp''', also known as '''Experiment 077''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to annoy individuals with his loud snoring. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "[[:Category:Mrs. Hasagawa's experiments|cats]]".

==Background and appearances==
Experiment 077 was the 77th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to annoy individuals by snoring loudly. 077 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch (626)|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of [[Kauai]]. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 077's pod being one of them.

===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''===
At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 077's pod for an apricot and washed it, activating the experiment. However, as 077 was not a very evil or destructive experiment, he was able to live a peaceful life with her, due to the latter seeing the former as a mere stray cat who needed a home, though he frequently snored loudly.

When [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] discovered that Mrs. Hasagawa kept several experiments as pets, they thought they were a danger to her and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], decided to capture them all. 077's capture was easy, as Lilo simply woke the sleeping experiment up and led him into a [[Prison Capsule|container]], where he continued napping.

077 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 077 was then named Zawp.

In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Zawp was oddly seen as one of the captive experiments in [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison cell]], suggesting [[Gantu]] caught Zawp, but this was an error. Zawp was then sent back to Gantu after [[Woops (600)|Experiment 600]] caused mischief and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]].

===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''===
Zawp was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 547 instead of 077.

===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''===
The first 624 experiments, including Zawp, were rounded up by [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]] and taken to a [[Aloha Stadium|stadium]] to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben (625)|Reuben]] and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed.

Zawp participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], and  is seen under attack by Leroys.

The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Zawp is a fat, purple sloth/wombat-like experiment with black claws, a dark blue stripe around his torso between his chest and stomach, a dark blue circle on the top of his head, dark blue-striped ears, small beady eyes, a larger belly and a slightly smaller, gold nose.

===Special abilities===
Zawp can produce loud snoring from his enormous nose.

==Trivia==
*Zawp was [[:Category:Experiments Activated Off-Screen|activated off-screen]].
*In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Zawp erroneously appeared with Gantu's other captive experiments, but he was already living with Mrs. Hasagawa, and Lilo and Stitch discovered him while Gantu was asleep.
*Zawp is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.

'''Experiment 000''' (pronounced as "'''Experiment Zero'''"), or simply '''Zero''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and his earliest experiment before he began working with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] and numbering his genetic creations. He is designed to be an ultimate killing monster and has enhanced his body with cybernetics at some point after escaping imprisonment. He appears as a minor antagonist in the second season of the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Background and appearances==
===[[Stitch!|''Stitch!'' anime]]===
He was the first experiment created before [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] started assigning numbers to his experiments, though Jumba later refers to him as "Experiment Zero" in his [[Experiment Zero|eponymous debut]]. Jumba was attempting to create the ultimate killer monster, and he was successful. However, his success also resulted in him being unable to control the experiment. Eventually, Jumba was forced to suspended Zero's cell activity and imprison him on an icy planet. Zero was eventually able to escape and acquired mechanical body parts, making him even more powerful, and became a ruthless warlord with a cyborg army in the galaxy. When Zero targets Hanpipi Nebula, the [[Grand Councilwoman]] contacts [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]] to help defeat him. Zero puts up a fight at first, but he was eventually defeated and captured by Stitch. Once restrained, Zero reveals he has a supernova warhead and then initiates its launch toward the Grand Council's headquarters on [[Planet Turo]], threatening the entire galaxy. Stitch was able to redirect the warhead into a black hole forming nearby, saving everyone. It is unknown what happened to Zero and his cyborg army after his defeat.

==Personality==
As Jumba created him to be the ultimate killing monster, Zero is ruthless, brutal, cruel, ambitious, destructive, and sadistic. Zero's programming is like Stitch's before he abandoned his destructive ways, which is to destroy everything in his path. However, Zero is proven to be too powerful and rebellious to control even for Jumba, which led him to suspend Zero and imprison him on an icy planet. Following his escape, Zero set out his objective to destroy the galaxy. Due to being on the icy planet, Zero didn't know he had [[experiments]] that were created after him, such as meeting Stitch and asking him who he is. However, Zero is remorseless and disregards the notion of family, having refused to listen to Stitch and his values on the subject. This is exemplified when Zero tried to attack Jumba after he was created, as well as when he built an army of robots to destroy the galaxy. When Zero launched his supernova warhead to destroy the galaxy, he didn't even care he would be caught in the explosion as well.

Zero is also very confident in his abilities, as he took on the [[Galactic Armada Crewmembers|Galactic Armada]] with his robot army and even faced off against Stitch himself. However, his confidence borders on overconfidence and arrogance, as well as making him reckless. When Zero destroyed Stitch's spaceship, his ship crashed into Zero's. When Zero launched his supernova warhead, he felt sure that Stitch wasn't going to stop it, and even when he redirected it in a black hole, Zero claimed that Stitch wouldn't survive. However, both of his claims proved wrong, as Stitch not only saved the galaxy, but also escaped the explosion.

==Biology==
===Physical appearance===
Zero's resemblance was close to a purple version of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]]. Originally 100% organic, Zero is now a cyborg, part machine, part alien. His organic body is now black while the rest is mostly metal alloys and reinforced plastic. His form resembles a cross between a type of lizard and koala (and robot). He has a two cyborg arms, three spider-like legs, and half-helmet with a cyclonic-like right eye from some unknown incident. In cyborg form, he is missing his nose.

===Special abilities===
In his original form, Zero has all the powers of Stitch. In Zero's cyborg form, his cyborg arms serve many purposes, such as cybernetic wiry rope, laser guns, a forked harpoon and welding tool, and his cyborg eye has zoom functions and improves his aim. He can manufacture many weapons, such as android minions, spaceships, and a doomsday device (supernova warhead).

==Trivia==
*Zero is the first experiment to be created by Jumba before he began working with Hämsterviel and numbering his genetic experiments, so he is classified as Experiment 000. He is referred to as "Experiment Zero" instead of "Experiment Zero-Zero-Zero", given that the number is a single digit rather than a whole three-digit.
*There is a misconception that Zero is named "Cyber". This moniker was never the experiment's actual name in any official ''[[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|Lilo & Stitch]]'' media. It is likely that fans came up with a unique moniker for him  before it was made clear that he was never given a name by [[disney:The Walt Disney Company|Disney]].
*Zero is similar to [[Dark End]] but not different from [[627]] and [[Leroy (629)|Leroy]], as while the latter pair were unable to be rehabilitated, the former pair were never mentioned to be able to be rehabilitated. Regardless, Zero and Dark End most likely would be unable to reform, as Zero proved to be uncontrollable after being created, while Dark End is loyal to [[Delia]].
**Like 627 and Leroy, Zero and Dark End also serve as dark versions of [[Stitch (626)|Stitch]], with Zero being too difficult to control where he disregarded the notion of family, Dark End having a low opinion on family and friends, and both 627 and Leroy being extremely cruel and destructive monsters that cannot be rehabilitated. 627, Leroy, Zero, and Dark End all serve as what Stitch would have become if he had never met [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and her ''ʻohana'' and been introduced to the meaning of family.
*Due to being imprisoned on an icy planet for countless years, Zero didn't know that there were experiments created after him, as he was surprised to see Stitch and asked him who he is.
*Zero (in cyborg form), [[Shrink (001)|Shrink]], and [[Pix (214)|Pix]] are the only known experiments whose legs resemble a tripod.
*He is one of the few experiments that are actually villains, along with [[Chopsuey (621)|Chopsuey]], 627, Leroy and [[Leroy Clones|his clones]], and Dark End, while all the other experiments were following their primary function.
